title: Software Support & Maintenance for Command and Control
Specialist Smoking Cessation Services
Condition Based Monitoring - ESA Devices
description:
YW seek a fully integrated Electrical Signature Analysis (ESA) platform and managed predictive maintenance service to improve operational resilience, asset reliability, energy efficiency and environmental performance across its motor-driven asset base.
The management of rotating assets through reactive maintenance, periodic inspections or disconnected monitoring systems can result in reduced visibility of asset condition, increased risk of unplanned failures, higher maintenance costs and avoidable operational and environmental impacts. A unified monitoring solution is required to provide continuous condition assessment, actionable intelligence and estate-wide visibility from a single platform.
The solution must deliver all of the following capabilities within a single, integrated platform and managed service:
Electrical Signature Analysis (ESA) -Continuous monitoring of three-phase voltage and current signatures from motor-driven rotating assets through hardware installed within motor control centres (MCCs), without the need for sensors mounted directly on assets. The solution shall collect and analyse electrical data continuously to identify developing faults and operational issues.
Predictive Maintenance Analytics- A combination of artificial intelligence, machine learning and expert analyst validation capable of identifying developing faults before failure occurs. The solution shall provide early warning notifications together with fault diagnosis, operational impact assessment and recommended corrective actions.
The platform shall detect operational asset and network events including:
- Blockages, clogging and ragging: A shift in the pump's electrical load caused by restricted or abnormal flow
- Airlocks: A characteristic load-signature change when trapped air disrupts normal flow 
- Burst rising mains: Loss of system pressure and altered flow following a burst, seen as a change in the pump's load signature
- Cavitation:  The load signature characteristic of a pump operating in cavitation
- Dry running and loss of prime: An abnormally low load condition characteristic of dry running
- Off-curve or inefficient operation: Operation sitting away from the pump's best-efficiency point
- Excess energy consumption: Elevated true power for the duty delivered
The solution should provide real-time or near-real-time identification of these events to enable proactive intervention and reduce operational risk.
The platform shall be supported by a human-in-the-loop managed service where findings are reviewed and validated by qualified condition monitoring specialists prior to notification. The service shall provide:
- Continuous asset monitoring
- Expert validation of findings
- Recommended corrective actions
- Performance reporting
- Ongoing technical support
The managed service shall operate on a 24/7 basis
The platform must be fully developed and commercially available. For clarity this means the product is not in early-stage development, not unproven, and not awaiting first deployment or first operational results.
The solution must have already demonstrated successful outcomes with other water companies, preferably within the UK and particularly with other WASCs.
The platform must be capable of integrating with core utility systems (e.g., SCADA, telemetry, SAP, GIS) and must meet minimum interoperability requirements to interpret data from devices and sensors currently deployed in our network

title: 26018 Bikeability Cycle Training Contract
description:
Bikeability Child Cycle Training has been delivered in Cambridgeshire since 2007. The county is among the top 20 highest performing local authorities with around 6,000 pupils receiving the training per annum, representing approximately 80% of the eligible audience.
Bikeability cycle training equips service users to choose cycling to travel more actively, more safely and more often, thus upholding the Council's following priorities:
- Enable full, healthy lives for all (promoting active and independent living)
- Ensure fairness and opportunity (through the best start for children and young people, and physical access to jobs)
- Support a green and sustainable county
The Bikeability Cycle Training Contract is being developed specifically to deliver the existing Bikeability grant award (2026 - 2029) and fulfil The Authority's grant recipient obligations, including the designated course level allocations.
The Programme objective for training providers in 2026/2027 is:
- Increase participation in, and achieve rider outcomes of, Level 2 Bikeability by the end of primary school (Year 6) to improve road safety, promoting responsible cycling behaviour, and benefitting health and wellbeing.
To enable delivery of the overall objective, further sub-objectives have been outlined:
- Prepare children for Level 2 through Level 1 and Learn to Ride
- Encourage schools to take part in Bikeability Courses
- Encourage participation in the Bikeability programme of under-represented groups
Full details of the procurement procedure, the Contract, required Services, and the process for bidding for this opportunity are detailed within the associated tender documents.
The Council is providing the total estimated value of the Contract in accordance with the PA23 requirements on valuing contracts and for transparency purposes. The estimate is however provided purely as a guide and no guarantee is given as to the actual value of the contract under that maximum.
The Council reserves the right to abandon the procurement and is not bound to award any contract arising from this Tender Notice. Bidders are solely responsible for all costs and expenses incurred in relation to the preparation and submission of their Tender response.

title: Belgium – Advisory architectural services – Raamovereenkomst voor de opmaak van Vastgoedstrategische Studies en Plannen
description: In het kader van de beleidsdoelstelling voor een stedelijke vastgoedstrategie wenst AG Vespa meerdere Strategische Vastgoedplannen (SVP) op te maken tijdens deze legislatuur. Het Strategisch Vastgoedplan is voor AG Vespa een werkinstrument om aan de hand van een gefundeerde onderbouwing richting te geven aan keuzes over de toekomst van de stedelijke vastgoedportefeuille. Het biedt een gestructureerd overzicht van de huidige situatie en toekomstige mogelijkheden, waardoor gefundeerde beslissingen over investeringen en ontwikkelingsstrategieën mogelijk worden. Deze plannen omvatten een analyse van de risico’s en de potentiëlen van het vastgoed alsook een inzicht in het huidige gebruik van de gebouwen, inclusief gebruikerstypes, bezettingsgraad en potentieel voor breder gebruik. Het uiteindelijke doel is om strategische keuzes en prioriteiten te formuleren die inspelen op zowel huidige als toekomstige behoeften. Er worden twee hoofdtypen plannen onderscheiden: thematische en gebiedsgebonden SVP’s. Thematische plannen richten zich op specifieke thema's en gebruikersnoden, waarbij het vastgoed een ondersteunende rol speelt. Hierbij staat de vraag naar de ruimtebehoeften van specifieke gebruikers centraal. Gebiedsgebonden plannen daarentegen, hebben een bredere focus op strategisch vastgoed binnen een bepaald geografisch gebied, waarbij de nadruk ligt op het optimaliseren van het gebruik en het ontwikkelingspotentieel van het vastgoed in dat gebied, vaak met een multifunctioneel oogmerk.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – FE 03.0659/2025/LRB - Resiliente Notstromversorgung für Straßenmeistereien
description: Straßen- und Autobahnmeistereien müssen auch bei extremen Witterungsbedingungen und längeren Stromausfällen rund um die Uhr einsatzbereit sein. Mit der geplanten Umstellung auf batterieelektrische Winterdienstfahrzeuge steigt der Strombedarf zusätzlich deutlich an. Eine zuverlässige Notstromversorgung zur Aufladung der Fahrzeuge (E-LKW, E-MGT), zum Betrieb der Heizungsanlagen sowie zur Sicherstellung der Werkstattfunktionsfähigkeit für mindestens 72 Stunden ist daher zwingend erforderlich. Ziel des Forschungsvorhabens ist die Entwicklung eines Konzepts zur Notstromversorgung dieser Einrichtungen. Verschiedene Technologien, darunter Batteriespeicher und Notstromaggregate, werden anhand von Zuverlässigkeit, Wirtschaftlichkeit, Bedienbarkeit und CO₂-Emissionen systematisch bewertet. Die Ergebnisse liefern eine fundierte Entscheidungsgrundlage für die Planung geeigneter Systeme, stärken die Resilienz des Winterdienstes als kritische Infrastruktur und geben einen wichtigen Impuls für die weitere Elektrifizierung der Fahrzeugflotte.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Ortsgemeinde Kinderbeuern - Kindertagesstätte "Zauberwald" Kinderbeuern: Anbau, Umbau- und Sanierungsmaßnahmen, Los 2: Technische Ausrüstung HLS und Elektro (Kopie)
description: Die Auftraggeberin und Bauherrin, die Ortsgemeinde Kinderbeuern, Kondelstraße 24a, 54538 Kinderbeuern, möchte die bestehende, zweigruppige Kindertagesstätte "Zauberwald" in Kinderbeuern auf Grundlage des Kita-Zukunftsgesetzes zu einer dreigruppigen Einrichtung erweitern. Vorgesehen sind eine Nestgruppe für Kinder unter drei Jahren sowie zwei Regelgruppen mit einer Gesamtaufnahmekapazität von 54 Kindern. Die heutige Einrichtung deckt mit maximal 32 Plätzen den Bedarf nicht. Die Leistungsphasen 1-4 der Maßnahme sind bereits ausgeführt. Aufgrund der prognostizierten rückläufigen Kinderzahlen in der Ortsgemeinde musste die Bedarfsplanung durch die Ortsgemeinde und Jugendamt erneut überprüft werden, weswegen die Vergabe der Leistungsphasen 5-9 HOAI vorerst zurückgestellt wurde. Inzwischen liegt die Entscheidung über die Weiterführung der Baumaßnahme auf Grundlage der vorliegenden Planung vor, sodass die Vergabe der Leistungsphasen 5-9 HOAI erfolgen kann. Die Maßnahme umfasst zwei Anbaubereiche sowie umfangreiche Umbau- und Sanierungsarbeiten im Bestand: - Größerer Anbau mit Gruppenraum U3, Schlafraum, Wickelraum, Lagerraum, Flur mit Garderoben, Behinderten-WC, Personal-WC, Personalraum und Abstellraum; - Zweiter Anbau mit Technikraum, WC/Umkleide für die Hauswirtschaftskraft sowie neuer Küche mit Spülbereich, Vorraum und Magazin; Änderung des Eingangsbereichs/Windfangs; Umbau und Sanierung des Waschraums; - Umbau- und Sanierungsmaßnahmen im Bestand: Anlage eines Stiefelgangs am seitlichen Eingang, Abbruch von Innen- und Zwischenwänden zur Schaffung von Neben- und Bistroflächen, Erneuerung von Bodenbelägen, Einbau neuer Akustikdecken, energetische Maßnahmen (Decken, Fassade, Fußboden) und barrierefreie Erschließung; - Überarbeitung und Neuaufbau der Außenanlagen und Zuwegungen sowie Ergänzung von Einfriedung und Toren, soweit erforderlich. Während der Umsetzung findet der laufende Kitabetrieb in einem Ausweichquartier statt. Die Planung soll nach erfolgter Beauftragung zügig durchgeführt werden. Die Ausführung des Vorhabens ist bis Ende 2028 geplant.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Arbeitskräftepotenziale durch Digitalisierung und KI inklusiv nutzen
description: Der Erhalt und die zügige Befähigung einer digital kompetenten Arbeitsgesellschaft, die trotz demografischem Wandel und Fachkräftemangel zu einer produktiven und wettbewerbsfähigen Volkswirtschaft beiträgt, liegt im strategischen Interesse des Bundes. Für die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit von Unternehmen ist v.a. die Sicherung der Fachkräftebasis entscheidend. Angesichts einer alternden Gesellschaft besteht dringender Handlungsbedarf, die Beschäftigten möglichst lange unter guten und gesunden Arbeitsbedingungen in den Betrieben zu halten, ungenutzte inländische Potenziale zu erschließen und die Arbeitswelt inklusiver und diverser aufzustellen. Digitale Technologien und v.a. Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) bieten die Möglichkeit, Menschen mit altersbedingten, mit kognitiven oder mit psychischen Beeinträchtigungen länger und gesünder im Arbeitsmarkt zu halten oder zu integrieren und ein alters- und behinderungsgerechtes Arbeitsumfeld zu schaffen. Der zu vergebende Forschungsauftrag (Leistungszeitraum: 2027–2028) zielt auf die Identifikation der Möglichkeiten und Bedarfe von Kleinen und Mittleren Unternehmen (KMU) und Erwerbstätigen mit Beeinträchtigungen für die Nutzung technologischer Unterstützung im Betrieb und damit auf das Heben von Arbeitskräftepotenzialen mithilfe von Digitalisierung und KI. Da hierzu noch keine systematische und umfängliche Darstellung vorliegt, bedarf es der praxisorientierten und -tauglichen wissenschaftlichen Erforschung, wie KMU Beschäftigte mit Beeinträchtigungen durch den Einsatz neuer Technologien (z.B. KI) im Betrieb unterstützen können. Es soll auch ein Beitrag geleistet werden, das Erfahrungswissen der Beschäftigten zu sichern und bestehende (Beratungs-)Strukturen zu stärken, indem übergeordnete Institutionen (z.B. Inklusionsämter, Industrie- und Handelskammern, Wirtschafts-Spitzenverbände) unterstützt werden, KMU bei Fragen der digitalen Transformation zu beraten. Der Forschungsauftrag wird als Wettbewerblicher Dialog mit vorgeschaltetem Teilnahmewettbewerb europaweit ausgeschrieben. Die Leistungen können durch ein Konsortium erbracht werden. Um die gesetzten Ziele zu erreichen, sind durch die Auftragnehmenden, die das Forschungsvorhaben umsetzen, mind. folgende Arbeitspakete zu leisten. Die genaue Ausgestaltung soll durch die Bietenden im Rahmen des Wettbewerblichen Dialogs erläutert werden: 1. Grundlagenforschung und Bedarfsanalyse: o Durchführung einer empirisch-explorativen Studie zur Identifikation und systematischen Darstellung der Bedürfnisse von KMU und deren Beschäftigten mit Beeinträchtigungen. o Erstellung einer Übersicht geeigneter technologischer und KI-basierter Lösungen. o Eignungsprüfung von KI-Technologien für spezifische Arbeitsfelder; bei fehlender Eignung soll der Bedarf an alternativen Lösungen aufgezeigt werden. 2. Umsetzungsstrategien und Implementierung: o Erarbeitung von Umsetzungsvorschlägen und Hilfestellungen für die Implementierung und langfristige Nutzung der identifizierten Technologien. o Identifikation und Erstellung adressatengerechter Informationsmittel und -wege. o Einbindung von Feedback und Evaluation durch ko-kreativen Ansatz. 3. Überprüfung und Anpassung: o Überprüfung und Testung der entwickelten Informationsmittel und -wege sowie deren Präzisierung und Anpassung. o Prüfung der Wirksamkeit der (KI-)Unterstützungsinstrumente. 4. Dissemination inkl. eines breitenwirksamen Unterstützungsangebots in der Fläche: o Durchgängige Dissemination zur Verstärkung der Außenwirkung der Projektziele und -ergebnisse. Adressat*innen des Forschungsauftrags: Wissenschaftseinrichtungen, Hochschulen und Forschungsinstitutionen. Gegenstand und Adressat*innen der Forschungsmaßnahme: KMU und übergeordnete Institutionen, die entsprechend bei der Projektumsetzung einzubeziehen sind. Auch sind Perspektiven betroffener Erwerbstätiger, von Organisationen und Verbänden der Selbstvertretung, Beratung und Selbsthilfe von und für Menschen mit Behinderungen zu berücksichtigen.

title: Belgium – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – "Studie van de N32 Roeselare – omvorming rotonde Meensesteenweg x Meiboomlaan – van projectnota tot en met opvolging van de werken "
description: De rotonde Meensesteenweg Meiboomlaan te Roeselare, ook wel rotonde ‘Spillebad’ genoemd, vormt het gevaarlijkste kruispunt in West-Vlaanderen. De rotonde is zeer onveilig voor fietsers. De Vlaamse overheid wil dit kruispunt op relatief korte termijn infrastructureel aanpakken om de verkeersveiligheid te verbeteren, voor de weggebruikers in het algemeen en voor de zachte weggebruiker in het bijzonder. De heraanleg moet de leesbaarheid van het kruispunt verhogen, de infrastructuur aanpassen aan hedendaagse richtlijnen en de toegankelijkheid voor zwakke weggebruikers optimaliseren. Er wordt gestreefd naar een vlotte en maximaal conflictvrije afwikkeling van voetgangers, fietsers, openbaar vervoer en gemotoriseerd verkeer. Het kruispunt is een kruispunt met relatief hoge intensiteiten. Op de rotonde komen zowel de Meiboomlaan (N37), de Meensesteenweg (N32), de Westlaan als de Hippoliet Spilleboutdreef (N37) uit. De stad Roeselare benadrukt het belang van de ruimtelijke integratie van het kruispunt binnen de stedelijke context als ‘zuidelijke’ toegangspoort naar de stad. Ook de fietssnelweg F37 loopt over het kruispunt en moet hierin geïntegreerd worden. Recent werd “de Stroroute”, het deel van de fietssnelweg voor het deel ten zuiden van de R32 (Grote ring) gerealiseerd. In afwachting van een volledige herinrichting van de rotonde werden, als quick-win, werden reeds verhoogde verkeerseilanden geplaatst om de fietsers meer bescherming te bieden. Het projectgebied is gelegen binnen de bebouwde kom. Op alle takken geldt een snelheidsregime van 50 km per uur. Het betrokken kruispunt is op heden ingericht als een vijftaksrotonde. Het is een eenstrookrotonde met enkelrichtingsfietspaden, afgescheiden van de rijweg door middel van markeringen en/of plooibakens. Op de tak Meiboomlaan is een bypass aangelegd welke het verkeer afleidt naar de Meensesteenweg. Het kruispunt Meensesteenweg x Heilig-Hartstraat, ca. 40m ten zuiden van de rotonde, is ingericht als een rechts-inrechts-uit-kruispunt. De stad Roeselare wenst in het studiegebied de rioleringen toekomstgericht te ‘optimaliseren’. Deze toekomstgerichte optimalisatie dient vanuit de ontwerpopdracht bestudeerd te worden in functie van latere aangrenzende dossiers op de diverse aansluitende takken ( Noot : Voor het optimaliseren van de riolering is al voorbereidend onderzoek gebeurd, dat als vertrekbasis overgenomen kan worden ).De diensten omvatten: - de opmaak van een voorontwerp en bijhorende goedgekeurde projectnota - de opmaak en ingave van het dossier aanvraag omgevingsvergunning - de opmaak van een technisch ontwerp bovenbouw - de opmaak van een technisch ontwerp riolering - opvolging van de werken – voorbereiding en afronding - opvolging van de werken – tijdens uitvoering - het uitvoeren van een verkeerskundig onderzoek (GP): parkeeronderzoek + verkeerskundige impactanalyse - het opzoeken van de grenzen van het openbaar domein (lokale wegen) - de opmaak van eventuele onteigeningsplannen - het afpalen van innamegrenzen - opstellen van een boomeffectenanalyse AID-nummer: WWV/INV/N32/20/S2 7 - het uitvoeren van een bemalingsstudie, incl. opmaak bemalingsnota en monitoringsplan - het organiseren van coördinatievergaderingen - het organiseren van ontwerpproefsleuven - opmaak van 3D-visualisaties - geraamde som voor drukwerk in het kader van communicatie en participatie - ondersteuning in participatie en communicatie (profielen participatie- en communicatiedeskundige) Voor de volledige studieopdracht geldt: Om tijdens het volledige ontwerpproces de nodige aandacht aan verkeersveiligheid, verkeerstechniek, human factor en wegontwerp te verzekeren, moet er binnen ieder ontwerpteam minstens één lid over een getuigschrift van een erkende opleiding tot verkeersveiligheidsauditor beschikken (https://www.vlaanderen.be/mobiliteit-en-openbare-werken/verkeer/verkeersveiligheidsaudit). Het is de taak van dit lid om knelpunten met betrekking tot de verkeersveiligheid voor de verschillende categorieën weggebruikers op te sporen, de ernst daarvan te benoemen en het ontwerpproces daarop te (laten) bijsturen. Voor goedkeuring van projectnota en aanbestedingsfase uitvoering zal de opdrachtnemer een overleg voorzien waarbij de ontwerpplannen met opdrachtgever en het teamlid doorgenomen worden. Aandachtspunten en genomen afwegingen worden met de nodige achtergrondinformatie opgelijst in een naslagwerk zodat deze in de vervolgstappen (tot en met overdracht aan het bevoegde wegendistrict) niet telkens opnieuw in vraag gesteld worden.

title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – 10030774-Providing Technical Assistance on Industrial Decarbonisation, CBAM Readiness, Gender Inclusion, Pilot and Upscaling
description: India's industrial sector plays a central role in the country's economic growth, while also contributing significantly to energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. As India advances its climate ambitions, including the target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070, industrial decarbonisation and energy efficiency have become key priorities for enabling a sustainable and inclusive transition. In this context, the Indo-German bilateral cooperation between the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), implemented by GIZ, supports industrial decarbonisation through energy efficiency measures. Acting as a service provider and implementing agency for German international cooperation for sustainable development, GIZ works with Indian and German partners on project implementation and delivering effective solutions that contribute to sustainable transformation. The cooperation between the German side and BEE builds on a long-standing partnership in the field of energy efficiency and industrial transformation. Over the years, the collaboration has continuously supported the implementation of the Energy Conservation Act and contributed to a range of initiatives targeting both large industries and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). While significant progress has been achieved, considerable untapped potential for industrial energy efficiency and decarbonisation remains, underlining the need for strengthened policy frameworks, innovative market instruments, and scaled implementation approaches. Against this background, the project "Energy Efficiency" supports industrial decarbonisation through four key intervention areas: (a) developing strategies for industrial decarbonisation, including in the context of the Indian Carbon Market; (b) supporting the design and implementation of incentive schemes such as ADEETIE; (c) promoting industrial energy efficiency measures through demonstration projects and awareness campaigns; and (d) advancing gender equality and social inclusion in the industrial transition. Through these interventions, the project aims to strengthen policy frameworks, market mechanisms, institutional capacities, and inclusive approaches for a sustainable industrial transformation.

title: Germany – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Bundesinitiative „Hilfe und Unterstützung bei ungewollter Kinderlosigkeit“ - Aktualisierung der Studie Ungewollte Kinderlosigkeit 2020
description: In den Jahren 2012 und 2019 hat das BMFSFJ Studien zur Situation gewollt und ungewollt kinderloser Frauen und Männer beim Delta Institut in Auftrag gegeben. In 2012 wurde im Auftrag des BMBFSFJ durch das Delta Institut erstmals eine deutschlandweite Studie zur gewollten und ungewollten Kinderlosigkeit durchgeführt. Ziel war es, die Gründe und Ursachen von ungewollter Kinderlosigkeit zu erforschen und herauszufinden, ob ungewollte Kinderlosigkeit ggf. milieuspezifisch unterschiedlich häufig verteilt ist. So wurde deutlich, dass bei vielen Kinderlosen es zunächst eine gewollte Kinderlosigkeit gab, die aufgrund des Aufschiebens des Kinderwunsches in ein höheres Alter dann zu einer ungewollten Kinderlosigkeit führte. Gründe für das Aufschieben waren jedoch nicht nur eine fehlende Partnerschaft oder der Wunsch sich zunächst beruflich zu etablieren, sondern auch das mangelnde Wissen über Fertilität und reproduktionsmedizinische Behandlungsmöglichkeiten. Um die Lebenswirklichkeiten und Einstellungen von Menschen mit unerfülltem Kinderwunsch näher zu betrachten, wurde in 2019 eine umfangreiche Studie zur Situation ungewollt Kinderloser in Deutschland durchgeführt. Hierbei wurden unter anderem die Einstellung zum Kinderwunsch, die Gründe der ungewollten Kinderlosigkeit, die Kenntnisse von Fertilität im Lebensverlauf, die Inanspruchnahme reproduktionsmedizinischer Behandlungen, aber auch die Diskriminierungserfahrungen aufgrund von Kinderlosigkeit sowie die Angst vor Stigmatisierung erfragt. Es war und ist die erste repräsentative Studie in Deutschland, die ungewollt kinderlosen Frauen und Männern im Alter von 20 bis 50 Jahren in den Blick nimmt und ihre Einstellung und Erfahrungen erfragt. Ergebnisse waren unter anderem, dass jedes zehnte Paar zwischen 20 und 50 Jahren ungewollt kinderlos ist. Mittlerweile sprechen viele sogar von jedem achten, sogar siebten Paar. Diese Vermutung lässt sich durch die gestiegene Anzahl der reproduktionsmedizinischen Behandlungen (2019: 110.105; 2024: 134.281) stützen, bedarf jedoch einer wissenschaftlichen Validierung. Weiterhin wurde festgestellt, dass 44 Prozent der Frauen und 55 Prozent der Männer, die bereits viele Jahre einen unerfüllten Kinderwunsch haben, noch nie (!) auf den Gedanken gekommen sind, dass es auf natürlichem Wege nicht klappen könnte. Weitere bedeutende Ergebnisse der Studie waren, dass nur 25 Prozent aller ungewollt Kinderloser medizinisch hat abklären lassen, ob organische oder hormonelle Gründe eine Ursache für die Kinderlosigkeit sein könnten; gleichzeitig stellte mehr als die Hälfte aller Kinderlosen fest, dass ungewollte Kinderlosigkeit in der Gesellschaft tabuisiert sei und erklärte, bereits eigene Diskriminierungs- und Stigmatisierungserfahrungen gemacht zu haben. In den letzten beiden Studien konnte außerdem festgestellt werden, dass der Anteil der ungewollt Kinderlosen von allen Kinderlosen im Alter von 20-50 Jahren von 25% auf 32 % signifikant gestiegen ist. Anhand der gestiegenen reproduktionsmedizinischen Behandlungen liegt die Vermutung nahe, dass der Anteil weiter gestiegen ist. Dies muss jedoch wissenschaftlich fundiert überprüft werden. Trends nach Milieuzugehörigkeit und Lebensphase sind hier vor allem für zielgruppenspezifische Maßnahmen für eine wirkungsorientierte Maßnahmenentwicklung wichtig. Die Studien finden in der Wissenschaft aufgrund ihrer Einzigartigkeit immer noch großen Anklang. Zudem erhielt das Fachreferat häufig Anfragen zu den Ergebnissen der Studien sowie Nachfragen, ob eine Neuauflage geplant ist. Ungewollt Kinderlose sind im Querschnitt der Bevölkerung zu finden. Wichtig ist es deshalb, die verschiedenen sozialdemographischen- und bevölkerungsstrukturellen Hintergründe zu erforschen, um dem hochsensiblen und komplexen Forschungsgegenstand gerecht zu werden. Weiterhin wurde identifiziert, dass sich sowohl die Einstellungen zur Kinderlosigkeit als auch die damit verbundenen Erfahrungen deutlich unterscheiden. Gleichzeitig verfügen die Personen entsprechend über unterschiedliche soziale und kulturelle Ressourcen. Die letzte Studie zur ungewollten Kinderlosigkeit basiert auf Daten, die bereits sieben Jahre alt sind. Um die Entwicklungen beim Thema ungewollte Kinderlosigkeit zu überprüfen, soll auf Grundlage der Studie 2020 eine Aktualisierung vorgenommen werden. Durch die aktuell intensive Diskussion zur Reproduktionsmedizin nicht nur in Fachkreisen, sondern insbesondere in der medialen Öffentlichkeit hat sich möglicherweise die Wahrnehmung des Themas bei Betroffenen verändert. Auch dies soll mit der Studie kontrolliert werden. Ein zentrales Moment dieser Untersuchung soll die Vergleichbarkeit mit den Zahlen von 2019 sein. Daher soll die Untersuchung methodisch identisch angelegt sein. So sollen in der Repräsentativbefragung viele Fragen in gleicher Form gestellt werden, um Veränderungen in der Grundgesamtheit sowie in den verschiedenen Teilgruppen messen zu können. Trotzdem soll es Raum für Neues geben: Es sollen neue Fragen aufgenommen werden, um jüngere Entwicklungen sowie neue gleichstellungspolitische Erkenntnisinteressen (auch der Reproduktionsmedizin und psychosozialen Befragung) mit zu erfassen. Weiterhin soll die Studie, wie auch die Vorgängeruntersuchungen, als Mixed-Method-Ansatz angelegt sein. Durch die Kombination verschiedener Ansätze können Ergebnisse überprüft, ergänzt oder vertieft werden. In vier Gruppenwerkstätten sollen deshalb qualitative Erhebungen stattfinden. Die Vorteile der Methodenkombination sind u.a.: Höhere Glaubwürdigkeit und Validität der Ergebnisse; Umfassenderes Verständnis des Forschungsgegenstands; Ausgleich der Schwächen einzelner Methoden sowie die Möglichkeit der vertieften Untersuchung besonders spannender Milieus. Die Studie soll durch die Einbeziehung von fachwissenschaftlicher Expertise begleitet werden, um neueste Trends und Entwicklungen zu berücksichtigen und aktuelle wissenschaftliche Debatten zu berücksichtigen.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Ortsgemeinde Kinderbeuern - Kindertagesstätte "Zauberwald" Kinderbeuern: Anbau, Umbau- und Sanierungsmaßnahmen, Los 2: Technische Ausrüstung HLS und Elektro
description: Die Auftraggeberin und Bauherrin, die Ortsgemeinde Kinderbeuern, Kondelstraße 24a, 54538 Kinderbeuern, möchte die bestehende, zweigruppige Kindertagesstätte "Zauberwald" in Kinderbeuern auf Grundlage des Kita-Zukunftsgesetzes zu einer dreigruppigen Einrichtung erweitern. Vorgesehen sind eine Nestgruppe für Kinder unter drei Jahren sowie zwei Regelgruppen mit einer Gesamtaufnahmekapazität von 54 Kindern. Die heutige Einrichtung deckt mit maximal 32 Plätzen den Bedarf nicht. Die Leistungsphasen 1-4 der Maßnahme sind bereits ausgeführt. Aufgrund der prognostizierten rückläufigen Kinderzahlen in der Ortsgemeinde musste die Bedarfsplanung durch die Ortsgemeinde und Jugendamt erneut überprüft werden, weswegen die Vergabe der Leistungsphasen 5-9 HOAI vorerst zurückgestellt wurde. Inzwischen liegt die Entscheidung über die Weiterführung der Baumaßnahme auf Grundlage der vorliegenden Planung vor, sodass die Vergabe der Leistungsphasen 5-9 HOAI erfolgen kann. Die Maßnahme umfasst zwei Anbaubereiche sowie umfangreiche Umbau- und Sanierungsarbeiten im Bestand: - Größerer Anbau mit Gruppenraum U3, Schlafraum, Wickelraum, Lagerraum, Flur mit Garderoben, Behinderten-WC, Personal-WC, Personalraum und Abstellraum; - Zweiter Anbau mit Technikraum, WC/Umkleide für die Hauswirtschaftskraft sowie neuer Küche mit Spülbereich, Vorraum und Magazin; Änderung des Eingangsbereichs/Windfangs; Umbau und Sanierung des Waschraums; - Umbau- und Sanierungsmaßnahmen im Bestand: Anlage eines Stiefelgangs am seitlichen Eingang, Abbruch von Innen- und Zwischenwänden zur Schaffung von Neben- und Bistroflächen, Erneuerung von Bodenbelägen, Einbau neuer Akustikdecken, energetische Maßnahmen (Decken, Fassade, Fußboden) und barrierefreie Erschließung; - Überarbeitung und Neuaufbau der Außenanlagen und Zuwegungen sowie Ergänzung von Einfriedung und Toren, soweit erforderlich. Während der Umsetzung findet der laufende Kitabetrieb in einem Ausweichquartier statt. Die Planung soll nach erfolgter Beauftragung zügig durchgeführt werden. Die Ausführung des Vorhabens ist bis Ende 2028 geplant.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Negative-Trust-Architekturen (Ne-Trust)
description: Die Agentur für Innovation in der Cybersicherheit GmbH (Cyberagentur) kündigt für den 22.09.2026 ein Partnering Event zum Forschungsprogramm „Negative-Trust Architekturen“ (Ne-Trust) an. IT-Systeme sehen sich einer zunehmenden Bedrohung durch Innentäterinnen und -täter ausgesetzt, die sich oftmals unbemerkt innerhalb von Systemen bewegen, IT-Strukturen erkunden und Schäden anrichten. Die zunehmende Wahrnehmung dieses Angriffsvektors wird zusätzlich durch die Nutzung von künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) befeuert. Diese aktuellen und zukünftigen Herausforderungen machen auch vor den Toren von Verwaltung, Verteidigung und Sicherheitsbehörden nicht Halt. Um Bedrohungslagen wie diesen vorbereitet zu begegnen, haben IT-Sicherheitsparadigmen eine besondere Bedeutung: Sie prägen, wie IT-Systeme grundsätzlich entworfen, betrieben und geschützt werden. Als etabliertestes Beispiel gilt „Zero Trust“. Als Maßnahme gegen Insiderangriffe stößt dieser Ansatz jedoch an seine Grenzen. Zentrale Grundlagenwerke, unter anderem die NIST-Leitlinie SP 800-207, weisen auf verbleibende Lücken und offenen Forschungsbedarf hin. Vor diesem Hintergrund liegt die Notwendigkeit, ein weiterentwickeltes und neuartiges Paradigma zur effektiveren Abwehr von Innentäterinnen und -tätern zu erkunden. Ziel von Ne-Trust ist es deshalb, eine nachweisbar verbesserte Erkennung und proaktivere Abwehr von zunehmenden und veränderlichen Insider-Bedrohungen für IT-Systeme zu ermöglichen und somit über Zero Trust hinaus weiterzuentwickeln. Das Programm baut auf dem neuartigen Begriff „Negative Trust“ auf, der in Verbindung mit Zero Trust steht, jedoch als autarker Name für ein eigenes Paradigma ausgelegt werden kann. Es bestehen erste Versuche der begrifflichen Definition von Negative Trust, so z.B. in Richtung von Deception Technology. Eine wissenschaftliche und interdisziplinäre Auseinandersetzung mit dem Begriff in Richtung eines eigenständigen, weiterentwickelten IT-Sicherheitsparadigmas ist bislang aber noch nicht erfolgt. Ne-Trust setzt genau an dieser Lücke an und eröffnet die Möglichkeit für eine erstmalige wissenschaftliche Auseinandersetzung mit und Erarbeitung von Negative-Trust-Architekturen. Die Cyberagentur öffnet damit den Raum für neuartige und disruptive Forschungsperspektiven und setzt somit frühzeitige Impulse für Cybersicherheitsparadigmen und IT-Sicherheitsarchitekturen von und für Übermorgen. Diese Zukunftsperspektive, ebenso wie die sprunghafte Verbesserung in der Abwehrfähigkeit von IT-Systemen und die komplexe Betrachtung von konzeptionellen, technologischen, sozialen und rechtlichen Fragestellungen, unterstreichen sowohl den ambitionierten als auch den wagnisbehafteten Charakter des Forschungsprogramms. Die Cyberagentur lädt am 22.09.2026 von 14:00 bis 17:00 Uhr zu einem virtuellen Partnering Event für das Forschungsprogramm Ne-Trust ein. Es richtet sich an Unternehmen, Start-ups, Hochschulen und Forschungseinrichtungen, die sich mit IT-Sicherheitsarchitekturen, Cyberabwehr oder angrenzenden technischen, sozialen und rechtlichen Fragestellungen beschäftigen. Die fachliche Breite des Programms erfordert unterschiedliche Perspektiven. Das Partnering Event soll deshalb potenzielle Forschungspartner miteinander in Kontakt bringen und die Bildung interdisziplinärer Konsortien unterstützen. Nach einer Vorstellung der Cyberagentur und des Forschungsprogramms erhalten die Teilnehmenden die Möglichkeit, ihre fachlichen Schwerpunkte in jeweils zweiminütigen Kurzpräsentationen vorzustellen. Auf diese Weise können Kompetenzen sichtbar gemacht, Schnittstellen identifiziert und mögliche Partnerschaften für spätere Forschungsprojekte angebahnt werden. Die Anmeldung zum Partnering Event ist bis einschließlich 16. September 2026 unter folgendem Link möglich: https://www.cyberagentur.de/programme/ne-trust/ Teilnehmende, die sich während der Veranstaltung vorstellen möchten, senden ihre Präsentationsfolie bis spätestens 18. September 2026 an ne-trust@cyberagentur.de.

title: Prisoners Building Homes - Professional, Technical and Programme Delivery Support Services
description:
1. Background
Local Partnerships is the host organisation for Prisoners Building Homes (PBH), a government programme bringing together housing delivery and rehabilitation outcomes.
PBH works with public-sector organisations to unlock land for high-quality, affordable homes while creating employment, training and skills opportunities for people in prison and post-release.
PBH supports organisations across the housing development lifecycle, including site identification and assessment, feasibility, planning, procurement and construction support.
The PBH programme is growing and Local Partnerships is considering procuring external professional, technical and programme-delivery capability to supplement the PBH team and provide flexible capacity as the housing pipeline develops.
This Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) will inform the scope, structure, commercial model and procurement strategy for any future requirement. No final procurement structure has been determined.
2. Purpose and Delivery Principles
Local Partnerships has not predetermined the final procurement structure but wishes to avoid disconnected service delivery. 
The intention of the proposed procurement is to supplement, not replace, PBH's internal capability. Providers would work collaboratively with the PBH team and participating public-sector organisations, while PBH retains programme oversight, standards, client relationships and strategic direction.
In terms of any procured services, Local Partnerships does not intend to establish a fragmented model requiring management of multiple disconnected consultants across individual sites or development stages. The preferred outcome is an integrated model delivering continuity and clear accountability, potentially through a multidisciplinary consortium, lead delivery partner with an integrated specialist supply chain, or equivalent arrangement, providing:
•	continuity of site knowledge through the development lifecycle;
•	clear accountability for coordinating and progressing sites;
•	coordinated access to required specialisms and professional disciplines;
•	flexible capacity and scalability as the number, stage and complexity of sites change in a nationwide context;
•	access to specialist and SME capability without transferring supply-chain management to the PBH team;
•	consistent PBH processes, standards, data and reporting delivering value for money; and
•	opportunities for innovation (see section 4, below).
This PME will test the optimum contractual and commercial structure, including how SMEs and specialists can participate without increasing PBH's supplier-management burden.
3. Potential Scope of Services
The potential service requirements may include:
Portfolio and Site Assessment: portfolio review; identification of housing opportunities; desktop assessment; opportunities and constraints analysis; site grading/prioritisation; development capacity; feasibility/viability; and identification of planning, infrastructure and delivery constraints.
Development and Programme Management: development, programme and project management; multidisciplinary team coordination; programme planning; information, risk, issue and stakeholder management; governance/reporting; funding/delivery strategy; and coordination across multiple sites and clients.
Feasibility, Design and Planning: feasibility/capacity studies; concept design/layouts; architectural services; planning strategy, pre-application and applications; technical design coordination; specialist consultants/surveys; stakeholder engagement; and Section 106/planning support.
Commercial, Viability and Procurement: quantity surveying, cost planning, viability and commercial advice; funding-gap analysis; procurement strategy; risk allocation; tender documentation; specifications/contract particulars; procurement management; tender evaluation; and support appointing housebuilders/contractors.
Construction and Employer's Agent: Employer's Agent and contract administration; development/project management; programme monitoring; cost/risk management; quality assurance; issue resolution; stakeholder coordination; governance/client reporting; contractor performance information; and completion/handover support.
The model should support a large and changing pipeline and coordinate required disciplines as an integrated delivery team.
4. Technology, Data, Standardisation and Scalability
Local Partnerships wishes to understand how innovative use of technology, data, automation and standardisation could improve efficiency and scalability, including:
•	rapid site assessment and constraints analysis;
•	portfolio prioritisation and viability;
•	data and workflow management;
•	multidisciplinary coordination;
•	dashboards and performance reporting;
•	knowledge management and systems integration; and
•	standardised appraisal, feasibility, viability, governance, technical, procurement and reporting processes.
Local Partnerships welcomes approaches combining professional expertise, integrated processes, technology, data and automation to increase capacity efficiently while retaining appropriate professional judgement.
Note that technology relating to management of justice-involved individuals or PBH workforce integration is outside scope.
5. PBH Workforce Integration (NOTE - RETAINED FUNCTION)
Workforce integration is a core PBH function and IS NOT within the scope of the proposed external services.
PBH will retain responsibility for prison and justice-partner relationships; PBH housebuilder accreditation and standards; employer engagement/readiness; engagement with justice-involved individuals; matching to employment and skills opportunities; safeguarding and associated risk management; employment/skills pathways; and monitoring workforce and social-value outcomes.
External providers will not manage PBH participants or operate PBH's workforce-integration programme.
Providers will work alongside this retained function and, where relevant, provide project, programme, contractor and construction information enabling PBH to plan opportunities and monitor delivery.
6. Organisations We Would Like to Hear From
Local Partnerships welcomes expressions of interest from the broadest range of relevant organisations. 
This may include responses from multidisciplinary professional teams; existing or potential consortia; lead delivery partners; development/programme managers; property and construction consultancies; integrated architectural, planning, commercial and technical teams; Employer's Agent providers; quantity surveyors/cost consultants; specialist technical advisers; technology, PropTech, data and automation providers; and SMEs.
It is recognised that all capability may not reside within one single organisation and welcomes collaborative arrangements capable of providing an integrated multidisciplinary service.
7. Estimated Contract Value and Contract Dates
Local Partnerships is considering an initial 12-month contract commencing approximately 1 April 2027, with options for up to three further 12-month extensions, giving a potential maximum term of four years.
Extensions would be at Local Partnerships' discretion, taking account of performance, PBH programme requirements, pipeline, funding, PBH internal capability and value for money.
Anticipated expenditure is approximately £1m-£1.5m per annum, giving an indicative maximum contract value of up to £6 million over the full potential four-year period. There is no guarantee of minimum expenditure, annual spend, volume of work or number of sites. Actual expenditure will be demand-led and dependent on the number, stage and complexity of sites, services required and availability of PBH internal resource.
Local Partnerships is interested in commercial arrangements enabling capacity and expenditure to flex with the PBH pipeline while maintaining value for money.

title: Specialist Technical and Commercial Advisory for Rail and Other Transport Systems Framework (STARFour)
description:
In line with its commitment to increasing investment in the UK’s transport infrastructure, the Department for Transport (“DfT”) requires ongoing access to high-quality, specialist technical and commercial advice services. This need is currently fulfilled through the STARThree Framework, which succeeded the Specialist Technical Advisory for Rail (STARTwo) Framework—both managed by the Department’s Group Commercial Directorate (“GCD”).
DfT is now procuring the Specialist Technical & Commercial Advice for Rail & Other Transport Systems Framework (the “STARFour Framework”) to succeed the STARThree Framework (expiring 30 July 2027). 
The STARFour Framework will be a multi-lot, multi-supplier framework designed to provide specialist technical and commercial advice to support rail and wider transport programmes and projects.
The STARFour Framework will provide DfT and other qualifying bodies (as detailed below) with access to niche transport expertise across rail and other transport modes, supporting strategic planning, operations, commercial delivery, infrastructure and asset advice, and project and programme management. 
Building on the success of STARThree, the new STARFour Framework will champion SME participation, promote innovation, and deliver value for money through streamlined procurement routes, including mini-competitions and direct awards, as detailed in the STARFour Framework Agreement.
The STARFour Framework is essential to maintain a fit-for-purpose, flexible, and cost-effective route for specialist transport technical and commercial advice following the expiry of STARThree. As transport challenges evolve across a complex landscape including net zero strategies, decarbonisation, multi-modal integration, and industry restructuring, the STARFour Framework will ensure DfT and the other qualifying bodies have continued access to critical expertise across all transport sectors, not just rail.
The STARFour Framework is intended for use by DfT and other qualifying bodies known as “Clients”. These “Clients” are detailed in the “Contracting authorities that may use the framework” section below. In order to use the STARFour Framework the Clients will enter into an Access Agreement with DfT. The appointed consultants will not be party to these Access Agreements.

title: Supply of HVO fuel to RRS Discovery and RRS James Cook September 2026
description:
Supply of Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO) fuel to two National Oceanography Centre research vessels by way of two bunker deliveries at two ports on consecutive days.
Delivery D-01: RRS Discovery (IMO No. 9588029), Kings Wharf, Cardiff, UK. Estimated quantity (252,000 litres). Required delivery date 15 September 2026.
Delivery D-02: RRS James Cook (IMO No. 9338242), NOC Berth, Southampton, UK. Estimated quantity 430 metric tonnes, approximately 551,000 litres. Required delivery date 16 September 2026.
Aggregate estimated quantity approximately 803,000 litres. All quantities are estimates. The final invoiced quantity for each delivery will be confirmed by the Bunker Delivery Note for that delivery and by the actual density recorded on the Certificate of Analysis at 15 degrees Celsius.
Delivery is by road tank wagon (RTW) to each vessel at its stated berth.
Fuel must comply with EN 15940 and must be derived from used cooking oil (UCO) feedstock only, with no palm oil, palm oil sludge, POME, or animal fats. Sulphur content must comply with MARPOL Annex VI and the applicable MCA requirements, at less than 5 mg/kg (5 ppm). Flash point must be not less than 60 degrees Celsius, in line with SOLAS. CFPP must be minus 15 degrees Celsius or lower. Greenhouse gas emissions intensity of 15.86 gCO2e/MJ with a minimum 83 per cent saving against fossil diesel, and biogenic carbon (C14) testing on all imports.
The supplier must be registered on the Maritime and Coastguard Agency Local Fuel Oil Suppliers Register as compliant with MARPOL Annex VI.
At the time of each bunkering the supplier must provide the fuel specification, representative fuel samples, a Technical Data Sheet with Certificate of Analysis, and a Safety Data Sheet to the Chief Engineer. A Bunker Delivery Note must be provided in the MARPOL Annex VI Appendix V format, stating quantity in metric tonnes, carrying the supplier's signed declaration that the fuel meets the fuel quality requirements of MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18, together with the sulphur content statement and the flash point statement.
The following sustainability documentation is required for each delivery: proof of sustainability of the biofuel component, certified under either ISCC or RFAS 2 Heat-Power-Marine (RSB is not required), a biofuel delivery statement, and the greenhouse gas emissions data for the fuel supplied. Fuel is to be supplied on a non-obligated basis in line with the requirements for marine research use.

title: WSCC Independent Alternative Provision (IAP) Open Framework

To achieve this, we commission Independent Alternative Provision (IAP) to complement mainstream education, provide short-term interventions, and deliver Education Other Than At School (EOTAS) packages where appropriate.
This Framework will operate in addition to the Authority’s commissioned placements at the Ofsted-regulated West Sussex Alternative Provision College (APC), which offers full-time education.
The Framework aims to secure safe, high-quality Alternative Provision that: acts as an intervention, not a destination; supports timely reintegration and/or transition of Learners into long-term education, training, or employment; and meets the individual needs of Learners, particularly Learners with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) with a particular demand on provisions supporting Learners with Social Emotional Mental Health (SEMH) and Autism.
For Clarity the Framework is due to run from September 1st 2026 for an initial period of two years. Bidders can apply from September 1st 2026 until the end of the framework. Please disregard dates of award and submission deadline below.
The Framework has been updated to align with the Non-School Alternative Provision Voluntary National Standards (August 2025), ensuring Suppliers meet nationally recognized benchmarks for quality and safeguarding.
Structure of the Framework
This opportunity does not include separate Lots. Suppliers may apply for one or more Tiers and can request to add additional Tiers at any point during the Framework term.
Tier 1: Provision commissioned by schools for Learners at risk of placement breakdown (e.g., short-term intervention to maintain engagement).
Tier 2: Transitional placements commissioned by the Authority while seeking a permanent education setting.
Tier 3: Provision commissioned by the Authority for Learners with an agreed EOTAS package.
Tier 4: Specialist targeted support commissioned by the Authority for Learners supported by a multi-disciplinary team.

title: Remote Condition Monitoring Platform
description:
Network Rail owns and runs Britain's rail infrastructure and is committed to providing a world-class network for train companies, freight operators and for passengers. 
Network Rail maintains, manages and improves every aspect of the infrastructure.  Successfully planning and delivering maintenance, enhancements and renewals works to the infrastructure is the key to running a safe, reliable and efficient railway, serving customers and communities.
Network Rail is seeking information from the market to support the next evolution of its Remote Condition Monitoring capability, currently known as RADAR. Remote Condition Monitoring is a strategic asset-management capability that enables Network Rail to monitor the health, condition and performance of railway assets remotely, supporting a shift from manual, inspection-led maintenance towards proactive, insight-led intervention. The current RADAR capability has evolved over more than 25 years and is business critical, but the wider estate includes legacy and alternative systems operating in parallel, creating complexity, cost, integration and resilience challenges. The future platform, referred to as RADAR 3, is intended to consolidate and modernise this capability, support national-scale asset condition monitoring, and provide a foundation that can scale into the future Great British Railways operating model.
This procurement will be undertaken as an open market exercise using the Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 (PA23), with the objective of procuring an Examinations system application comprising licences, support, and minor configuration.  
The purpose of this PME is to engage with the supply base and request information relating to platform, software and managed service capabilities available in the market for large-scale, enterprise Remote Condition Monitoring. Specifically, this RFI will look to address the following areas:
•	Identify existing large-scale IoT, industrial data, asset condition monitoring and alarm management platforms available in the market
•	Understand the functional and technical capabilities available for data ingestion, real-time historian services, alarm and alert management, asset configuration, visualisation, event replay, analytics, GIS/EAM integration and open API access
•	Identify indicative commercial models, implementation approaches, operating models, support arrangements and cost drivers for candidate solutions
•	Identify additional capabilities, delivery considerations, migration approaches and innovation opportunities that Network Rail may not yet have considered, including future Great British Railways interoperability requirements
Please note that any content received via response to this RFI will be used purely for information purposes only and will not be deemed as forming part of any proposed bid now, or any potential future tender.

title: CEFAS26-87 ITT for eDNA analysis of samples from Beyond the Reef survey
description:
The Blue Belt Programme is the UK Government’s flagship marine conservation programme, working with a number of the UK Overseas Territories to safeguard more than four million square kilometres of the World’s oceans. Earlier this year, the Blue Belt Programme conducted its first offshore research expedition ‘Beyond the Reef’ to the Caribbean UK Overseas Territories of Anguilla, Cayman Islands and Turks and Caicos Islands.
As a component of the ‘Beyond the Reef’ survey, Cefas undertook water sampling, yielding 417 filters (348 samples, 69 field negatives). Our overall aim is to identify the composition and distribution of teleost fishes and elasmobranchs around Anguilla, and the Turks and Caicos Islands in the Caribbean.
We require a Supplier to process these samples using a metabarcoding workflow and provide us with the raw sequence data. As we are aiming to publish this research, we require a high level of transparency on, and input into, the laboratory procedures used.
Full specification details can be found in the Bidder Pack.
Services required include:
- Extract DNA from the Sterivex (0.22 µm; PES) filters (348 total; triplicated per sampling station/depth; 4 L filtered total) and field negatives (69; one per station) provided by Cefas.
- PCR amplify a ~170 bp fragment of the 12S rRNA region, with two primer sets: one targeting teleost fishes (MiFish-U) and another targeting elasmobranchs (MiFish-E).
- Pooled PCR products will then be indexed.
- Sequence the library(s) on a suitable High Throughput Sequencing Platform, e.g. NextSeq 1000 P1 XLEAP-SBS, to an appropriate level of sequence depth.
- Provide Cefas with demultiplexed paired-end read sequence data.
buyer: CENTRE FOR ENVIRONMENT, FISHERIES AND AQUACULTURE SCIENCE

title: LUV01377- Website and Content Management System
description:
The University of Leicester is embarking on a strategic initiative to modernise its digital infrastructure through the implementation of a cloud-managed, headless content management system (CMS). This project is a cornerstone of the University’s broader digital engagement strategy, designed to enhance the efficiency, flexibility, and sustainability of its online presence across le.ac.uk and associated digital platforms.
The new CMS must deliver a secure, scalable solution that supports modern web architecture and multi-channel content delivery. It should integrate seamlessly with existing systems, enable content publishing across diverse devices and platforms, and accommodate future development needs.
Operationally, the University aims to transform how content is created, managed, and maintained. With over 200 trained editors currently using the existing system, the new platform should streamline workflows, reduce reliance on technical support, and empower staff to manage content more effectively. It must support decentralised content creation while ensuring robust governance and quality control. A key objective is to consolidate the University’s digital infrastructure and establish a single source of truth for content and data, thereby reducing maintenance costs and reliance on external development.
The project will be delivered in phased stages, including technical discovery, procurement, system implementation, content review and migration, staff training, and decommissioning of the current infrastructure. Completion is anticipated by the end of the 2026/27 financial year. Suppliers should demonstrate experience in delivering similar projects, including dual running of legacy and new CMS platforms, and the ability to collaborate closely with internal teams throughout the transition.
The University is committed to ensuring the new CMS supports its wider institutional goals; enhancing the digital experience for users, supporting staff in their roles, and maintaining a secure and efficient digital environment. The selected supplier will be expected to meet the technical and operational requirements outlined in this tender and to work in partnership with the University to deliver a successful implementation.
The University of Leicester is conducting a Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023. This procedure will be run in stages, allowing us to identify the most suitable suppliers and ensure a fair and transparent process.
All submissions must be made via the Delta Procurement Portal. We will not accept responses via email or any other mechanism. To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/8KST953R74

title: 28833 Community Cohesion Strategy
description:
Plymouth City Council, alongside City Leadership Group partners, seeks to procure specialist support to develop a city-wide Community Cohesion Strategy and accompanying delivery framework for Plymouth. The requirement covers a four-stage programme comprising: inception and assessment; stakeholder and community engagement; strategy co-production and launch; and implementation, monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL).

title: MD26098 - Plan Mid Devon Green Infrastructure Strategy
description: 1. Aims and objectives of the tender exercise To appoint a suitably qualified consultant through a fair, transparent and proportionate competitive process to prepare the Plan Mid Devon Green Infrastructure Strategy. The commission will provide a robust and proportionate Local Plan evidence base that establishes the existing green infrastructure baseline; assesses the likely individual and cumulative impacts of planned growth; identifies mitigation, enhancement and investment priorities; and translates the findings into practical policy, site-allocation, infrastructure-delivery and development-management recommendations. The procurement also seeks value for money, timely delivery, transparent methodology and assumptions, high-quality editable GIS/data outputs, knowledge transfer to Council officers, and outputs that remain usable following Local Government Reorganisation. 2. Description of the requirement and background to the procurement Mid Devon District Council is preparing Plan Mid Devon, a new Local Plan for the proposed period 2026-2046. The emerging evidence identifies a local housing need of approximately 570 dwellings per annum, existing commitments of approximately 6,646 dwellings and a need for around 6,000 additional allocations, subject to the continuing evolution of the evidence base. The scale and distribution of growth requires up-to-date evidence showing how green and blue infrastructure, ecological networks, biodiversity, access to nature, active travel, landscape, water and flood-risk functions can be protected, connected, enhanced and delivered. The Council therefore requires a comprehensive Green Infrastructure Strategy to support spatial strategy decisions, site assessment and allocations, Sustainability Appraisal/Habitats Regulations Assessment where relevant, the Infrastructure Delivery Plan and future development-management decisions. The work must align with the Devon Local Nature Recovery Strategy and relevant national and local policy and evidence. It must also be structured so that parish-, settlement- and district-level findings and datasets can be used by the proposed Exeter and Devon successor authorities following Local Government Reorganisation, currently expected to take effect from 1 April 2028. 3. What is being purchased and why The Council is purchasing specialist professional planning, green-infrastructure, environmental and GIS consultancy services. The principal outputs are an inception note and method statement; data audit and gap analysis; baseline assessment and mapping; growth scenario and site assessment; draft and final Green Infrastructure Strategy; delivery plan/IDP schedule; policy and site-allocation recommendations; executive summary; editable GIS and mapping package with metadata; and briefing material if required. The work is being purchased externally because it requires specialist multidisciplinary expertise and sufficient capacity in green infrastructure planning, ecology/nature recovery, GIS and spatial analysis, climate resilience, infrastructure delivery, planning policy and proportionate stakeholder engagement. External procurement also provides independent, auditable evidence suitable for Local Plan purposes. 4. Procurement route, value and timetable The RFQ proposes a single-stage competitive procedure under the regulated below-threshold provisions of the Procurement Act 2023. Award will be based on 70% quality and 30% price, with published pass/fail participation requirements and quality criteria. The specification states a maximum budget of £35,000 including VAT. An earlier general RFQ paragraph refers to an anticipated budget in the region of £30,000 including VAT; Procurement should reconcile these figures before publication so that the tender contains one unambiguous budget statement. The intended contract period is November 2026 to June 2027, with internal approvals scheduled for the week commencing 26 October 2026 and intended contract award on 13 November 2026. 5. Decision-making and approvals The RFQ states that contract award is subject to the Council's formal approval process and that no contract will be entered into until all necessary approvals are obtained. The procurement value is well below £1 million, so Corporate SLT and Cabinet approval is not indicated by the RFQ. Procurement and the budget holder should confirm the applicable delegated decision and financial approval route, the authorised officer, and whether any formal decision record is required before the tender is issued and before award. 6. Risk assessment and mitigations A project-specific Risk and Opportunity Register has been completed. The main risks concern supplier capacity and competition; scope clarity; budget pressure; programme slippage; data gaps and licensing; stakeholder/Council availability; Local Government Reorganisation; confidentiality and data protection; quality assurance and audit trail; conflicts of interest and fair treatment; and environmental impacts from delivery. Mitigations include the detailed specification and deliverables; transparent evaluation criteria; portal-based clarifications; conflict declarations; an early inception meeting and data audit; agreed milestones and interim outputs; regular progress/risk reporting; transparent assumptions and audit trail; Council review and supplier QA; secure data handling; transferable GIS/data formats; and LGR-ready reporting at parish, settlement and district level. 7. Impact assessment The procurement is for a professional evidence-base service and is not expected to create material direct adverse equality impacts. The Strategy is intended to support positive outcomes including access to nature, health and wellbeing, active travel, climate resilience, biodiversity and more sustainable growth. Potential impacts include unequal participation in engagement, inaccessible outputs, privacy risks associated with stakeholder contact details/comments, and the possibility that GI recommendations could create tensions between recreation, access, biodiversity, heritage and landscape objectives. These will be mitigated through Council-led proportionate engagement, accessible materials, data minimisation and privacy screening, transparent assessment of trade-offs, and site-specific mitigation and stewardship recommendations. Procurement should confirm whether a separate Equality Impact Assessment or Data Protection Impact Assessment/privacy screening is required under Council procedures before engagement commences. 8. Sustainability Impact Matrix and Social Value Act considerations A Sustainability Impact Matrix has been completed. The procurement supports environmental objectives by commissioning evidence and recommendations for nature recovery, biodiversity net gain, green and blue infrastructure networks, climate resilience, natural flood management, access to nature and sustainable growth. Direct contract-delivery impacts are expected to be limited but will be reduced through remote meetings where appropriate, efficient combined site visits, digital-first outputs, controlled data storage and reuse of existing evidence. Social value is proportionate to the contract value and subject matter. Relevant opportunities include knowledge transfer to Council officers; accessible evidence and mapping; support for healthier and more inclusive places; engagement with town/parish councils and relevant community/environmental groups; openness to capable SMEs and specialist consultancies; reusable datasets and methods; and identification of deliverable GI projects and funding mechanisms. These benefits should be secured through the core specification and contract management rather than disproportionate standalone requirements. 9. Procurement Key Themes Checklist The completed checklist records how the procurement addresses climate and ecological objectives, local economy and SME access, social value, digital delivery, contract management, value for money, commercial options, risk management, partnership working, workforce skills, transparency, data protection, legal compliance, modern slavery and Local Government Reorganisation. Items still requiring confirmation are the procurement reference, delegated approval route, authorised officer/contract manager, evaluation-panel equality training status, whether Information Governance input is required, and any final Procurement or Legal compliance review. 11. Recommended approach and outstanding confirmations Proceed with the single-stage competitive RFQ, subject to Procurement confirming the delegated approval route and procurement reference; reconciling the £30,000 and £35,000 budget statements in the RFQ; confirming the authorised officer, contract manager and evaluation panel; completing individual conflict declarations; confirming any equality/privacy/Information Governance requirements; and completing the final procurement and legal compliance check before issue.

title: RBWM Events Management Procurement - Market Engagement Webinar
description:
The Authority would like to underline that this is the second preliminary market engagement notice for this requirement. We have previously invited suppliers to respond to our survey (for which we received a very healthy number of responses) but now the Authority would like to build on this engagement by way of a webinar. This will also be an opportunity would you to ask questions. Se the participation section for registration information. 
See below the summary from the previous notice: 
The Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead (RBWM) is seeking to engage with experienced event management suppliers in advance of a future procurement for the delivery of a diverse programme of high-profile ceremonial, civic and nationally significant events over an anticipated eight-year period.
The appointed supplier will be required to provide and maintain a strategic event management, operational planning and delivery support for a range of events and provide including, but not limited to:
•	Royal Visits
•	State Visits
•	Royal Weddings
•	Royal Funerals
•	National and Civic Ceremonies
•	Large-scale public celebrations and commemorations
These events are likely to attract significant national and international attention, substantial media interest, and large public audiences, regularly involving complex security, operational and stakeholder requirements.
Supplier Requirements
RBWM is seeking suppliers that can demonstrate a proven and successful track record in the planning (maintenance of plans), and delivery of major public events within Windsor town centre or similarly complex and sensitive environments.
Suppliers should be able to evidence experience in:
•	Delivering events in busy operational town centres while maintaining business-as-usual activities and minimising disruption to residents, businesses and visitors.
•	Working in partnership with multiple agencies and stakeholders, including but not limited to: 
o	Security services
o	Police forces
o	Emergency services
o	The Royal Household
o	The Crown Estate
o	Central government departments
o	Transport operators
o	National and international media organisations
•	Managing complex stakeholder engagement and governance arrangements.
•	Planning and delivering large-scale infrastructure installations, including temporary event structures, security installations, media compounds, public viewing areas and crowd management systems.
•	Developing and implementing comprehensive event management plans, operational orders, communication strategies, contingency plans and emergency response procedures.
•	Managing extensive media operations, accreditation processes and communications activity associated with internationally significant events.
Capacity and Capability
The successful supplier must demonstrate the organisational capacity, resources and resilience to manage events of exceptional scale and complexity, including events that may attract in excess of 100,000 attendees.
Suppliers should be capable of:
•	Coordinating multi-agency operational planning and delivery.
•	Managing significant crowd safety and public protection arrangements.
•	Recruiting, deploying and managing a stewarding workforce of over 800 personnel, including associated welfare, briefing, training and supervisory requirements.
•	Providing experienced event management personnel across all phases of event delivery, from feasibility and planning through to live operations and post-event review.
•	Maintaining robust business continuity arrangements and the ability to respond to events that may arise at short notice.
Market Engagement
This notice is intended to inform the market of RBWM's future requirements and to identify suppliers with the specialist expertise, experience and capacity necessary to deliver events of national significance within the unique operating environment of Windsor.
The Authority is particularly interested in engaging with organisations that can demonstrate excellence in event delivery, stakeholder management, crowd safety, security integration, operational resilience and the successful management of high-profile events operating under intense public, media and stakeholder scrutiny.
The resulting contract cannot guarantee a level of regular events as some of the events outlined above are unplanned or "no notice" events. So, it will be expected the successful provider may for the most part be monitoring and maintaining plans for events listed above until they are activated.

title: Targeted Catchment Investigation and CCTV & Cleaning
description:
Lot 1 - Targeted Catchment Investigations (TCI) This lot covers the delivery of Targeted Catchment Investigations (TCIs) across Thames Water's wastewater network to identify and reduce the risk of sewer blockages, pollution incidents, sewer flooding and customer service disruption.
Suppliers will be required to undertake investigations within defined catchment areas identified by Thames Water. Activities may include sewer and manhole inspections, sewer cleaning, CCTV surveys, identification of root causes of network issues, delivery of first time-fix activities where appropriate, and the development of recommendations for follow-on works.
Suppliers will be responsible for providing all labour, vehicles, equipment and associated resources necessary to deliver the services, together with the collection and submission of inspection data, CCTV records, photographs and other required outputs.
The framework will operate across the Thames Water region. Work packages will be issued by Thames Water throughout the term of the framework and may vary in size, volume and location.
Successful suppliers will be required to work collaboratively with Thames Water to support operational performance, environmental protection and customer outcomes.
Lot 2 - CCTV & Cleaning This lot covers the provision of planned CCTV inspection and sewer cleaning services across Thames Water's wastewater network, including specialist cleaning activities and associated support services such as flow management, waste disposal, and related operational works.
Suppliers will be required to undertake sewer cleaning and CCTV investigations to identify, record, and report on blockages, silt build-up, structural defects, root ingress, and other operational issues within the network. Services may include CCTV enabling activities, defect identification and coding, emergency response works, pollution escalations, and customer and stakeholder engagement where required.
Suppliers will provide all labour, vehicles, plant, equipment, permits, licences, traffic management, and associated resources required to deliver the services in accordance with relevant industry standards and Thames Water procedures. Services may be delivered across public highways, private land, and other locations throughout the Thames Water region, and may include both planned and reactive activities. title: UK6 - Tender Notice Prevention of Peripheral Cold Injuries
description:
Description
The UK Armed Forces are more frequently operating in cold environments to contribute to NATO’s deterrence in the High North and on the Eastern flank; but data suggest that the number of cases of peripheral cold injuries is increasing in deployed Service Personnel (SP), even during short deployments. Given our growing presence in the Nordic-Baltic regions, Defence urgently needs to identify and protect SP susceptible to cold injuries and improve the clinical assessment of injured SP for their safe and timely return to cold environments. This work will aim to reduce the risk of peripheral cold injuries by developing a prediction tool to identify susceptible SP; and improve deployability by developing a clinical assessment tool to enable clinicians to assess injured SP safely and efficiently, year-round. This laboratory-based research will largely take place at the climate chamber in North Yorkshire.

title: Community Navigation following Suicide-related A&E Attendance in North Central London
description:
The NCL Suicide Prevention Programme is a partnership between the London Boroughs of Barnet, Camden, Enfield, Haringey and Islington, North London NHS Foundation Trust and West and North London Integrated Care Board. The programme has an overall aim to ‘Reduce the suicide rate across the NCL geography through population-based suicide prevention measures as well as programmes targeted to those at highest risk, through improved support to those who have self-harmed and improved support for people bereaved by suicide.’
Individuals who present to emergency departments for suicide-related behaviours have a high rate of repeat self-harm and death by suicide. Early engagement and therapeutic intervention soon after emergency department attendance is thought to be beneficial in reducing suicide-related behaviours.
London Borough of Barnet, on behalf of NCL Suicide Prevention Programme are seeking to commission service(s) to provide community navigation support for people who have presented to A&E with suicide-related behaviours.
Service Aims and Priorities 
•To provide community navigation support for people who have presented to A&E with suicide-related behaviours after they have been discharged to the community. 
•Suicide-related behaviours within this specification are defined as self-harm (with or without suicidal intent), attempted suicide, or a presentation of suicidal thoughts with no harm/injury. 
•Community navigation is defined as a professional working with a person to identify community services or suitable alternatives that can support them with a variety of concerns relating to suicidal behaviours.  Support could include mental health provision as well as offers addressing socioeconomic concerns for an individual. 
•This is an opportunity for services offering community navigation support to develop their existing offer by building stronger connections with NHS crisis pathways and their readiness to support people with suicidal thoughts.

title: Electrification Works at Bradford Depot
description: As part of the introduction of the Weaver Network in West Yorkshire, the Combined Authority intends that electric buses will operate from the Bradford Depot for the purposes of providing local services under the West Yorkshire bus franchising scheme. The Combined Authority is currently negotiating purchase of depots, but the Operator is likely to have exclusive access to the depot prior to franchised services commencing and the Combined Authority requires that the Operator procure the electrification works at the Depot to be in place prior to that. As a result, the Combined Authority intends to fund the electrification of the depot from the Joint Air Quality Unit and West Yorkshire Transport Fund. Whilst the Combined Authority has agreed to grant fund this electrification, it acknowledges that, as the works will ultimately benefit the Combined Authority the funding agreement could be viewed as a Works contract, and therefore the Combined Authority has chosen to comply with the Procurement Act 2023 in procuring the funding and delivery of these Works. The works consist of Electrification works. Direct award justification Single supplier - intellectual property or exclusive rights At the point of award and commencement of works, First will have exclusive rights in respect of access to the depot, either as owner of the depot, or, where First has sold the depot to the Combined Authority, through its rights of quiet enjoyment to deliver its bus services prior to the introduction of franchising. As a result, the Combined Authority is unable to procure the Works at the depot from any other party, due to First's exclusive rights of occupation. Whilst the Combined Authority has considered whether the Works can be delivered at other locations this will not achieve the overall franchising strategy of the Combined Authority which requires certain strategic depots to be electrified. Delaying the works until the Combined Authority has greater control over the depot would mean that electrification was not delivered by the time franchised services commenced and would therefore fail to deliver the Combined Authority's policy objectives for the procurement. As a result, the Combined Authority therefore intend to direct award in accordance with paragraph 6 of Schedule 5 Procurement Act 2023 on the basis that First's exclusive rights mean that they are the only party that can deliver the Works, and there are not viable alternatives to deliver of the Works at this site.
