title: UK1 - Pipeline Notice -715933488 IBES
description:
There is an enduring requirement for contracted labour and personnel support across aviation engineering, logistics information systems, airworthiness records, supply and enabling functions at RAF Odiham, RAF Benson and RNAS Yeovilton. The Authority are seeking a Contractor who shall provide suitably qualified and experienced personnel (SQEP) to supplement Service personnel and deliver the defined outputs where military capacity is constrained. This is an output-based personnel support requirement; it does not prescribe fixed posts or transfer the Authority’s responsibility for directing and assuring Defence outputs.
The requirement is informed by persistent Service workforce pressure across engineering, logistics and enabling functions. Workforce gap data may be used by the Authority to inform planning and prioritisation; however, such data is contextual only and shall not be interpreted as a fixed staffing requirement, guaranteed workload or commitment to any specific workforce construct.
The requirement supports the Authority’s need to generate, sustain and recover SUPPORT HELICOPTER FORCE  (SHF) and COMMANDO HELICOPTER FORCE  (CHF) capability in support of Defence-directed tasks, readiness commitments, force generation activity, contingency response and wider operational outputs. Delivery shall contribute to aircraft availability, maintenance throughput, logistics resilience, airworthiness assurance and safe operating outputs across the SHF and CHF enterprises.
The Contractor shall deliver support that enables the Authority to prioritise scarce engineering, logistics, supply and enabling resources against variable operational demand. Support shall remain responsive to flying programme requirements, maintenance activity, emergent tasking, readiness cycles, future capability transition and changes in workload across output groups, functions, locations and time.
The Authority does not guarantee a fixed volume of tasking. Activity assumptions, historic data and annexed output schedules are indicative and shall not be interpreted as guaranteed workload, fixed workforce demand or a prescriptive staffing schedule.

Sussex & Brighton Strategic Authority (SBSA) has been pre-selected by Department for Transport (DfT) to apply for the Integrated Transport Digital Twin (ITDT) opportunity. 
SBSA was pre-selected for this opportunity through a national assessment process by DfT that identified authorities with the potential to generate transferable learning for the transport sector. DfT recognised SBSA’s strategic transport leadership role and its anticipated contribution to developing an integrated and connected transport network across the area.
SBSA and the East Sussex Procurement Hub (ESPH) are undertaking proportionate pre-procurement preliminary market engagement to test the deliverability, affordability and sustainability of the proposed Integrated Transport Digital Twin bid for Sussex & Brighton. 
This engagement will include discussions with potential suppliers and delivery partners, supported by procurement colleagues, to understand market capability, implementation approaches, ongoing operational requirements and key delivery risks. 
Feedback from the market will assist in informing the final delivery plan, risk management approach and sustainability arrangements; providing assurance to both SBSA and DfT that the proposed solution can be delivered using currently available technologies and services. This approach aligns with DfT guidance for applicants to the fund, which encourages applicants to engage with potential contractors and delivery partners to demonstrate market readiness.
Full details of this exercise can be found in the Preliminary Market Engagement document.

title: Future Cash Systems - Cash Processing & CViT Transport (Track & Trace)
description:
O V E R V I E W 
Post Office Limited (POL) is preparing for the replacement and improvement of its Cash Processing & CViT Transport (Track & Trace) System. This is the system that manages and facilitates the logistics of physical cash across its 11,500+ branches and other customers across the UK.
S E R V I C E   S U M M A R Y
A highly specialised, business-critical cash management system used in POL's cash centres and Cash & Valuables in Transit (CViT) depots (as opposed to POL branches) supporting the movement, processing, reconciliation, control and reporting of cash and valuables across POL's national supply chain.
Functions of the system may also include demand planning and cash forecasting, customer order management and fulfilment, end-to-end consignment and chain-of-custody tracking, route planning and optimisation, real-time operational visibility, exception and investigation management, multi-currency cash processing, inventory forecasting and optimisation, digital proof of collection and delivery, advanced reporting and self-service analytics, audit and regulatory compliance, master data management, and operational performance monitoring either delivered directly, or through integrations to POL strategic systems. 
The solution is expected to support configurable workflows, automation, predictive analytics, and the efficient management of cash, valuables, assets and transport operations across the end-to-end supply chain.
The solution must support POL's independent network of customers, including POL Branches and banking hubs.
The future supplier(s) is expected to implement and provide a replacement and enhanced application together with associated application management services, including maintenance, support, development, security management, service transition, operational readiness, testing, knowledge transfer and ongoing service improvement. The application(s) must integrate with internal and external systems, such as POL's national-wide Electronic Point of Sale (EPOS) system, finance system, high-speed note counting machine, data warehouse, and foreign currency exchange. 
S C O P E 
The current minimum scope under consideration is:
 1. Applications (software(s) for both the Cash Centre processing and CViT Track & Trace); and
 2. Applications Management (maintenance, support and development).
POL is also considering, as informed by this preliminary market engagement (PME) exercise, whether the additional services below should be added to the scope:
 3. Hosting
 4. Service Management (integrator, incident mgmt., reporting)

description:
Ofwat is procuring an Independent Monitor (IM) to provide independent monitoring, analysis and reporting in relation to Thames Water's turnaround programme, financial resilience and compliance with undertakings accepted by Ofwat following a breach of licence condition P26.

The role is expected to operate in a dynamic and evolving environment. The nature, scope and intensity of the IM's activities may increase or decrease during the contract term to reflect Thames Water's progress, risk profile, recapitalisation activities, regulatory developments and wider turnaround programme. The contract has therefore been designed to support a scalable and proportionate monitoring approach.
The IM will be appointed by Ofwat, will act independently of Thames Water, and will provide recommendations and advice to Ofwat only.

description:

The service will be available to adults (aged 18 and over) receiving structured treatment for drugs and/or alcohol within Leicestershire and Rutland’s Integrated Substance Use Treatment Service.  Eligible individuals will be those who are out of work or at risk from losing their employment and are entitled to work in the United Kingdom.
The aim is to deliver a fully utilised IPS provision across Leicestershire & Rutland, which adheres to the IPS approach and meets the needs of individuals in treatment, including consideration of their treatment and recovery journey, their individual preferences for work and the personalised support they might need. The Provider will also need to have consideration of the rurality of the area and the barriers to accessing support and employment that may create.
The purpose is to support those individuals to find and sustain meaningful paid work. IPS should also be person centred, offer pre-employment support and guidance, as well as in-work support to ensure long-term job retention. The IPS model also follows eight principles, and a 25-item fidelity scale which the Provider will be expected to meet.
	Aim to get people into paid, competitive employment
	Is open to all those who want to work
	Find jobs consistent with people’s preferences
	Works at pace
	Teams are embedded in and integrated with the treatment services
	Employer engagement
	Provide ongoing, individualised support for the person and their employer
	Benefits advice is included
The contract value for the initial 2 years is £463,190 (year 1 allocation is £228,215 and year 2 allocation is £234,975.  If future funding is agreed by central government, the Councils anticipate the total contract value (for 4 years) to be approximately up to £975,000.

title: "Airlock" Output Checking System OCS Decision Engine Development Partner
description:
UKB is seeking to further improve its technical controls and intends to implement a functional mechanism to check data egress requests
to ensure that participant record-level data is not being removed and does not contain information that can identify individual
participants. This Output Checking System (OCS) functionality will allow UKB to enhance the security of the UKB-RAP, reduce the
risk of advertent and inadvertent data breaches and importantly increase the trust and transparency of the UKB resource. UKB intends
to commence a procurement exercise to procure a replacement for the current UKB-RAP in 2027, which will come into effect in 2028.
The OCS will need to be integrated with the new UKB-RAP.
To develop and deliver the OCS, UKB is separating the procurement into two elements which will need to be fully interoperable:
1. OCS User Interface (UI) and Workflow (subject to a separate tender exercise completed via the CCS G-Cloud 14 framework): The
development of a seamless UI and Workflow for the OCS, including secure movement of data and integration with existing UKB
infrastructure.
2. The OCS Decision Engine (this procurement): The development of the core algorithms to allow an automated assessment of the data
being egressed, giving an overall confidence assessment score and a Red/Amber/Green (RAG) rating for decision making
The OCS Decision Engine is made up of two components:
1. Data Trust Engine: reviews the egressed file(s) from UKB-RAP to detect the presence of sensitive information. Through the
application of transparent, heuristic rules and configurable thresholds, the Data Trust Engine will create a score for how 'disclosive' the
egressed data is that, when coupled with the researcher confidence score below, provides a Red (fail), Amber (unclear) or Green (pass)
egress rating.
2. Researcher Behaviour Engine: derives the overall credibility of a given researcher within AMS and UKB-RAP, and assigns a
confidence score, which will dictate how human-review decisions are made for 'Amber' outcomes from the Trust Engine.
This procurement relates to a development partner to design and deliver the OCS Decision Engine, which will include the Data Trust
Engine and Researcher Behaviour Engine.

title: ANDBC Pre-Qualification Questionnaire - Provision of Integrated Consultancy Services for Urban Waterfront and Public Realm under Bangor Waterfront Redevelopment
description: Ards and North Down Borough Council seeks to appoint an Integrated Consultancy Team (ICT) to design, manage and deliver a transformational solution for the redevelopment of Bangor’s Urban Waterfront and Public Realm, from RIBA Stage 0 through to RIBA Stage 7. This project is one of five constituent projects included in the Bangor Waterfront Redevelopment programme, to help re-establish Bangor as a thriving City and prime visitor attraction in Northern Ireland. The Bangor Waterfront Redevelopment project is a tourism led regeneration scheme which has secured funding through the Belfast Region City Deal to turn Bangor into a ‘destination of choice’, as a place to live, work, visit, study and invest, through a series of interconnected developments and experiences along Bangor Waterfront. The services required under this contract are for the design and delivery of the Urban Waterfront and Public Realm Redevelopment project (Constituent Project 1 in the wider redevelopment programme). The Urban Waterfront and Public Realm Redevelopment project aims to transform a 2 mile stretch of waterfront in Bangor, to uplift, connect, and rejuvenate the entire waterfront route and provide a strong foundation for the seamless integration of the other four, interdependent constituent projects under the Bangor Waterfront Redevelopment Programme. The project site extends across five diverse Character Areas, each requiring its own site-specific, sensitive, and sustainable design response, to address existing deficiencies and unify the waterfront route through interconnected spaces, buildings, facilities, place making initiatives and public realm improvements. The site proposed for redevelopment, is located in Bangor, a large seaside City situated on the southern side of Belfast Lough and within the Belfast Metropolitan area. Bangor is the third largest urban development in Northern Ireland, with a catchment population of circa 170,000 persons within a 20-minute drive time and circa 475,000 persons within a 30-minute drive time. In May 2022, the town was awarded City status as part of the Queen’s Platinum Jubilee Celebrations. The redevelopment site extends across a 2 mile stretch of coastline in Bangor, County Down, between Skippingstone Beach to the west (near Pickie Fun Park) and Banks Lane, Ballyholme, to the east. The site is comprised of five key ‘Character Areas’ which are diverse in character, identity, topography, environment, activities, role and function. The identified Character Areas are Skippingstone (north of Pickie Fun Park), Bangor Marina and Harbour, Seacliff Road (including the Long Hole), Kingsland and Ballyholme Promenade and adjoining areas. The Character Areas described above collectively make up the site area proposed for the UWPR redevelopment.

title: Energetik Primary Heating Network Extensions Part 2 (PSDS)
description:
Energetik intends to award a contract to Proven Project (District Heating) Ltd for the design and construction of two separate extensions to the Meridian Water Heat Network (MWHN), comprising the Northern Extension and the Western Extension. 
The western extension is from Church Street near Edmonton Green to Winchmore School and Edmonton County (Bury Campus) School.  The northern extension is from Ponders End High Street near Ponders End Park to Capital College and Waverley School. 
The pre-construction work for the contract is due to commence upon contract award on or before 22nd September 2026. As well normal pre-construction work required under the contract, further GPR work, design and trial holes will be permitted as part of preconstruction. Construction work is expected to commence on or before 5th January 2027 following a successful planning application by the Employer, and subject to the Contractor agreeing S50 licences with Enfield Highways. 
As the project is grant funded and the grant will be lost if the contract spend does not achieve certain minimum thresholds each financial year, the contract has a sectional completion date of 31st March 2027 and Practical Completion by 31st March 2028.
Note that liquidated damages are £20,000 per day if these dates are not achieved.
Key to the success of the project is the liaison with Enfield Highways team and to develop a route design and traffic management proposals that permit the granting of Section 50 licences for the works. Note that Section 50 licence fees, deposits and bonds will be paid by the Employer to Enfield Highways.  Full road closures are highly unlikely to be permitted, and multiple gangs will only be permitted where it does not cause undue traffic chaos to commuter sand businesses on Enfield’s roads.
The contract includes extending the existing Logstor leak detection system, cleaning the pipe installed, hydraulically testing the pipe installed using treated water to the same standard as the existing MWHN and commissioning of the extensions to provide “heat on” to the extended network.     
The duration of the Contract is expected to be approximately 18 months and in accordance with the contract terms, JCT Major Construction Contract 2024 edition, the completion date shall be as stated in the Contract Particulars or fixed from time to time in accordance with clause 18 (Extension of Time).
Total Contract value - £12,162,500.76 (exc. VAT). 
This contract award is being made following the completion of the one stage procurement process via an open procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 and advertised on 19th March 2026 under Tender notice – Procurement Act 2023 – Notice identifier 20260722-000001.
In accordance with Section 51 of the Procurement Act 2023, a mandatory standstill period of eight (8) working days will commence on the day this Contract Award Notice is published.
Communication about this contract shall be via the Contracting Authority’s Procurement Portal, 'Atamis' https://londonboroughofenfield.my.site.com

title: Gambling Needs Assessment
description:
Sandwell Council is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced organisation to undertake a comprehensive Gambling Harms Needs Assessment and support the development of a local Gambling Harms Strategy. The successful supplier will work with key stakeholders to assess local need, identify priority populations and areas for intervention, and provide evidence-based recommendations to inform future commissioning, prevention and partnership activity.
Objectives:
•	Undertake a population-level needs assessment covering all age groups
•	Understanding of gambling behaviours across different communities in Sandwell 
•	A clear picture of the local gambling landscape 
•	Assess harms across online and in-person gambling
•	Identify and understand the impact on affected others (families, carers, communities)
•	Deliver an in-depth qualitative research component
•	Map current services, pathways and gaps
•	Identify priority populations and inequalities. 
•	Explore the relationship between ethnicity, racism and gambling-related harms in Sandwell, including any differential experiences, barriers to support and evidence relating to structural inequalities
•	Develop an evidence-based local Gambling Harms Strategy aligned to national guidance, including the OHID menu of interventions, and local system priorities
•	Produce a delivery plan with prioritised, actionable recommendations

title: LUV01495 Procurement of Quad Systems C4 NMR Spectrometer and associated peripherals
description:
The University of Leicester, Department of Molecular and Cell Biology, is expanding its capabilities to study the dynamics and structure of molecules using NMR spectroscopy. To support this, funding has been secured from the BBSRC to procure a highly specialised instrument: the Quad Systems C4 NMR spectrometer and associated peripherals. This instrument integrates cutting-edge technology into a single coherent system.
The Quad Systems C4 NMR spectrometer will be installed at the University to support its research activities, particularly in areas involving nucleic acid-protein, protein-protein, and small-molecule-protein interactions. It includes a range of probeheads optimised for maximum sensitivity in biologically relevant solvent systems and integrated LED systems with a range of wavelengths (280, 390, 460, 490, 530 and 600nm) for photo-CIDNP applications. This comprises a fully integrated system which is required to maintain the scientific edge of our ongoing biophysical and molecular research.

title: Provision of a Digital Delivery Partner for Development of an Integrated Digital Platform
description:
The Integrated Digital Platform Project is a core component of SEPA's Transformation Programme, shifting the organisation from designing change to delivering it in practice. It responds directly to our Annual Operating Plan 2026/27, which emphasises improved service delivery, better use of data, and greater efficiency in the context of increasing environmental and financial pressures.  
At present, SEPA operates through a fragmented landscape of systems and manual processes. Information is often held across multiple platforms, requiring re-entry and interpretation, which increases effort, reduces consistency, and limits the organisation's ability to respond effectively to growing demand.  
The Integrated Digital Platform Project will address these issues by creating an integrated digital platform spanning customer, regulatory and data services. This will enable workflows and data to move effectively across the organisation, reduce manual handling, and support more consistent and timely service delivery.
SEPA will be using Government Commercial Agency Digital Outcomes and Specialists 7 (DOS7), Lot 2 - Digital Capability and Delivery Partners, using a single-stage competition.

title: Independent Monitor - South East Water
description:
Ofwat is procuring an Independent Monitor (IM) to monitor, assess and report South East Water's progress in delivering a turnaround in their operational performance and resilience.
The scope of the Monitor's role is intended to be consistent with undertakings accepted by Ofwat in its enforcement decisions concerning water supply resilience and customer care during supply interruption incidents, and compliance with a licence condition requiring the company to hold two Issuer Credit Ratings that are Investment Grade Ratings.
The IM will support Ofwat's monitoring of the company's delivery of remediation actions required under the undertakings, including the development and implementation of a Performance Improvement Plan.
The IM will provide independent assessment of progress, governance, risk management and delivery confidence, identify material risks to compliance and delivery, and report findings to Ofwat. The IM will support proportionate, risk-based regulatory oversight, while maintaining clear accountability with the company for delivery of the required improvements.
The scope is expected to evolve during the contract term in response to the company's performance, risk profile and progress against the undertakings. The monitoring approach must therefore be scalable, risk-based and proportionate.
The IM will be appointed by Ofwat, act independently of the company and provide advice and recommendations to Ofwat only.
The costs of the independent monitor will be met by the Company, and will not impact on customer bills.

title: Preliminary Market Engagement: Supply of Printed Materials, Educational Resources and Promotional Products
description:
Trinity Multi Academy Trust (Trinity) is a growing multi-academy trust serving communities across Yorkshire. The Trust operates a diverse portfolio of primary, secondary, and post-16  academies and is committed to delivering high-quality education, operational excellence, and value for money.
As part of its ongoing commitment to securing high-quality goods and services, Trinity is undertaking a preliminary market engagement exercise to inform the development of a potential multi-supplier framework agreement for printed materials, educational resources and promotional products.
The proposed framework may include, but is not limited to:
•	School planners and diaries
•	Exercise books and workbooks
•	Notebooks
•	Lanyards and identification accessories
•	Brochures and prospectuses
•	Leaflets and flyers
•	Promotional literature
•	Corporate stationery
•	Branded merchandise
•	Marketing and event materials
•	Other associated printed and promotional products
Trinity is considering a multi-lot framework structure, with multiple suppliers appointed across one or more lots to meet the diverse requirements of its academies and central services. 
The final lot structure has not yet been determined and will be informed through this market engagement exercise.
The purpose of the engagement is to:
•	Understand the current supplier market and supplier capabilities.
•	Gather feedback on the proposed framework and potential lot structure.
•	Explore innovative products, services, and delivery models.
•	Inform the procurement strategy and framework design.
•	Assist in defining the specification and requirements.
•	Understand sustainability initiatives and added-value offerings available within the market.
This preliminary market engagement exercise is being conducted solely for information-gathering purposes.
This notice is not a commitment to purchase, a call for competition, or an invitation to tender. Participation in this engagement exercise will not guarantee any future business opportunity. Information provided by suppliers will be used only to inform the Trust's procurement strategy, framework design, specification, and requirements.
Should Trinity decide to proceed with a formal procurement process, the opportunity will be advertised through the appropriate public procurement channels to ensure all interested suppliers are notified and have the opportunity to participate.

title: North East London Community Dermatology Service
description:
Market Engagement Event
The proposed North East London (NEL) Community Dermatology Service will provide a consultant-managed service, aligned with British Association of Dermatologists (BAD) guidance, delivering specialist assessment, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up care for patients with skin, hair and nail conditions within community settings. The service will operate across Barking & Dagenham, Havering, Redbridge, Newham, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest, supporting timely access to care, improving patient experience and ensuring that patients receive treatment in the most appropriate setting. The service is expected to include referral assessment and triage, Advice & Guidance (A&G), specialist outpatient consultations, diagnostic investigations, minor dermatological procedures and the ongoing management of both acute and long-term dermatological conditions.
The service will work collaboratively with primary care, acute trusts and other healthcare partners to provide integrated pathways of care and clear arrangements for onward referral where specialist hospital-based intervention is required. The model will focus on delivering high-quality, safe and effective care, improving equity of access across North East London, and making best use of community-based provision to meet population health needs.
Market Engagement:
To assist the Commissioners with testing its assumptions and proposed service requirements, a market engagement event will take place to explore the market's feedback on the following areas:
• Outline of service requirements and key outcomes;
• Timescales for procurement and mobilisation of the new contract;
• Proposed contract duration and financial model;

title: Domestic Abuse - Intersecting Needs Safe Accommodation
description:
This project is the recommissioning of support and accommodation services within the scope of the Domestic Violence and Abuse Safe Accommodation Grant, which aims to provide first stage advice to support victims and survivors of domestic violence and abuse.
The purpose of this provision is to offer accommodation for individuals and groups who may be marginalised and facing multiple, intersecting disadvantages, in addition to their experiences of domestic violence and abuse. Many of those accessing this accommodation may not be suited to traditional models of safe accommodation with support, as they do not align with the typical profile of victims and survivors of domestic violence and abuse. Marginalisation can take many forms and often involves a range of complex and overlapping needs. Therefore, it is essential that support within this provision is tailored to the specific circumstances of each household, avoiding a one-size-fits-all approach. 
Therefore, this service specification outlines the provision of safe accommodation with support, which is inclusive, accessible, and responsive to the complex realities of people's lives. It forms a key part of the contractual framework for any provider commissioned to deliver this service.

title: Research Services for Pensions illustrations: presenting uncertainty and variability
description:
BACKGROUND
The FRC is the UK's independent regulator responsible for issuing and maintaining technical actuarial standards. It is responsible for Actuarial Standard Technical Memorandum 1 (AS TM1), which specifies the assumptions and methods used to calculate statutory illustrations of money purchase, or defined contribution, pensions.
Pension illustrations are based on assumptions about future investment returns, inflation and retirement choices. The uncertainty and variability inherent in future retirement outcomes can be challenging for defined contribution (DC) savers to understand. The FRC is interested in how this uncertainty and variability can be communicated clearly and effectively to support savers in understanding and assessing the adequacy of their pension arrangements.
PURPOSE
This research will gather evidence on how information can be presented to help DC savers understand the uncertainty and variability of their estimated pension income. It will inform the development of pension illustrations and related communications and support savers in understanding and assessing the adequacy of their pension arrangements.
The FRC is considering the information provided in the following contexts:
•	For pensions illustrations given to DC savers in early- and mid-career, there are uncertainties in the estimates of projected pension income; the further away from retirement, the greater the uncertainty. 
•	For pensions illustrations given to DC savers approaching retirement, there is uncertainty and variability in both the amount and pattern of income beyond the first point of accessing DC savings. 
The primary focus of the research will be on the presentation of pensions illustrations information. The successful contractor(s) will therefore need strong knowledge and experience of savers' behavioural responses to such information; they will also need sufficient technical knowledge of the investment, inflation, longevity and retirement timing risks inherent to pensions planning.
SCOPE
The research project will comprise three phases: 
1.	Literature review of the relevant academic and professional expert research in this area. 
2.	Solution development - drawing on phase 1, the successful contractor(s) will work closely with the FRC policy team to develop a range of potentially viable solutions for communicating DC pensions uncertainty and variability. 
Activities will include: 
•	developing alternative wording and narrative approaches; 
•	developing presentation formats and visualisations; 
•	considering how savers may interpret and respond to communications; 
•	assessing the extent to which communications may support informed decision-making. 
Outputs will include: 
•	behavioural design principles; 
•	prototype communications; 
•	visual mock-ups;  
•	supporting rationale for proposed approaches. 
3.	Empirical testing - drawing on phase 2, the FRC will select the approaches to be taken forward for empirical testing, taking account of the objectives of the research and the evidence gathered during phase 1. The successful contractor(s) will then carry out empirical testing of these approaches, allowing for a segmentation of DC savers, for example by stage of career, and any other relevant categorisation.
FEEDBACK SOUGHT
We are looking for feedback on a range of delivery approaches, including but not limited to:
SCOPE
•	Are there any additional or alternative phases or activities that are required to meet the Purpose of the project?
•	Are there relevant insights from other sectors or jurisdictions that could be adapted to improve how uncertainty and variability are communicated to DC savers?
RESEARCH METHODS
•	What approaches and methods could be used, and what issues might we encounter, in each of the following:
- Defining suitable bodies of academic and professional literature to review, and upon which to draw.
- Developing the potential solutions for communicating DC pensions uncertainty and variability; working closely with the FRC team in doing so.
- Selecting among the above potential solutions for field based empirical testing with users.
- Conducting that testing with rigour and inclusiveness, using suitable techniques and population samples.
STRUCTURE
•	What key milestones and dependencies would you envisage? What would be the best way(s) of involving the FRC team in review phases, and key decision-making?
•	How could responsibilities and interfaces between different parts of the project be managed, especially if delivered by different contractors?
TIMETABLE
•	The realistic overall duration of the project and indicative time needed for each of the three phases.
•	The lead time required for participant recruitment, research approvals, data collection, analysis and reporting, and any seasonal or market factors that could affect delivery.
ADDITIONAL COMMENTS
•	Are there any other insights that you could provide?
PRELIMINARY MARKET ENGAGEMENT PROCESS
The process comprises two parts (a)  questionnaire for your completion and (b) A virtual market engagement session.
IMPORTANT :- You must register your interest to procurement@frc.org.uk (no later than 5.00pm 14/09/2026) to receive the questionnaire / further details. 
CONDITIONS OF PARTICIPATION 
The FRC welcomes participation from potential contractors with demonstrable experience, capacity and capability relevant to the proposed services. Contractors will be required to confirm their independence (in relation to the scope of this research) and declare any actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest. Such matters may be taken into account as part of the procurement process, particularly where an entity tendering for this work is subject to direct or delegated regulation by the FRC.

title: TESS 6 Floating Support Service: Substance misuse and Criminal justice issues & Newlands
description: This service specification applies to a 22- unit floating support service delivering flexible housing related support to people experiencing substance misuse issues and/or criminal justice issues. The aim of this project is to provide housing support to improve outcomes for people at risk of homelessness to access information, advice, support and resources to enable them to make informed choices. The service working with individual service users involves a tailored support plan that best meets their needs. The plan focuses on both practical and emotional issues, in order that each person has the best opportunity of living independently as a responsible member of their community. The service will work with the service user to develop that person’s capacity to live independently in accommodation or sustain his/her ability to do so. While service users will have a variety and individual intensity of need, there is an expectation that support services will over time be reduced as service users achieve higher levels of independence. Therefore, support provision must be needs led, outcome focused and time scaled. The support provider will be responsible for monitoring all aspects of the services provided through the project.

title: Care Support Services for Children with a Disability (2026)
description:
Hampshire County Council Children’s Services commissions care support for children and young people with disabilities. The children and young people requiring care support services will include those with severe disabilities such as learning disabilities, physical disabilities, autistic spectrum conditions, behaviour that challenges and complex physical or mental health needs. The Services are part of a holistic support package for the child / young person that meets identified outcomes as part of a Care Plan as agreed by the Council’s County Allocation Panel.
This Service is part of Hampshire County Council’s Children’s Services Department’s continuum of services which support children and young people with disabilities. Care support is a Tier 4 specialist service, which can be offered to a family following a social care assessment where the Disabled Children’s Team criteria has been met and/or an unmet social care need has been identified.
The Services will have the following features:
• provides a time limited or ongoing intervention for families, dependent on need
• provides a range of different types of support to be available (e.g. domiciliary care, personal care, support in the community, overnight care etc.)
• provides flexible levels of support to meet individual needs (some families may only need light touch, and some will need intensive)
• provides support at both the times that is assessed as a need by the Social Worker and requested by families, for the time period required (e.g., one hour at the beginning and / or end of the day)
• provides suitably trained, reliable, consistent workers; known to the child or young person, all of whom will have an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Services (DBS) check, to ensure continuity and stability for families
• delivers Excellent / Good care in accordance with Care Quality Commission guidance for providers of health and social care services for children and young people
• identifies opportunities for the use of assistive care technologies and equipment to enable families to support their child independently in their own home or for the young person to access the community independently
• can support a child or young person in their own homes whilst the parent or carer is not present
• can support a child or young person in a residential home, foster home or their own home
• can support the child or young person in their local communities
The current Care Support for Children with a Disability Framework was developed by Hampshire County Council to address growing and evolving needs in social care, for children who require support in their home environment and to safeguard these children. The service is coming to the end of it's life span and is required to be retendered to ensure Hampshire may meet the needs of its eligible residents.
The new framework will be an evolution from the current Framework and the Authority is looking is looking for contracts for services under the Framework to commence from 01/09/2026.
This is a light touch contract as set out in section 9 of the Procurement Act 2023. As such the Council is establishing a Framework which will be open for new entrants across it's entire term. However, the Council reserves the right to temporarily pause the Framework for new entrants at any point. Any pause will be communicated through the Councils electronic tendering system. 
The Timetable in section 4.1 relates to the initial application window. Once the Framework commences it will be reopened for new applications and suppliers will be able to apply at any point up until 3 months before the Framework expires.

title: Analysis of VECTO data for HGVs
Biological control of invasive plants 2026/27
description:
Invasive non-native plant species like Himalayan balsam (HB) and Australian swamp stonecrop (ASS) significantly reduce biodiversity by crowding out native vegetation and limiting plant and animal species diversity. ASS deoxygenates water and reduces numbers of small invertebrates, amphibians and fish. Traditional methods for the control of HB and ASS are generally ineffective. Chemical control with herbicides is the most effective but often inappropriate next to or in waterbodies or protected nature conservation sites. 
The contract includes field and lab based experiments and release of relevant biological control agents (mites and rust fungus) to manage these two plant species. Pilots and testing projects are an important part of understanding the benefits and effectiveness of biological controls and the problems these species cause.  This investment now in biological control methods and their effective implementation have the potential to provide considerable benefits in terms of reduced costs and impacts as described above in future years.

Tai Tarian recognises that Tenderers may utilise third-party software components as part of their proposed solution. Such arrangements will be permitted provided the Tenderer assumes full responsibility for the delivery and performance of the overall solution and demonstrates that the proposed solution operates as a fully integrated and cohesive solution.

title: Grimsby Dock Tower Refurbishment
description:
Associated British Ports (ABP) is issuing this Preliminary Engagement Notice to inform the market of an upcoming procurement opportunity relating to the conservation, refurbishment and restoration of the Grade I Listed Grimsby Dock Tower. 
The purpose of this notice is to provide advance information to specialist heritage contractors with relevant experience in working on nationally significant listed structures and complex conservation projects. 
Background 
The Grimsby Dock Tower is a Grade I Listed structure, representing the highest level of protection afforded by The Historic Buildings and Monuments Commission for England (Historic England). The tower is a nationally significant heritage asset and an iconic landmark within the Port of Grimsby. 
The proposed project seeks to appoint a suitably qualified contractor to undertake detailed design, conservation, refurbishment and restoration works to address the deterioration of a number of critical structural and historic elements of the tower. 
The works include the replacement, refurbishment and conservation of original listed features, including water pipes, access structures, parapets, decking and the tower spire. Conservation works are also required to preserve the original spiral staircase and historic water supply infrastructure. 
The condition of several key elements has deteriorated significantly and has reached a stage where they have either failed or have no remaining serviceable life. Failure to undertake the required works could result in further deterioration of the asset, potential enforcement action by Historic England and adverse local and national publicity. 
Procurement Strategy
The estimated contract value is below the applicable threshold for Works Contracts under the Procurement Act 2023 and associated Procurement Regulations 2024.
As a result, ABP intends to undertake a closed, invitation-only tender process, inviting a select number of specialist heritage and conservation contractors with demonstrable experience of delivering works to Grade I and other highly protected historic structures.
Tender submissions will be evaluated using a combination of quality and price criteria. The quality assessment is expected to consider:
•	Project delivery methodology.
•	Construction programme and sequencing.
•	Health and Safety management approach.
•	Experience of heritage conservation and listed building works.
•	Proposed project team and key personnel.
•	Risk management arrangements.
Price will be assessed using a transparent like-for-like comparison methodology.

This floating support service will provide rapid, effective, and tailored support to the City of London Women’s Project with the goal of empowering survivors of domestic abuse to prepare them to move into safe, healthy and independent housing.
The service will support intersectionally marginalised service users with a range of needs, focusing on removing barriers to resettlement and ensuring their safety and wellbeing, with built-in understanding of the added needs surrounding neurodiversity and homelessness.
The service will interact with the local Domestic Abuse MARAC and IDVA’s where appropriate to ensure support is coordinated and client focussed whilst supporting the service users to develop and work through their personal housing plans.

Warwickshire County Council is seeking bids for care home block contracts for Pathway 2 Residential Short Stay Bed block contracts, commissioned for patients whose discharge from hospital is being led by Adult Social Care (currently short stay social care assessments beds and moving on beds).
Pathway 2 Residential Short Stay Beds provide short-term residential care for people who are medically optimised for discharge from hospital but are unable to return home, therefore requiring a short stay in a care home setting to support their recovery and time for assessment for future needs. People will stay in the service until their assessment and ongoing arrangements have been determined.
Moving On Beds: are for people that are medically fit for discharge and can return home but require further support and time before this can take place. People that use a MOB typically return home once environmental or social issues are resolved and have an average length of stay of 6 weeks.
D2A Short Stay Beds: are for people that are medically fit for discharge whose needs have increased since their admission to hospital meaning they are unable to return to their normal place of residence. They require assessment and time to recover to understand their future requirements, whether this is to return home or to go into long term care.
People that use a D2A Short Stay Bed have an average length of stay of 4 weeks. The Council is seeking to award approximately 52 D2A short stay beds and 8 Moving on beds across three Place areas in Warwickshire, these being North Warwickshire, Rugby and South Warwickshire.

title: Below 2 Bar Risk Model
description:
Cadent, working with Northern Gas Networks, SGN and Wales & West Utilities, is seeking information from the market to inform the potential development of a future Below 2 Bar Risk Model. The capability would support public-safety risk assessment, network planning and regulatory decision-making associated with GD4 / RIIO-4 and beyond.
The current Mains Replacement Prioritisation System has supported the Iron Mains Risk Reduction Programme. The participating Gas Distribution Networks are now considering how a shared, defensible and future-proof approach could preserve safety performance while improving transparency, auditability and consistency across networks.
1.1 Current context:
•	The future model is intended to provide transparent intelligence that supports intervention and investment prioritisation, without itself making operational decisions or generating work packages.
•	Its core purpose is public-safety risk assessment for relevant distribution assets operating up to 2 bar. Worker risk, monetisation and economic factors are outside the core risk calculation.
•	The model must be capable of supporting regulator scrutiny and consistent interpretation across the participating Gas Distribution Networks.
1.2 Information sought from the market:
This RFI is deliberately concise. It seeks an early indication of market capability, material gaps and relevant experience. It is not intended to request a detailed solution, delivery plan, commercial proposal or evidential response at this stage. More detailed information may be requested through the subsequent Expression of Interest, Pre-Qualification Questionnaire and Invitation to Tender stages.
High Level Scope:
The proposed capability is a common, transparent and auditable public-safety risk model for relevant gas distribution assets operating at pressures up to 2 bar. It should provide risk intelligence that enables the participating Gas Distribution Networks to understand and compare risk consistently, identify the assets and factors that contribute to risk, and support defensible planning, investment and regulatory decision-making. The model is expected to inform decisions rather than make operational decisions or generate work packages.
The scope includes relevant mains, services and risers, with the potential for delivery to be phased or modular while retaining a common methodology, units of measure and governance framework. The capability should address risk to individuals and groups, cumulative risk from multiple assets, attribution of risk to contributing assets and factors, consequence and injury or fatality likelihood, and the effect of property, building and occupancy characteristics. It should also accommodate differences in available data, data quality and maturity across the participating networks.
The future model should be capable of validation, independent assurance and regulatory scrutiny. Its calculations, assumptions, coefficients, data inputs and outputs should be explainable to technical and non-technical users. The participating Gas Distribution Networks should be able to govern and sustain the methodology over the long term, including controlled updates, a common national baseline with justified local variation, and appropriate ownership of methodology, configuration, parameters and intellectual property.
This RFI is not asking respondents to design the complete solution. Respondents should consider whether their organisation can meet the overall scope, identify any material capability or feasibility gaps, and highlight where an aspect of the emerging requirement may be unrealistic or would benefit from clarification, simplification or phasing.
Please email arun.thakore@cadentgas.com to receive the RfI documentation. This will include all the information required to submit your response.
Please note: This RFI is for information and market-engagement purposes only. It does not constitute a commitment to procure. The scope and outcomes are indicative and emerging, allowing respondents to propose alternative methods and good practice.

title: Preliminary Market Engagement Notice - School and Special Transport Open Framework
description:
Bedford Borough Council has a statutory duty to provide free home to school travel for compulsory school-aged children who meet nationally prescribed eligibility criteria and for post-16 students who meet locally determined criteria. To fulfil this duty, the Council commissions transport services from external providers using a range of vehicle types to meet the diverse needs of routes and individual passengers. In addition, the School and Specialist Transport Team arranges transport for a range of Adult and Children's Social Care requirements, including contact sessions, day services, and respite provision. To support the efficient and compliant procurement of these services, the Council is establishing a new Open Framework to replace the existing Passenger Transport Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS).
Bedford Borough Council is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement in relation to the establishment of this new Open Framework for the provision of Home to School, Specialist Transport, and related passenger transport services. The Framework will replace the Council's existing Passenger Transport Dynamic Purchasing System and will be used to procure transport services for eligible children, young people, adults and other service users as required.
The Council is publishing this notice to inform the market of the proposed procurement, provide an overview of the service requirements, and invite interested providers to engage with the opportunity. The procurement process is expected to be conducted electronically through the ADAM eProcurement System, with approved providers being eligible to participate in future call-off opportunities under the Open Framework.
Indicative timescales are:
Publication of procurement documents: Early September 2026
Evaluation of applications: October 2026
Notification of framework admission outcomes: November 2026
Framework award and commencement: November/ December 2026
These dates are indicative only and may be subject to change.
This notice does not commence the procurement process and is intended solely to support market awareness and engagement ahead of the formal tender opportunity.
Interested providers are encouraged to register their interest and participate in the forthcoming procurement opportunity when advertised.

description:
Gwent Police is undertaking a Preliminary Market Engagement exercise to inform the future provision of catering and canteen services at Gwent Police Headquarters, Cwmbran.
Prior to commencing any formal procurement process, Gwent Police wishes to engage with the market to gain an understanding of the options available for the operation, management and development of the existing canteen facilities. Scope of Engagement
Gwent Police is seeking input from suppliers with experience in the provision of catering, café, restaurant, hospitality and workplace food service operations.
Suppliers are invited to review the existing facilities and provide feedback on:
- Potential operating models.
- Service delivery options.
- Opportunities for improving utilisation of the facility.
- Commercial viability considerations.
- Innovation and best practice within the sector.
- Potential investment requirements.
- Sustainability and social value opportunities.
Site Visits
Interested suppliers are invited to attend an individual site visit at Gwent Police Headquarters.
To ensure commercial confidentiality and to accommodate operational requirements, site visits will be arranged on an individual basis. Suppliers will not attend site visits jointly and no group engagement sessions will be held.

title: Housing Kitchen Replacement Programme
description:
North Lanarkshire Council is undertaking preliminary market engagement in relation to a proposed Supply and Install Kitchen Replacement Programme across its Council housing stock.
The Council is planning a significant programme of investment for the supply, delivery and installation of replacement domestic kitchens within occupied Council properties. The current indicative investment profile is forecast to be approximately 65 million GBP over the period 2027/28 to 2030/31.
Through this Prior Information Notice (PIN) and accompanying Request for Information (RFI), the Council wishes to engage with contractors, to gain a better understanding of current market capacity, supply chain capability, contract structures, mobilisation requirements, and innovation opportunities associated with the delivery of large-scale housing kitchen replacement programmes.
The Council is aware of a number of national framework arrangements currently operating within the marketplace and of the various procurement routes available under the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015. At this stage, no decision has been made regarding the preferred procurement strategy or route to market. The Council may consider a range of options including existing frameworks  or a future open market procurement.
The purpose of this exercise is to gather information that will help inform the Council's future procurement strategy and delivery approach. The Council is particularly interested in obtaining feedback on market capacity.
This PIN is issued solely as a market engagement and information gathering exercise.
It does not constitute a call for competition, a commitment to procure, or a commitment to award any contract.

Hankinnan kohteena oleva palvelu voi tapauskohtaisesti kohdistua yhteen tai useampaan päätyövaiheiseen. Hankinnan kohteen tarkempi kuvaus tilattavasta palvelusta oli kuvattu liitteessä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Vantaan kaupungin sopimusta voivat käyttää kaikki Vantaan kaupungin toimialat. title: Finland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Digital exhibition design, software development and production for the reopening exhibition for the National Museum of Finland.
description: The Finnish Heritage Agency, the Exhibitions and Events department of the National Museum of Finland (hereinafter the “Procurement unit”) invites suppliers to submit tenders for media design and production (hereinafter the “Service”) in this call for tenders and its attached annexes. The Service consists of programming, project management and technical delivery of an artificial iIntelligence System in the form of an interactive media software which will be used according to attached plans. The entire deliverable procurement is referred to in hereinafter as the "System". The National Museum of Finland will conduct the procurement through an open tendering procedure. The aim is for production to begin immediately after the selection of the supplier in approximately September 2026, and for delivery to the Procurement Unit to be completed no later than January 2027. The procurement documents are available in English. The Procurement unit requests a tender for: 1. Exhibition Media, AV and Interactive Elements including: - Lobby Screen - Intro to the Universe (projection) - Chatty objects - 9 interactive conversational artificial intelligence stations: - Chatty Objects Birds - Chatty Object Scarab - Chatty Object Meteorite - Chatty Object Shiva - Chatty Object Canoe - Chatty Object Turtle Seats - Chatty Object Raven Mask - Chatty Object Chilkat Blanket - Chatty Object Bad Luck Bird - Chatty Object Scarab - Projection (Hybrid element) - Agnicayana film projection solution -Exhibition wide - soundscapes including: - Anvil & hammer - Chatty Objects Birds - Audio - Egg - Chatty Object Meteorite - (hybrid element) - Chatty Object Canoe - (hybrid element) - Chatty Object Raven Mask - (hybrid element) - World tree - Conch - Universe - Overhead Screen - Universe - Chatty Universe The following items are not included within this tender: - Film content for the Agnicayana film projection - Recording of poem for the Egg Soundscape 2. Software, Services and Project Management including: - Software development and testing - Software installation and configuration - Technical and user documentation - Support and on-call services during the exhibtion run - Training for the client's staff in the operation of the delivered systems - Project management covering the entire Procurement 3. Documentation set: - Technical documentation (architecture, APIs, content formats, deployment instructions). - Operational documentation for daily use by exhibition staff. - Maintenance instructions, including restart procedures and troubleshooting steps. - Documentation required under the attached Annex 3 "03_Data and privacy requirements annex". - The tenderer shall provide sufficient documentation to enable re-installation and re-use of the System by the Procurement unit without dependency on the tenderer if the Procurement unit wants to use the System in the future after the exhibition. 4. Installation & on site deployment The tenderer shall: - Install all required system software components on site in coordination with the AV integrator contractor (procured separately) and the Procurement unit's team. - Integrate "The Universe" content into existing overhead LED screen and newly purchased hardware. - Conduct full system testing. 5. Training for museum staff The tenderer shall: - Provide training sessions for Procurement unit's staff on System operation, daily use and safety as applicable and needed for the procurement. - Provide training materials (slides, troubleshooting guides, quickstart sheets). 6. Final handover package The tenderer shall provide: - Final approved versions of all media assets. - Backup copies of the System and its configurations. - A complete inventory of all delivered software. - End of project report summarizing methods, design decisions, and technical notes. The procurements requirements are explained in more detail further on in this call for tenders and its attached annexes. The estimated value of the procurement is according to the Procurement unit 400 000 - 550 000 EUR (VAT 0%). Some of the attached annexes in the call for tenders contains confidential information. The documents are available upon request via email to hankinnat@museovirasto.fi. The tenderer shall in its request to receive the documents ensure, that it keeps the information received from the Procurement unit only to itself and uses that information for its tender according to this procurement process. The information is considered confidential even after the procurement process has ended.

title: Netherlands – Research services – Onderzoek Draadslachtoffers en Effectiviteit Hawk Eye-draadmarkeringen Verbinding Vierverlaten Ens 380 kV
description: Voor het project Verbinding Vierverlaten-Ens 380 kV (VVL-ENS380) moet er onderzoek worden uitgevoerd naar de effectiviteit van Hawk Eye (nieuwe vorm van draadmarkering, zie deze link naar artikel op TenneT website ) en actualisatie van kengetallen naar draadslachtoffers per soort. Beide zijn nodig voor de vergunningverlening voor het project, maar moeten ook TenneT-breed kunnen worden toegepast voor andere lijnenprojecten. Voor de bepaling van het aantal draadslachtoffers onder hoogspanningsverbindingen wordt momenteel gebruikgemaakt van onderzoeksgegevens uit 1987. Deze gegevens sluiten niet langer aan bij de huidige situatie en bieden onvoldoende basis om de ecologische impact van hoogspanningsinfrastructuur zorgvuldig te onderbouwen. Hierdoor ontstaat onzekerheid over de omvang van de effecten op vogelpopulaties en over de effectiviteit van eventuele mitigerende maatregelen. Het beoogde onderzoek kent daarom twee samenhangende doelstellingen. Allereerst wordt een actuele nulmeting uitgevoerd om inzicht te verkrijgen in het aantal draadslachtoffers onder en in de directe omgeving van de bestaande 220 kV-hoogspanningsverbinding tussen Vierverlaten en Ens. Vervolgens wordt de effectiviteit van mitigerende maatregelen onderzocht door deze op geselecteerde masten en geleiders toe te passen en de resultaten te monitoren. Een belangrijk onderdeel van het onderzoek betreft de beoordeling van de effectiviteit van verschillende typen vogelmarkeringen. Binnen de organisatie bestaat een voorkeur voor toepassing van de Hawk Eye-draadmarkering als mitigerende maatregel. Voor een bredere implementatie ontbreekt momenteel echter nog de wetenschappelijke onderbouwing van de effectiviteit ervan onder Nederlandse omstandigheden. Het onderzoek dient daarom de kennisbasis te leveren die nodig is om onderbouwde keuzes te maken over de inzet van deze maatregel en om de bijdrage ervan aan het verminderen van draadslachtoffers aantoonbaar te maken.

title: Germany – Energy and related services – 10021886-Provision of standardised consultancy services for On- & Off-Grid Regulation and Market Development
description: GET.transform, is a technical assistance program supporting national and regional partners and institutions in advancing their energy transitions. GET.transform is a component of the GET.pro (Global Energy Transformation Programme), which is a global multi-donor platform and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The three instruments of GET.pro are: - GET.invest mobilises private investments in clean energy by building a pipeline of bankable investment projects. - GET.transform supports partner governments by developing bankable frameworks for clean energy investment. - The Secretariat for Africa-EU Energy Program promotes strategic political dialogue between Africa and Europe on energy. Thematic and geographic scope: The implementation structure of GET.transform is organised along the Thematic and Geographic Approach. GET.transform offers structured advisory services on four key transformational topics: 1) Long-Term Energy Planning 2) Renewable Energy Grid Integration 3) On-Grid Regulation and Market Development 4) Off-Grid Regulation and Market Development On-Grid Regulation and Market Development measures enable power sector market reform allowing for renewable energy participation, increased investment, and promotion of private markets. Power system transformation processes should be supported by a background of technically sound energy planning, a well-functioning governance structure, policy and regulatory framework. The goal is to ensure that electricity resources, including generation, transmission, and distribution systems, are allocated efficiently. In addition, market model mechanisms can be designed and implemented to facilitate a sustainable, secure, competitive and affordable electricity system. To meet the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 target of universal access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services by 2030, decentralised renewable energy solutions such as off-grid solutions have been proven to be efficient at providing energy access to rural communities. Off-grid solutions can power over 400 million people across Africa and LAC. Off- Grid Regulation and Market Development establishes a framework for public partners to strengthen institutional capacities to accomplish their rural development mandates, as well as market incentives that promote private sector participation and finance for scaling projects. ? In addition to its core activities, GET.transform has implemented TA services to other GIZ- programs in Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as Asia and Europe. GET.transform is therefore offering activities potentially in all countries where GIZ energy portfolio is active by efficiently offering standardised solutions and scaling activities and contributing towards the concept of Vision 100 of GIZ, which serves as a guiding principle for the realignment of the GIZ portfolio for the global energy transition.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Erweiterung und Sanierung der Astrid-Lindgren-Grundschule in Waldalgesheim, Los 2 - Planungsleistungen der Technischen Ausrüstung HLS und Elektro
description: Die Verbandsgemeinde Rhein-Nahe plant die Erweiterung und Sanierung der Astrid-Lindgren-Grundschule in Waldalgesheim, um den schulischen Bedarf gemäß dem Schulentwicklungsplan Rheinland-Pfalz sicherzustellen. Die Schule besteht aus mehreren Gebäudeteilen aus den späten 1950er-Jahren. Die Gesamtnutzfläche beträgt ca. 1.930 m², der umbaute Raum beträgt ca. 8.300 m³. Ziel der Maßnahme ist es, zusätzliche Räume für den Schulbetrieb zu schaffen und bestehende Gebäudebereiche funktional und technisch zu modernisieren. Zudem soll die barrierefreie Erschließung der wesentlichen Nutzungsbereiche gewährleistet werden. Mit Abschluss der Maßnahme soll ein funktional, technisch und energetisch zeitgemäßer Grundschulstandort entstehen, der die pädagogischen Anforderungen erfüllt, zusätzliche Raumkapazitäten bereitstellt und langfristig den Vorgaben des Schulentwicklungsplans entspricht. Eine Machbarkeitsstudie (Stand: 20.11.2025) liegt vor und wird zur Verfügung gestellt. Die Inhalte sind nicht verbindlich, sondern dienen als Orientierung für die weitere Planung. Die konkrete Ausarbeitung erfolgt im Rahmen der zu beauftragenden Planungsleistungen. Erweiterung - zusätzliche Räume für Verwaltung, Betreuung, Bibliothek und Differenzierung - pädagogische Ergänzungsflächen (insbesondere MINT-Bereich) - barrierefreie Erschließung der neuen und bestehenden Bereiche - Anbindung an den Klassentrakt und die Turnhalle Umbau und Sanierung der Bestandsgebäude - Sanierung und Neuordnung der WC-Anlagen - Anpassungen an Erschließung und Fluren (Übergänge Alt-Neu) - teilweise Erneuerung der technischen Anlagen, insbesondere im Hausanschlussraum (HLS, Elektro, IT) - mögliche Umnutzung einzelner Räume (ehem. Lehrmittelraum, Hausmeisterraum etc.) Gebäudehülle / Energie - Austausch eines Teils der Fensteranlagen in Klassenräumen und Fluren - energetische Maßnahmen gemäß GEG, u. a.: o punktuelle Verbesserungen an Gebäudehülle und Bauteilanschlüssen o energetische Optimierung in Verbindung mit der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung Außenanlagen - Anpassung der Außen- und Freianlagen im unmittelbaren Baufeld - barrierefreie Wegeführung und Anbindung an die Bestandsflächen Allgemein: Die Bauausführung erfolgt im laufenden Schulbetrieb. Dabei sind insbesondere folgende Aspekte zu berücksichtigen: - Sicherheit von Schülern und Lehrkräften - Lärm- und Staubschutz - abschnittsweise Bauabläufe - temporäre Wegeführungen - Abstimmung der Arbeiten mit der Schulleitung Für die Maßnahme wird eine Förderung im Rahmen der Schulbauförderung des Landes Rheinland-Pfalz angestrebt. Energetische Einzelmaßnahmen, insbesondere der Fensteraustausch, können zusätzlich über Bundesprogramme (z. B. BAFA) gefördert werden. Die Fördervoraussetzungen werden im Zuge der weiteren Planung fortgeschrieben und mit den zuständigen Stellen abgestimmt. Die anrechenbaren Kosten werden auf Grundlage der in der Machbarkeitsstudie dargestellten Variante 3 in Höhe von 3.159.115 EUR netto angesetzt. Diese Kosten dienen ebenfalls ausschließlich als Orientierungswert für die Ausschreibung der Planungsleistungen. Die Variantenuntersuchung ist nicht bindend; die konkrete Planung wird in den weiteren Leistungsphasen gemeinsam mit den Planungsbeteiligten entwickelt und fortgeschrieben.

Por otro lado, la sociedad de hoy, cada vez más sensibilizada con valores de protección ambiental y optimización de recursos, demanda a su vez creatividad, diseño, empleo de tecnología moderna, desarrollo de elementos de calidad que eviten su rápido deterioro, utilización de elementos de bajo consumo, mínimo impacto y escasa contaminación lumínica capaces de crear diferentes atmósferas, con una estética integrada en el entorno y en una época de crisis como la actual y todo ello al menor coste posible. title: Germany – Research and development consultancy services – Projektträgerschaft für das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) „Quantentechnologien und Photonik“
description: Die Hightech-Agenda Deutschland (HTAD) steht für mehr Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, Wertschöpfung und Souveränität Die Quantentechnologie gehört zu den sechs Schlüsseltechnologien der HTAD. In diesem Rahmen und im Rahmen des Programms „Forschungsprogramm Quantensysteme“ fördert das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) Forschungs- und Entwicklungsaktivitäten (F&E), die gemeinsam mit Wissenschaft und Wirtschaft durchgeführt werden. Das Forschungsprogramm steht unter dem Motto „Spitzentechnologie entwickeln. Zukunft gestalten.” Es beschreibt den innovationspolitischen Rahmen für die Forschungsförderung in diesem Bereich bis 2032. Mit dem Programm fördert das BMFTR die Zukunftsthemen Photonik und Quantentechnologien erstmals unter einem gemeinsamen Dach. Denn Photonik und Quantentechnologien sind nicht nur wesentliche Innovations- und Wachstumsmotoren für den Wirtschafts- und Wissenschaftsstandort Deutschland, sondern auch für die moderne Gesellschaft. Als Schlüsseltechnologien sind sie außerdem inhaltlich eng miteinander verknüpft. Daraus ergeben sich Synergien, die das BMFTR gezielt nutzt, um beide Technologien voranzubringen. Das BMFTR finanziert im Rahmen des hier ausgeschriebenen Förderbereichs F&E-Vorhaben. Die Förderung erfolgt i.d.R. im Rahmen von Projekten sowie anhand anderer Förderinstrumente (z.B. Forschungskäufe). Grundlage dafür sind Förderbekanntmachungen, in denen zu Projektvorschlägen aufgerufen wird. in der Projektförderung anzuwendenden Bestimmungen und Verfahren sind im Einzelnen im Handbuch der Projektförderung dargestellt. Aufgabe des Auftragnehmers ist die Unterstützung des BMFTR bei der Umsetzung der genannten Programme bzw. ihrer Weiterentwicklungen. Hierzu gehört die Unterstützung bei der Weiterentwicklung bestehender Förderlinien und -maßnahmen sowie die Unterstützung bei der Entwicklung neuer Förderansätze, insbesondere solcher mit einem starken Fokus auf Transfer und Wertschöpfung. Dies ist ein fortlaufender Prozess. Der AN berät das BMFTR in der Weise, dass Anregungen und neue Rahmenbedingungen aus dem Forschungsumfeld aufgegriffen und ggf. in Vorschläge für die Weiterentwicklung der Programme umgesetzt werden. title: Enterprise Geospatial Licensed Maps &  Data
description:
National Grid currently procures geospatial (GIS) data independently across Business Units, driven by project specific needs. This decentralized approach has led to duplication of datasets, inconsistent coverage, variable quality, and limited reuse. A single view is required of what geospatial data is owned, licensed, open, and stored. The project supports National Grid's ambition to move to enterprise wide data reuse, stronger governance, and improved commercial outcomes; a single tool that provides a variety of datasets such as ordnance survey, natural resources, environmental etc. 
•	Objectives:
•	Establish a single, enterprise-wide procurement and governance model for all geospatial (GIS) data across NG Group, UK.
•	Replace fragmented, project-led data purchasing with standardized, centrally managed access.
•	Eliminate duplication, inconsistent coverage, and limited reuse caused by historic Business Unit-led procurement.
•	Improve visibility, control, and availability of both licensed/premium and open geospatial datasets.
•	Enable cost reduction and greater value through enterprise-wide reuse and optimized licensing.
•	Successful supplier will  supply, license, and support core geospatial datasets and 
•	Enable access to both premium and open datasets.
The maps and data should be provided through electronic means, via a suitable software platform.

title: Children & Young People Pathfinder - Supported Systems
description:
The commissioned activity relates to the development of child sexual abuse (CSA) systems and pathways across the South West region, building on work already undertaken to strengthen local responses to children and young people affected by CSA.
The project responds to the recognised need for improved coordination, accessibility and consistency of services across health, justice, safeguarding and voluntary sector systems. Current arrangements vary across the region, creating challenges in service accessibility, workforce confidence, governance arrangements and multi-agency working.
The organisation undertaking this work is the Bluestar Project (a Community Interest Company, in partnership with The Green House charity). 
The project aims to improve coordination, accessibility and consistency of responses to children and young people affected by CSA across health, justice, safeguarding and voluntary sector services. The work will include needs assessments, service mapping, workforce development, governance and pathway improvement, and the promotion of trauma-informed, CPS-compliant practice. Children, young people and families will be involved through co-production activities.
Bluestar will build on existing work in Swindon & Wiltshire and Dorset and undertake further systems development activity, including sequential needs assessments in Devon & Cornwall and Gloucestershire, to identify service gaps and opportunities for improvement.
At the heart of this programme is a simple aim: to support sustainable, system-wide change so that every child who experiences sexual abuse can access a timely, compassionate, and coordinated response. Achieving this requires more than new services - it demands equipping the children's workforce across all agencies with the skills, confidence, and structures to act together, and embedding a culture of listening, believing, and responding. By laying these foundations, the programme enables to move beyond fragmented provision towards lasting, joined-up systems of care. 
The Bluestar Project also led national development of pre-trial therapy guidance, training and accreditation, working alongside the police and CPS. This has been rolled out nationally.

title: Animated videos for Negotiation Support Package for Adult Social Care Fair Pay Agreement
description:
The Improvement and Development Agency for Local Government (IDeA) is working through the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and supported by sector partners including ADASS, to deliver the Adult Social Care Fair Pay Agreement Negotiation Support Package (NSP). The programme aims to increase awareness and understanding of the proposed Fair Pay Agreement, which will establish a national process for negotiating pay, terms and conditions, and career development for eligible adult social care workers in England. Given the sector’s size and diversity, with around 18,000 providers and 1.7 million workers, the NSP will provide accessible resources to help employers and organisations engage with the process.
As part of this work, IDeA is seeking a supplier to create one initial short, high-quality animated video, with the option to commission up to four additional videos. These videos will form part of a wider outreach and engagement campaign and should explain complex information in a clear, accessible and engaging way. Content must be based solely on factual, policy and legal information provided or approved by IDeA, and the videos must not offer legal advice, employee-facing pay guidance or independent interpretations of policy.
The primary audience for the videos is adult social care employers and organisations, including large providers, SMEs, micro-providers, voluntary sector organisations, individual employers, provider bodies and employer representative networks. Secondary audiences include councils, commissioners, NHS trusts, workforce leads, trade unions, DHSC and other sector partners who may need to understand the programme or direct stakeholders towards it. The overall objective is to improve sector readiness and understanding of the Fair Pay Agreement process and the role of the Adult Social Care Negotiating Body.
