title: Passenger Transport Open Framework
description:
North Yorkshire Council (the Authority) is seeking tenders from suitably qualified suppliers to join its Passenger Transport Open Framework. The Open Framework is being established to provide a range of passenger transport services, including Home to School Transport and other transport-related services, through a diverse network of approved Suppliers with relevant expertise and capabilities. The Open Framework will be divided into the following Lots
• Lot 1 - Vehicles with up to 8 passenger seats (including accessible vehicles)
• Lot 2 - Vehicles with 9 to 16 passenger seats (including accessible vehicles)
• Lot 3 - Vehicles with 17 or more passenger seats
Lots are categorised according to vehicle seating capacity and/or accessibility provisions rather than vehicle size. Suppliers may apply for all Lots that are relevant to the services they are able to provide.
The majority of the transport will be provided within the North Yorkshire boundary however there is an element that will be delivered out of the area.
This tender notice is for the award of a public contract through an open procedure in accordance with section 20(1) and (2)(a) of the PA 2023.
To support the development of this procurement, the Authority issued a Request for Information (RFI) on 3 February 2025. The RFI was published to the market to gather feedback from existing and potential suppliers on key aspects of the proposed framework, including:
• Procurement processes and documentation
• Pricing approaches and market conditions
• Barriers to participation and supplier engagement
In addition, the Authority worked in partnership with Go4Growth to deliver a supplier engagement webinar. The session provided an overview of the Open Framework model and covered topics including:
• Understanding Open Frameworks
• Registration requirements for the Central Digital Platform
• Available support tools to assist with the tendering process
• The proposed high-level procurement timetable
This market engagement activity has helped inform the development of the Open Framework and ensures that the procurement process is accessible, transparent, 
and reflective of current market conditions.

title: Wormwood Scrubs Masterplan Biodiversity & Improvement Works
description:
London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham Council (the "Council") invited tenders seeking a supplier who is suitably qualified and experienced in landscaping and the creation and management of ecologically sensitive habitats.
Wormwood Scrubs is an open space located at the northern end of the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham. It is the largest open space in the Borough, at around 80 ha (200 acres), and is one of the largest areas of common land in London.
The work is to implement the proposals in the AEM (Alternative Ecological Mitigation) Masterplan for Wormwood Scrubs open space. The overall objective of the AEM Masterplan is to improve and enhance biodiversity on the Scrubs and at the same time improve drainage across the site to better manage surface water and improve access.
The work is split into two phases:
Capital works - this phase of work should be completed in 6-8 months and will include the creation of a SUDs (Sustainable Urban Drainage scheme) made up of a series of scrapes and swales to the south of the site and the northwest corner of the site. Retention ponds will be created in the existing wet woodlands in the southeast of the site. Tree planting will take place at various locations and existing vegetation will be improved along with the creation of meadows and grasslands. Hibernacula's will be created and bird and bat boxes installed.
Maintenance and Management Plan (MMP) - Phase 2 of the work will be a 10 year Management and Maintenance Plan (MMP) which will include the management of the features implemented as part of the Phase 1 Capital Works including the SUDs scheme and meadows and will also involve the management of the existing woodland, scrubland and meadows that have not previously been regularly managed and are in need of ongoing management to improve conditions for wildlife and increase biodiversity. For example, selective thinning in woodland areas will allow more light in to allow a greater variety of woodland plants to grow in the understorey.

title: UK2 Notice: Preliminary Market Engagement - Asylum Seeker Travel Services
description:
The Home Office (the Authority) has a statutory duty under Section 55 of the Borders, Citizenship and Immigration Act 2009 to discharge its immigration and asylum functions having regard to the need to safeguard and promote the welfare of children in the UK. 
In addition to this, under the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999, the Home Office has a statutory obligation to provide temporary support for Asylum Seekers who appear to be destitute or are likely to become destitute within a prescribed period.  
These obligations include Unaccompanied Asylum-Seeking Children (UASC) who arrive in the UK and enter the immigration system without a parent or guardian as well as an adult Asylum Seeker Cohort.
The service includes the arrangement of transport on behalf of local authorities, as well as the Home Office, for the movement of UASC when these movements are required. A number of core business units will utilise this contract. Further details will be provided through additional materials that will be made available to parties, upon completion and receipt of a signed Non-Disclosure Agreement (more information for which is set out in this document). 
This service will not be used for Home Office staff transport and is intended as a civilian travel programme only.  The Home Office is still considering all of its options with regards to aggregation and disaggregation and therefore encourages suppliers who may not be able to deliver the full scope of services to still participate in any subsequent market engagement activity.
The purpose of this engagement is to better understand market capability, capacity, delivery models, and commercial approaches available to support the future service. Information regarding service requirements, volumes and operational arrangement will be shared with interested organisations as part of this engagement activity. Please refer to “Engagement process description” below.

title: Regenerative Schools Pilot - Academic Assurance Partner
description:
The Department for Education and the Education Estates Strategy
The Department for Education (DfE) is the UK government’s Department responsible for the schools in England. As part of this role, we oversee the safety, condition, and long‑term sustainability of the education estate. This includes ensuring that current and future school buildings are provided with safe, high‑quality environments where children can learn and thrive.
On 11th February 2026 the Department published its 10-year plan for the Education Estate, the Education Estates Strategy, A decade of national renewal. The Regenerative Schools Pilot was outlined within the strategy:
“Testing new solutions, technologies and construction methods – we will continue to look at how we can go further for our future design specifications as part of a research and development programme supported by £33 million to 2029-30. This will prioritise regenerative approaches looking at a wide range of outcomes from energy storage to bio-based construction materials, such as timber and working closely with Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) on the Timber in Construction Road Map.”
The Regenerative Schools Pilot, Introduction:
The Department for Education intends to research, develop, and deliver a series of single and dual classroom, ultra‑low‑carbon school buildings under the Regenerative Schools Programme. This will be accompanied by a package of landscaping and retrofit interventions which will support biodiversity, passive heat‑reduction (such as tree shading), fabric upgrades to existing buildings (cladding and windows), sustainable drainage systems and the creation of outdoor learning spaces. This programme will also produce case studies, guidance and resources for schools.
This notice outlines the Department's intent to award a contract to the successful supplier for the Academic Assurance Partner role. As communicated in prior notices, we intend to publish a separate notice for the Innovation Lead role shortly. These organisations will produce feasibility studies, research the building materials and techniques required to produce ultra‑low‑carbon school buildings and develop 6 standard designs. Then, in 2027, the Department plans to appoint a contractor to deliver the works, using the materials and methods specified by the Innovation Lead and Academic Assurance Partner. Separate market engagement and tender events will be held for the construction contractor’s appointment.
The Academic Assurance Partner
The Academic Assurance Partner will complement the Innovation Lead’s technical work by focusing on the social, educational, and behavioural dimensions of the programme. You will use your research capabilities and academic expertise related to ultra-low-carbon materials to advise the Department and Innovation Lead. Your role will begin with the creation of a school‑ready engagement toolkit and the delivery of inclusive engagement across the participating regions. This will involve working directly with pupils, staff, governors, parents, and other stakeholders to build a picture of community needs, aspirations, and challenges, ensuring these insights inform both retrofit strategies and the design of the new learning spaces. You will translate these findings into clear design inputs so that lived experience directly shapes feasibility work and guidance documents. 
As projects move into delivery and buildings begin to be used, the Academic Assurance Partner will lead a structured programme of post‑occupancy evaluation, bringing together qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand how the new and refurbished environments perform in practice. Your work will consider internal and external environmental factors (such as air quality, temperature, and acoustics), wellbeing, nature‑connectedness, and educational impact, helping the Department understand what works and where further development may be required. The insights you produce will be shared through publications, reports, and case studies, contributing to future policy and guidance for the wider education estate. 
Working with the Innovation Lead
The Innovation Lead and Academic Assurance Partner are intended to operate in parallel, each with a distinct focus but with close coordination throughout. The Innovation Lead will ensure technical feasibility, safety, and low‑carbon performance, while the Academic Assurance Partner will ensure that the programme responds to the needs and experiences of the schools and communities involved. Together you will provide the Department with the combined academic, social, and technical expertise required to develop a set of replicable, ultra‑low‑carbon solutions that are grounded in real‑world school environments and capable of informing future national delivery.
For the avoidance of doubt, the publication of this notice triggers the mandatory 8 day standstill period and this period will end at 17:00 on 08/09/2026.

title: DLSITT1101 - K14 SWIFT Beamline Kirkpatrick-Baez (KB) Mirrors System for Diamond Light Source
description:
Located on the Harwell Science & Innovation Campus in Oxfordshire, Diamond Light Source (DLS) is a leading-edge facility for science, engineering and innovation. DLS allows researchers from academia and industry to investigate the structure and behaviour of the world around us at the atomic and molecular level. 
To continue delivering the world-changing science that Diamond enables, the facility is being upgraded to Diamond-II, a co-ordinated programme of development that combines a major machine upgrade with new instruments and complementary improvements to optics, detectors, sample environment and delivery capabilities, and computing, as well as integrated and correlative methods. This will be transformative in speed and spatial resolution and will offer users streamlined access to enhanced instruments for life and physical sciences.
The scope of the contract is for the design, supply of material, manufacture, assembly, test, delivery, installation and commissioning of a two-mirror combined system (a pair of
Kirkpatrick-Baez (KB) mirrors) and its position adjustment systems. The mirrors will focus the beam onto a sample positioned in the K14 beamline second end-station. 
• The minimum scope of the contract should include: HFM - Horizontally Focusing Mirror  Horizontally (outboard) reflecting, monochromatic beam mirror & mechanics.
• VFM - Vertically Focusing Mirror- Vertically (upward) reflecting, monochromatic beam mirror & mechanics.
• Temperature monitoring for interlocking.
• Vacuum vessel. 
• Support frame. 
• Interface to beamline services. 
• Training for Diamond personnel in the operation of the mirrors 
• Installation of the mirrors in their benders at the DLS Optics Metrology Lab (OML).

title: Complex Move on Contract
description:
This UK5 transparency notice informs the market of the Authority’s intention to award a contract directly to Langley Trust for the provision of the Complex Move on service. 
The Complex Move On service provides specialist risk management services, rehabilitation and resettlement support for people on probation with complex needs who are accommodated within pre-existing specialist accommodation settings. 
The service supports His Majesty Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) in managing individuals who require enhanced levels of care and risk management, by providing access to supported housing and other relevant support to individuals with complex needs with the aim of reducing the risk of reoffending. The funding from the Authority enables HMPPS to make referrals into these services by covering the additional costs associated with managing increased forensic risk and delivering appropriate criminogenic interventions. Funding for the accommodation and other support services will be obtained and managed by the supplier separately. Accordingly, the Authority does not have exclusive rights to the bed spaces used to deliver the service.
The support service is to be delivered within a portfolio of accommodation operated or accessed by the supplier, including: 
•	24/7 registered care home provision (Care);
•	24/7 staffed provision (Extra Care); and 
•	step-down supported accommodation in the community which is not staffed (Supported Housing).
The service is expected to be provided in at least 8 out of the 11 Probation Service regions in England - listed below:
- North East
- North West
- Yorkshire and the Humber
- West Midlands
- East Midlands
- South West
- South Central
- East of England
- London
- Kent, Surrey and Sussex
- Greater Manchester
The Authority expects to refer, as a maximum, 350 people at any one time within the service.
The cohort will include individuals subject to Multi Agency Public Protection Arrangements (MAPPA) Level 2 and Level 3 management, including those convicted of offences such as arson and sex offences.
Individuals referred to the service may present with a wide range of complex needs/risk levels, vulnerabilities and health conditions including autism spectrum conditions, dementia, hearing impairment, visual impairment, learning disability, mental ill health, personality disorder, physical disability, and poor physical health.
Referrals into the service will be made by Probation Practitioners and subject to capacity and suitability assessments, the provider will be expected to accept referrals where an appropriate placement is available.  
There is no maximum duration for an individual’s eligibility for the service. Where living independently is part of the individual’s sentence plan, the supplier will assist the individual to support that transition through appropriate accommodation, rehabilitation and support interventions. The Supplier does not claim VAT as part of their payment for the performance of this contract.

title: All Age Carers Hub
description:
Cheshire East Council is recommissioning its support offer for carers across the borough. The service will support adult age carers who provide unpaid care and support to family members, friends and neighbours living within Cheshire East.
The Council is currently reviewing its future operating model for supporting unpaid carers and the role of commissioned provision within the wider carers support system. This review has involved extensive engagement and co-production with carers, Adult Social Care, health services, voluntary and community sector organisations, and other key stakeholders. The final scope of the procurement, including the respective roles of commissioned provision, Council-delivered functions and partnership arrangements, will be confirmed following market engagement and completion of the service design process.
Under the Care Act 2014, the Local Authority has a statutory responsibility to identify, assess need and support carers. The Council recognises the vital contribution unpaid carers make to sustaining families, communities, health services and social care and is committed to ensuring carers are recognised, valued and supported as equal partners in care.
The recommissioned service will move beyond a traditional advice and support model, delivering a strengths-based, preventative and outcomes-focused approach that enables carers to maintain their health, wellbeing, independence and quality of life. The service will play a key role in identifying carers, promoting wellbeing and reducing the risk of deterioration in carer wellbeing, reducing loneliness and social isolation, and ensuring carers can access the right support at the right time.
The commissioned service will act as a strategic partner within the wider health and care system, working collaboratively with social care, health partners, voluntary and community sector organisations and people with lived experience to improve outcomes for carers and the people they support. The service will be expected to champion co-production, ensuring carers' voices continue to influence service design, delivery and continuous improvement.
The contract is expected to include:
•	Provision of clear, consistent, accessible and tailored information, advice and guidance. 
•	Proactive and preventative support that is responsive to differing levels of need, including evening and weekend provision. 
•	Early identification, outreach and engagement with carers.
•	Wellbeing, resilience and preventative interventions, including training, skills development and support to access local community-based provision.
•	Interventions that enable carers to maintain interests, relationships and opportunities beyond their caring role. 
•	Training opportunities to upskill carers
•	Borough-wide opportunities for peer support, mutual aid and community connection, delivered through a range of accessible channels. 
•	Digital and innovative approaches to engaging and supporting carers.
•	Co-production activity and mechanisms that enable carers to shape and influence local service design and delivery.  
•	Developing a strong partnership across VCSE, social care and health services.
•	Targeted support for carers experiencing inequalities or additional barriers to accessing support.
The contract is anticipated to commence in July 2027 and is expected to run for an initial period of five years, with options to extend

description:
The Local Government Association (LGA) is the national membership body for local authorities. It works on behalf of member councils to support, promote, and improve local government. The LGA delivers a programme of children’s services leadership support to councils and corporate and political leaders. This programme is supported through grant funding from the Department for Education (DfE), with a focus on:
• Building leadership capacity and capability within local authorities, equipping corporate and political leaders with the skills, confidence and knowledge to lead SEND improvement and deliver SEND reforms.
• Strengthening leadership readiness for SEND reform, including improving strategic oversight, system leadership and the effective use of learning and best practice.

The contract period will begin soon as possible following award of contracts and will cover delivery of work in the period up to 31 March 2027.
Price Payable: The daily rate is £700 excluding VAT. Reasonable travel and accommodation expenses will also be paid on the production of valid receipts and invoices in accordance with LGA policies. Up to 60 days will be allocated for each of the Health Engagement Advisors up to the completion date of 31 March 2027. This represents a maximum contract value per role of £42,000 (exclusive of VAT).
The successful associates will work as part of a national SEND improvement programme, partnering with councils, Integrated Care Boards (ICBs), NHS England and other stakeholders to strengthen SEND services and readiness for reform. title: Supply & Maintenance of Platelet Agitator and Incubator equipment
description:
Background 
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is responsible for collecting, processing, testing and supplying blood components to hospitals across England. As part of this role, NHSBT operates a network of blood centres, manufacturing facilities and hospitals services departments that require the safe and compliant storage of platelet components.
Platelets must be stored under controlled conditions and maintained under continuous agitation to ensure product quality, safety and compliance with applicable regulatory and quality requirements (JPAC/BSQR). NHSBT currently utilises Helmer platelet agitators and incubators across its sites to support these activities. Helmer models in operation include: PC4200, PC1200, PC900, PC2200 
NHSBT is undertaking a Preliminary Market Engagement exercise to gain a better understanding of the current market, available technologies, product developments and service models relating to platelet agitators and incubators. The information gathered will help inform the development of the technical specification, procurement strategy and future requirements.
Requirements
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is seeking to engage with the market in advance of a potential future procurement for the supply, installation and maintenance of platelet agitator and incubator equipment used for the storage of platelet components within NHSBT facilities.
The engagement process seeks to better understand the following (but is not limited to):
• Current products and technologies available within the market.
• Equipment platelet storage capacity
• Configuration options (connectivity to environmental monitoring systems).
• Regulatory compliance
• Validation support.
• Maintenance and servicing arrangements.
• Sustainability and energy efficiency considerations
• Supply chain resilience and lead times.
NHSBT anticipates that the future requirement may include a range of platelet storage solutions across multiple locations and operational settings. These include:
• Large floor-standing platelet incubator and agitator systems.
• Smaller benchtop platelet agitators and incubators.
• Solutions capable of accommodating both agitating and non-agitating platelet storage within the same unit or integrated system.
NHSBT requires platelet storage solutions capable of maintaining platelet components in accordance with applicable regulatory and quality requirements, including controlled storage at 20°C to 24°C and continuous agitation where required.
NHSBT is seeking feedback from suppliers regarding the availability of such solutions, associated configurations, capacity ranges and any alternative approaches that may offer operational, technical or commercial benefits.
Proposed Lot Structure
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is considering a procurement comprising three separate lots. The final lot structure and scope will be informed by the outcome of this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise.
Lot 1: Supply and Maintenance of Platelet Incubators and Agitators
This lot will include the supply, installation, commissioning, validation support, maintenance and repair of:
• Large floor-standing platelet incubator and agitator systems.
• Smaller benchtop platelet agitators and incubators.
• Associated accessories, spare parts and consumables where applicable.
• User training and technical support services.
Lot 2: Supply and Maintenance of Dual-Function Platelet Storage Solutions
NHSBT are considering a separate lot for this requirement due to limited understanding of the availability of this technology in the market. This lot will include the supply, installation, commissioning, validation support, maintenance and repair of solutions capable of accommodating both agitating and non-agitating platelet storage within the same unit or integrated system.
NHSBT is interested in understanding the range of solutions available within the market, including capacity options, operational benefits, monitoring capabilities and maintenance requirements.
Lot 3: Maintenance of Existing Platelet Incubators and Agitators
This lot will include maintenance and support services for around 170 platelet incubators and agitators currently operated by NHSBT, including:
• Preventative maintenance
• Calibration to two points as a minimum
• Equipment servicing and inspection.
• Breakdown and emergency repair services.
• Supply of replacement parts.
• Technical support

title: SWAST-5143-F Clinical Training Manikins and Simulation Equipment Maintenance
description:
Background
South Western Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust is undertaking preliminary market engagement to identify suppliers capable of providing preventative maintenance, servicing, repair, refurbishment, spare parts support and lifecycle management services for its portfolio of clinical training manikins and simulation equipment located across the South West.
The Trust is seeking information from suitably experienced organisations to better understand market capability, service models and indicative pricing structures in advance of any future procurement exercise.
This notice does not constitute a call for competition and no contract will be awarded as a result of this market engagement exercise.
Scope of Requirement
The Trust currently operates a significant estate of clinical training manikins and simulation equipment, primarily manufactured by Laerdal Medical and Limbs & Things.
The approximate equipment portfolio includes:
Equipment Type- Approximate Quantity
Resusci Anne QCPR / Little Anne QCPR - 44
Resusci Junior QCPR / Little Junior QCPR - 34
Resusci Baby QCPR - 40
Airway Management Trainer - 25
Multi-Venous IV Training Arms - 23
PROMPT Flex Birthing Simulators - 17
Pneumothorax Trainers - 4
The portfolio may increase or decrease during the life of any future contract.
Service Requirements Under Consideration
The Trust is interested in understanding supplier capability to provide:
Preventative maintenance programmes.
Planned servicing.
Inspection and condition assessments.
Repair and refurbishment services.
Replacement components and consumables.
Collection and return logistics.
Mobile engineer/site visit support.
Technical diagnostics and fault finding.
Annual service reporting.
Asset condition reporting.
Lifecycle planning and replacement recommendations.
Support for future purchases and newly acquired equipment.
Integration with asset management systems where available.
Calibration, testing and certification services (where applicable).
Equipment Locations
Equipment is currently distributed across multiple education and training locations including:
Gloucestershire
Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG)
Bath, Swindon and Wiltshire (BSW)
Somerset
Devon
Dorset
Cornwall
Suppliers should indicate whether support can be delivered across all locations.
Information Requested
Interested suppliers are invited to provide information in a single PDF regarding:
Organisation Details
Company name.
Relevant experience.
Service coverage areas.

title: RFQ - Investigating the hygrothermal and dynamic thermal properties of English traditional solid wall construction for resilience in a changing climate  - literature review and gap analysis (UID 332)
description:
This project forms part of Historic England’s Technical Guidance Review, which has the overarching aim to ensure our guidance is up to date, reflective of current understanding and best practice for historic building climate change mitigation and adaptation. To this end, Historic England has identified that robust, evidence-based solutions for climate change mitigation in English buildings of traditional construction are needed that demonstrably balance savings in energy and carbon (operational and embodied) across heating and cooling seasons, whilst supporting the climate resilience of fabric and their occupants through the anticipated changes to our climate.
As a first step, a literature review and gap analysis is required to determine the current level of understanding of the topic and help steer the development of further research. It will focus on the following research questions: 
1.	How do the hygrothermal and dynamic thermal properties of English traditional solid wall construction affect whole-building overheating risk and passive cooling performance, and how are these affected by insulation retrofit and future climate scenarios? 
2.	How do these wall-related effects interact with other whole-building factors, including orientation, solar gain, ventilation, occupancy/use, moisture condition, heating/cooling patterns and other mitigation and adaptation measures?
The findings will be presented as an article for publication in a peer-reviewed journal (journal to be agreed) and for publication in Historic England’s Research Report Series format. They will be disseminated through Historic England’s Technical Tuesday webinar series.

title: Young People’s Supported and Semi-Independent Accommodation and Support Services
description:
The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham has a statutory duty to ensure that there is sufficient, good quality and safe provision for the young people in its care in accordance with Section 22G of the Children Act 1989. The Council is advertising to seek tenders from suitably experienced and qualified organisations to join our new open framework of providers for the provision of Young People’s Supported and Semi-Independent Accommodation and Support Services, for our looked-after young people aged 16 and older (up to a maximum age of 25).  
The aim of the Open Framework is to establish a range of placement provisions that best meet the individual needs of our looked-after young people, acknowledging that these needs are often ongoing. The Open Framework will be composed of four (4) lots and will seek providers as follows:    
Providers of supported accommodation for those aged 16-17 years, under the new supported accommodation regulations (OFSTED), that do not provide semi-independent accommodation;    
Providers of semi-independent accommodation for those over 18 who have not, or cannot, move into independent accommodation, that do not provide supported accommodation;   
Providers of both supported accommodation and semi-independent accommodation types in order to ensure consistency and continuity of care and relationships for a Young Person; and    
Providers of both supported accommodation (OFSTED regulations) and semi-independent accommodation types in order to ensure consistency and continuity of care and relationships for Young People that are parents.    
The new framework is expected to run for a period of eight (8) years commencing on Monday 20th April 2026. Entry on to the framework will be based on providers meeting the necessary quality standards. Contracts will be awarded based on the individual needs of our young people. This will be an Open Framework, as defined under the new Procurement Act 2023, which provides for the award of successive frameworks on substantially the same terms at regular periods.  
The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Commissioning team is planning on reopening the Framework within two years of the original day of award and then in two-yearly cycles, up to the eighth year of the original day of award, in line with the new regulations.  
To achieve our vision, we will need to work with contractors who can demonstrate specific experience for this specialist area of work. Organisations who wish to express an interest must:  
Have within the Organisation (or anyone within the proposed staffing), at least two years’ experience in providing support to vulnerable children and young people accommodated by children’s social care 
Be registered with Ofsted to deliver under: The Supported Accommodation (England) Regulations 2023 (the Regulations) and Quality Standards, if they are planning to deliver supported accommodation for those aged 16-17 years 
Employ staff (keyworkers) who have a minimum of a QCF/NVQ Level 3 in Health and Social Care (Children & Young People) or equivalent 
Employ a Contract Manager/Manager (who will supervise all keyworkers) with a minimum QCF/NVQ Level 4 in Health and Social Care or equivalent  
The Framework Contracts will have no minimum value, nor will any commitment to expenditure by the Council be stipulated within the contract itself. Expenditure will only be incurred when placements are made. The estimated value of the eight-year framework will be approximately £50 million based on the Council’s current spend; however, the Council has no obligation to spend through the framework.

title: Impact of HPV self-testing- insights & good practice in FGM, sexual abuse&trauma
description:
With the planned roll-out of HPV self-testing, we may see improvements in uptake rates, however there will still be a need for cervical screening for those where self-testing indicates high risk HPV, meaning that there will be an ongoing need to provide culturally competent and trauma informed interventions in cervical screening services.
Previous insights suggest that although there are a small number of specialist services concentrated in major cities in England which provide a range of women’s health services for women who have experienced FGM, including cervical screening, many women are unaware of these or are unable to access them.
This project aims to ensure that there is sufficient access to culturally sensitive trauma informed staff able to respond to this need. This will support the objectives of the NHS England » Cervical cancer elimination by 2040 – plan for England.
The project will consist of 5 phases:
1. Explore accessibility to HPV self-testing and cervical screening for victims of sexual abuse/trauma/FGM (working with stakeholders).
2. Scope interventions deployed in other countries to ensure self-testing and screening is accessible for these groups.
Comprehensive review of published material detailing effective pathways into and subsequent to HPV self-testing, including how those with positive high risk HPV tests are supported in cervical screening.
3. Scope existing educational and informational resources and training in England for healthcare practitioners.
Scope what existing educational and informational resources and training has been developed/evaluated to equip healthcare practitioners in supporting women and people with a cervix who have experienced FGM and other types of trauma to engage in HPV self-testing and cervical screening
4. Engage with practitioners to assess current competence and confidence.
Engage with practitioners including CS sample takers to assess extent to which they are trained in TIC and how confident they are in their skills and competence in providing TIC, including those in GP and specialist settings. Identify knowledge and training gaps and co-produce any assets required to address identified gaps, e.g. development of content/e-learning /video to include in the NHS Cervical Screening Sample Taker Update Training - (working with relevant sexual abuse/trauma charities).
5. Trial assets and training and evaluate impact with a small group of practitioners
Trial a selected set of assets and training with a small group of practitioners supported by training and evaluate the impact on their reported competence and confidence.

The Successful Tenderer will have the capability to effectively deliver on a diverse range of multi-disciplinary analysis requirements across both the UK and Ireland as part of a single, cross-nation, multi-jurisdictional evaluation of the benefits and impacts of the tournament. title: WP4051 ICS Pathway 1 Services and a Community Reablement Service
description:
"Reablement is a strengths-based, person-centred approach that promotes and maximises independence and wellbeing. It aims to ensure positive change using user-defined goals and is designed to enable people to gain, or regain, their confidence, ability, and necessary skills to live as independently as possible, especially after an illness, deterioration in health or injury. Reablement focuses on enabling people to do things for themselves rather than having things done for them.
Reablement will be achieved by working in partnership with individuals to support them to undertake tasks themselves, promoting choice, control, and functional ability rather than providing task-based care.
Reablement in the Borough will be aided by technology to deliver positive outcomes for each Service User, ensuring their support is effective, innovative, and tailored to their individual needs.
There are two types of Reablement Pathways.
1) ICS Pathway 1 Services
All Referrals to Pathway 1 Reablement service will be made by appropriate ICS staff. Individuals may be residing in acute hospitals, both inside and outside the borough, or in their own homes. (but only for the purposes of permitting the Referral of Adults who are ordinarily resident in the Borough).
Pathway 1 Reablement provides short-term, intensive, therapy-led support following hospital discharge or admission avoidance. Delivered through an integrated multidisciplinary approach, it focuses on helping people regain skills, achieve personal goals, and undertake daily activities independently wherever possible.
Pathway 1 Social provides short-term interim support for individuals who do not require Reablement, have reached their Reablement potential, or are awaiting longer-term care arrangements or other appropriate services. It ensures continuity of care while longer-term solutions are put in place, and service users may move between the Reablement and Social pathways as their needs change.
2) Community Reablement Pathway
Referrals into the Community Reablement Service will be made via the Council's customer experience centre/operational teams in Adult Social Care.
Community Reablement provides preventative, short-term support for people living in the community who are experiencing a decline in their functional ability. Delivered through a partnership between the Council's therapy team and the Provider, it aims to restore independence, improve wellbeing, and reduce the need for ongoing care and support.
This is a cost and volume contract therefore the value of the total contract value may change, dependant on client need. "

description:
This tender is being published by BlueLight Commercial on behalf of the National Police Air Service (NPAS) who are seeking to award contracts for 'the Provision of a Design, De-modification and Installation Service for Communication Equipment in Police Rotary and Fixed Wing Aircraft.' 
Scope:
The Authority requires a UK Part 21 approved modification that provisions the installation of Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) namely a new Aircraft Communication System (ACS) as part of the Emergency Services Mobile Communication Programme (ESMCP). Thereafter, the Authority requires the execution of an approved installation and associated testing of the ACS along with a Certificate of Release to Service (CRS).
For the Authority to successfully transition onto the new Emergency Services Network (ESN), the Authority requires the de-modification (removal) of existing TETRA radio equipment and the installation of compatible replacement new hardware that initially supports a new TETRA solution and pre-positions for the future ESN LTE capability via dual wiring looms and antennae. This will provide the Initial Operating Capability (IOC) to ensure continued operational capability during the ESMCP transitional period and compliance with the future ESN requirements.
The scope includes the removal of the existing TETRA, and where applicable, marine band VHF radio suite, the design for the installation of the replacement solution; and the subsequent installation of IOC and marine band VHF hardware across the Authority’s aircraft fleet. 
Total aircraft to be modified:
Rotary Wing =11
Fixed Wing = 4
This contract is being tendered on behalf of the West Yorkshire Combined Authority (WYCA) who are the contracting authority for NPAS. NPAS is not a separate, incorporated entity and therefore WYCA currently enters into contractual arrangements on behalf of NPAS.
The Chief Constable of West Yorkshire is responsible for the operational delivery of NPAS. BlueLight Commercial provides commercial support services to police forces and blue light organisations across England and Wales and has been appointed by WYCA to administer the Procurement.
The requirement will be tendered as two separate lots as follows;
• Lot 1: Rotary Wing  
• Lot 2: Fixed Wing
Bidders may bid for either one or both lots.
BlueLight Commercial reserves the right to refine the award criteria at Stage 3 of this procurement process, in accordance with Section 24 of the Procurement Act 2023. The final award criteria and associated weightings will be published prior to the invitation of final tenders at Stage 3 of the procurement. Refinements to the award criteria may include, but are not limited to:
a. adding sub-criteria to those set out in the tender notice/associated tender documents;
b. adding more detail to existing main criteria set out in tender notice/associated tender documents;
c. adding more detail to existing sub-criteria set out in the tender notice/associated tender documents;
d. changing weightings within the pre-existing range as indicated in the table above.
The potential range of the Award Criteria weightings are detailed as follows:
Price: 40% - 50%
Quality: 40% - 50%

title: BF1085 Fuel Monitoring System
description:
Bedfordshire Fire and Rescue Authority is inviting suitable qualified organisations to bid for a modern, fit for purpose self-managed cloud-based Fuel Monitoring System. 
Bedfordshire Fire and Rescue Authority operate six (6) sites with bunkered diesel vehicle fuel stations, three of which contain dual tanks. The sites are located within the county of Bedfordshire: Fire Headquarters Kempston (2 tanks / 1 dispenser), Bedford Fire Station (2 tanks / 2 dispensers), Stopsley Fire Station (1 tank / 1 dispenser), Luton Fire Station (2 tanks / 2 dispensers), Leighton Buzzard Fire Station (1 tank / 1 dispenser) and Dunstable Fire Station (1 tank / 1 dispenser). 
The objectives are to:
•	Provide real-time monitoring of six bunkered fuel site and eight fuel dispensers 
•	Enable full auditability of fuel usage
•	Reduce human error in recording and reporting as a result of manual processes 
•	Provide accessible management information across the organisation
•	Support automated fuel reordering and monitoring
•	Enable all BFRS vehicles to access bunkered fuel with appropriate recording mechanisms 
•	Improve overall fleet fuel management, including non-bunkered fuel users
The high level requirements include but are not limited to:- 
•	Installation of Electronic Fuel Capacity Gauges and an Electronic Fuel Monitoring System at each fuelling station.
•	The information gathered at each fuelling station will be cloud based and be accessed from PCs at BFRA Headquarters Workshops for analysis.
•	The Fuel Monitoring System must provide relevant monitoring information.
•	The Fuel Monitoring should, where technically possible, be compatible with the existing High/Low level alarms.
•	The system must record the mileage of the vehicle as well as the vehicle registration, time of refuelling, and quantity of fuel dispensed into the vehicle.

title: Provision of Asylum Support and Accommodation Services
description:
The Future Asylum Contracts Transformation (FACT), formerly Asylum Support and Accommodation Programme (ASAP), is a long-term transformation programme in the delivery of asylum support and accommodation services. 
The objective is a transformative re-procurement of services to replace the following contracts: 
•	Asylum Accommodation Support Contracts (AASC)
•	Advice Issue Reporting and Eligibility (AIRE)
•	Bridging Accommodation and Travel Services (BATS)
•	Asylum Support Payments (ASP)
The Home Office will be going to market for supplier(s) who can:
1.	Accommodation Provision – Identify, acquire, and maintain a diverse range of safe, suitable, and legally compliant accommodation types within agreed timescales and contracted regions to meet the varied needs of asylum seekers. Ensure accommodation aligns with statutory and regulatory standards, and is approved and allocated in collaboration with Local Authorities to support lawful use, community integration, and minimal impact on local services.
2.	Accommodation Management – Maintain accommodation to defined standards throughout its lifecycle, with robust systems in place for maintenance, temporary housing, and complaint communication and resolution to ensure a safe, suitable, and responsive living environment for asylum seekers.
3.	Transport – Arrange, manage, and deliver a 24/7/365 transportation service that is safe, timely, and responsive to asylum seeker needs in line with Home Office policy, whether independently or as directed by the Home Office. This includes the use of suitable, appropriately equipped, roadworthy vehicles and professional drivers, supported by an appropriate IT booking system, and ensuring the transport of asylum seekers, their dependents, and permitted belongings with appropriate assistance and within agreed timescales.
4.	Sustenance – Ensure that asylum seekers receive appropriate interim support through food vouchers or cash, including issuing food vouchers as a temporary or emergency measure until a Section 4 payment card is provided or replaced, and providing cash where full board accommodation is not available.
5.	Safety and Security – Ensure the safety and security of all staff and asylum seekers by implementing appropriate training, incident management, cross-provider collaboration, and vetting procedures.
6.	Audit & Assurance Services – Monitor provider compliance and performance through a structured assurance framework, combining inspections, desk-based reviews, and data analysis to identify trends, risks, and areas for improvement. The assuror must also produce clear, evidence-based reports to support supplier management and meet the reporting requirements of external assurance bodies.
7.	Service User Assistance – The Provider must ensure that asylum seekers receive clear, accessible, and timely information and support throughout their asylum journey - from initial application and arrival at accommodation to integration into the community. This includes maintaining a reliable single point of contact, delivering oral and written communication in a way asylum seekers can understand, assisting with access to local services, and continuously monitoring and improving the asylum seeker experience through inclusive feedback mechanisms.
8.	Wellbeing and Safeguarding – Establish effective communication channels with relevant partners to ensure timely notification and coordination on safeguarding and wellbeing matters. Where safeguarding concerns are identified, specialist safeguarding staff must be deployed and follow the prescribed action plan.
Proactively prevent and reduce safeguarding incidents, the Provider must offer ongoing support to asylum seekers and ensure that all staff and asylum seekers have access to resources that help them recognise, respond to, and report safeguarding concerns.
Regular welfare checks must be conducted for all asylum seekers.
-------
The Home Office intends to procure a proportion of the services under the Light Touch regime in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. 
For the avoidance of doubt  following the delivery model change in relation to Service User (SU) Assistance and External Assurance.
To clarify, Service User Assistance will be procured via a separate Competitive Flexible Procedure (CFP), supported by its own Market Engagement (ME) activity, and is therefore out of scope of the current procurement.
In addition, External Assurance will be procured via an alternative route and does not form part of this CFP.
Suppliers are requested to continue monitoring the original PMEN for any updates or further clarifications relevant to the current procurement.
**The content of this Notice, including the nature of works and services including start date of contract, may be subject to change.**

title: Hounslow Community Services
description:
This is the core NHS contract for Hounslow Community Services, underpinning the delivery of integrated community-based care across the London Borough of Hounslow. Hounslow Community Services comprise a large-scale integrated community
services model incorporating;
• Adult community health services;
• Children's community health services;
• Multidisciplinary neighbourhood teams;
• Long-term condition and specialist pathways;
• Community nursing and therapy services;
• Musculoskeletal (MSK) services;
• Wheelchair services;
• Diabetes services;
• Urgent community response services;
• Rehabilitation services;
• Care home support services;
• Integration with primary care;
• Integration with local authority services;
• Interfaces with acute and mental health services; and
• Neighbourhood-based models of care.

These services are delivered through multidisciplinary neighbourhood teams and specialist pathways operating across community settings, primary care, schools, care homes and patients' homes.

Collectively, these services support the delivery of neighbourhood health, prevention, early intervention, proactive management of long-term conditions and coordinated multidisciplinary care, enabling residents to receive care closer to home and reducing reliance on hospital-based services.

The contract operates through established clinical pathways, workforce infrastructure, digital systems, governance arrangements and partnerships across the Hounslow health and care system. It is a key enabler of integration across community, primary care, local authority, acute and mental health services, supporting seamless patient pathways, population health
management and the strategic objectives of the Hounslow Borough Based Partnership and the wider Integrated Care System.

The ICB's strategic intentions remain focused on strengthening
neighbourhood-based delivery models, supporting integrated care and continuing the shift of care from hospital settings into community settings. The continuing requirement is therefore not simply for the delivery of individual community services, but for the operation of a fully integrated borough-wide
community services model that brings together multiple service lines, workforce groups, delivery settings and system partners.

title: Kew Wakehurst Controlled Environment Facility
description:
The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew (RBG Kew) is seeking to procure the design, supply and installation of environmental control chambers within a new controlled environment research facility at its Wakehurst site.
The facility will support plant science research through the precise and reproducible control of environmental conditions, including temperature, humidity, lighting and, where required, CO2 concentrations. The requirement is expected to include environmental control chambers capable of supporting a range of plant growth and research activities, including seed regeneration, germination studies, pollination experiments and accelerated breeding programmes.
Prior to commencing the formal procurement process, RBG Kew is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) to refine its emerging requirements, understand market capability and potential delivery approaches, and inform the development of the final specification and procurement strategy.
Interested suppliers are strongly encouraged to participate in the PME exercise and complete the Preliminary Market Engagement questionnaire. Responses will be used solely to inform RBG Kew's approach to the subsequent procurement and will not form part of any future tender evaluation.
Following completion of the PME exercise, RBG Kew anticipates commencing a competitive procurement process. Further information regarding the final scope, procurement procedure and timetable will be published in due course.

title: Architect / Engineers and Cost Consultant Team - Lymington Sea Water Baths
description:
Lymington and Pennington Town Council is seeking to appoint one integrated Architect, Engineering and Cost Consultant Team to deliver Phase 1 of the Lymington Sea Water Baths Restoration Project.
The project is supported by the National Lottery Heritage Fund and will develop the technical, design and cost evidence needed to inform the future restoration and sustainable operation of the Baths.
The Lymington Sea Water Baths are a nationally significant historic coastal leisure facility. The site is affected by substantial structural deterioration, marine saltwater exposure, historic settlement, potentially unstable tidal deposits, ageing infrastructure, accessibility limitations and outdated facilities.
The appointed team will be responsible for delivering and coordinating the architectural, structural engineering, geotechnical engineering, mechanical and electrical engineering, marine and environmental consultancy, quantity surveying and technical survey services required to complete the Phase 1 feasibility work and develop coordinated proposals to RIBA Stage 2.
The Council requires a single integrated consultant team with clear lead responsibility for the coordination, management and quality assurance of all design, engineering, survey and cost information produced through the commission.
The Phase 1 services will include:
Mobilisation and project coordination
• Participate in an inception workshop with the Council, Project Manager and other appointed consultants.
• Confirm the design and technical programme, survey schedule, responsibilities, communication arrangements and information requirements.
• Review and refine the scope of services, project risks, site constraints, dependencies and opportunities.
• Coordinate the architectural, engineering, cost and technical survey workstreams.
• Attend project meetings and provide progress information to the Council and Project Manager.
Technical surveys and investigations
The appointed team will lead, commission, manage or directly undertake the technical surveys and investigations required to support RIBA Stage 2.
These are expected to include:
• Structural condition surveys.
• Concrete sampling, testing and condition mapping.
• Structural integrity assessment.
• Geotechnical investigations, including boreholes, trial pits or other appropriate investigations.
• Assessment of settlement, groundwater and hydrogeological conditions.
• Review of existing pumping, circulation and water-management systems.
• Mechanical and electrical services assessment.
• Drainage, outfall and marine water-management assessment.
• Electrical infrastructure and lighting assessment.
• Environmental, climate resilience and sustainability assessments.
• Assessment of opportunities for low-energy systems and sustainable materials.
The team will be responsible for determining the precise investigations required, coordinating access and sequencing, managing survey information and ensuring that the results are incorporated into the design proposals.
The required outputs will include technical survey reports, drawings, testing results, data summaries, risk information and recommendations informing the RIBA Stage 0 to 2 process.
RIBA Stage 0 and Stage 1
The appointed team will undertake the appraisal, briefing and initial design work required to establish a clear and deliverable basis for the project.
This will include:
• Site appraisal and constraints mapping.
• Review of existing infrastructure, buildings, structures, heritage features and the marine setting.
• Identification of technical, operational, access, environmental and conservation constraints.
• Development of the project brief in collaboration with the Council and other consultants.
• Initial accessibility and inclusion strategy.
• Sustainability and climate resilience principles.
• Feasibility layouts and concept proposals.
• Integration of relevant findings from heritage research, business analysis and community engagement.
RIBA Stage 2 design development
The team will prepare coordinated RIBA Stage 2 proposals for the full Baths site.
The work will include:
• Developed architectural layouts.
• General arrangement drawings, sections and elevations.
• Structural design strategy.
• Geotechnical design advice.
• Mechanical and electrical outline strategies.
• Pumping, circulation, drainage and water-management proposals.
• Accessibility and inclusive design proposals.
• Landscape and public realm strategy.
• Conservation-led proposals informed by the Heritage Consultant's work.
• Visualisations and illustrative materials.
• Sustainability and climate resilience proposals.
• Programme and construction phasing strategy.
• Recommendations for materials suitable for a marine and heritage environment.
The design must respond to the site's heritage significance, ground conditions, structural deterioration, marine exposure, operational requirements, accessibility objectives and long-term maintenance needs.
Cost consultancy
The Quantity Surveyor will prepare and maintain cost information throughout the Phase 1 design process.
The services will include:
• Preparation of the RIBA Stage 2 cost plan.
• Advice on affordability and value for money.
• Construction phasing cost analysis.
• Design risk and cost risk assessment.
• Preparation and maintenance of a cost risk register.
• Lifecycle and maintenance cost projections.
• Cost advice to support the Business Options Appraisal.
• Identification of assumptions, exclusions, inflation allowances and contingencies.
The Quantity Surveyor will work closely with the design team, Project Manager and business planning specialists to ensure that capital and lifecycle costs are properly reflected in the wider feasibility evidence.
Consultation and engagement support
The team will support the appointed Consultation and Engagement Consultant by:
• Preparing accessible drawings, visualisations and explanatory materials.
• Attending relevant public exhibitions, workshops or design feedback sessions.
• Explaining the technical and design proposals to non-specialist audiences.
• Reviewing and responding to consultation findings.
• Demonstrating how relevant engagement feedback has informed the final RIBA Stage 2 proposals.
Collaboration with the wider consultant team
The appointed team will be expected to collaborate with the Council, Project Manager, Heritage Consultant, Consultation and Engagement Consultant, business planning specialists and other project advisers.
The team must ensure that design decisions are informed by:
• Heritage significance and conservation principles.
• Technical survey findings.
• Community and stakeholder engagement.
• Operational and business planning requirements.
• Capital and lifecycle costs.
• Accessibility and inclusion.
• Climate resilience and environmental sustainability.
Final Phase 1 outputs
The required final outputs will include:
Coordinated RIBA Stage 2 Design Report.
General arrangement drawings, sections and elevations.
Architectural, structural, geotechnical, mechanical and electrical design narratives.
Full technical survey and investigation reports.
Developed accessibility and inclusive design narrative.
Sustainability and climate resilience statement.
Landscape and public realm proposals.
RIBA Stage 2 cost plan.
Capital cost, lifecycle cost and construction phasing information.
Design, technical and cost risk registers.
Visualisations and materials for consultation and funding purposes.
Programme and recommendations for subsequent project stages.
Contributions required for National Lottery Heritage Fund reporting, evaluation and future funding evidence.
All documents must be coordinated, clearly presented, accessible and suitable for use by the Council, the National Lottery Heritage Fund and other project stakeholders.
The Phase 1 contract value is up to £120,000 excluding VAT. The fee must include the professional services of the architect, structural engineer, geotechnical engineer, mechanical and electrical engineer, marine or environmental specialists, Quantity Surveyor, all required technical surveys and testing, and preparation of the required drawings, reports and RIBA Stage 2 deliverables.

title: Consultation and Engagement Consultant - Lymington Sea Water Baths
description:
Lymington and Pennington Town Council is seeking to appoint one suitably experienced Consultation and Engagement Consultant to design, manage and deliver an inclusive public and stakeholder engagement programme for Phase 1 of the Lymington Sea Water Baths Restoration Project.
The project is supported by the National Lottery Heritage Fund and will develop the technical, heritage, community, business and operational evidence required to inform the future restoration and sustainable use of the Baths.
The Lymington Sea Water Baths were established in 1833 and are one of the earliest surviving open-air seawater bathing facilities in the United Kingdom. The site is an important heritage and community asset with strong connections to local identity, leisure, health and wellbeing. The Phase 1 engagement programme must ensure that community values, needs, aspirations and barriers to participation inform the development of the project and the RIBA Stage 0 to 2 design proposals.
The appointed consultant will be responsible for providing accessible opportunities for residents, users, community organisations and other stakeholders to participate in the project. The programme must seek broad and representative participation and actively engage people and groups who may otherwise be underrepresented.
The services required will include:
Engagement strategy and delivery planning
The consultant will prepare a comprehensive Engagement Strategy and Delivery Plan setting out:
• The purpose and objectives of the engagement programme.
• The proposed engagement methods and timetable.
• Target audiences and stakeholder groups.
• Arrangements for reaching underrepresented communities.
• Accessibility and inclusion measures.
• Communications and public-facing messaging.
• Data protection, consent and ethical arrangements.
• Risks, dependencies and mitigation measures.
• Methods for recording, analysing and reporting feedback.
Priority audiences are expected to include young people, older residents, disabled people and accessibility groups, lower-income households, leisure and sports users, local residents, community organisations, heritage stakeholders and environmental groups.
Engagement Round 1
The consultant will design and deliver an initial round of engagement focused on community values, needs, aspirations and priorities for the future of the Baths.
This is expected to include:
• An online public survey, with a target of at least 300 responses.
• One or two public drop-in engagement sessions.
• Three facilitated stakeholder workshops.
• Accessible materials explaining the project, its purpose and the matters on which feedback is being sought.
The engagement will explore matters including:
• Community aspirations for the Baths.
• Current and potential future uses.
• Barriers to access and participation.
• The heritage and cultural value of the site.
• Priorities for accessibility and inclusion.
• Desired improvements, facilities and activities.
• Concerns, opportunities and community expectations.
The required outputs will include survey materials, workshop plans, facilitation, analysis of responses and a summary findings report for the Council and Design Team.
Targeted engagement
The consultant will undertake focused outreach with groups and individuals who may not participate through general public consultation.
The targeted programme is expected to engage approximately 40 to 60 participants and may include small group sessions, facilitated discussions, interviews, outreach activities or other suitable methods.
The consultant must identify barriers to participation, adapt engagement methods where necessary and ensure that the findings are incorporated into the wider project evidence base and the development of the RIBA Stage 1 and Stage 2 proposals.
The required outputs will include a Targeted Outreach Plan and a report summarising participation, findings and recommendations.
Engagement Round 2
The consultant will deliver a second round of engagement to gather feedback on the emerging RIBA Stage 2 design proposals.
The consultant will work with the appointed Architect, Engineering and Cost Consultant Team to ensure that drawings, visualisations and technical information are presented in a clear and accessible format.
The second round is expected to include:
• One in-person public exhibition or consultation event.
• An online presentation of the emerging proposals.
• Digital and in-person feedback opportunities.
• Structured collection and analysis of responses, with a target of at least 100 participants or responses.
The consultant will facilitate the engagement, analyse feedback and identify matters requiring consideration by the Council and Design Team.
Analysis and reporting
The consultant will maintain appropriate records of participation throughout the commission and provide qualitative and quantitative analysis of the engagement findings.
The final Engagement Report must include:
• A summary of the methodology used.
• Details of engagement activities undertaken.
• Participation and demographic information.
• Evidence of the groups and communities reached.
• Key themes, concerns, aspirations and priorities.
• Identified barriers to access and participation.
• Accessibility and inclusion findings.
• An explanation of how feedback informed or influenced the project and design proposals.
• Matters that could not be incorporated and, where appropriate, the reasons.
• Recommendations for future engagement and community participation.
The consultant must also prepare a concise National Lottery Heritage Fund formatted summary suitable for inclusion in project reporting, evaluation and future funding submissions.
Collaboration and project coordination
The appointed consultant will be expected to work collaboratively with:
• The Council's client team.
• The appointed Project Manager / Project Coordinator.
• The Architect, Engineering and Cost Consultant Team.
• The Heritage Consultant.
• Business planning and market research specialists.
• Relevant museums, community organisations and project partners.
The consultant will attend project meetings and coordination sessions as reasonably required and provide timely findings to ensure that engagement evidence can influence the project while proposals are still being developed.
The consultant must manage expectations through clear communication about the scope of the Phase 1 project, the matters that remain subject to further funding and approval, and how consultation feedback will be considered.
Required Phase 1 outputs
The required outputs will include:
Engagement Strategy and Delivery Plan.
Inclusive engagement methodology.
Engagement Round 1 survey, workshop and public engagement materials.
Facilitation and reporting for Engagement Round 1.
Targeted Outreach Plan and findings report.
Accessible materials for Engagement Round 2.
Facilitation and reporting for Engagement Round 2.
Participation and demographic analysis.
Final Engagement Report.
National Lottery Heritage Fund summary and contribution to the Phase 1 evaluation evidence.
All engagement materials and reports must be written in clear, accessible language and be suitable for use by the public, the Council, the wider consultant team and the National Lottery Heritage Fund.
The contract value is up to £23,500 excluding VAT. The fee must include all consultant time, project management, meetings, travel, engagement materials, digital tools and licences, venue hire where required, analysis, reporting and delivery of the required outputs.
Appointment and mobilisation are expected in late September 2026. The consultant must coordinate the engagement programme with the wider Phase 1 project timetable. All engagement activities, reports and final contributions to the Phase 1 evaluation must be completed no later than 31 August 2027. The original brief establishes the requirement for two engagement rounds, targeted outreach, inclusive participation and a comprehensive final Engagement Report.

title: Heritage Consultant - Lymington Sea Water Baths
description:
Lymington and Pennington Town Council is seeking to appoint one suitably experienced Heritage Consultant to undertake a comprehensive heritage review of the Lymington Sea Water Baths as part of a National Lottery Heritage Fund supported feasibility and development project.
The Lymington Sea Water Baths were established in 1833 and are among the earliest surviving open-air seawater bathing facilities in the United Kingdom. The site has significant architectural, cultural and social heritage value, but is at risk because of structural deterioration, historic alterations and continued exposure to the marine environment.
The consultant will provide an authoritative assessment of the historical development, architectural features, surviving fabric, cultural value and heritage significance of the site. The work will inform architectural and engineering design up to RIBA Stage 2, community engagement, interpretation planning, conservation decision making and the evidence base for future capital funding applications.
The commission will include:
• Reviewing existing reports, historic surveys, photographs, maps, newspapers, trade directories, archives and local records.
• Undertaking archival and documentary research, including engagement with relevant local museums, archives, historians and heritage organisations.
• Establishing a detailed chronology of the development and use of the Baths, including their earlier origins, subsequent alterations and changing role within the community.
• Assessing the heritage significance of the pool layout, historic engineering, aeration fountains, concrete structures, buildings, setting, views and surviving architectural features.
• Assessing the social and cultural history of the Baths, including their contribution to leisure, health, wellbeing, tourism and local identity.
• Identifying heritage sensitivities, constraints, risks and opportunities that should inform the design process.
• Advising the appointed architectural and engineering team during the development of proposals up to RIBA Stage 2.
• Preparing conservation principles and heritage guidance to support future decisions concerning repair, alteration, restoration and development.
• Working collaboratively with the Council, Project Manager, Design Team, Quantity Surveyor, Consultation and Engagement Consultant and other appointed specialists.
• Providing accessible heritage stories, themes and supporting content for public consultation, exhibitions and future interpretation.
• Supporting the integration of heritage considerations into community engagement and design development.

Procurement description
Lymington and Pennington Town Council is seeking to appoint one suitably experienced Project Manager / Project Coordinator to manage, coordinate and quality assure Phase 1 of the Lymington Sea Water Baths Restoration Project.
The project is supported by the National Lottery Heritage Fund and will develop the technical, heritage, community, market and business evidence required to inform the future restoration and sustainable operation of the Baths.
The appointed consultant will provide a single point of coordination for the Phase 1 project and will be responsible for bringing together the work of the Council, Design Team, Quantity Surveyor, Heritage Consultant, Consultation and Engagement Consultant and any specialist subconsultants appointed through this commission.
The consultant will not replace the Council's client role and will not have authority to commit Council expenditure without written approval.
The services required are:
• Preparation and maintenance of an integrated Phase 1 project programme.
• Coordination of all Phase 1 workstreams, dependencies, deadlines and required approvals.
• Management of project meetings, agendas, notes, action logs and decision records.
• Preparation and maintenance of project risk and issue registers.
• Monthly progress reporting to the Council.
• Support with National Lottery Heritage Fund reporting, monitoring, evidence collation and the final Phase 1 evaluation submission.
• Coordination of inputs from the architectural and engineering Design Team, Quantity Surveyor, Heritage Consultant and Consultation and Engagement Consultant.
• Review and quality assurance of outputs to ensure that the technical, heritage, engagement, market and business evidence is consistent, practical and suitable for use by the Council and the National Lottery Heritage Fund.
• Advice to the Council on programme sequencing, dependencies, risks, governance and decision-making requirements.
• Management, coordination and quality assurance of any specialist subconsultants delivering elements of this commission.
In addition to project management and coordination, the commission includes responsibility for delivering or managing the following specialist workstreams:
Comparator Study
The consultant will identify and examine between five and seven relevant United Kingdom lidos, seawater pools or comparable heritage leisure assets.
The study will consider matters including:
• Governance and ownership arrangements.
• Operating models.
• Pricing and income generation.
• Programming and activities.
• Audience development.
• Financial and environmental sustainability.
• Relevant successes, risks and lessons.
The required outputs will include a Comparator Study Report, individual case study summaries and recommendations for Lymington.
Market / Regional Profile Review
The consultant will assess the current and potential market for the Lymington Sea Water Baths.
The work will include:
• Analysis of existing and potential audiences.
• Consideration of regional tourism, leisure, health and wellbeing markets.
• Assessment of competitors and complementary local and regional attractions.
• Identification of opportunities to increase participation, visibility and off-season use.
• Consideration of inclusion, accessibility and barriers to participation.
The required outputs will include a Market / Regional Profile Review, audience segmentation and strategic recommendations for the future positioning and promotion of the Baths.
Business Options Appraisal
The consultant will assess the potential future operating and governance arrangements for the Baths.
The appraisal will include:
• Evaluation of Council-led, charitable trust, community interest company, operator-led and hybrid delivery models where relevant.
• Development of 10-year financial projections.
• Identification of potential income streams and pricing strategies.
• Integration of capital and lifecycle cost information supplied by the Quantity Surveyor.
• Assessment of risks, assumptions and sensitivity scenarios.
• Recommendation of a preferred operational and governance model, supported by clear evidence and reasoning.
The required outputs will include a Business Options Appraisal Report, a financial modelling workbook and summary presentation materials for the Council.
The consultant will be expected to work collaboratively with the wider project team and ensure that business and market evidence informs the development of the RIBA Stage 0 to 2 design proposals. Emerging design decisions must be considered in relation to future operation, affordability, management, accessibility and long-term sustainability.
The final Phase 1 outputs will include:
Project initiation note and confirmed delivery programme.
Monthly progress reports.
Meeting records, action logs and risk and issue registers.
Comparator Study.
Market / Regional Profile Review.
Business Options Appraisal and financial modelling workbook.
Executive summary for the National Lottery Heritage Fund feasibility evidence pack.
Presentation of findings to the Council and relevant stakeholders.
Final coordination and handover report setting out recommendations, risks, next steps and future project requirements.
The consultant may deliver the Comparator Study, Market / Regional Profile Review and Business Options Appraisal directly or through suitably qualified subconsultants. Any proposed subconsultants must be identified in the tender submission. The appointed lead consultant will remain responsible for the management, integration and quality assurance of all subcontracted work.
Tenderers must provide a fixed fee for Phase 1, separately identifying the project management and coordination fee, specialist workstream fees, any subcontracted elements, expenses, assumptions and exclusions.
Appointment and mobilisation are expected in late September 2026. Project initiation must take place within one week of appointment. All Phase 1 outputs must be completed, approved where required, and the final evaluation submitted no later than 31 August 2027.
