title: Provision for a Tobacco Track and Trace System
description:
HMRC intend to award a concession contract to a single supplier for the United Kingdom's Tobacco Track and Trace system, in support of the World Health Organization Protocol to Eliminate Illicit Trade in Tobacco Products.
The UK currently has a supplier providing services to enable the continued tracking and tracing of tobacco products manufactured in or imported into the UK. The existing contract is expected to expire at the end of October 27, and HMRC intends to appoint a supplier to deliver the service on a replacement basis.
The purpose of this Notice is to alert interested parties and gain interest.  The intention is to award a concession contract with an anticipated duration of up to five years.
The UK ratified the WHO Protocol to Eliminate Illicit Trade in Tobacco Products in 2018. The Protocol requires parties to implement an effective traceability system for tobacco products manufactured in or imported into their territory, taking account of regional specific requirements and international best practice. The UK system operates as a standalone national system and must also support specific arrangements for Northern Ireland in accordance with the Northern Ireland Protocol.
The provider's main responsibilities are expected to include delivery of an end to end Tobacco Track and Trace service, including: 
- an ID issuer service, to ensure tobacco products manufactured in or imported into the UK are assigned a unique identifier; and
- a data routing and repository service, to securely receive, validate, store and make available traceability data relating to tobacco products, accessible to HMRC and other authorised authorities.
The service is expected to operate at national scale, support high volume transactional data, and meet applicable UK and international legislative requirements. The contract will be awarded under a concession model, with costs recovered from industry users rather than HMRC.
HMRC may refine and further define the detailed requirements during the procurement process, including operational, technical, performance, security, and transition arrangements.

title: Denmark – Repair and maintenance services of building installations – CTS-ydelser til Aalborg Universitet (genudbud)
description: AAU har en samlet CTS-platform, der dækker universitetets tre campusser i Aalborg, Esbjerg og København. Systemet består udelukkende af Schneider Electric EcoStruxure Building Operation (EBO) som hovedstation. CTS-platformen er etableret i AAU’s eget virtuelle servermiljø. Platformen består af i alt ca. 200 automationsservere (AS), 1029 Xenta-centraler og ca. 20 Sigma-centraler, som dækker en samlet bygningsmasse på ca. 235.000 m² fordelt på ca. 63 bygninger. Campus Aalborg og Campus Esbjerg anvender en fælles enterprise-server, mens Campus København har sin egen – men alle hovedstationer kan tilgås på tværs af campusser via ét samlet login og brugeradministration gennem AAU’s Identity Management-system. CTS-anlæggene styrer og overvåger universitetets ventilations-, varme-, køle- og belysningsanlæg, samt brandalarmer, beredskabsfunktioner og øvrige kritiske tekniske systemer. Det omfatter bl.a. forsyninger til datacentre, dyrestalde, forskningsudstyr og installationer med særlige drifts- og sikkerhedskrav. Systemet fungerer samtidig som et centralt værktøj til energiovervågning, fejlforebyggelse og optimering af drift, og understøtter dermed AAU’s målsætning om en bæredygtig, effektiv og standardiseret bygningsdrift på tværs af alle campusser. AAU ønsker med dette udbud at indgå en aftale med en primær og sekundær aktør til udførelse af følgende ydelser: A. CTS-arbejder bestående af service, vedligehold og opdatering af alle AAU’s CTS-installationer af mærket Schneider inkl. både software og hardware. Software opgradering og opdatering skal ske til den til enhver tid nyeste EcoStruxure Building Operation version og min. en gang årligt og er defineret ved den samlede proces fra planlægning, varsling og backup til installation, funkti-onskontrol, kontrol af integrationer og endelig dokumentation. B. CTS-entrepriseopgaver fx i forbindelse med nybyg, ombygning og renoveringsprojekter samt andre tekniske projekter. C. C. Support på AAU’s CTS-platform i form af døgnbemandet teknisk remote support med mulighed for fysisk support ved tilkald (hasteopgaver). Supporten skal dække alle AAU’s lokationer og Schneider Electric CTS-anlæg inkl. både platform, software og hardware. Ydelser i henhold til Aftalen udføres som udgangspunkt ved den primære leverandør, dog kan udførelse af ydelser ved den sekundære leverandør blive relevant i følgende situationer: • Hvis den primære leverandør ikke kan udføre en ydelse som følge af forbigående forhindringer, såsom mandskabsmangel eller andet, kan bestillingen i stedet gå til den sekundære leverandør. • Hvis AAU har fastsat en tidsfrist for færdiggørelse af en konkret opgave, og den primære leverandør ikke kan tilbyde at udføre ydelsen inden den af AAU fastsatte tidsfrist, kan ydelsen i stedet udføres af den sekundære leverandør. • Hvis den primære leverandør væsentligt misligholder Aftalen, kan AAU ophæve Aftalen med denne leverandør, hvorefter den sekundære leverandør bliver den primære leverandør af alle ydelser i henhold til aftalen. De beskrevne situationer dækker over, at AAU ønsker en fast samarbejdspartner i form af en primær leverandør, som ikke blot kan udføre service og vedligehold af CTS-installationer, men også kan anvendes til større opgaver inden for arbejder relateret til CTS-arbejder. AAU ønsker i tillæg til dette at have en fast samarbejdspartner i form af en sekundær leverandør, som kan sikre driften af CTS-installationerne i tilfælde af, at den primære leverandør ikke kan dette – nærmere bestemt i de tilfælde, der er oplistet i aftalens pkt. 3.1.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – [InSuReCS] Intelligent Surfaces for Resilient Communication and Sensing
description: The greatest risk to cyber security on the battlefield is the threat to own wireless radio communication from enemy electronic warfare (EloKa). In addition to ensuring the integrity and security against interception of the transmitted information using modern cryptographic methods and the availability of information links even under jamming measures, the protection of one’s own electromagnetic signature against the enemy’s positioning methods is an often overlooked but operationally critical component of communications security (COMSEC). Particularly in the case of direct communication between two transmitting stations, there is a risk that one’s own transmission will be intercepted and decoded by enemy forces or that one’s own location will be disrupted or localized with the help of EloKa measures. Troop units in the field are currently responding with technical measures (direct sequence spread spectrum/frequency hopping procedures, burst transmissions, radio relay) or tactical measures (short transmission cycles, radio discipline, high mobility), which limits the use of wireless communication and its advantages in operations. On the other hand, the uninterrupted availability of the information flow in the “Military Internet of Things” is playing an increasingly important role on the battlefield, e.g. for the creation of highly precise and continuously updatable situation pictures, and requires the use of tactical data links with high data rates. This requires, for example, new adaptive waveforms in the VHF range and higher, which are currently being developed on the basis of Software Defined Radio (SDR), e.g. as part of the ESSOR project. Flexible modulation methods, integrated encryption and high resilience allow secure radio connections to be realized. At the same time, such waveforms also enable simultaneous communication and reconnaissance (Integrated Communication and Sensing, ISAC) and are therefore particularly interesting for military applications. As part of the InSuReCS research programme, an adaptively controllable transmission and reception technology based on meta-surfaces (e.g. Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS)) is to be developed that enables indirect communication and reconnaissance (active and passive) and thus further minimizes the risk of reconnaissance of one’s own position through a continuously adaptable transmission path. Indirect communication and reconnaissance is to be realized by an intermediate or relay station that is capable of forwarding incoming and highly focused transmissions between source and sink in a targeted manner. The transmission and reception technology to be developed can be used to supplement existing radio technology and expand its capabilities (e.g. with regard to bandwidth, frequency bands used, directional characteristics), but can also focus on future military-relevant radio applications. The aim is to develop a transmission and reception technology that enables mobile field teams to provide highly available, broadband and secure communication and long-range reconnaissance with high directionality. To this end, intelligent meta-interfaces, which are intended for use in the upcoming 6G mobile communications standard, for example, are to be adapted for highly flexible use in conflict and crisis management scenarios. Prioritized requirements such as largely platform-independent usability, good integration into existing and future radio applications and continuous adaptation of the RIS configuration in a highly mobile deployment scenario are key innovation goals of the research program.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF - Evaluation der Potentiale sektorspezifischer Cybersicherheitsprofile
description: Eisenbahnspezifische Cybersicherheitsprofile legen geeignete Anforderungen und Spezifikationen für bestimmte Prozesse oder Komponenten in Bausteinen vergleichbar zum BSI-IT-Grundschutz fest. Es soll bestimmt werden, inwieweit diese das Security-Engineering beschleunigen, sowie den sicheren Betrieb von Systemen im Eisenbahnsektor vereinfachen und verbessern können und für welche Teile des Eisenbahnsektors eine umfassende Erarbeitung solcher Profile lohnenswert wäre. Die Digitalisierung und steigende Bedrohungslage machen Cybersicherheit in der kritischen Infrastruktur Eisenbahn besonders wichtig. Die Systemkomplexität, regulatorische Anforderungen (z. B. NIS2, CRA) und der Bedarf an Spezialwissen wächst. Normen wie ISO/IEC 27000, Common Criteria und IEC 62443 oder noch spezifischer die CLC/TS 50701 geben einen umfassenden Rahmen vor, sind aber umfangreich und lassen viel Spielraum, sodass individuelle Risikobewertungen aufwendig bleiben. Der BSI-IT-Grundschutz zeigt beispielhaft, wie standardisierte Bausteine allgemeine Anforderungen für typische Prozesse/Systeme bündeln können und damit Engineering und Betrieb vereinfachen. Für das System Eisenbahn gibt es aber bisher kein eigenes ähnliches Konzept. Der EU-Rail System-Pillar-Ansatz gibt hingegen möglichst präzise Spezifikationen für ein generisches Systemmodell vor. Eisenbahnspezifische Cybersicherheitsprofile könnten die Vorteile beider Konzepte vereinen.

description: Auftraggeber des Projektes ist die TEN Thüringer Energienetze GmbH & Co. KG. Dieser ist ein regionaler Verteilnetzbetreiber. Die Thüringer Energienetze GmbH & Co. KG plant den Abriss und Neubau des Umspannwerkes in Leinefelde. Es ist geplant, innerhalb von zwei Bauabschnitten zuerst den Ostteil und später den Westteil des Geländes vollständig neu zu strukturieren. Hierbei soll die komplette Freischaltanalage des UW Leinefelde mit dem dazugehörigen Unterbau neu errichtet werden. Das Los "Ingenieurbau" umfasst die Herstellung der Ingenieurbauwerke, Verkehrsanlagen und Freianlagen für das gesamte Umspannwerk. Es sind u.a. folgende Bestandteile des neuen Umspannwerks herzustellen: - Einzelfundament und Schächte (9 Portalfundamente, ca. 150 Kleinfundamente für Gerätetische, ca. 10 Blitzschutzfundamente, Fundamente für Videoüberwachung, 2 Trafofundamente, ca. 15 Kabelziehschächte, 1 E-Spulenfundament) - Werkstraßen, Wege und Flächen (Asphaltflächen, geschotterte Flächen, gepflasterte Flächen) - Freianlagen (zu begrünendes Gelände, Zaunanlage) - verschiedene Kabelleerrohrtrassen, Schutzrohrtrassen sowie Entwässerungsleitungen Dazu gehören in den wichtigsten Punkten zusammengefasst u.a. folgende Leistungen: Erdbauarbeiten - Fertigteilfundamente - Beton- und Stahlbetonarbeiten- Entwässerungskanalarbeiten - Straßenbauarbeiten - Landschaftsbauarbeiten - in geringem Umfang Stahlbauarbeiten Explizit nicht enthalten sind die Primär- und Sekundärarbeiten (Geräteinstallation, Kabelzieh- und Anschlussarbeiten). Das Baufeld besteht aus der Fläche der bestehenden 110-kV-Schaltanlage. Die gesamte Anlage wird im laufenden Betrieb umgebaut, die Bauleistungen und die Primär- sowie Sekundärinstallationen erfolgen dabei sequenziell, sodass die Errichtung der Neuanlage in zwei Bauabschnitten erfolgt. title: Provision of General Medical Services at Tollgate Practice, Colchester
description:
NHS Essex Integrated Care Board (the Authority) is undertaking a competitive procurement process under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 for the award of a General Medical Services (GMS) contract for Tollgate Practice, located in Stanway, Colchester.

The procurement seeks to identify a suitably qualified and experienced provider to deliver safe, effective, sustainable and accessible primary medical services to the registered patient population of Tollgate Practice. The commercial schedule currently assumes an actual patient list of 10,206 and a weighted patient list of approximately 8,832, subject to future list size adjustments in line with national General Medical Services arrangements.

The successful provider will be required to deliver the full range of services associated with a nationally prescribed GMS contract, including management of a registered patient list, provision of core primary medical services, clinical governance, workforce management, patient access requirements and integration with local health and care services.

The procurement is being undertaken following caretaker arrangements that were implemented to maintain continuity of services whilst the practice recovered from historical quality and regulatory concerns.

The contract is intended to secure the long-term provision of stable and resilient primary medical services beyond the caretaker period.

All 9 schools listed above (8 primary and 1 secondary) – are participating in this tender.  Please note this is a growing trust where additional schools may join during the new contract term. Additional schools that join may, at the Trust’s discretion, be added to this contract.
The successful tenderer will be required to provide excellent catering services to the schools. 
The contract term being tendered is for three years, 1st September 2026 – 31st August 2029. There is an option for a further extension period for up to two additional years to 31st August 2031.

Management must be present and engaged, actively building relationships at both school and Trust level and driving the contract forwards at all times. Monthly management information is expected to be timely, accurate and easy to interpret.
The Trust is not obliged to accept the lowest price submitted for this tender, rather each school is keen to secure ‘best value’ from this contract and to deliver ‘best value’ to its students. Innovative and creative ideas as to how the services can be developed and value added, will be welcomed. The Trust seeks a contractor that is keen to work in partnership and who will deliver to its highest abilities, at all times. 
Competitive Flexible Procedure 
This procurement will be run under the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will follow a two stage approach, with stage 1 being the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ). Here a minimum of 5 candidates (or less, in the event less than 5 meet the minimum criteria) and a maximum of 10 candidates, will progress to stage 2. Any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement and a minimum score of 60% must be achieved. 
Selected tenderers will then be invited to stage 2, the Invitation To Tender (ITT). Here, the evaluation of tender response will be set as 40% price and 60% quality.
Value of contract:
The annual value of the current contract is £950,000
Therefore, the value of this contract is £4,750,000 
The contract shall be a guaranteed performance contract with any hospitality requirements billed separately.
The tender process will be run under a two stage Competitive Flexible procedure. 
Additional requirements and information:
•The Trust has a minimum requirement for a contractor’s employers' liability and public liability insurances of £5 million. 
•The minimum annual turnover that your company must have achieved to be considered for this opportunity is £2 million.

•The catering services are currently contracted to Aspens Services and HCL.
•As above, please note this is a growing Trust and any other schools that may join the Trust during the tenure of this new catering contract may, at the Trust’s discretion, be added to this contract.
•Please note that the successful tenderer will be required to pay the RIVA tender fee for this project directly to RIVA, upon their contract award.

title: Quantifying the difference that nature recovery can make to selected risk events in the National Risk Register (informed by the State of Natural Capital Report)
description:
This commission sits within Natural England's Natural Capital and Economics Teams, which work on evidence to ensure that nature, and the multiple benefits it provides, are considered in decision-making.
In 2024, Natural England published a State of Natural Capital Report State of Natural Capital Report (SONC). It brings together the best available evidence on the state of England's natural capital. It aims to wake up policymakers, and other decision-makers, to risks from natural capital loss and convince them to invest in, and protect, nature. 
SONC contains significant quantitative information. However, its output is qualitative. The lack of quantification means that audiences who are unfamiliar with environmental evidence are unable to weigh the importance of our risk ratings against other risk ratings in their own policy area.  This project aims to extend the SONC work into quantification, specifically through reference to 7 risks in the National Risk Register National Risk Register 2025 (NRR).
We are working with the idea that changes in the chronic risks impact on the future likelihood and impact of the event risks in the NRR. Specifically, we are interested in the potential of nature recovery to mitigate expected increases in the likelihood and impacts of a selected group of NRR risks which are nature related.
Project Aims:
This project has two aims. These are:
1) to make the case for nature recovery, through demonstrating the potential for nature recovery to mitigate increases in selected NRR risks.
2) to develop our ability to make quantified connections from SONC to other policy areas to support future work. We are looking for strategic, proportionate and complexity-sensitive quantification, and set out further what we mean by this below.

- Palaeontology "Science Lab" Interactive Zone

The contractor shall design and deliver a 10m x 10m fully immersive "Jurassic Seas" box and environment. This space will utilise high-quality projection, projection mapping and sensor based interactive technology to create a convincing underwater Jurassic marine experience. The environment will depict ichthyosaurs, plesiosaurs, ammonites, marine flora, sediment movement and light dappled water conditions. Content sequences should move between calm exploratory moments and more dramatic encounters, including large-scale ichthyosaur and other marine fossil sequences, to create emotional variation and sustained visitor engagement.

title: DLSITT1105 - New Diamond Website
description:
Located on the Harwell Science & Innovation Campus in Oxfordshire, Diamond Light Source (DLS) is a leading-edge facility for science, engineering and innovation. DLS allows researchers from academia and industry to investigate the structure and behaviour of the world around us at the atomic and molecular level. To continue delivering the world-changing science that Diamond enables, the facility is being upgraded to Diamond-II, a co-ordinated programme of development that combines a major machine upgrade with new instruments and complementary improvements to optics, detectors, sample environment and delivery capabilities, and computing, as well as integrated and correlative methods. 
Our current corporate website, https://www.diamond.ac.uk/, is a critical channel for:
•	Communicating scientific capability and impact and promoting science to broader audiences
•	Supporting user-centric operations, including access to beamlines and facilities
•	Engaging industry partners and collaborators, and generating leads for the Industrial Liaison Office
•	Supporting recruitment into key roles, attracting the best candidates
The site was launched nearly 15 years ago and, whilst the CMS (Magnolia-CMS) has received regular technical upgrades and is up to date with the latest security and functionality features, it has become a sprawling information repository for everything Diamond does. Our vision is to develop a new corporate website from the ground up, with new, more concise and more strategically targeted content. The new website will primarily focus on four strategic communications objectives, as outlined in the Diamond Communications and Engagement Strategy:
•	Supporting user-centric operations.
•	Generating leads for the Industrial Liaison Office.
•	Supporting recruitment.
•	Increasing the awareness and positive perception of Diamond as a world-class hub for cutting-edge research and innovation.
See specification forfurther details.

title: Social Care Provision in Prisons
description:
City of Doncaster Council (CDC) has statutory responsibility for the provision of social care services within the prison setting. 
CDC was not involved in NHS England's procurement process for services commencing on 1 September 2026 and therefore had no input into the social care requirements or associated costs. 
Whilst the healthcare contract was awarded to PPG, no social care provision was included within the new NHS England arrangements. 
The delivery of social care services within a prison environment requires specialist expertise and the ability to operate within a complex and highly regulated secure setting. Providers must work closely with prison management, healthcare professionals and wider support agencies, whilst complying with prison security requirements, safeguarding arrangements, information governance protocols, access controls and established operational procedures. 
As the current provider of both healthcare and social care services within Doncaster prisons, PPG has established relationships, operational processes, governance arrangements, security-cleared staff and integrated care pathways already in place. 
Continuity of provision through PPG will minimise mobilisation risk, support effective partnership working and ensure the ongoing delivery of safe and effective services to vulnerable individuals within the prison population.

title: Compressed Air Systems Servicing & Inspection 2026
description:
DVSA intends to appoint a single supplier capable of providing a national service across Great Britain for its still in service 16 air compressor equipment. 
In addition to planned and reactive maintenance activities, there may be a limited requirement for the supply and installation of replacement compressor units where existing equipment is deemed beyond economical repair.
The compressor estate varies significantly in age and specification, with assets ranging from approximately one year old to almost forty years old. The successful supplier will therefore need to demonstrate the capability to maintain and support equipment of differing ages and configurations.
DVSA is continuing its strategic programme of transforming vehicle testing services by reducing the number of Government Vehicle Testing Stations (GVTS) and increasing the use of privately operated Authorised Testing Facilities (ATFs) and Vehicle Examination Facilities (VEFs). This approach brings testing services closer to vehicle operators and maintainers while supporting a more flexible and efficient delivery model.
As a result of this ongoing estate rationalisation programme, DVSA anticipates that the number of operational sites requiring air compressor support will reduce from 16 to approximately 9 over the duration of the contract.
The objective of this future tender is to secure a single supplier that can provide a cost-effective, reliable and nationally coordinated maintenance service throughout this period of the contract, ensuring the continued safe and efficient operation of DVSA's compressed air equipment.

title: South West Net Zero Hub - Aggregated Renewable Energy Feasibility Studies
description:
The West of England Combined Authority is looking to aggregate approximately seven upcoming renewable energy feasibility projects into a single contract and are seeking input from the market to inform the procurement strategy. 
Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole Council Photovoltaic Rollout Support - This commission builds on previous work that has already identified a portfolio of suitable rooftop solar opportunities. The focus is not on determining whether solar is feasible, but on providing technical, commercial and financial development support to package projects into investment ready portfolios, assess delivery models and prepare business cases for engagement with investors and delivery partners, including Great British Energy. The outputs are project development and commercialisation. Estimated value: £80,000.
Havant Borough Council Landfill Site with Community Energy Broadmarsh - Site specific development commission to progress a known renewable energy project towards delivery. The work includes grid and off taker engagement, planning and environmental activities, technical surveys, and support to develop Heads of Terms between Havant Borough Council and Havant Community Energy. Bristol City Coucil Community Assets Solar and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Demonstrator - This commission includes strategic portfolio appraisal, commercial and community delivery model development, stakeholder engagement, knowledge transfer, and integration with the Bristol City Leap programme. The commission is intentionally designed with decision gateways so that sites can either transfer into the City Leap delivery programme or continue through further development.  Estimated value: £150,000.
Cornwall Council County Farms Renewables Feasibility - This project will assess renewable energy opportunities across the County Farms estate through technical, planning, environmental, grid and commercial appraisal to identify and prioritise viable projects for future development. The outcome is the identification of suitable opportunities. Estimated value: £140,000.
Gloucestershire County Council Renewables Assessment - This commission includes an assessment of renewable energy opportunities and its purpose is to develop a strategic pipeline of investment opportunities across Gloucestershire's public sector estate. The work is driven by immediate political priorities and is intended to identify, prioritise and shape projects capable of progressing into delivery. Estimated value: £80,000.
Torbay Council Solar Sites Assessment - Techno-economic assessment of TC's portfolio, including rooftop solar, solar carports and energy audits. Output will be technical feasibility assessments and business case ready for Torbay Council internal approval. Estimated value: £40,000.
Mid Devon District Council Phoenix Lane Solar - Detailed assessment of the proposed Phoenix Lane Solar PV project, building on previous feasibility work to develop an investment-ready business case. Estimated value: £30,000.
We invite suppliers to participate in our market engagement survey found here: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/q7jBKGUFcf

title: Skerry of Ness and Hoxa Head Lighthouse Refurbishments
description:
Skerry of Ness is a tidal station. Hoxa Head is located on land and can be accessed at all times. To utilise the contractor’s time, its envisaged that Skerry of Ness will take priority to work around tidal times as required, and Hoxa Head works can be carried out around Skerry of Ness activities.
Hoxa Head:  
Location: 
Hoxa Head is located on the Hoxa peninsula on the North East coast of South Ronaldsay, Orkney. The site is located on the longitude and latitude of 58°49.315 N, 003°02.085 W. The site is 400m away from a road end. There are field tracks from the road end to close to the site.
Description of station: 
7m high Aluminium “splat” structure, fixed to concrete base. White GRP daymark panels are fixed to the elevations of structure. The optic is powered by batteries, charged by the 6No panel solar array. The extent of the station is determined by a post and wire boundary fence designed to keep livestock out. There are no welfare facilities at this station.
Description of works: 
The works are of a purely civil nature. The works will include:  Wash down and remove lichen/marine growth from surfaces of all structures (GRP, Concrete and Metal work). Repairs to GRP daymark panels and metalworks as required. Existing fence to be re-strung. No electrical works shall be involved and the optic shall remain operational throughout.
Skerry of Ness:  
Location: 
Skerry of Ness is located south of the town of Stromness on the mainland of Orkney. The site is located on the longitude and latitude of 58°56.960 N 003°17.830 W. Together with Hoy Loy Lighthouse the station denotes the entry to the port of Stromness. The station is located in tidal waters 200m from the mainland. The shoreline can be access via Guardhouse Park Road leading from the town of Stromness.  The station can be accessed at low tide by foot. At high tides, boat access is required.
Description of station: 
10m high post-tensioned white concrete column, topped with concrete platform. The main concrete column is fixed to a square concrete foundation fixed to the sea bed. The platform is accessed via a ladder. There are fenders to each side of the ladder to allow a boat to access the ladder at high tides. The platform is guarded by a handrail and safety gate to the top of the ladder. The optic cubicle is located on the edge of the platform, with solar panels fixed to the seaward facing side of the cubicle. The optic is powered by batteries stored within the cubicle, which are trickle charged by the solar panels. There are no welfare facilities at this station.
Description of works: 
The works are of a purely civil nature. The concrete structure is to be power washed to remove lichen/marine growth from surfaces. Any concrete repairs will be carried out as necessary following power washing. Any corroded metalwork or fixings shall be replaced, this may involve replacement of ladders, handrails, and fenders. The structure shall be redecorated. No electrical works shall be involved and the optic shall remain operational throughout.
Minimum Certification Requirements
Contractor will need rope access certificates (IRATA Certification)
[Important Note to Bidders:  There is a mandatory site visit in Orkney on 10 September -  further details will be given via the message facility.  Those parties who have expressed interest in a future Orkney refurbishment at Hoy Sound (High) can visit this site on 11 September.  To avoid the need for two trips. There will be a separate site visit planned for those parties who have only expressed an interest in Hoy Sound in due course.  Those attending site visits will need to bring suitable PPE and clothing, further details to follow via the messaging facility.]
Please note all details and dates included are subject to change.

title: TEN-2627-047 (PA2023) – Asset Allocation System
description:
Nest is seeking to appoint one supplier to provide, implement and support one hosted software-as-a-service solution for Nest Invest, comprising two mandatory capabilities: Asset Allocation and Total Portfolio View.
The Asset Allocation capability must support Nest Invest’s multi-level fund-of-funds structure and its controlled, model-driven asset allocation process. This includes strategic and tactical asset allocation, portfolio modelling and optimisation, configurable targets, limits and tolerances, portfolio rebalancing, asset restrictions, workflow and approval controls, auditability, scenario analysis and the generation of implementation instructions or outputs for downstream parties.
The Total Portfolio View capability must provide a consolidated view of Nest Invest’s portfolio across public and private assets, including positions, exposures, performance and look-through information where available. It must support aggregation and analysis across Nest Invest’s fund structure.
The supplier will be required to provide software licensing or subscription services; implementation and configuration; integration with retained data sources and Nest Invest’s planned cloud data platform through appropriate data interfaces and APIs; transition and migration from the incumbent IRP solution; testing and user acceptance support; training and documentation; go-live and transition support; and ongoing hosting, maintenance, technical support and product-roadmap services.
The solution must be configured for Nest Invest and supplied electronically as a hosted service. Investment and portfolio data will be received from retained sources, including the fund administrator and custodian, and the solution must generate the required information, reporting and implementation outputs for Nest Invest and its downstream processes.
The contract will be awarded to one supplier for an initial term of five years. Nest may extend the contract for an additional two years and subsequently for a further one year, giving a maximum potential term of eight years. The contract does not guarantee any minimum volume of services or minimum expenditure.

title: Rochdale Team Around the Young Person Accommodation Model (TAYPAS)
description:
Rochdale Borough Council is seeking to commission a Young People's Supported Accommodation Service based on the Team Around the Young Person (TAYPAS) model using a Competitive Flexible Procedure via Light Touch Regime as per Procurement Act 2023.
The service will deliver specialist, psychologically informed supported accommodation for young people aged 18-25 with support needs who are at risk of, or experiencing, homelessness.
The provision will deliver 24/7 support and management across our newly developed, purpose-built accommodation of 28 x self-contained units of accommodation. All three sites are council-owned assets, which will remain in Council ownership and be leased to the successful provider.
To maximise competition and encourage a broad range of high-quality bids, the accommodation will be leased. This can be a Registered Provider (RP), a charitable organisation, community interest company, specialist housing provider, or another suitably experienced organisation.
Bids may be submitted by a single organisation or through a partnership arrangement, including but not limited to an RP working alongside a support provider or other relevant delivery partner.
The accommodation provision relates to three separate sites, which are expected to become operational on a phased basis as units achieve practical completion at different times. Bidders should therefore demonstrate their ability to mobilise and scale services in line with the phased handover programme, ensuring accommodation and support are available as each site becomes operational.
The accommodation provision will be supported through a separate revenue-funded support contract, ensuring the effective and sustainable delivery of both housing management and person-centred support services.
Bidders must demonstrate appropriate experience, financial standing, operational capacity, and governance arrangements to deliver the required accommodation and support outcomes, either directly or through established partnership arrangements.
This flexible delivery approach is intended to maximise competition, innovation, and value for money within the market, and compliant landlords, whilst ensuring residents are provided with safe, high-quality accommodation and tailored support that enables positive outcomes and greater independence.

title: RFI - VHF FM Transmission Equipment / FM Transmitters
description:
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: BBC World Service expects to undertake a procurement exercise for the supply of FM broadcast transmission equipment for its terrestrial Global Radio Network. During any future exercise, the BBC expects to assess equipment manufacturers capability to satisfy its requirements before selecting a preferred supplier or suppliers.
The BBC operates re-broadcast FM relays across a range of territories and operating environments. Many sites are located in remote or hard to access locations and may be exposed to demanding environmental and electrical conditions, including significant temperature fluctuations, high humidity, condensation, dust ingress, corrosive atmospheres, and inconsistent power quality. Local technical support resources may be limited, while the procurement and delivery of equipment and spare parts can present logistical challenges and incur significant costs. Consequently, transmitters designed for enhanced resilience in such environments including the use of conformal coating for improved protection against moisture, dust, and corrosion would be highly advantageous.
The BBC is therefore seeking information from manufacturers and suppliers able to provide robust, maintainable and supportable VHF FM transmitter systems that can be installed, operated, fault found and maintained with minimal specialist intervention, while supporting simplified module replacement and long-term operational resilience.

title: Sexual Health Locally Commissioned Services - LARC + HIV Testing
description:
The contract is for the provision of Long-Acting Reversible Contraception ("LARC") services and HIV Testing services to improve sexual health outcomes by:
•    Increasing the use of Long-Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC), giving more individuals and families reliable control over their reproductive health.
•    Contributing to a reduction in the number of unintended pregnancies and terminations including teenage conceptions.
•    Contributing to reducing health inequalities by improving access to good reproductive health services for vulnerable groups.
•    Increasing the knowledge of risks associated with STIs and referring clients who may have been at risk of STIs to an appropriate service.
•    Diagnosing more previously undiagnosed HIV through enhanced testing of at-risk populations, contributing to a reduction in late diagnosis and the associated harm.  
The contract term duration is 33 months, with an option for a period of extension of another 24 months, through to 31st March 2031.  The Council is intending to award this contract under the Direct Award Procedure C of  The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. title: SPS-02372 Conservation Strategy for Selected SPS Historic Estate Assets
description:
The Scottish Prison Service (SPS) requires a suitably qualified multidisciplinary supplier to prepare three (3) Conservation Strategies for selected historic assets across its estate.  The commission will cover the following sites: HMP Barlinnie (Glasgow), HMP Castle Huntly (near Dundee) and HMP Perth (Perth). The Conservation Strategies will act as practical, significance-led management tools to support maintenance, repair, operation, adaptation, and future decision-making for historic and listed buildings.
The work will include (but is not limited to):
1) Review of baseline information and historic development
2) Building and fabric surveys
3) Structural appraisal input
4) Significance assessments
5) Condition surveys and defect registers
6) Preparation of marked-up drawings showing significance and risk
7) Development of prioritised action plans (short to long term)
8) Maintenance and operational guidance for estates teams
9) Advice on statutory consent and engagement with Historic Environment Scotland and planning authorities
10) Site-specific conservation policies
The outputs will comprise three Conservation Strategies, one per site, supported by drawings, action plans, and guidance documents.

title: Community Wrap Around and Night Support Service
description:
Stoke-on-Trent City Council is seeking to appoint one Provider for Lot 1 and one Provider for Lot 2 to deliver two specialist short-term home-based support services for adults aged 18 and over. 
The services are designed to support people to remain safely within their own homes during periods of increased need, crisis, recovery, assessment or transition, whilst avoiding unnecessary hospital admissions and long-term residential care placements. 
Providers may bid for one or both Lots; however, each Lot will be awarded to a single Provider. 
Lot 1 - Night Support Service
Lot 1 is a short-term overnight support service delivered through block rota arrangements. The service is intended for individuals who require short-term support, supervision, observation or reassurance during night-time hours from 11pm - 6am. 
The successful Provider will deliver overnight support within an individual's home, typically during periods of crisis, hospital discharge, deterioration in health, carer breakdown, increased risk or whilst assessments are being undertaken. The service will provide a physical staff presence overnight to monitor wellbeing, manage identified risks and respond to support needs as they arise. 
A key function of the service is to gather evidence about an individual's overnight needs and provide professional observations to support future care planning and decision-making by the Council. 
Lot 2 - Wrap Around Support Service
Lot 2 is a flexible short-term wrap around support service delivered through block support arrangements for individuals who require a higher level of support throughout the day.
The successful Provider will deliver short-term intensive home-based support to individuals whose needs require regular monitoring, observation and intervention across extended periods of the day. The service is designed to bridge gaps in support, promote recovery and independence, and provide evidence to inform longer-term care and support planning.

The works consist of earthworks, drainage and other ancillary works as remedial measures e.g. works involving cleansing of existing watercourses and re-lining or the construction of new.
The Contractor will be required to assist Blaenau Gwent and Torfaen Councils in the planning stages (co-ordination and programming) as well as offering expertise in respect of buildability and preferred treatments.
It is proposed to carry out a prescribed programme of maintenance work throughout the year, where weather conditions allow and to also undertake ad-hoc remedial measures following periods of severe adverse weather where immediate remedial measures are required.

title: Southampton Smokefree Service
description: Southampton City Council ("the Council") invited Tenders from suitably qualified service providers ("Potential Suppliers") for the provision of a Southampton Smokefree Service. This Procurement was conducted in accordance with the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 using the Competitive Procedure. The contract being procured is for the delivery of a Smokefree Southampton Service that will provide: An oversight role dedicated to maintaining high standards of quality across our commissioned and embedded stop smoking services; expertise, training, CPD, quality assurance, a telephone helpline and service development to support the embedded stop smoking model within the wider workforce; direct Support for people with complex needs, underserved groups or people experiencing health inequalities; the sub-contracting of services within Primary Care Networks and Pharmacies drug and alcohol treatment and support services. The term of the contract shall be from 1st October 2026 until March 31st 2030 (i.e. 3 years 6 months ) with the option to extend for up to a further period of 2 years (i.e. until 31st March 2032) at the sole discretion of the Council. Anticipated funding for the first 6 months (01/10/26 - 31/03/27) of the service (based on current funding) totals £307,500. The anticipated funding for the following 12 months (01/04/27 - 31/03/28) of the service (based on current funding) totals £615,500. This provides for an estimated minimum contract value of £3,382,500 covering the term of contract plus extension period. If there are funding increases the Council is likely to require the provision of additional Services which could be up to a 40% increase in service scope and contract value. Additionally, in recognition of as yet unknown requirements for Services that may exist following Local Government Re-organisation, and the potential widening of the geographic area and level of need that the Contract may need to be modified to address, there may be a requirement to further increase the contract value by 81% from 2028/29. Therefore, the potential maximum contract value, could be up to £7,148,262 for the term of contract plus extension period. Suppliers interested in bidding were required to register with Proactis at: https://supplierlive.proactisp2p.com/Account/Login and search for the project using reference number SPR/1000794 or REQ/1000458. title: DSIT -  Revelio Labs
description:
This procurement is a proportionate, time-limited 12-month data access arrangement designed to meet an urgent evidence need for DSIT/AI Security Institute. The requirement is for access to an existing commercial workforce intelligence dataset, rather than consultancy or bespoke analytical services, and will enable DSIT to test, validate and strengthen the evidence base on AI adoption and labour market impacts. The arrangement is capped at £80,000, with no extension options or open-ended spend commitment, and will be managed within existing programme budgets and governance.
DSIT's AI Security Institute is looking to direct award Revelio Labs for workforce intelligence data to support DSIT's research programme on AI adoption and its impact on the labour market, with a particular focus on skill dynamics, workforce composition, and career trajectories.
Objectives:
1.  Understand how AI adoption reshapes skill demand and supply at the firm level. By acquiring granular, firm-level workforce data (job postings, employee profiles, skill taxonomies, and workforce flows), DSIT's AI & the Future of Work Unit will measure how skill composition evolves at firms actively adopting AI compared to those that are not. 
2.  Provide an empirical benchmark for AI exposure measurement.  Workforce intelligence data enables DSIT to identify which skills actually co-occur with AI adoption at the firm level, providing ground-truth validation of theoretical classifications and improving future measurement frameworks.
3.  Replicate and extend published research on early-career labour market outcomes. To credibly replicate, validate, and extend these estimates for UK policy purposes, DSIT requires access to comparable data of equivalent granularity and structure.
4.  Inform UK workforce and education policy. The evidence generated will directly support policy advice on (examples): which skills retraining programmes should prioritise; where skill gaps are emerging; how curricula should adapt to changing employer expectations; and whether skill dynamics can serve as leading indicators of broader labour market disruption.
5.  Establish early warning capability. By tracking skill shifts that may precede larger employment effects, DSIT aims to build an analytical early warning system that identifies workforce risks before they become visible in aggregate official statistics.
The Arrangement is intended to be entered into by the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology. It is anticipated that the rights and liabilities of the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, including those arising under this Arrangement once executed, will in due course transfer to the Secretary of State for the Cabinet Office pursuant to an Order in Council (secondary legislation) made under section 2 of the Ministers of the Crown Act 1975.

title: BRENT PARKING IT SYSTEM
description:
The purpose of this Pre-Market Engagement (PME) is to assist the Council in understanding current market capability, available commercial models, potential procurement routes and approaches to securing value for money, quality and innovation in the provision of parking IT services.
The Council is seeking information and market feedback on modern parking management solutions suitable for the London Borough of Brent. In particular, the Council is interested in understanding the current market offering and the capability of suppliers to provide an integrated cashless parking solution alongside PCN/Notice Processing and Permit Management functionality.
The Council is also exploring the potential for collaborative or joint procurement arrangements and would welcome market views on the benefits, challenges, commercial models and procurement approaches associated with such an arrangement. The Council is interested in understanding whether these services are best delivered through a single integrated solution or through separate but interoperable systems.
Suppliers are invited to provide information on their current and planned capabilities, solution architecture, commercial models, implementation approach, integration capabilities and experience of delivering parking IT services within the public sector.
This PME is intended solely to inform the Council's understanding of the market and the development of its future procurement strategy. It is not a call for tenders or an invitation to submit a formal tender, and participation in the PME will not give any supplier preferential treatment in any subsequent procurement process.
Please refer to the PME Notice for further details, including the scope of the engagement and the questions to be addressed. Suppliers are requested to complete and submit their responses to the PME questions by the stated deadline.

title: CEFAS26-107 Support services for the Coastal Health Programme
description:
ollowing on from the work delivered in the pilot phase of the Coastal Health programme, The Association of Inshore Fisheries and Conservation Authorities (IFCA) has been selected to support delivery of core requirements as follows:
1. 	Work with all IFCAs to review, update and test protocols and tools to improve our preparedness, response and intelligence gathering processes, and trial their implementation at a national scale. This will include advising Cefas in the development of a scenario testing exercise, and attending preparatory meetings to ensure IFCA processes are adequately captured and tested in this exercise
Actions:
· Continue to circulate and receive input from IFCAs on the protocols and guidance.
· Set up an external shared drive with protocols, guidance and training material.
· Run through a scenario testing exercise with the IFCA Technical Advisory Group, Chief Officers Group and the National Inshore Marine Enforcement Group.
· Run through protocols and guidance at the IFCA Training Course in Brixham in February.
· Promote the work of the Coastal Health programme at relevant national conferences attended by AIFCA (including Coastal Futures and SAGB).
2. 	Building on work started by the AIFCA, create stakeholder maps for each IFCA district of their key local and regional fisheries and environmental stakeholder groups, including a database of contacts.
Actions:
· Work with all IFCAs to pull together lists of stakeholders in each IFCA district, including contact details, and pull together into stakeholder maps.
· Continue to engage with the Coastal Partnerships Network to build on stakeholder mapping across England.
3. 	Key representation for the AIFCA in attendance at the Coastal and Marine Health programme board every two months. Provide updates into the PgB pack. Attendance at CHEPARD and other Coastal Health meetings.
Actions:
· Attendance at meetings and sending over progress updates.
· Production of reports every 2 months to be delivered to the PgB.
4.	 Facilitating engagement with local IFCA's and industry stakeholder groups. This will consist of at least three planned engagement sessions:
a) To present and discuss Coastal Health work on cockles and mussel mortalities in the Wash estuary, with industry representatives and EIFCA officers.
b) To present and discuss the cockle baseline study led last year to relevant industry representatives and IFCA officers, Location TBC.
c) To set up a pilot 'Changing seas' study in an IFCA district (e.g. Sussex), to understand local community perspectives on changing species distribution and abundance in key fisheries.
Actions:
· Work with Eastern IFCA to to present on Cefas cockle work to stakeholders. This will include organisation of the meeting (or facilitation of other means of engagement), producing information to circulate, and travel time.
· Similar to above for second workshop presenting cockle baseline study.
· Changing Seas study
o Work with Cefas to develop design of surveys and interviews for the study.
o To work with an IFCA (e.g. Sussex) and local partners to reach out to local fishermen and wider community members.
o Conduct an engagement session or quayside interviews.
o Support write up and reviewing of final report.
o Support Cefas with scoping national study for next financial year 2027-28.
As needed, ad hoc meetings may be set up to engage with stakeholders' groups in the event of adverse coastal health events

title: Point of Care Testing (POCT) for North Northamptonshire's NHS Health Checks Service
description:
North Northamptonshire Council is seeking to procure a Point of Care Testing (POCT) solution to support delivery of the NHS Health Checks programme from 1 April 2027. The requirement includes POCT analysers, consumables, maintenance, repair and replacement arrangements, quality assurance, training, technical support and account management.
POCT enables trained NHS Health Checks providers to obtain cholesterol and HbA1c results during the health check appointment, supporting immediate risk assessment, patient discussion and appropriate follow-up. Further review has confirmed that the current screening-based POCT model remains clinically appropriate and proportionate for the NHS Health Checks pathway.
The current contract expires on 31st March 2027. The Council's analyser estate is ageing, with a significant proportion of devices expected to require replacement during the new contract period. Contract management concerns have also been identified in relation to asset tracking and external quality control oversight. The proposed procurement will therefore secure a comprehensive and clearly managed POCT contract, reducing fragmentation and strengthening quality assurance, lifecycle management and Council oversight.

title: RCC-1668 Palaeontology Gallery (Science Lab) Rutland County Museum
description:
Rutland County Council ("the Council") is inviting proposals from suitably qualified and experienced suppliers to design, build, and install a new permanent gallery at Rutland County Museum.
The proposed gallery will form a key part of the Museum's future offer, presenting Rutland's early natural history through a dedicated Palaeontology Gallery. Central to the wider visitor experience will be a 10m x 10m immersive box installation, which will be procured through a separate tender process. This commission relates specifically to the design and delivery of a "Science Lab" Gallery which needs to complement and contextualise the immersive experience.
The gallery will explore life on Earth from approximately 400 million years ago through to the period preceding the Stone Age. It will provide visitors with a clear and engaging narrative of evolution, while also highlighting the role and work of palaeontologists in advancing our understanding of the natural world.
The Council's vision is to create a high-quality, "Science Lab" type gallery environment that complements the digital experience of the immersive box. The space should deliver an informative and engaging visitor experience, supporting 	learning, discovery, and curiosity for a broad and diverse audience.
The Council is seeking a supplier capable of delivering a fully integrated, end-to-end service, including concept design, detailed design development, technical design, fabrication, installation, and testing and handover. The completed gallery must be accessible, durable, and designed to a high standard, ensuring a long-lasting and impactful addition to Rutland Museum's offer.

title: Request for information: In-Orbit Demonstration Payloads / Technologies
description:
he Office of the Chief Engineer (OCE), within the Space Chief Technology Officer (CTO) Group, are a team within the UK Space Agency supporting the portfolio of projects and programmes across the wider Agency primarily through technical assurance and research & development activities. This involves investigation of potential new activities that help achieve the aims and objectives of the UK Government’s space strategy. The OCE are currently investigating the need for government intervention to support in-orbit demonstration (IOD) activities for emerging payloads and technologies. This Request for Information (RFI) has been published to better develop our understanding. 
The UK Space Agency would like to understand from space payload and technology providers if there are any payloads/technologies that are currently being developed which would benefit from an IOD opportunity. The Agency would also like to understand the potential benefits unlocked by demonstrating the payload / technology in orbit, and the current perceived barriers experienced in bringing these payloads / technologies to market. The Agency would then like to understand if and how government are best placed to support unlocking the opportunities of bringing these payloads / technologies to market. 
This RFI will inform the OCE’s approach to future IOD opportunities, deepen our understanding of the current pipeline of payloads and technologies being developed that would most benefit from IOD opportunities and help the Agency develop the most appropriate intervention.  
Our aims – what we want to achieve 
The aims of this Request for Information are: 
To understand space payloads and technologies currently being developed in the UK which may benefit from In-Orbit Demonstration; 
To understand the technical requirements of those payloads and technologies; 
To understand the barriers experienced in bringing these payloads and technologies to market; 
To understand the perceived opportunity unlocked by demonstrating the organisation’s payload or technology in orbit that would not otherwise be realised by demonstration and validation through ground testing; 
To understand how government could support addressing these barriers and unlocking future opportunities by demonstrating your payload or technology in orbit. 
In addition to this RFI and to further support our programmatic thought process on any potential interventions, the UK Space Agency will be hosting an in-person workshop based on the responses to this RFI as well as other related topics that we feel require industry's input. This workshop will bring together industry and enable us to gain insights from organisations whose payloads and technologies may benefit from In-Orbit Demonstration. 
To register your interest in attending a workshop, please complete the Organisation & Contact Information section within the RFI and mark your interest in follow-up in Question 8. 
Further details, including the workshop date, agenda and venue, will be provided in due course. Participants will initially be selected on a first-come-first-serve basis to organisations deemed relevant by the UK Space Agency. The outcomes of the Workshop, including any findings, recommendations, and summary outputs, will be made available to attendees and open to wider industry upon request. 
How the information provided will be used and treated 
Responses received will be used alongside wider available information to guide the UK Space Agency’s considerations on future activities to support in-orbit technology demonstrations. 
All information provided may be considered by the UK Space Agency and other government departments for use in policy development. In providing the information requested in this document the respondent confirms that they are giving written consent that the information provided may be shared with other departments, agencies, public bodies, and subsidiaries owned by the above, and their advisors. Where information is shared within government, it will be anonymised and will not identify any specific individual or organisation who provided it.  
Information provided in response to this Request for Information, including personal information, may be disclosed in accordance with any applicable law (including the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004), by order of a court or as required by any body or inquiry which has the power to compel disclosure. 
The RFI participation process, including how to send responses, appears in the section directly after the questionnaire, below. If the respondent wants the information provided to be treated as confidential, they are asked to please inform us. No commercially sensitive information will be shared outside of government. Please be aware that we cannot guarantee confidentiality in all circumstances. For any questions about this process, please email: UKSA.commercial@dsit.gov.uk  
We will process any personal data included in the responses for this Request for Information in accordance with all applicable data protection laws. Our privacy notice is available in the section below titled “PRIVACY NOTICE”.  
The information gathered will not be used beyond the stated purpose without explicit permission. 
RFI Terms 
This RFI is not related to any ongoing or future funding calls from the UK Space Agency. 
The UK Space Agency does not commit to cover any cost incurred in the preparation or submission of any response to the RFI.  
Responding or failing to respond to this RFI will not preclude the respondents from participating in any future UK Space Agency calls or requests for information or other opportunities.  
The deadline for responses is 23:59 BST, 22 September 2026. 
If more time is needed to provide a response or if there are additional questions about the process, please contact UKSA.commercial@dsit.gov.uk with “In-Orbit Demonstration Payload / Technology RFI” as the subject line. 
An email confirmation of receipt from the UK Space Agency will be sent within a one-week period to the designated point of contact. 
The UK Space Agency reserves the right to follow-up and ask clarification questions on any responses.

description:

The Council is seeking information and market feedback on modern parking management solutions suitable for the London Borough of Brent. The Council is also exploring the potential for collaborative or joint procurement arrangements and would welcome market views on the benefits, challenges, commercial models and procurement approaches associated with such an arrangement. title: Working Collaboratively Opportunity – Supporting School Access to Adrenaline Auto-Injectors (AAIs)
description:
Keeping children and young people with allergies safe while in school is a key priority for the Government. Section 34 of the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 (www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2026/21/section/34/enacted) places new allergy safety duties on schools. We have published new statutory guidance on Allergy safety in schools (www.gov.uk/government/publications/allergy-safety-in-schools). Currently under the Human Medicines (Amendment) Regulations 2017, schools in England are permitted to purchase “spare” adrenaline auto-injectors (AAIs) without a prescription for emergency use in cases of anaphylaxis. The Government intends to require all schools to stock “spare” AAIs.  Further education (FE) colleges and other post‑16 institutions are not included in this exemption. Any extension would require regulatory change, which has not yet been implemented. Suppliers should therefore continue to operate in line with the current legal framework.
This early engagement supports the Department for Education’s (DfE) preparatory work ahead of new statutory guidance, with the aim of ensuring schools can access “spare” adrenaline auto-injectors (AAIs) quickly, reliably and affordably to support pupil safety.
The Department is therefore initiating early market engagement with organisations that supply AAIs, including manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers and other authorised suppliers, to better understand the current market landscape and the options available to support schools in accessing “spare” AAIs. 
This engagement will inform consideration of a potential working sponsorship approach, through which the provider market may develop voluntary commercial offers directly to schools in return for a rights package. The intention is to support improved affordability, simplify access, and enhance reliability of supply, while maintaining schools’ independence in purchasing decisions.
To inform this approach, the Department is seeking insight into existing routes to market through which schools purchase AAIs, as well as the practical and operational considerations faced by suppliers, delivery models, and any relevant regulatory factors. This includes understanding potential risks or constraints associated with scaling supply at a national level.
The Department intends to hold a market engagement webinar via Microsoft Teams on Tuesday 11 August at 11:30 – 12:00 to provide further context on this initiative. Following this webinar, the Department intends to hold 1-to-1 discussions with interested organisations, to support a more detailed exploration of market capability and gather more detailed insight. 
To register your interest in attending this event and/or the 121 discussions, please email Adrenalinedevices.PARTNERSHIP@education.gov.uk before 12:00 on Monday 10 August. 
Please note that this notice is for early market engagement and exploratory purposes and is not a call for competition. The Department reserves the right not to enter any formal processes or agreements. Accordingly, the Department will not be liable for any cost, expenditure, work, or effort incurred by a provider in acting based on this notice.

The Minister announced a consultation exercise, which ended on 11 January 2026. The Minister stated that “once the consultations have concluded, the Government will assess the proposals against the criteria in the invitation and decide, subject to parliamentary approval, which, if any, proposals are to be implemented, with or without modification”. description:

Please note that this is not a call for competition. This is a soft market testing exercise is undertaken on behalf of Trafford Council under the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023. 
Purpose: Part IV of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 mandates a statutory duty on local authorities to provide safe accommodation for people fleeing domestic abuse. In Trafford we currently provide safe accommodation in the form of refuges for women, families and male survivors of domestic abuse. We also provide dispersed accommodation for some survivors when they move on from refuges. 
Trafford Council are undertaking this soft market testing exercise to fully understand what the market can offer and the challenges in procuring and setting up this service. It is hoped that this will be an opportunity for us to obtain an insight of how participants might approach delivery of the service, and how they might address circumstances that may impact on the service. We anticipate that should a tender exercise be undertaken, the maximum annual value for the contract might be in the region of £357,559, and the duration to be 5 years, with an initial period of 12 months with the option to extend for period(s) of up to 48 months. 
We are therefore seeking expressions of interest from participants with the relevant expertise and experience to assist us in determining the feasibility of this project by answering the questions that are published on the Chest portal - Project Ref DN827443.

title: NLP Condition Survey Programme
description:
North Lanarkshire Properties (NLP) has a requirement to update its asset management register in respect of the condition of its property estate to ensure compliance with its statutory and legal obligations and to inform a multiyear investment strategy. There are 674 properties in the portfolio and information is required on the following split;
-	5 Business Centres
-	28 Offices
-	233 Retail
-	403 Industrial
-	5 Miscellaneous
-	674 Total
The procurement is for the appointment of suitably qualified and experienced building surveyor (a “Contractor”) to carry out condition surveys across a number of properties within the NLP portfolio.
The aim of the resulting Agreement is to obtain by means of visual inspection consistent, accurate and actionable information regarding the physical condition, statutory compliance, risks, and investment needs of the defined buildings within the estate. Applying the findings to inform a data driven investment strategy to maximise portfolio value. The objectives are to:
-	Establish the current physical condition of each property asset defined.
-	Identify defects, risks, and compliance issues.
-	Provide an assessment of each asset’s life.
-	Provide prioritised maintenance actions. Year 1-5 with year 1 being the faults in most urgent need         of attention.
-	Provide costs as a basis for estimating and to identify the level of funding required for future capital and revenue expenditure.
-	Provide sufficient information to allow a maintenance programme to be developed over a planned period that will support operational planning and asset management decision making
-	Deliver the condition survey in accordance with the following mandatory professional standards:
a.	RICS Building Surveying Standards & Guidance
b.	RICS Surveying Safely
c.	RICS New Rules of Measurement (NRM) for cost estimation
d.	PFI Asset Condition Playbook (2025) – survey methodology and reporting guidance
e.	General Implementation Guidance (2025) for asset condition hand back surveys
f.	Centre of Best Practice (CoBP) specification (where applicable)

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Juristische Begleitung der Umsetzung des neuen EU-Klimaziels und Fortentwicklung Klimaschutzrecht
description: Das Vorhaben soll das Bundesministerium für Umwelt, Klimaschutz, Naturschutz und nukleare Sicherheit (BMUKN) bei der Aufarbeitung von rechtlichen Fragestellungen im Bereich des Klimaschutz-, Umwelt- und Energierechts unterstützen. Dies umfasst die Klärung von rechtlichen Fragen in den Bereichen Energie, Industrie, Verkehr, Gebäude, Abfallwirtschaft, Landwirtschaft, Landnutzung, Landnutzungsänderung und Forstwirtschaft (LULUCF) sowie die Berücksichtigung und Bearbeitung von europarechtlichen einschließlich beihilferechtlichen und von verfassungsrechtlichen Fragestellungen. Hierzu zählen auch mögliche Querverbindungen zum EU-Klimasozialfonds. Das Vorhaben umfasst auch die Bewertung von Vorschlägen für Klimaschutzrechtsnormen und Klimaschutzmaßnahmen auf europäischer und nationaler Ebene. Dabei soll ihre Konsistenz mit dem bestehenden nationalen und europäischen Rechtsrahmen und insbesondere dem gesetzlich festgelegten Ziel der Treibhausgasneutralität bis zum Jahr 2045 analysiert werden. In etwa einem Viertel der Fälle ist neben der Klärung von Rechtsfragen auch eine wirtschaftliche, soziale oder rechtstatsächliche Wirkungsanalyse erforderlich. In etwa 10 % der Fälle sollen im Einzelfall auch wesentliche juristische, ökonomische und soziale Vorfragen für eine mögliche Weiterentwicklung von Klimaschutzrechtsnormen oder Klimaschutzmaßnahmen ausgearbeitet werden können, soweit dies aus Rechtsgründen oder auf Grundlage rechtstatsächlicher Wirkungen notwendig ist. Das Vorhaben soll das BMUKN bei der Vorbereitung von relevanten Dossiers auf EU-Ebene und Vorfragen zu deren Umsetzung auf nationaler Ebene sowie der Fortentwicklung des nationalen Rechtsrahmens unterstützen. Ziel ist es, rechtliche sowie rechtstatsächliche, ökonomische und soziale Vorfragen aufzubereiten und mit empirischen Daten und juristischen Analysen zu unterlegen, um die Grundlagen für eine effektive und nachhaltige Klimaschutzpolitik zu verbessern.

title: Denmark – Construction work – Kvalifikationsordning - Entrepriseydelser ifm. etablering af luft-til-vand varmepumper til/for Kredsløb
description: Kvalifikationsordningens formål er at etablere en liste over kvalificerede entreprenører, som inden for forskellige kategorier kan levere entrepriseydelser for/til Kredsløb Transmission A/S (herefter benævnt: "Kredsløb") ifm. etablering af luft-til-vand varmepumper. Dvs. med kvalifikationsordningen får Kredsløb en forud kvalificeret (”forhåndsgodkendt”) gruppe af leverandører at vælge fra ifm. Kredsløbs senere udbud vedr. entrepriseydelser ifm. etablering af luft-til-vand varmepumper. Med denne bekendtgørelse inviterer Kredsløb potentielle ansøgere til at ansøge om optagelse på kvalifikationsordningen. Kvalifikationsordningen er opdelt i fire kategorier: 1) Teknik-entrepriser 2) Bygnings-entrepriser 3) Elforsyning-entrepriser 4) VAK-entrepriser Det er muligt at søge om optagelse i kvalifikationsordningen ift. en, flere eller alle de fire kategorier. Kvalifikationsordningen er tidsubegrænset og den udløber først på det tidspunkt, hvor Kredsløb vælger at lade kvalifikationsordningen ophøre (i Kredsløbs udbudssystem ("Ethics") skal der angives en udløbsdato, for at ansøgere kan tilmelde sig "udbuddet" og indsende ansøgning om optagelse - derfor er der i Kredsløbs udbudssystem indsat en fiktiv udløbsdato "31-12-2099 23:59"). Der kan i hele kvalifikationsordningens løbetid indsendes en anmodning om at blive omfattet af ordningen, ligesom der løbende kan optages nye entreprenører på ordningen. Kredsløb er ikke forpligtet til at anvende kvalifikationsordningen, men kan vælge at anvende denne i forbindelse med indkøb omfattet af kvalifikationsordningen. Optagelse på kvalifikationsordningen er ikke ensbetydende med, at entreprenøren er garanteret opgaver eller invitationer til at deltage i de udbud, som Kredsløb måtte afholde i henhold til kvalifikationsordningen. Optagelse på kvalifikationsordningen betyder således, at entreprenøren kan, men ikke nødvendigvis, vil, blive inviteret til at deltage i et eller flere af de udbud, som Kredsløb måtte afholde i henhold til kvalifikationsordningen. Optagne entreprenører kan kun blive indbudt til udbud inden for den/de kategorier, hvor entreprenøren er optaget. Kredsløb vil ved de konkrete udbud, som afholdes i henhold til kvalifikationsordningen, tage stilling til kriterier for tildeling af de enkelte kontrakter samt kontraktens vilkår.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Untersuchung der wirtschaftlichen Optimierungspotenziale der Tunnellängsentwässerung
description: Die Tunnellängsentwässerung ist ein wesentlicher Bestandteil von Straßentunneln und trägt maßgeblich zur Dauerhaftigkeit, Betriebs- und Verkehrssicherheit bei. Sie sorgt für die kontrollierte Ableitung von Oberflächen-, Sicker- sowie im Ereignisfall von Lösch- und Gefahrstoffflüssigkeiten und erfüllt zudem im Brandfall eine wichtige Funktion zur Begrenzung der Brandausbreitung. In Deutschland werden derzeit überwiegend Systeme aus Schlitzrinnen und separaten, geschlossenen Entwässerungsleitungen eingesetzt. Diese sind jedoch sowohl in der Herstellung als auch im Betrieb kostenintensiv und führen durch regelmäßige Wartungsmaßnahmen zu Einschränkungen im Verkehr. Vor diesem Hintergrund wächst das Interesse an alternativen, wirtschaftlicheren Lösungen. Ein vielversprechender Ansatz ist der Einsatz von Dükern innerhalb von Schlitzrinnen zur Ausbildung von Brandabschnitten. Während solche Systeme in Ländern wie Österreich und der Schweiz bereits etabliert sind, bestehen in Deutschland noch sicherheitstechnische Vorbehalte, insbesondere hinsichtlich ihres Verhaltens im Brandfall. Es fehlt an belastbaren Erkenntnissen über die Funktionsfähigkeit und Dichtheit von Dükern unter thermischer Beanspruchung sowie über mögliche Auswirkungen auf die Brandausbreitung und die Gesamtfunktion des Entwässerungssystems. Darüber hinaus bestehen Wissenslücken hinsichtlich des Zusammenspiels von hydraulischer Leistungsfähigkeit, Konstruktion und Brandschutz. Zudem fehlt bislang eine ganzheitliche Bewertung der Wirtschaftlichkeit über den gesamten Lebenszyklus verschiedener Entwässerungssysteme, insbesondere unter Einbeziehung angrenzender Trogstrecken. Das Forschungsvorhaben zielt daher darauf ab, eine fundierte Grundlage für eine wirtschaftlich optimierte und zugleich sichere Ausgestaltung von Entwässerungssystemen zu schaffen. Dazu sollen unterschiedliche Lösungen vergleichend hinsichtlich Wirtschaftlichkeit, Betriebssicherheit und Verfügbarkeit bewertet werden. Ein besonderer Fokus liegt auf der Klärung, unter welchen Bedingungen der Einsatz von Dükern sicher möglich ist und wie sich deren potenzielles Versagen auswirkt. Die Ergebnisse sollen Entscheidungsgrundlagen verbessern, Regelwerke weiterentwickeln und langfristig zur Optimierung von Sicherheit, Verfügbarkeit und Wirtschaftlichkeit im Tunnelbau beitragen.

Participation in the market dialogue is neither a condition for nor an impediment to submitting a tender at a later stage, and information from the dialogue that is relevant to competition will be included in the tender documents and made available to all tenderers. This notice is for information only and does not constitute a call for competition. The procedure, scope and timetable have not been finally decided, and the notice does not bind Banedanmark. The procurement is expected to be published by a separate contract notice in October 2026.
