(b)     be called as a witness to give evidence concerning any dispute before arbitrator(s) appointed for any arbitration under the Contract; or

(c)     be liable for any claims for anything done or omitted in the discharge or purported discharge of the Member’s functions, unless the act or omission is shown to have been in bad faith.

The Employer and the Contractor hereby jointly and severally indemnify and hold the Member harmless against and from claims from which he is relieved from liability under the preceding paragraph.

Whenever the Employer or the Contractor refers a dispute to the DB under GCC Sub-Clause 46.3, which will require the Member to make a site visit and attend a hearing, the Employer or the Contractor shall provide appropriate security for a sum equivalent to the reasonable expenses to be incurred by the Member. No account shall be taken of any other payments due or paid to the Member.

6.       Payment

The Member shall be paid as follows, in the currency named in the Dispute Board Agreement:

(a)     a retainer fee per calendar month, which shall be considered as payment in full for:

(i)      being available on 28 days’ notice for all site visits and hearings;

(ii)    becoming and remaining conversant with all project developments and maintaining relevant files;

(iii)    all office and overhead expenses including secretarial services, photocopying and office supplies incurred in connection with his duties; and

(iv)    all services performed hereunder except those referred to in sub-paragraphs (b) and (c) of this Clause.

The retainer fee shall be paid with effect from the last day of the calendar month in which the Dispute Board Agreement becomes effective; until the last day of the calendar month in which the Taking-Over Certificate is issued for the whole of the Facilities.

With effect from the first day of the calendar month following the month in which Taking-Over Certificate is issued for the whole of the Facilities, the retainer fee shall be reduced by one third This reduced fee shall be paid until the first day of the calendar month in which the Member resigns or the Dispute Board Agreement is otherwise terminated.

(b)     a daily fee which shall be considered as payment in full for:

(i)      each day or part of a day up to a maximum of two days’ travel time in each direction for the journey between the Member’s home and the site, or another location of a meeting with the Other Members (if any);

(ii)     each working day on site visits, hearings or preparing decisions; and

(iii)    each day spent reading submissions in preparation for a hearing.

(c)     all reasonable expenses including necessary travel expenses (air fare in less than first class, hotel and subsistence and other direct travel expenses) incurred in connection with the Member’s duties, as well as the cost of telephone calls, courier charges, faxes and telexes: a receipt shall be required for each item in excess of five percent of the daily fee referred to in sub-paragraph (b) of this Clause;

(d)     any taxes properly levied in the Country on payments made to the Member (unless a national or permanent resident of the Country) under this Clause 6.

The retainer and daily fees shall be as specified in the Dispute Board Agreement. Unless it specifies otherwise, these fees shall remain fixed for the first 24 calendar months and shall thereafter be adjusted by agreement between the Employer, the Contractor and the Member, at each anniversary of the date on which the Dispute Board Agreement became effective.

If the Parties fail to agree on the retainer fee or the daily fee the appointing entity or official named in the PCC shall determine the amount of the fees to be used.

The Member shall submit invoices for payment of the monthly retainer and air fares quarterly in advance. Invoices for other expenses and for daily fees shall be submitted following the conclusion of a site visit or hearing. All invoices shall be accompanied by a brief description of activities performed during the relevant period and shall be addressed to the Contractor.

The Contractor shall pay each of the Member’s invoices in full within 56 calendar days after receiving each invoice and shall apply to the Employer (in the Statements under the Contract) for reimbursement of one-half of the amounts of these invoices. The Employer shall then pay the Contractor in accordance with the Contract.

If the Contractor fails to pay to the Member the amount to which he/she is entitled under the Dispute Board Agreement, the Employer shall pay the amount due to the Member and any other amount which may be required to maintain the operation of the DB; and without prejudice to the Employer’s rights or remedies. In addition to all other rights arising from this default, the Employer shall be entitled to reimbursement of all sums paid in excess of one-half of these payments, plus all costs of recovering these sums and financing charges calculated at the rate specified in accordance with GCC Sub-Clause 12.3.

If the Member does not receive payment of the amount due within 70 days after submitting a valid invoice, the Member may (i) suspend his/her services (without notice) until the payment is received, and/or (ii) resign his/her appointment by giving notice under Clause 7.

7.       Termination

At any time: (i) the Employer and the Contractor may jointly terminate the Dispute Board Agreement by giving 42 days’ notice to the Member; or (ii) the Member may resign as provided for in Clause 2.

If the Member fails to comply with the Dispute Board Agreement, the Employer and the Contractor may, without prejudice to their other rights, terminate it by notice to the Member. The notice shall take effect when received by the Member.

If the Employer or the Contractor fails to comply with the Dispute Board Agreement, the Member may, without prejudice to his other rights, terminate it by notice to the Employer and the Contractor. The notice shall take effect when received by them both.

Any such notice, resignation and termination shall be final and binding on the Employer, the Contractor and the Member. However, a notice by the Employer or the Contractor, but not by both, shall be of no effect.

8.       Default of the Member

If the Member fails to comply with any of his obligations under Clause 4 concerning his impartiality or independence in relation to the Employer or the Contractor, he/she shall not be entitled to any fees or expenses hereunder and shall, without prejudice to their other rights, reimburse each of the Employer and the Contractor for any fees and expenses received by the Member and the Other Members (if any), for proceedings or decisions (if any) of the DB which are rendered void or ineffective by the said failure to comply.

9.       Disputes

Any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this Dispute Board Agreement, or the breach, termination or invalidity thereof, shall be finally settled by institutional arbitration. If no other arbitration institute is agreed, the arbitration shall be conducted under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce by one arbitrator appointed in accordance with these Rules of Arbitration.

 

Appendix A

DISPUTE BOARD GUIDELINES

1.         Unless otherwise agreed by the Employer and the Contractor, the DB shall visit the site at intervals of not more than 140 days, including times of critical construction events, at the request of either the Employer or the Contractor. Unless otherwise agreed by the Employer, the Contractor and the DB, the period between consecutive visits shall not be less than 70 days, except as required to convene a hearing as described below.

2.         The timing of and agenda for each site visit shall be as agreed jointly by the DB, the Employer and the Contractor, or in the absence of agreement, shall be decided by the DB. The purpose of site visits is to enable the DB to become and remain acquainted with the progress of the execution of the Contract and of any actual or potential problems or claims, and, as far as reasonable, to prevent potential problems or claims from becoming disputes.

3.         Site visits shall be attended by the Employer, the Contractor and the Project Manager and shall be coordinated by the Employer in co-operation with the Contractor. The Employer shall ensure the provision of appropriate conference facilities and secretarial and copying services. At the conclusion of each site visit and before leaving the site, the DB shall prepare a report on its activities during the visit and shall send copies to the Employer and the Contractor.

4.         The Employer and the Contractor shall furnish to the DB one copy of all documents which the DB may request, including Contract documents, progress reports, variation instructions, certificates and other documents pertinent to the performance of the Contract. All communications between the DB and the Employer or the Contractor shall be copied to the other Party. If the DB comprises three persons, the Employer and the Contractor shall send copies of these requested documents and these communications to each of these persons.

5.         If any dispute is referred to the DB in accordance with GCC Sub-Clause 46.3, the DB shall proceed in accordance with GCC Sub-Clause 46.3 and these Guidelines. Subject to the time allowed to give notice of a decision and other relevant factors, the DB shall:

(a)        act fairly and impartially as between the Employer and the Contractor, giving each of them a reasonable opportunity of putting his case and responding to the other’s case, and

(b)       adopt procedures suitable to the dispute, avoiding unnecessary delay or expense.

6.         The DB may conduct a hearing on the dispute, in which event it will decide on the date and place for the hearing and may request that written documentation and arguments from the Employer and the Contractor be presented to it prior to or at the hearing.

7.          Except as otherwise agreed in writing by the Employer and the Contractor, the DB shall have power to adopt an inquisitorial procedure, to refuse admission to hearings or audience at hearings to any persons other than representatives of the Employer, the Contractor and the Project Manager, and to proceed in the absence of any Party who the DB is satisfied received notice of the hearing; but shall have discretion to decide whether and to what extent this power may be exercised.

8.         The Employer and the Contractor empower the DB, among other things, to:

(a)        establish the procedure to be applied in deciding a dispute,

(b)       decide upon the DB’s own jurisdiction, and as to the scope of any dispute referred to it,

(c)        conduct any hearing as it thinks fit, not being bound by any rules or procedures other than those contained in the Contract and these Guidelines,

(d)       take the initiative in ascertaining the facts and matters required for a decision,

(e)       make use of its own specialist knowledge, if any,

(f)        decide upon the payment of financing charges in accordance with the Contract,

(g)       decide upon any provisional relief such as interim or conservatory measures,

(h)       open up, review and revise any certificate, decision, determination, instruction, opinion or valuation of the Project Manager, relevant to the dispute, and

(i)        appoint, should the DB so consider necessary and the Parties agree, a suitable expert/s  (including legal and technical expert(s)) at the cost of the Parties to give advice on a specific matter/s relevant to the dispute.

9.         The DB shall not express any opinions during any hearing concerning the merits of any arguments advanced by the Parties. Thereafter, the DB shall make and give its decision in accordance with GCC Sub-Clause 46.3, or as otherwise agreed by the Employer and the Contractor in writing. If the DB comprises three persons:

(a)        it shall convene in private after a hearing, in order to have discussions and prepare its decision;

(b)       it shall endeavor to reach a unanimous decision: if this proves impossible the applicable decision shall be made by a majority of the Members, who may require the minority Member to prepare a written report for submission to the Employer and the Contractor; and

(c)         if a Member fails to attend a meeting or hearing, or to fulfil any required function, the other two Members may nevertheless proceed to make a decision, unless:

(i)        either the Employer or the Contractor does not agree that they do so, or

(ii)       the absent Member is the chairman and he/she instructs the other Members to not make a decision.

  1. Purpose

  1.   2. To this end, the Bank:
  1. Defines, for the purposes of this provision, the terms set forth below as follows:
  1. “corrupt practice” is the offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting, directly or indirectly, of anything of value to influence improperly the actions of another party;
  2. “fraudulent practice” is any act or omission, including misrepresentation, that knowingly or recklessly misleads, or attempts to mislead, a party to obtain financial or other benefit or to avoid an obligation;
  3. “collusive practice” is an arrangement between two or more parties designed to achieve an improper purpose, including to influence improperly the actions of another party;
  4. “coercive practice” is impairing or harming, or threatening to impair or harm, directly or indirectly, any party or the property of the party to influence improperly the actions of a party;
  5. “obstructive practice” is:
  1. deliberately destroying, falsifying, altering, or concealing of evidence material to the investigation or making false statements to investigators in order to materially impede a Bank investigation into allegations of a corrupt, fraudulent, coercive, or collusive practice; and/or threatening, harassing, or intimidating any party to prevent it from disclosing its knowledge of matters relevant to the investigation or from pursuing the investigation; or
  2. acts intended to materially impede the exercise of the Bank’s inspection and audit rights provided for under paragraph 2.2 e. below.
  1.   2. In addition to the legal remedies set out in the relevant Legal Agreement, may take other appropriate actions, including declaring misprocurement, if the Bank determines at any time that representatives of the Borrower or of a recipient of any part of the proceeds of the loan engaged in corrupt, fraudulent, collusive, coercive, or obstructive practices during the procurement process, selection and/or execution of the contract in question, without the Borrower having taken timely and appropriate action satisfactory to the Bank to address such practices when they occur, including by failing to inform the Bank in a timely manner at the time  they knew of the practices;
  3. Pursuant to the Bank’s Anti- Corruption Guidelines and in accordance with the Bank’s prevailing sanctions policies and procedures, may sanction a firm or individual, either indefinitely or for a stated period of time, including by publicly declaring such firm or individual ineligible (i) to be awarded or otherwise benefit from a Bank-financed contract, financially or in any other manner;[15] (ii) to be a nominated[16] sub-contractor, consultant, manufacturer or supplier, or service provider of an otherwise eligible firm being awarded a Bank-financed contract; and (iii) to receive the proceeds of any loan made by the Bank or otherwise to participate further in the preparation or implementation of any Bank-financed project;

TERMS OF PAYMENT

 

Schedule No. 1.  Plant and Equipment Supplied from Abroad

In respect of plant and equipment supplied from abroad, the following payments shall be made:

Ten percent (10%) of the total CIP amount as an advance payment against receipt of invoice and an irrevocable advance payment security for the equivalent amount made out in favor of the Employer.  The advance payment security may be reduced in proportion to the value of the plant and equipment delivered to the site, as evidenced by shipping and delivery documents.

Eighty percent (80%) of the total or pro rata CIP amount upon Incoterm “CIP”, upon delivery to the site within forty-five (45) days after receipt of documents.

Five percent (5%) of the total or pro rata CIP amount upon issue of the Completion Certificate, within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice.

Five percent (5%) of the total or pro rata CIP amount upon issue of the Operational Acceptance Certificate, within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice.

Schedule No. 2.  Plant and Equipment Supplied from within the Employer’s Country

In respect of plant and equipment supplied from within the Employer’s Country, the following payments shall be made:

Ten percent (10%) of the total EXW amount as an advance payment against receipt of invoice, and an irrevocable advance payment security for the equivalent amount made out in favor of the Employer.  The advance payment security may be reduced in proportion to the value of the plant and equipment delivered to the site, as evidenced by shipping and delivery documents.

Eighty percent (80%) of the total or pro rata EXW amount upon Incoterm “Ex-Works,” upon delivery to the site within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice and documents.

Five percent (5%) of the total or pro rata EXW amount upon issue of the Completion Certificate, within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice.

Five percent (5%) of the total or pro rata EXW amount upon issue of the Operational Acceptance Certificate, within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice.

Schedule No. 3.  Design Services

In respect of design services for both the foreign currency and the local currency portions, the following payments shall be made:

Ten percent (10%) of the total design services amount as an advance payment against receipt of invoice, and an irrevocable advance payment security for the equivalent amount made out in favor of the Employer. 

Ninety percent (90%) of the total or pro rata design services amount upon acceptance of design in accordance with GCC Clause 20 by the Project Manager within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice.

Schedule No. 4.  Installation Services

In respect of installation services for both the foreign and local currency portions, the following payments shall be made:

Ten percent (10%) of the total installation services amount as an advance payment against receipt of invoice, and an irrevocable advance payment security for the equivalent amount made out in favor of the Employer.  The advance payment security may be reduced in proportion to the value of work performed by the Contractor as evidenced by the invoices for installation services.

Eighty percent (80%) of the measured value of work performed by the Contractor, as identified in the said Program of Performance, during the preceding month, as evidenced by the Employer’s authorization of the Contractor’s application, will be made monthly within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice.

Five percent (5%) of the total or pro rata value of installation services performed by the Contractor as evidenced by the Employer’s authorization of the Contractor’s monthly applications, upon issue of the Completion Certificate, within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice.

Five percent (5%) of the total or pro rata value of installation services performed by the Contractor as evidenced by the Employer’s authorization of the Contractor’s monthly applications, upon issue of the Operational Acceptance Certificate, within forty-five (45) days after receipt of invoice.

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET)

PROJECT ID-P171305

LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980

REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/26-27/00005

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:  CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR WEBTRUST AUDIT AND AATL RECOGNITION PROGRAMME FOR THE UGANDA NATIONAL PUBLIC KEY INFRASTRUCTURE

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority - Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project - Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultancy services for Webtrust Audit and AATL Recognition Programme for the Uganda National Public Key Infrastructure

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include consultancy services for Webtrust Audit and AATL Recognition Programme for the Uganda National Public Key Infrastructure.

 

The objective of the assignment is to obtain independent, internationally recognized assurance and trust-list recognition for Uganda’s National Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), thereby strengthening its credibility, security and interoperability with internationally recognized digital trust frameworks. Specifically, the assignment will engage a licensed and independent WebTrust for Certification Authorities practitioner to conduct a formal audit, including evidence review, remediation tracking and certification support for one year; prepare, submit and coordinate the Adobe Approved Trust List (AATL) recognition process to facilitate document-signing trust and interoperability, including coverage of the annual programme fee for one year; and provide ongoing certification maintenance and query-response support throughout the one-year assurance period.

 

The Implementation period of the assignment is Five (5) Months from the date of signing the contract.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.nita.go.ug/opportunities/bids-and-tenders

 

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The Shortlisting Criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are:

 

  1. The firm should have completed at least Two (2) WebTrust for Certification Authorities audits or equivalent assessments (e.g., ETSI EN 319 401/411) for CA/PKI environments within the last five (5) years.
  2. Submit the firm’s organogram to demonstrate the firm’s technical and managerial capability;
  3. Presence of appropriate skills among staff; Lead WebTrust Auditor / Practitioner and AATL AATL Technical Liaison Specialist (please do not submit CVs and biodata of experts at this stage).

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16, of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025 (Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Least Cost Selection (LCS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations “Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025”.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours at the address below 08:00 to 17:00 hours from Monday to Friday at the address given below.

 

Expressions of Interest (One original plus two copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) on or before 3rd September 2026 at 11:00am Consultants not located in the Country may submit their REOIs through the provided email address.

 

The packages must be clearly marked as; “Expression of Interest for consultancy services for Webtrust Audit and AATL Recognition Programme for the Uganda National Public Key Infrastructure”

National Information Technology Authority-Uganda Palm Courts, Plot 7A Rotary Avenue,1st Floor Kampala-Uganda,

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

Country: Ethiopia

Name of Project: Eastern and Southern Africa Girls’ Empowerment and Resilience (EAGER) programme

Grant No: P179293

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant as Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant

Reference No. ET-AUC-561624-CS-INDV

The African Union Commission has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Eastern and Southern Africa Girls’ Empowerment and Resilience (EAGER) programme and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include maintaining and regularly updating M&E databases, tracking tools, and information management systems to ensure accurate and reliable programme records. Specific tasks include:

 

  • Designing and managing databases to store programme data and ensure accurate reporting.
  • Maintaining and regularly updating M&E databases, tracking tools, and information management systems to ensure accurate and reliable programme records.
  • Regularly collecting, compiling, analyzing, and synthesizing data and monitoring project progresses against established indicators and targets.
  • Assisting in the administration of surveys, assessments, evaluations, and other data collection activities, including questionnaire preparation, data entry, and initial analysis.
  • Maintaining organized records of M&E documents, reports, datasets, tools, and supporting evidence for audit and reporting purposes.
  • Conducting regular data quality checks and support data verification exercises to ensure completeness, accuracy, consistency, and reliability of reported information
  • Following up with implementing partners and relevant stakeholders on submission of required monitoring data and reporting information, under the guidance of the M&E Officer.
  • Providing regular updates on programme achievements, challenges, and risks to program team and stakeholders
  • Assisting the preparations of monitoring reports, dashboards, data visualizations, and other knowledge products
  • Supporting the preparation of periodic project progress reports, including data summaries, indicator tracking tables, and supporting documentation for governance structures such as the Technical Working Group (TWG), Project Management Team (PMT), and Project Steering Committee (PSC).
  • Supporting the organization of M&E-related meetings, workshops, training sessions, and learning events, including preparation of materials and documentation of proceedings.
  • Supporting the documentation and dissemination of evaluation findings, lessons learned, and good practices.
  • Coordinating routine communication with implementing partners and AU Member States regarding submission of monitoring data and reporting requirements.
  • Supporting the operationalization of the AU Gender and Youth Observatory (AUGYO) through data management, documentation and reporting support.
  • Performing any other related duties assigned by the supervisor.

 

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The African Union Commission now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Social Sciences, International Development, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is an added advantage.
  • Minimum of three years of relevant experience supporting monitoring, evaluation, reporting, or data management functions within development, gender equality, education, or related programmes.
  • Demonstrated experience in data collection, data entry, data management, and preparation of monitoring reports.
  • Experience supporting the use of M&E tools, databases, tracking systems, and data visualization platforms.
  • Basic understanding of results-based management (RBM), monitoring frameworks, indicators, and reporting processes.
  • Knowledge and experience in collecting and managing gender-sensitive data and indicators is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to organize, interpret, and present programme data in a clear and concise manner.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills, including experience in preparing reports, summaries, and documentation.
  • Experience working with development partners, government institutions, or international organizations, preferably within the African development context.
  • Proficiency in relevant data management and reporting tools (e.g., Excel, databases, data visualization tools, or other M&E information management systems).
  • Proficiency in English and at least one of the African Union working languages. Good command of French and/or Portuguese is an advantage. 

 

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 0900 to 1700 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 05 August 2026.

MONITORING AND EVALUATION ASSISTANT FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA GIRLS' EMPOWERMENT AND RESILIENCE (EAGER) PROGRAMME

 

REF: ET-AUC-561624-CS-INDV

  1. Background

 

The African Union Commission (AU) and the World Bank Group have established a strategic partnership and an extensive collaboration in various areas over the past years. Following increased engagement between the Commission and the World Bank, existing collaborations and new programmes on gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) have been established. In 2023, the AUC and World Bank signed an agreement to implement the East and Southern Africa Girls’ Empowerment and Resilience (EAGER) project, to be implemented from 2024 to 2029. The project provides a platform to directly collaborate with AU Member States across Eastern and Southern Africa on women and girls’ empowerment.

 

The EAGER project seeks to increase girls’ and women’s educational attainment and earnings and to strengthen the institutional capacity to implement gender equality policies. The project components include boosting human capital accumulation, enabling access to productive employment, and building the enabling environment to generate change across both formal and informal institutions including development of policies and regulatory frameworks, markets, and social norms that support the adoption of progressive gender equality reforms.

 

  1. Goals and Objectives

 

To maintain and regularly update M&E databases, tracking tools, and information management systems to ensure accurate and reliable programme records.

 

  1. Duty Station

 

The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant is expected to be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia at the African Union Headquarters, specifically within the Women, Gender and Youth Directorate (WGYD). He/She shall avail time for any travel pertinent to EAGER as requested by the Women, Gender and Youth Directorate (WGYD), and/or the Department of Health, Humanitarian Affairs and Social Development (HHSD), and/or the African Union International Centre for Girls and Women’s Education in Africa (AUCIEFFA).

 

  1. Activities and Deliverables

 

The African Union Commission seeks the services of a qualified professional to execute the role of Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant.

 

    1. The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant is responsible for:

 

  1. Designing and managing databases to store programme data and ensure accurate reporting.
  2. Maintaining and regularly updating M&E databases, tracking tools, and information management systems to ensure accurate and reliable programme records.
  3. Regularly collecting, compiling, analyzing, and synthesizing data and monitoring project progresses against established indicators and targets.
  4. Assisting in the administration of surveys, assessments, evaluations, and other data collection activities, including questionnaire preparation, data entry, and initial analysis.
  5. Maintaining organized records of M&E documents, reports, datasets, tools, and supporting evidence for audit and reporting purposes.
  6. Conducting regular data quality checks and support data verification exercises to ensure completeness, accuracy, consistency, and reliability of reported information
  7. Following up with implementing partners and relevant stakeholders on submission of required monitoring data and reporting information, under the guidance of the M&E Officer.
  8. Providing regular updates on programme achievements, challenges, and risks to program team and stakeholders
  9. Assisting the preparations of monitoring reports, dashboards, data visualizations, and other knowledge products
  10. Supporting the preparation of periodic project progress reports, including data summaries, indicator tracking tables, and supporting documentation for governance structures such as the Technical Working Group (TWG), Project Management Team (PMT), and Project Steering Committee (PSC).
  1. Supporting the organization of M&E-related meetings, workshops, training sessions, and learning events, including preparation of materials and documentation of proceedings.
  2. Supporting the documentation and dissemination of evaluation findings, lessons learned, and good practices.
  3. Coordinating routine communication with implementing partners and AU Member States regarding submission of monitoring data and reporting requirements.
  4. Supporting the operationalization of the AU Gender and Youth Observatory (AUGYO) through data management, documentation and reporting support.
  5. Performing any other related duties assigned by the supervisor.

 

    1. Deliverables

 

With guidance and under supervision of the Regional Programme Coordinator and working closely with the Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, the Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant will deliver, at a minimum, the following:

  • Routine programme monitoring data collected, compiled, verified, and recorded under approved M&E systems in a timely manner.
  • M&E databases, tracking tools, and reporting templates maintained and updated regularly with accurate and complete information.
  • Monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc monitoring and reporting inputs and reports prepared and submitted according to programme requirements.
  • Data quality assurance protocols developed.
  • Consolidated data summaries, dashboards, factsheets, and other knowledge products developed to support programme monitoring and decision-making.
  • Programme achievements, lessons learned, success stories, and good practices documented and compiled for reporting, learning, and knowledge management purposes.
  • Any other related assignment assigned by the Regional Project Coordinator in support of the EAGER Project

 

  1. Reporting and Supervision

 

The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant will report to the Regional Programme Coordinator and work under the supervision of the Women, Gender and Youth Directorate (WGYD) of the African Union Commission.

 

  1. Qualifications and Work Experience Required

 

a) Bachelor’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Social Sciences, International Development, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. A postgraduate qualification is an added advantage.

b) Minimum of three years of relevant experience supporting monitoring, evaluation, reporting, or data management functions within development, gender equality, education, or related programmes.

c) Demonstrated experience in data collection, data entry, data management, and preparation of monitoring reports.

d) Experience supporting the use of M&E tools, databases, tracking systems, and data visualization platforms.

e) Basic understanding of results-based management (RBM), monitoring frameworks, indicators, and reporting processes.

f) Knowledge and experience in collecting and managing gender-sensitive data and indicators is an advantage.

g) Strong analytical skills with the ability to organize, interpret, and present programme data in a clear and concise manner.

h) Good written and verbal communication skills, including experience in preparing reports, summaries, and documentation.

i) Experience working with development partners, government institutions, or international organizations, preferably within the African development context.

j) Proficiency in relevant data management and reporting tools (e.g., Excel, databases, data visualization tools, or other M&E information management systems).

 

  1. Language Requirement

 

The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant should be proficient in English and at least one of the African Union working languages. Good command of French and/or Portuguese is an advantage. 

 

  1. Terms of Payment and Duration

 

The Monitoring and Evaluation Assistant shall be remunerated based on experience, task load and will be guided by AUC considerations on equivalent professional level and rates. The contract will cover a 12-month period, with the possibility to extend based on successful performance.

ARCHITECT

The Government of Malawi has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of digital development in Malawi “Digital Malawi Acceleration Project” and intends to apply part of the proceeds for hiring of Data Centre Cloud Architect.

 

The overall aim of the Digital Malawi Acceleration Project is to increase access to, and inclusive use of, the internet and improve the Government's capacity to deliver digitally enabled services.

 

The project has four components, namely, Affordable broadband and secure data hosting, Interoperable and secure data platforms, High impact digital services and productive digital usage and Project management. Under Component 2, the Project is expected to cover the Next Generation Digital ID and identity verification services, including electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). To strengthen the capacity for the Department of e-Government, the project wishes to recruit a Data Centre Cloud Architect as part of the project support personnel. This position will be tenable at the National Data Centre in Lilongwe.

 

The Data Centre Cloud Architect, with the support of the Data Centre Manager, will carry out assigned duties and tasks with complete compliance with the best practice. The Data Centre Cloud Architect shall be responsible for designing, planning, and implementing cloud solutions within our data centre environment.

The Public Private Partnership Commission (PPPC) now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The consultant shall be an individual with relevant qualifications and experience. The shortlisting criteria shall be:

  1. A minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field. Master's degree is not required but an added advantage with a minimum of five (5) years of experience in cloud architecture, with at least 2 years in a data centre environment.
  2. Should Demonstrate having relevant certifications such as AWS Certified Solutions Architect, Microsoft Certified. Azure Solutions Architect Expert, or Google Professional Cloud Architect will be an added advantage.
  3. Should Demonstrate having experience in hybrid cloud environments, cloud security practices and tools, including identity and access management, encryption, and firewalls
  4. Demonstrate having a strong understanding of Data Centre technologies, including servers, storage, networking, and virtualization
  5. Should be proficient in infrastructure-as-a service.
  6. Should be familiar with containerization and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.

 

A successful candidate will work with the Department of E-Government for a period of two (2) years renewable annually with the possibility of extending the contract subject to satisfactory performance. The performance will be measured based on timely submission and quality of all deliverables, advancement of the respective activities, and the feedback from management and technical team members at the e-Government Department focused on technical competency, professionalism, responsiveness, and teamwork.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS)

 

 

Country: Nigeria.

Date Issued: 31st July 2026

Name of Project: Nigeria healthcare Sector-wide Approach (SWAp Coordination office).

     Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare.

 

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No: P504693

 

Assignment Title: Establishment of a Prequalified Individual Technical Assistance Consultant Pool under the Technical Assistance Coordination and Resource Alignment (TACRA) Framework

 

Reference No: NG-HOPE-PHC- 559057-CS-INDV.

 

The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare (FMOH&SW) is implementing an ambitious health sector transformation agenda through the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative (NHSRII) and the adoption of a Sector-Wide Approach (SWAp) to improve coordination, efficiency, accountability, and health outcomes across the country.

The NHSRII serves as the Government of Nigeria’s flagship reform platform for strengthening primary healthcare, improving maternal, newborn, child, adolescent and elderly health outcomes, expanding financial protection, strengthening governance and accountability systems, and accelerating progress toward Universal Health Coverage (UHC). The reform agenda is supported by multiple government institutions, development partners, donors, and implementing entities operating across federal, state, and local government levels. The Government has received financing from the World Bank and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include:

  • Establish a pool of qualified individual consultants with demonstrated expertise in priority health sector reform areas.
  • Provide a flexible mechanism for rapid mobilization of technical assistance.
  • Strengthen implementation of NHSRII priorities and Annual Operational Plans (AOPs).
  • Support delivery of health sector reform milestones and HOPE PHC Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).
  • Enhance institutional capacity across federal, state, and local government institutions.
  • Improve alignment, coordination, quality, and accountability of technical assistance delivered under the SWAp framework.
  • Strengthening sustainability of reforms through knowledge transfer and institutional strengthening.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website:https://www.swap.gov.ng/jobsandpostings

 

The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare- Nigeria healthcare Sector-wide Approach (SWAp Coordination office now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

    1. Minimum Qualification Requirements

The individual consultant should possess the following qualifications and expertise:

  • Minimum of a master’s degree in a relevant discipline (PhD or equivalent professional qualifications will be an added advantage).
  • Minimum of three (3) years of relevant professional experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in at least one priority thematic area.
  • Experience working with government institutions.
  • Experience supporting donor-funded programs or health sector reforms.
  • Strong analytical and communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.
  • Experience working at federal and subnational levels.

     1.2      Selection and Evaluation Criteria

  • Educational Qualifications
  • Relevant Professional Experience
  • Technical Expertise in Priority Areas
  • Experience Supporting Government Reforms.
  • References and Past Performance.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

The Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method (IC) set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

   Applicable Procurement Regulations

The establishment and management of the Technical Assistance Provider Pool shall be conducted in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, the Financing Agreement for HOPE PHC, and applicable Government of Nigeria procurement requirements.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 to 1700 hours.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) and soft copy by 14th August 2026.

 

Only consultants meeting the minimum qualifying threshold shall be admitted into the pool.

 

Nigeria Healthcare Sector-wide Approach (SWAp Coordination office).

Request for Expressions of Interest

China: Emerging Infectious Diseases Prevention, Preparedness and Response Project – Hainan Province Project (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project)

Loan No.: 9084-CN

Procurement No.: 0733-26092482

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant Services (Project Assistant)

Contract No.: HN-IC-9

The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank to finance the China: Emerging Infectious Diseases Prevention, Preparedness and Response Project – Hainan Province Project (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project), and intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for the provision of this consulting service.

The main scope of services under this assignment (hereinafter referred to as the “Services”) includes:

  1. Providing consulting advice on the organization and structuring of One Health data resources; assessing the status of existing data and literature resources; providing recommendations on approaches and methodologies for extracting, organizing, and consolidating information from unstructured materials using AI tools such as large language models; and providing continuous support during the database development process.
  2. Providing consulting services for the planning of the One Health Data Management and Knowledge Service Platform; identifying practical requirements for the integration, retrieval, and analysis of large-scale academic literature; and, considering application scenarios of large language models in literature retrieval, question answering, and information integration, providing recommendations on platform functions and application scenarios.
  3. Conducting systematic literature reviews and research landscape analyses in key One Health-related research areas according to the Client’s requirements; identifying cutting-edge developments, research hotspots, and existing foundations of work; and providing recommendations on research directions and priority areas.
  4. Completing other consulting tasks related to this project as assigned by the Client.

This consulting service will engage one Individual Consultant as a Project Assistant. The estimated total input is 18 person-months, and the implementation period of the consulting service is expected to be 18 months (from the date of contract signing until the World Bank loan project closing date of December 31, 2027). The expected commencement date of the consulting service is July 2026.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this consulting service are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

Hainan University (hereinafter referred to as the “Client”) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide relevant documents (Letter of Proposal, Financial Proposal, Curriculum Vitae (CV) of the Individual Consultant (in the format provided in “3. Individual Consultant CV Template”), and supporting documents demonstrating that the Individual Consultant meets the requirements specified in Section VII “Requirements for Individual Consultant” of the TOR, including but not limited to copies of the front and back of the ID card, copies of graduation certificate and degree certificate or equivalent educational qualification certificates, documents proving relevant work experience, Individual Consultant’s Commitment Letter, and a copy of the National College English Test Band 4 (or above) score report) as well as any other documents deemed necessary by the Individual Consultant (if any), to demonstrate that they possess the qualifications and relevant experience required to perform the Services.

The specific criteria for the selection of the Individual Consultant are as follows:

The Project Assistant shall possess an appropriate level of professional competence, relevant experience in project management, proficiency in office software applications, and strong writing skills. The specific requirements are as follows:

(I) Basic Requirements

  1. Shall hold the nationality of the People’s Republic of China and be able to work and reside in Haikou City on a full-time basis;
  2. Shall comply with the laws and regulations of the People’s Republic of China and have no record of violations of laws or disciplines;
  3. Shall have good personal integrity and professional ethics;
  4. Shall possess the physical condition and psychological capacity required to perform the duties of the position normally;
  5. Shall be born after January 1, 1998;
  6. Shall hold a bachelor’s degree in a professional field related to One Health, such as public health, veterinary medicine, zoology, ecology, environmental science, or other relevant disciplines;
  7. Shall have the ability to read and write in both Chinese and English, and possess a College English Test Band 4 (CET-4) certificate or above;
  8. Shall have practical experience in using AI tools such as large language models to conduct literature reviews, information extraction, text organization, and related tasks; shall understand the limitations of AI tools in scientific research applications (such as verification of content accuracy and traceability of sources); and shall be familiar with basic data organization methods (such as tabular data processing and the use of batch text processing tools).

(II) The Individual Consultant shall not fall under any of the following circumstances
(The Individual Consultant shall provide a Commitment Letter in the format specified in “4. Individual Consultant Commitment Letter”.)

  1. Having been subject to any criminal penalties;
  2. Having been dismissed from public employment;
  3. Being currently under investigation for violations of laws or disciplines;
  4. Having outstanding Party disciplinary or administrative sanctions that have not yet been lifted;
  5. Being a conscripted citizen who refuses to perform or evade military service obligations and refuses to make corrections; or being a military service member who refuses to perform duties or deserts for the purpose of evading military service, resulting in dismissal from the military, discharge from military service, or being subject to criminal liability in accordance with the law;
  6. Being listed as a dishonest judgment debtor (person subject to enforcement for dishonesty).

Interested Individual Consultants shall note the provisions on conflict of interest stipulated in Sections 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of Chapter III of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Borrowers, November 2020 edition), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflicts of interest.

The Individual Consultant will be selected through the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method specified in the Procurement Regulations.

The Republic of Tajikistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the "Tajikistan Digital Foundations Project" and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for conducting Public Awareness Campaigns.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Consultancy Service for conducting Public Awareness Campaigns.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/10lCz7x4WfBevzvReKdsWiAc9MXSIhyKa/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=115133111040801685890&rtpof=true&sd=true

The State Institution "Projects Implementation Center for Tajikistan Digital Foundations" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

  • Develop a comprehensive Public Awareness Strategy and Communication Plan, covering target audience profiles; key messages per audience; preferred outreach channels (TV, radio, newspapers, posters, public events, direct mail, workshops, advocacy events, etc.); geographic coverage; and thematic phasing across the project implementation.

  1. CONTEXTE

Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger, avec l'appui financier de l'Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) de la Banque mondiale, met en œuvre le Projet d'Appui au Développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l'Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA). Ce projet vise à contribuer à l'amélioration durable de la productivité agricole et animale, au renforcement de l'accès aux marchés ainsi qu'à l'accroissement de la résilience économique des producteurs et des acteurs des chaînes de valeur ciblées.

Le PACIPA est structuré en cinq (05) composantes :

  • Composante 1 : Renforcement de la capacité de production agricole résiliente
  • Composante 2 : Amélioration des infrastructures agricoles et des marchés de l’élevage
  • Composante 3 : Facilitation de l’accès au financement
  • Composante 4 : Coordination et renforcement institutionnel
  • Composante 5 : Intervention d’urgence contingente (CERC).

Dans le cadre de la Composante 2 consacrée à l'amélioration de l'accès aux marchés et au renforcement des infrastructures de commercialisation, le PACIPA prévoit la réalisation d'un programme d'investissements portant sur la construction et la réhabilitation d'infrastructures agropastorales marchandes destinées à soutenir le développement des chaînes de valeur prioritaires du projet.

Au titre du Plan de Travail et Budget Annuel (PTBA) 2026, il est prévu la réalisation d'environ cent cinquante (150) infrastructures agropastorales marchandes réparties dans six régions d'intervention du Projet. Ces investissements concernent notamment dix (10) marchés à bétail à construire, cinq (05) marchés à bétail à réhabiliter, dix (10) centres de collecte de lait, huit (8) magasins de stockage du Riz, cinq (5) mini-rizeries, quatre (4) magasins de stockage du riz et cent (100) magasins de stockage de l'oignon.

Ces infrastructures constituent des investissements structurants devant contribuer directement à l'atteinte des objectifs de développement du PACIPA, notamment l'amélioration de la compétitivité des filières agricoles et animales, la réduction des pertes post-récolte, le développement des circuits de commercialisation et l'amélioration des revenus des producteurs. À l'horizon 2029, le Projet ambitionne notamment que 30 % du volume des chaînes de valeur soutenues soit commercialisé par les ménages bénéficiaires et que plus de 600 000 producteurs aient accès à des actifs productifs et des services agricoles améliorés. Aussi, il est envisagé qu’au moins cinquante (50) coopératives agricoles et de producteurs soient reliées aux marchés.

Compte tenu de l'ampleur du programme d'investissement envisagé, de la diversité des ouvrages à réaliser, de leur dispersion géographique ainsi que des exigences de qualité attendues pour les infrastructures financées sur ressources de la Banque mondiale, la mise en place d'un dispositif performant de suivi, de contrôle et de supervision des travaux constitue une condition essentielle pour garantir la bonne exécution des marchés et l'atteinte des résultats du Projet.

Les missions de contrôle devront notamment permettre de s'assurer de la conformité des travaux aux études techniques approuvées, aux spécifications techniques des marchés, aux normes nationales applicables, aux délais contractuels ainsi qu'aux exigences environnementales et sociales du Projet et de la Banque mondiale. Elles devront également contribuer à la maîtrise de la qualité des ouvrages, à la prévention des risques techniques et à l'optimisation de l'utilisation des ressources mobilisées.

Par ailleurs, les marchés de travaux financés dans le cadre du PACIPA intègrent des exigences spécifiques relatives à la gestion environnementale et sociale, à la santé et sécurité au travail, à la prévention et à la gestion des risques d'exploitation et d'abus sexuels ainsi que de harcèlement sexuel (EAS/HS), et au fonctionnement des mécanismes de gestion des plaintes. Le respect effectif de ces exigences nécessite un accompagnement rapproché des entreprises à travers une mission de contrôle qualifiée et expérimentée.

Au titre de l’année 2026, le PACIPA vise la construction de dix (10) centres de collectes de lait dans les régions de Diffa, Maradi, Tillaberi, Tahoua et Zinder. A cet effet, le recrutement d'un cabinet spécialisé est retenu pour le suivi, contrôle et la supervision des travaux. 

  1.            Objectifs et Résultats de la mission
  2. Objectif Global

 

L’objectif général de la mission est d’assurer le suivi et le contrôle technique, environnemental et social des travaux de construction de dix (10) centres de collectes de lait dans les régions de Diffa, Maradi, Tillaberi, Tahoua et Zinder afin de garantir la qualité des ouvrages, le respect des coûts, des délais et des normes contractuelles.

  1. Objectifs Spécifiques

De manière spécifique, la mission visera à :

  • Assurer le contrôle technique de la bonne exécution des travaux conformément aux plans et spécifications techniques ;
  • Superviser la mise en œuvre des mesures environnementales et sociales prévues dans le Plan de Gestion Environnemental et Social (PGES) ;
  • Veiller au respect des normes de santé, d’hygiène, de sécurité et de protection de l’enfant sur les chantiers ;
  • Contrôler la conformité administrative et financière, notamment en vérifiant et certifiant les décomptes et paiements présentés par les entreprises ;
  • Appuyer le maître d’ouvrage dans la gestion des litiges, réclamations et conflits éventuels liés à l’exécution des travaux ;
  • Garantir une communication fluide et transparente entre l’ensemble des parties prenantes et organiser régulièrement des réunions de suivi de chantier ;
  • Préparer et superviser les réceptions provisoires et définitives des ouvrages, ainsi que le suivi pendant la période de garantie.
  1. Résultats attendus

La mission de suivi et contrôle des travaux de construction des centres de collectes de lait dans les régions de Diffa, Maradi, Tillaberi, Tahoua et Zinder doit aboutir aux résultats suivants :

  1. Travaux exécutés conformément aux études et aux normes : Les ouvrages réalisés répondent intégralement aux spécifications techniques, environnementales et sociales prévues dans les documents contractuels.
  2. Suivi environnemental et social effectif : Les mesures de prévention, d’atténuation et de gestion des risques (environnement, santé, hygiène, sécurité, genre et protection de l’enfant) sont correctement appliquées et documentées.
  3. Respect des délais et des coûts : Les travaux sont achevés dans les délais impartis et dans les limites budgétaires fixées, grâce à un suivi rigoureux du planning et des décomptes financiers.
  4. Appui au maître d’ouvrage : L’UGP PACIPA dispose d’analyses techniques fiables, de rapports réguliers et de recommandations opérationnelles pour la prise de décision et la résolution des litiges éventuels ;
  5. Communication fluide et transparente avec le Maitre d’ouvrage ;
  6. Réceptions conformes : Les ouvrages sont réceptionnés (provisoire et définitive) sans réserve majeure.

 

  1. ÉTENDUE DE LA MISSION

 

  1. Description détaillée des travaux

La mission de suivi et contrôle confiée au Consultant couvrira l’ensemble du processus de réalisation des travaux, depuis la préparation du chantier jusqu’à la période de garantie. Elle s’articule autour de quatre blocs complémentaires : le contrôle technique de tous les travaux exigés pour garantir la qualité requise conformément aux normes en vigueur, le Contrôle administratif et financier, la surveillance environnementale et sociale des travaux ainsi que les réceptions des travaux et le suivi pendant la période de garantie.

  1. Contrôle technique

Le contrôle technique est la mission phare de l’Ingénieur-contrôle (Ingénieur). Le consultant doit, sans débrouille, prendre les dispositions idoines pour faire réaliser les infrastructures répondant aux besoins et normes en vigueur. Sans être exhaustif, l’Ingénieur doit :

  • Examiner et approuver les plans d’exécution, dossiers techniques et plans de récolement préparés par les entreprises ;
  • Organiser et contrôler l’implantation des ouvrages ;
  • Assurer le contrôle technique des travaux à chaque étape (fondations, maçonneries en élévation, structures en béton armé, couvertures, etc.) ;
  • Vérifier la conformité des matériaux et équipements, approuver les échantillons avant approvisionnement ;
  • Suivre la mobilisation du matériel et des ressources humaines des entreprises ;
  • Contrôler le respect des délais techniques (Chronogramme) ;
  • Assurer la tenue et la mise à jour régulière d’un dossier de chantier (programmes, correspondances, procès-verbaux, etc.) ;
  • Permettre et recevoir les missions de supervision de l’administration dirigées par la DGGR assurant le rôle de maitre d’ouvrage délégué.
  • Étendre la mission au contrôle des installations électriques, solaires, hydrauliques, sanitaires, frigorifiques et aux équipements de collecte et de conservation du lait.
  1. Contrôle administratif et financier

Le contrôle financier permet au Maitre d’ouvrage (MO) de payer les travaux réellement exécutés et conformes aux prescriptions. Suivant les phases des travaux, la mission de suivi et contrôle doit :

  • Vérifier la conformité des documents administratifs : garanties de bonne exécution, assurances, autorisations réglementaires ;
  • Examiner et valider le programme de travail, le plan d’assurance qualité et les procédures d’approvisionnement des entreprises ;
  • Vérifier contradictoirement les attachements et décomptes de travaux ;
  • Certifier les paiements intermédiaires et préparer les propositions de certificat de paiement final ;
  • Évaluer les avenants éventuels au contrat (techniques, financiers, délais) et en analyser les impacts ;
  • Préparer et transmettre régulièrement des rapports financiers et techniques consolidés à l’UGP PACIPA ;
  • Organiser et animer les réunions de coordination de chantier, en produire les procès-verbaux ;
  • Accompagner et assister le Maitre d’ouvrage lors des missions de visite de sites.
  1. Surveillance environnementale et sociale

La surveillance environnementale et sociale sera assurée par l’Ingénieur chargé de la mission de contrôle et de supervision des travaux. Elle vise à garantir la conformité environnementale et sociale des travaux aux dispositions réglementaires nationales, aux exigences contractuelles ainsi qu’aux Normes Environnementales et Sociales (NES) de la Banque mondiale.

A cet effet, le Consultant exercera un contrôle permanent de la mise en œuvre des mesures de prévention, d'atténuation et de gestion des risques et impacts environnementaux et sociaux liés aux activités du projet. Il veillera au strict respect, par les entreprises, de l'ensemble de leurs obligations environnementales, sociales, sanitaires et sécuritaires pendant toute la durée des travaux.

A. Cadre environnemental et social applicable

Dans le cadre de sa mission, le Consultant veillera à l'application des exigences des Normes Environnementales et Sociales (NES) suivantes :

  • NES 1 : Évaluation et gestion des risques et impacts environnementaux et sociaux ;
  • NES 2 : Emploi et conditions de travail ;
  • NES 3 : Utilisation rationnelle des ressources et prévention de la pollution ;
  • NES 4 : Santé et sécurité des populations ;
  • NES 5 : Acquisition de terres, restrictions à l’utilisation des terres et réinstallation involontaire ;
  • NES 10 : Mobilisation des parties prenantes et gestion des plaintes.

Le Consultant s’appuiera notamment sur les instruments environnementaux et sociaux du Projet, comprenant :

  • le Cadre de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (CGES) ;
  • les Plans de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale de Chantier (PGES-Chantier) élaborés par les entreprises ;
  • le Plan de Gestion de la Main-d’œuvre (PGMO) ;
  • le Plan de Mobilisation des Parties Prenantes (PMPP) ;
  • le Cadre de Politique de Réinstallation (CPR) ;
  • les éventuels Plans d’Action de Réinstallation (PAR).

Ces documents constituent le référentiel de contrôle du Consultant et lui sont opposables dans l’exécution de sa mission.

 

B. Objectifs et résultats environnementaux et sociaux

La surveillance environnementale et sociale poursuivra notamment les objectifs suivants :

  • assurer la conformité des travaux aux PGES-Chantier et aux exigences des NES applicables ;
  • réduire les risques environnementaux, sociaux, sanitaires et sécuritaires associés aux travaux ;
  • garantir la protection des travailleurs et des communautés riveraines ;
  • assurer un traitement efficace et transparent des plaintes ;
  • promouvoir les principes d’inclusion, d’égalité des chances et de non-discrimination.

Le Consultant suivra notamment les indicateurs suivants :

  • taux de conformité des chantiers aux PGES-Chantier ;
  • nombre d’incidents et d’accidents enregistrés ;
  • taux de réalisation des mesures correctives ;
  • nombre de plaintes enregistrées et traitées ;
  • délai moyen de traitement des plaintes ;
  • taux de résolution des plaintes.

Les résultats attendus comprennent notamment :

  • la mise en œuvre effective des PGES-Chantier ;
  • le respect des conditions de travail prévues dans le PGMO ;
  • le fonctionnement efficace du mécanisme de gestion des plaintes ;
  • l'amélioration continue des performances HSS des entreprises ;
  • la conformité des bases-vie éventuelles aux exigences en matière de santé, d’hygiène, de sécurité et de bien-être des travailleurs.

C. Libération des emprises et conformité à la NES5

Avant toute émission d’ordre de service autorisant le démarrage des travaux, le Consultant devra vérifier et confirmer :

  • la libération effective des emprises concernées ;
  • le paiement des compensations et indemnisations dues aux personnes affectées par le Projet ;
  • la conformité des procédures appliquées avec les dispositions du CPR, des éventuels PAR et de la NES 5 ;
  • la disponibilité des preuves documentaires attestant la libération des terrains.

Aucun chantier ne pourra démarrer sans validation préalable de ces exigences.

D. Approbation et suivi du PGES -Chantier

Le Consultant examinera et validera les PGES-Chantier préparés par chaque entreprise avant le démarrage des travaux.

À cet effet, il devra :

  • analyser la conformité des PGES-Chantier avec les exigences du Projet et les NES applicables ;
  • formuler les observations et recommandations nécessaires ;
  • approuver les PGES-Chantier avant toute mobilisation des entreprises ;
  • contrôler régulièrement leur mise en œuvre sur le terrain.

Le Consultant mettra en place les outils de suivi suivants :

  • check-lists hebdomadaires de conformité environnementale et sociale ;
  • fiches de non-conformité environnementale et sociale ;
  • registre des actions correctives ;
  • tableau de bord de suivi environnemental et social.

Il réalisera au minimum une mission de supervision environnementale et sociale par mois sur chaque chantier, indépendamment des visites techniques de routine.

Par ailleurs, il vérifiera :

  • la mise en œuvre du plan de gestion des déchets ;
  • le tri, le stockage, le transport et l'élimination des déchets conformément à la réglementation nationale ;
  • la provenance légale des matériaux utilisés ;
  • les autorisations des zones d’emprunt, carrières et sites de prélèvement ;
  • l’intégration des mesures de résilience climatique, notamment le drainage des eaux pluviales, la protection contre l’érosion et les mesures d’adaptation aux aléas climatiques.

E. Personnel environmental et social

Le Consultant mobilisera un Spécialiste Environnemental et Social qualifié ayant une expérience avérée en suivi environnemental et social des projets d’infrastructures financés par les partenaires techniques et financiers.

Le Spécialiste E&S devra :

  • assurer une présence régulière sur les chantiers conformément aux exigences contractuelles ;
  • effectuer un nombre minimum de jours de mission sur site défini dans le contrat ;
  • tenir un registre des missions et visites effectuées ;
  • disposer d’une formation attestée en matière de prévention et de prise en charge des risques de VBG/EAS-HS ;
  • assurer des séances périodiques de sensibilisation du personnel de la mission de contrôle et des entreprises sur les exigences environnementales et sociales du Projet.

F. Calendrier, notification des incidents et livrables

Le Consultant élaborera dès le démarrage de sa mission :

  • un Plan de Surveillance Environnementale et Sociale (PSES) ;
  • des check-lists de contrôle environnemental et social ;
  • des fiches de constat et de non-conformité ;
  • un dispositif de suivi des indicateurs environnementaux et sociaux.

Tout incident grave, notamment :

  • accident mortel ;
  • accident ayant entraîné des blessures graves ;
  • incident majeur de pollution ;
  • conflit social majeur ;
  • incident de VBG/EAS-HS ;

devra être signalé au Maître d’Ouvrage et à l’Unité de Gestion du Projet dans un délai maximal de 24 heures après sa survenance.

Le volet environnemental et social des rapports mensuels comprendra au minimum :

  • les indicateurs de performance E&S ;
  • le suivi des PGES-Chantier ;
  • les check-lists de conformité ;
  • les actions correctives engagées ;
  • le registre des plaintes ;
  • le registre des incidents et accidents ;
  • les activités de sensibilisation réalisées ;
  • les registres de présence du Spécialiste E&S ;
  • une documentation photographique des chantiers.

A l’achèvement des travaux, le Consultant produira un rapport de réception environnementale et sociale, distinct du rapport de réception technique, attestant de la conformité environnementale et sociale des ouvrages réalisés.

  1. Réception et suivi des garanties

DISPOSITIONS RELATIVES A LA GESTION DES PLAINTES

Le Consultant assurera un contrôle indépendant du mécanisme de gestion des plaintes (MGP) mis en place par les entreprises et veillera à sa conformité avec les exigences du Projet, de la réglementation nationale applicable et de la NES 10 relative à la mobilisation des parties prenantes et à la gestion des plaintes.

A cet effet, il vérifiera que chaque entreprise a mis en place, opérationnalisé et maintient un mécanisme de gestion des plaintes accessible, transparent, inclusif et efficace, en étroite coordination avec le dispositif de gestion des plaintes du Projet.

L’entreprise met en œuvre le MGP des travailleurs tandis que le Consultant en vérifie la conformité et le fonctionnement.

Le Consultant s’assurera notamment que le mécanisme :

  • est accessible aux travailleurs, aux communautés riveraines et aux autres parties prenantes, en tenant compte des considérations liées au genre, à la langue et à la vulnérabilité ;
  • dispose de canaux diversifiés de réception des plaintes (points focaux, téléphone, boîtes à plaintes, réunions communautaires, etc.) ;
  • garantit l’enregistrement systématique et la traçabilité des plaintes dans un registre dédié ;
  • permet l’analyse, le traitement et la résolution des plaintes dans des délais appropriés
  • assure la mise en œuvre et le suivi des mesures correctives convenues ;
  • garantit la confidentialité des plaignants et la protection contre toute forme de représailles ;
  • contribue à la prévention et à la résolution des conflits liés à la mise en œuvre des travaux ;
  • fait l’objet d’activités régulières d’information et de sensibilisation auprès des parties prenantes.

Le Consultant assurera le suivi périodique des performances du mécanisme à travers les indicateurs suivants :

  • nombre total de plaintes reçues ;
  • nombre de plaintes traitées et résolues ;
  • nombre de plaintes en cours ou non résolues ;
  • délai moyen de traitement des plaintes ;
  • taux de résolution des plaintes ;
  • nombre de plaintes sensibles, notamment celles liées aux cas de VBG/EAS/HS.

Dans le cadre de sa mission de surveillance environnementale et sociale, le Consultant réalisera un contrôle mensuel du fonctionnement du MGP de chaque entreprise et présentera, dans ses rapports mensuels, un tableau de bord synthétique des plaintes, des actions correctives engagées et de leur état d’avancement.

Les plaintes sensibles, notamment celles relatives aux cas de VBG/EAS/HS, seront traitées conformément aux protocoles de référencement et de confidentialité du Projet. Elles devront être signalées à l’Unité de Gestion du Projet dans un délai maximal de 24 heures après leur enregistrement, sans divulgation d’informations permettant d’identifier les survivant(e)s.

 

 

                                            MODALITES DE PAIEMENT

Les paiements seront mensuels après dépôts du rapport et la facture correspondants. Chaque paiement est conditionné par l’approbation du rapport, à la mobilisation effective du personnel et à l’atteinte des indicateurs à définir dans le contrat.
