Government of Nepal

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) –

Sisneri Water Supply Project

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL)

First Date of Publication: 27th August 2026

Environmental Specialist - Ref No. KVWaSIP-IC-04-083/84

1.0 Background

The Government of Nepal (GoN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services include providing technical, procurement, financial management, environmental and social, contract management, and other professional support required for effective implementation of the Project through the Project Management Unit (PMU)

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide a detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating that they possess the required educational qualifications, professional experience, and technical competence to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria for each assignment are specified in the respective Terms of Reference (TOR), which may be obtained from the address or website indicated below

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Environmental Specialist and requests applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position.

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The overall objective of this assignment is to support the PMU in preparation of the environmental safeguard measures under KV WaSIP.

Specific objectives of the assignment are to:

  • Support the PMU in the preparation of environmental and social assessments and instruments commensurate with the project’s environmental and social risks and impacts, to ensure project readiness for appraisal and implementation.
  • Ensure compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards and the environmental requirements set out in the project’s Environmental and Social Management Framework.
  • Guide and support the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments, Environmental Management Plans, and other relevant instruments for future subprojects in accordance with the ESF, World Bank requirements, and applicable Government of Nepal legislation.
  • Support the PMU in ensuring that environmental mitigation measures, monitoring requirements, and reporting obligations are integrated into project design, procurement documents, contracts, and implementation arrangements.
  • Assist in the timely review, endorsement, and signing of key environmental and social documents required for project preparation and implementation.
  • Facilitate and follow up on all required environmental clearances, approvals, permits, and no-objection processes from relevant authorities.
  • Ensure that project activities comply with the Government of Nepal’s applicable laws, regulations, and policies related to environmental management, tree clearance, forest land acquisition, Occupational health  and safety (OHS), and downstream water use rights.
  • Lead and coordinate stakeholder mapping, consultations, and stakeholder engagement activities relevant to project preparation and implementation, ensuring that environmental and social risks and concerns are adequately identified and addressed.
  • Build the institutional capacity of the PMU, PIUs, and other relevant counterparts on environmental and social risk management, including the implementation of mitigation measures, monitoring, documentation, and reporting.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

The duties of the Specialist is mentioned in the Terms of Reference in detail.

4. Qualifications and Experience

All applications will be evaluated against the assignment’s required qualifications below.  

Candidates who comply with the minimum qualifications will be scored according to predefined criteria. A minimum of three candidates will be shortlisted and interviewed. The candidate with the highest score will be invited to negotiate a contract. Referees of the selected candidate may be contacted to verify prior experience, performance, and interpersonal skills. 

Qualifications and Relevant Experience

  • Education:
    • Master’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, or environmental management.
    • Training in environmental impact assessment
  • Work Experience:
  • At least 10 years of experience in the environmental safeguard sector.
  • Working experience with water or hydropower dam projects will be beneficial.
  • Experience in the preparation and review of safeguard documents under multilateral development bank safeguard policy frameworks and the ESF.
    • Experience in reviewing E&S policy documents will be an advantage..
  • Interpersonal Skills
    • Strong analytical and report writing skills in both English and Nepali.
    • Ability to coordinate effectively with concerned stakeholders at construction sites.
    • Willingness to undertake regular field visits, including to project areas that may be remote.
    • Familiarity with the Government of Nepal's legal framework on forest and environmental management.
    • Ability to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team.

5. Evaluation and Selection Method

The Senior Dam Specialist will be hired by the PMU using the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method following “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) Seventh Edition 2025. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations”.

6. Duration of the Assignment

The Environmental Specialist will be engaged on a full-time basis throughout the grant implementation period (approx. 17 months). Based on the performance and if the project is approved, the Environmental Specialist may continue in this role for the project implementation. 

7. Remuneration

A market-based salary package commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications will be offered.

8. Reporting

The Environmental Specialist will report directly to the Project Manager, PMU. He/she will maintain close coordination with the World Bank's Environmental Specialist and other relevant Bank team members throughout the assignment.

9. Location

  • The consultant will be based at the PMU office and may be required to travel outside the valley as needed for project-related procurement activities.
  • The Project shall provide following facilities to consultant during his tenure of service:
  • Office space
  • Email and internet access
  • Required office stationery and other materials
  • Photocopying/printing facilities

10. Application Process

Interested candidates shall submit a complete application package comprising:

  1. Up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV).
  2. Copies of academic and professional certificates.
  3. Contact details for at least three (03) professional references familiar with the candidate’s relevant work.

Applications shall be submitted electronically no later than 17.00 PM on 11th September 2026 to the following e-mail address: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com. Only complete applications received by the deadline will be considered.

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project – Sisneri Water Supply Project

Address: Jawlakhel, Lalitpur

Attention: Executive Director

Email: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com

Website: www.kvwsmb.org.np

ELECTRICITY SECTOR IMPROVEMENT AND ACCESS PROJECT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTANT SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

ACTIVITY: CONTRACT MANAGEMENT SPECIALIST

Reference No.: AO-MINEA - GEPE-567353-CS-INDV

 

The Government of the Republic of Angola (GoA) has received financing from the International Bank of Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and co-financing from the French Development Agency (AFD) towards the cost of the Electricity Sector Improvement and Access Project (ESIAP), whose objective is to improve the operational and commercial performance of the electricity sector utilities and increase electricity access in Angola. The Project is being implemented by the Ministry of Energy and Water and consists of five complementary components: (i) Widening access to electricity and improving revenue collection; (ii) Improving electric service; (iii) Enhancing PRODEL's capacity and strengthening sustainable management of power plants; (iv) Supporting project management; and (v) Responding to Contingent Emergencies.

A Project Coordination Unit (PCU) of ESIAP intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing to procure the services of an individual consultant for the position of Contract Management Specialist.

The primary objective of the Contract Management Specialist consultancy is to support the PCU and Utilities in ensuring effective, compliant, and timely management of contracts across all components of the Angola Electricity Sector Improvement and Access Project. The specialist will play a critical role in overseeing contract administration, facilitating coordination among key stakeholders — including PRODEL, RNT, and ENDE — and providing strategic advice to enhance the operational performance of the utilities.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Project Coordination Unit (PCU) now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest in providing the services by sending a signed Cover Letter, Curriculum Vitae (CV), in a letter addressed to the Project Coordinator, along with a copy of their identification document and proof of education and skills, as indicated in the CV. Interested consultants should provide information (Statement) showing that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to carry out the work, according to the ToRs.

The selection criteria are:

Education

  • Degree in Engineering, Law, Business Administration, Project Management, or a related field, from a recognized University.
  • Relevant professional certifications in contract management or procurement (e.g., PMP, CIPS, FIDIC) are highly desirable.

Experience

  • Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in contract management for large-scale infrastructure projects, with at least 5 years in the energy or power sector, preferably involving transmission and distribution networks.
  • Demonstrated experience in the preparation, negotiation, administration, and monitoring of complex works and goods contracts, including FIDIC or similar international contract standards.
  • Proven experience in managing contracts: Works (at least two contracts valued USD 20,000,000.00 each), Goods and/or Non-Consulting Services (at least two contracts valued USD 2,000,000.00 each), as well as Consultancy Services (at least two contracts valued (USD 1,500,000.00 each). {Applicant to submit evidence of experience}
  • Proven track record in managing contract-related risks, claims, and dispute resolution in the context of donor-funded projects. Exposure to World Bank or other Multilateral Financing Institutions procedures will be considered an advantage.
  • Experience working in multiple countries or regions, including in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable environments, is required. Work experience in Angola will be considered an advantage
  • Prior involvement in capacity building and knowledge transfer to local counterparts is an advantage.
  • Experience in using the WB STEP system is an added advantage

Skills and Competencies

  • In-depth knowledge of the best international practices in contract management, procurement regulations, and project implementation for infrastructure investments.
  • Strong analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to address technical, legal, and financial aspects of contract management.
  • Excellent organizational and time management abilities, with a demonstrated capacity to manage multiple contracts and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Proficiency in contract management and project management software; advanced skills in Microsoft Office Suite are essential.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English; knowledge of Portuguese is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary and multicultural teams, and to interact with government officials and utility staff.
  • High ethical standards, attention to detail, and commitment to delivering results under tight deadlines.

The Contract Management Specialist will work in Angola, Luanda, in the office assigned to ESIAP . The role may also necessitate periodic travel to project implementation sites across Angola, including visits to project sites or utility offices as necessary to support project implementation and oversight.

The duration of the assignment of the Contract Management Specialist will be for a period of 18 months, on a full-time basis, with possible extension upon satisfactory performance.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, seventh edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (IC) selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Interested individual consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 08:00 to 16:00 hours local time.

Expressions of interest must be preferably delivered e-mail or delivered by mail or in person, to the address below, by September 14, 2026 at 16:00 hours (local time) and mention “Expression of Interest – Contract Management Specialist”.

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated in a two-stage process:

  1. Curriculum Vitae (CV) Evaluation (Mandatory);
  2. Interview (Only for candidates shortlisted following the CV evaluation).

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Multinational

Name of Project: Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project

Grant No.: P P514153

Assignment Title: Procurement of Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway

Reference No: 926/AUDA/DITIR/RESILIENTIRRIGATIONF/QCBS/2026

Method: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS)

 

  1. Introduction

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and process workflows, including a unified data interoperability Layer that meets vPIC standards and aligns with the Africa RISE Regional Geospatial Analytics Platform and national irrigation monitoring systems.  The architecture shall specify: (a) the endpoints and payload schemas through which national data collection tools, the Regional Geospatial Platform,  and other authorized external data sources submit and validate benchmarking data; (b) the data lineage and version control mechanisms ensuring that published benchmarks are traceable to their submission source; and (c) the traffic-light alert logic that translates performance indicator values into color-coded risk flags for display in the executive dashboard. Task 3: Technical Assistance (TA) and Capacity Building: Develop and deliver a structured, tiered capacity-building programme and associated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. Task 4: Sustainable Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Model for the Gateway: Assess the technical and operational requirements for sustained operation of the Gateway, including hosting, security, data management, updates, user support and maintenance schedules and prepare indicative annual cost projections for the post-project period. Task 5: Envisaged functionality of the Africa RISE Gateway: The Africa RISE Gateway, as a go-to information and knowledge solution, is envisaged to serve.

 

  1. Level of Effort for Key staff:

Person-Days

55

80

  1. Duration of the assignment

 Total duration: 56 weeks from the date of contract signature

 

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the following website: https://www.nepad.org/corporate-procurement#tenders

 

  1. Shortlisting criteria:

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • The firm shall demonstrate at least ten (10) years of proven institutional experience in designing, developing, deploying and supporting large-scale digital platforms of similar scope and complexity, preferably for regional, public sector or international development programmes.

 

  • The firm should have completed at least three (3) comparable assignments involving enterprise system architecture, API-first platform development, knowledge management systems, data integration, analytics dashboards, workflow management, cloud hosting, cybersecurity, user support and long-term system maintenance.

 

  • Relevant experience should include assignments involving interoperability with existing digital ecosystems, geospatial or remote sensing data integration, benchmarking and performance monitoring dashboards, multilingual knowledge repositories, data governance, user access controls and institutional handover.

 

  • The firm should also demonstrate experience working with government institutions, regional organisations, development partners and multi-country stakeholder groups in Africa, including the delivery of virtual consultations, capacity building, documentation and post-launch technical support.

 

  • Experience in agriculture, irrigation, water management, climate resilience, infrastructure, innovation financing or related sectors will be an added advantage.

 

  • The firm should have evidence of at least 3 assignments of similar nature in the region

 

  1. Conflict of interest

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025  (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

  1. A firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Goods, Works, or Non-consulting Services for a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that firm), shall be disqualified from providing Consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to, those Goods, Works, or Non-consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

 

  1. A firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Consulting Services for the preparation or implementation of a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Consulting firm), shall be disqualified from subsequently providing Goods, Works, or Non-consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to those Consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

 

  1. Neither a Consultant (including personnel and sub-consultants), nor an affiliate (that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Consultant), shall be hired for any assignment that, by its nature, creates a conflict of interest with another assignment of the Consultant;

 

  1. Consultants (including their experts and other personnel, and sub-consultants), that have a close business or family relationship with a professional staff of the Borrower, or of the project implementing agency, or of a recipient of a part of the Bank’s financing, or any other party representing or acting on behalf of the Borrower, that is directly or indirectly involved in any part of: (i) the preparation of the TOR for the assignment; (iii) the selection process for the contract; or iii. the supervision of the contract, may not be awarded a contract, unless the conflict stemming from this relationship has been resolved in a manner acceptable to the Bank throughout the selection process and the execution of the contract.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered to the address below by email on or before September 11th, 2026, 14:30 hours (South African Time). All EOI’s must be marked “926/AUDA/DITIR/RESILIENTIRRIGATIONF/QCBS/2026 – Procurement of Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway” in the subject line of the email.

 

EOIs can also be sent by email, addressed to the address below. Interested Consultants may also obtain further information at the address below during office hours (09:00 - 17:00 South Africa time):

TÜRKYE

TÜRKYE PREPAREDNESS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCIES PROJECT

Loan No.: 9754-TR

Assignment Title: Software Development, Updating, Maintenance and Support Services for the Infectious Disease Surveillance and Early Warning System (ZC) Web and Mobile Applications

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TPPHEP/SBSGM/2026/CS/D.2.1.5.1/QCBS/1

1. The Republic of Türkiye has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Türkiye Preparedness for Public Health Emergencies Project (TPPHEP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (the “Services”) include the analysis, design, software development, testing, training, deployment, updating, maintenance and support of the Infectious Disease Surveillance and Early Warning System (ZC) Web Application and the development of a synchronized ZC Mobile Application. The assignment includes examination and migration of the existing systems; preparation of the Project Management Plan; analysis and requirements definition; UX/UI and technical design; development of disease-specific surveillance modules and an event management system; secure integrations with Ministry systems and external stakeholders; artificial-intelligence-supported early-warning and spatio-temporal analysis capabilities; testing, data migration, deployment and commissioning; training; and maintenance, operational support and additional development. The assignment is expected to be implemented over 30 (thirty) months and to require a multidisciplinary team of at least 16 personnel, as detailed in the TOR.

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR), including the Minimum Requirements Document (MRD), can be found at the following websites.

https://sbsgm.saglik.gov.tr/

https://www.saglik.gov.tr/

4. The Ministry of Health, General Directorate of Health Information Systems now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

5. A consulting firm is allowed to submit the Expression of Interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for Consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if Consultants choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, such associations may be in the form of a Joint Venture (in which all members shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or sub-consultants (for whose services the Consultant shall remain responsible). In the case of an association, the Consultants shall explain in the EOI submission: (a) the rationale for forming the association; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each Joint Venture member and/or each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment. Failure to provide this explanation may result in the association not being shortlisted. For shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of Joint Venture members will be taken into account; the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered.

6. The shortlisting criteria are as follows, in which the specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance:

i. General Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) in providing consulting services in the IT sector under contracts of comparable size. The Consultant shall demonstrate the successful completion, within the last five (5) years preceding the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest, of at least one software development project under a single contract with a value of at least USD 6,000,000 or equivalent. The project shall have included a data warehouse, artificial intelligence (AI), and other related software components.

ii. Specific Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) relevant to the assignment in providing similar services under contracts of comparable size. The Consultant shall demonstrate the successful completion, within the last five (5) years preceding the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest, of at least one software development project in the field of health information systems under a single contract with a value of at least USD 4,000,000 or equivalent. The project shall have included web-based and mobile applications, integration and interoperability with health information systems, data warehouse or high-volume health-data processing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) or spatio-temporal analysis, artificial-intelligence-supported early-warning capabilities, data migration, information-security arrangements, testing, commissioning, maintenance and operational support.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the EOI shortlisting stage, and CVs of Key Experts should not be submitted with the EOI.

7. To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting criteria, Consultants are requested to submit, at a minimum, the supporting documentation listed below. A Consultant firm may use only its own qualifications and experience, and not those of its parent, sister or subsidiary companies or its employees:

i. The firm’s incorporation, trade or registration documents issued by the competent government authority in the country of the firm;

ii. The firm’s company brochure, including its core areas of business and years in business; and

iii. Completed Form-1 (attached to this REOI) providing information on similar contracts. The information shall include the contract name and reference number, a brief description of the scope and main deliverables, the contract value and the amount attributable to the firm, the contract period, the name of the Client and country of assignment, and the Consultant’s role. Copies of completion certificates or Client references for completed contracts are not required with the EOI. At the subsequent proposal stage, the Client may request shortlisted Consultants to submit supporting completion certificates.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

9. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

10. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 10:00 to 17:30 (Türkiye time) on Business Days.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Ukraine

Name of Project: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant No.: TF0C5794

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Establishment and Operationalisation of Supervisory Boards in Vocational Education Institutions

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): LEARN-2.3-VET-SB

 

Ukraine has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (hereinafter –   the Services) include supporting the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in scaling up the establishment and operationalisation of at least 300 Supervisory Boards (SBs) in vocational education (VE) institutions nationwide. Supervisory Boards are intended to serve as structured platforms for cooperation between VE institutions, founders (local authorities), employers, and local communities. Their role includes strategic oversight, support to institutional development, and facilitation of alignment between training provision and labour market needs.

The Services are expected to commence in autumn 2026 and will be provided over a period of 12 months.

The required objective of the Services must be achieved by the Consultant within the agreed program and in accordance with the Ukrainian legislation, the World Bank’s policies and rules and requirements of the Terms of Reference (TOR), which is attached.

Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (hereinafter – Client/MOES) now invites eligible consulting firms (hereinafter – Consultants) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The evaluation of the expressions of interest provided by the Consultants will be carried out based on the following criteria:

Legal status

  • The company is registered as a legal entity in Ukraine or abroad (in the case of foreign company, the representative office/JV/consortium with local firm should exist by the date of the Contract signing)..

 

Core Business and Experience

  • At least 6 (six) years of experience in the education sector governance, institutional development, public administration reform, or related fields;
  • At least 4 successfully completed assignments during the last 6 years in one or more of the following areas:
    • capacity building programs;
    • governance reform;
    • institutional management support;
    • vocational education  or education sector projects.

In case of a JVCA, the Lead Member shall demonstrate substantial compliance with the above requirements, including at least:

  • 6 ( six) years of relevant experience; and
  • participation in at least 2 (two) relevant assignments.

The JVCA as a whole must meet all qualification requirements.

Financial stability

Consultancy Services for Establishment and Operationalisation of Supervisory Boards in Vocational Education Institutions

Contract LEARN-2.3-VET-SB

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$451 million provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

 

Under the GPE-financed institutional capacity activities Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (hereinafter referred to as MoES)  intends to engage a qualified Consultant to support the nationwide establishment and operationalisation of at least 300 Supervisory Boards in VE institutions. The Assignment will focus on scaling up implementation, strengthening institutional capacities, providing structured communication and training support, and introducing standardised monitoring and analytical tools to ensure evidence-based policy development.The Assignment shall be implemented over a period of twelve (12) months from the Effective Date of the Contract.

The Assignment is expected to be implemented in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable Ukrainian legislation.

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of the Assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in scaling up the establishment and operationalisation of at least 300 Supervisory Boards (SBs) in vocational education (VE) institutions nationwide.

Supervisory Boards are intended to serve as structured platforms for cooperation between VE institutions, founders (local authorities), employers, and local communities. Their role includes strategic oversight, support to institutional development, and facilitation of alignment between training provision and labour market needs.

Initial regulatory groundwork has already been undertaken by the Ministry. Model provisions, standard documentation templates, and role descriptions for Supervisory Boards have been developed or are under finalisation. Policy signalling and initial communication regarding SB establishment have been launched at the national level.

However, large-scale operationalisation of Supervisory Boards across VE institutions requires structured support. Challenges remain in consistent interpretation and application of the regulatory framework at the regional and institutional level; ensuring that trained individuals are those who will actively serve on Supervisory Boards; providing practical, legal and facilitation support during the first operational cycle of Boards; and establishing a unified monitoring and feedback mechanism connecting institutional governance to national policy refinement.

Specifically, the Assignment aims to:

1.   facilitate the practical implementation of the existing regulatory framework governing Supervisory Boards;

2.  strengthen institutional capacities of VE institution directors, designated SB secretaries, founders and SB members for effective governance;

3.  provide structured legal, methodological and facilitation support during the first operational cycle of Supervisory Boards;

4.    ensure coherent nationwide rollout through strategic communication and regional engagement;

5.  introduce standardized data collection and digital monitoring mechanisms to assess SB functionality;

6.  generate analytical evidence and policy recommendations to support further institutionalisation of Supervisory Boards within the national vocational education reform framework.

The Consultant shall achieve the above objectives in full compliance with applicable Ukrainian legislation, relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, and procurement and implementation requirements of the World Bank.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant shall provide comprehensive technical, organizational and analytical support to MoES for the nationwide establishment and operationalisation of Supervisory Boards (SBs) in VE institutions.

The Assignment shall include, but not be limited to, the following activities.

3.1 Overall Approach

The Assignment shall build upon the regulatory framework and standard documents already developed by MoES. It shall not redesign Supervisory Boards from scratch but shall focus on large-scale operationalisation, capacity building, and system-level integration.

The implementation logic shall follow a structured sequence:

  1. Dissemination and onboarding of institutions and founders;
  2. Capacity building and operational support;
  3. Formal establishment and activation of Supervisory Boards;
  4. Monitoring, data collection, analysis and policy integration.

The Consultant shall ensure that all training participants are directly involved in the establishment or operation of Supervisory Boards to guarantee immediate practical applicability.

3.2 Components

Component 1. Development of Scale-up Plan and Mobilisation of Expert Team

The Consultant shall:

  • Develop a detailed scale-up implementation plan for the establishment of at least 300 Supervisory Boards in accordance with the updated regulatory requirements effective from 2025, including VE institutions where Supervisory Boards previously existed under prior legislation;
  • Define clear sequencing, timelines, regional coverage and risk mitigation measures;
  • Mobilise and manage an expert team to deliver all components of the Assignment.
  • Ensure coordination with MoES and regional education authorities.

The scale-up plan shall include measurable milestones and a clear allocation of responsibilities.

Component 2. Strategic Communication and Stakeholder Engagement

The Consultant shall design and implement a targeted communication campaign to support nationwide rollout of Supervisory Boards.

The communication shall:

  • Clearly position Supervisory Boards within the ongoing vocational education  reform and the new Law on Vocational Education;
  • Explain their governance role (accountability, employer engagement, institutional autonomy);
  • Target directors, founders, SB members and regional authorities;
  • Engage employers and business associations as governance partners. Involve civil society organisations to support stakeholder engagement, transparency, and inclusiveness.
  • Incorporate insights from consultations (including focus group discussions, where appropriate) to tailor communication approaches to different stakeholder groups.

To achieve the above, the Consultant shall:

  • Develop and submit for MoES approval a Communication Strategy for the nationwide rollout of Supervisory Boards, including detailed action plan;
  • Produce and disseminate at least five (5) information and advocacy materials, including policy briefs, explanatory notes, and guidance materials, distributed in digital format and printed in a minimum print run of 1,000 copies each;
  • Develop and publicly distribute in digital format and printed in a minimum print run of 1,000 copies each a package of visual communication materials, including infographics explaining the role and functioning of Supervisory Boards;
  • Conduct at least ten (10) regional stakeholder briefings for VE institutions directors, founders, Supervisory Board members, and regional authorities;
  • Organise and conduct one (1) national conference on Supervisory Boards in hybrid format with a minimum of 500 participants.

Activities shall include publications, media materials, infographics, regional briefings, and one national conference. The MoES agreement to all communication materials shall be obtained prior to publishing.

Component 3. Capacity Building

The Consultant shall design and deliver a structured capacity-building programme consisting of:

  1. Twenty-five (25) regional in-person training seminars shall be conducted (one per region), with approximately 15 participants per seminar (total ~375 participants), including VE institutions directors, SB secretaries, and Supervisory Board members. Training venues shall be agreed with MoES, considering accessibility and the security situation. The Consultant shall ensure compliance with safety requirements,including the selection of appropriate venues with access to certified shelters,  basic emergency procedures, and flexibility to adapt the format if needed.

The training programme shall be designed in accordance with adult learning principles and the European approach to micro-credentials, and approved by MoES prior to launch. Each regional training seminar shall comprise a total of 12 academic hours (1 academic hour = 45 minutes), including 6 academic hours of in-person instruction and 6 academic hours of independent preparatory work, equivalent to 0.4 ECTS credits. For each training seminar, the Consultant shall define: target groups and participant eligibility criteria; measurable learning outcomes assessed against transparent standards; form of participation and type of assessment; and a Quality Assurance Plan incorporating participant and peer feedback as a basis for continuous improvement. The training shall be learner-centred and directly relevant to the operational needs of Supervisory Board members. Upon successful completion, participants shall receive certificates confirming the achieved learning outcomes.

  1. Development and launch of one official MoES online course hosted on an existing MoES-approved digital platform, targeting up to 2,000 registered participants nationwide, with at least 1,500 successfully completing the course and receiving certificates.

The online course shall be designed in accordance with the European approach to micro-credentials and adult learning principles. The total notional workload of the online course shall comprise 30 academic hours  (1 academic hour = 45 minutes), equivalent to 1 ECTS credit. The Consultant shall ensure that the course includes the following elements:

    • Target groups and participant eligibility criteria, ensuring relevance to the operational needs of Supervisory Board members, VE institutions directors, SB secretaries, and founders' representatives;
    • Learning outcomes, defined in a measurable and transparent manner, specifying the knowledge, skills and competences participants are expected to acquire upon completion;
    • Type of assessment and form of participation, ensuring that learning outcomes are assessed against transparent standards;
    • Quality Assurance Plan, incorporating learner feedback, peer review mechanisms, and procedures for continuous improvement of course content;
    • Certification, confirming achieved learning outcomes upon successful completion, issued through the MoES-approved digital platform.

The online course shall be designed in close cooperation with MoES as a standalone micro-credential with the possibility of stacking with other learning achievements within the broader VE governance professional development framework.

The trainings and online course shall focus on:

  • roles and responsibilities of SB members;
  • application of MoES-approved standard documents;
  • organisation of SB meetings and decision-making;
  • first-year operational challenges;
  • interaction between SBs, founders and institutional management.

The MoES agreement to a proposed online course curriculum shall be obtained prior to launch.

Component 4. Operationalisation, Monitoring and Policy Integration

This component shall focus on ensuring that Supervisory Boards are not only formally established but also function effectively.

The Consultant shall:

  • Support activation of at least 300 Supervisory Boards;
  • Provide structured legal consultations and facilitation support to institutions during the initial operational phase of Supervisory Boards. At least 100 legal consultations (each lasting 2 hours, approximately 20 consultations per month, delivered over a 5-month period according to the Time Schedule) should be provided to vocational education institutions and supervisory board members in online and in-person formats, with documentation and reporting on the results achieved through such consultations,under the capacity building component.
  • Develop, in close collaboration with MoES, a standardised data collection mechanism and monitoring instruments, and submit them for MoES approval prior to the commencement of data collection. The development of monitoring tools shall be initiated no later than Month 6 of the Assignment.
  • Collect and analyse data from at least 300 SBs and a minimum of 600 respondents;
  • Design and launch one national digital dashboard integrating regional data;
  • Produce one analytical report identifying implementation challenges, trends and good practices;
  • Produce one policy brief with recommendations for MoES regarding further support, regulatory refinement and institutionalisation of monitoring;
  • Organize one national forum “Supervisory Boards: One Year of Transformation” (hybrid format, minimum 500 participants).

This Scope ensures that Supervisory Boards are operationalised at scale, supported during their first implementation cycle, monitored through standardized tools, and embedded into long-term governance reform of the VE sector.

Reports Submission and Acceptance Procedure

The following procedure shall apply to all reports submitted under this Assignment: the Inception Report (Deliverable 1), the Strategic Communication and Stakeholder Engagement Report - Interim Report 1 (Deliverable 2), the Capacity Building Report - Interim Report 2 (Deliverable 3), and the Final Completion Report (Deliverable 4).

The exact format of the reports will be discussed and agreed upon with MoES, Implementation group, and where applicable with the World Bank, upon contract signing and before the commencement of the Assignment. All reports and deliverables will be submitted in minimum 2 (two) hard copies in English and 2 (two) hard copies in Ukrainian language. GOBI CONNECTIVITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT PREPARATION (P514972)

 

GFPP Grant No.: TF0D0692

 

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Feasibility Study and Preliminary Design of Ulaanbaatar - Mandalgovi Road Reconstruction Project

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): ZTYa/20260804057

 

The Government of Mongolia has received a grant financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), through the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), under Grant No. TF0D0692 to support the preparation of the Gobi Connectivity Improvement Project. The objective of the grant is to facilitate the preparation of a proposed project designed to enhance the efficiency, safety, and climate resilience of transport along the Ulaanbaatar–Mandalgovi road corridor, while strengthening institutional capacity for its sustainable maintenance.

 

The Ulaanbaatar–Mandalgovi (A0201) corridor is a nationally significant transport artery that forms a central spine in Mongolia’s north–south mobility network. Stretching approximately 272km, the corridor links Ulaanbaatar with the aimag centers of Tuv and Dundgobi while providing a gateway to southern regions with economies shaped by livestock, mining, tourism, and services. The road is also an important feeder into broader regional transport and trade corridors, including routes serving large scale mining operations and cross border freight movements.

 

Originally constructed in 2012–2013 to Asian Highway ClassIII standards, the existing two-lane road has reached a critical stage of deterioration. The corridor’s geometric design, originally intended for lower traffic volumes and slower heavy vehicle growth, no longer aligns with current or projected operational demands.

 

In response to these factors, the Ministry of Road and Transport (MRT) seeks a comprehensive feasibility assessment, including the preparation of preliminary design, that evaluates the potential of upgrading the A0201 corridor to a fourlane Class I standard. This upgrade would enhance freight fluidity, reduce travel times, strengthen supply chain reliability, and improve road safety outcomes. In line with the Government of Mongolia’s Action Plan for 2024–2028, which sets the objective of initiating the fourlane expansion of this corridor, the assessment and preliminary design will serve as the analytical backbone for subsequent safeguard instruments, procurement strategies, and engineering design stages, ensuring that the reconstruction approach is fit for purpose, fiscally prudent, and environmentally and socially responsible.

As a crosscutting requirement, the assignment will also encompass environmental and social due diligence tasks, including screening against the World Bank's Environmental and Social Standards (ESS1–ESS10), preparation of the Environmental and Social Management Plan (PESMP), and inputs into subsequent safeguard instruments such as a Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the consulting services for feasibility study and preliminary design can be found at the following website.

 

Tender.gov.mn

The Ministry of Road and Transport now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

1. General Experience

Minimum 10 years of experience in preparing feasibility studies and preliminary/detailed engineering design of major road infrastructure projects in cold climate regions, including economic/financial analysis and safeguard integration.

In addition, demonstrated experience in at least one assignment involving the preparation of environmental and social safeguard instruments for World Bank-financed projects or projects financed by comparable multilateral development banks, including at a minimum one of the following: Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), or Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP). Evidence should be provided in the firm's EoI.

 

2. Specific Experience in Similar Assignments

  • Proven experience in preparing feasibility studies and preliminary design of major road corridors during the last 5 years, with contract amount not less than USD 500,000 (five hundred thousand USD);
  • Experience in projects financed by international financial institutions (e.g., ADB, World Bank, JICA, EBRD, etc.) will be considered an advantage.
  • The consulting team must also include dedicated Environmental and Social Specialists with demonstrated experience applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent international safeguard/environmental and social risk management standards. At minimum, the team must demonstrate capacity to address environmental screening, social impact assessment, resettlement risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and GBV/SEA/SH risk management.

 

3. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” seventh edition dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 09.00 to 17.00 (GMT+8) on Business Day.  

 

The assignment will be carried out in compliance with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and the World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines. ESF competency will be assessed during the subsequent Request for Proposals (RFP) stage as part of the technical evaluation.

Assignment Title

CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO ESTABLISH A FISHERIES DATA COLLECTION AND STORAGE FRAMEWORK FOR COASTAL FISHERIES MANAGEMENT IN FSM

Reference No.

FM-NORMA-539887-CS-CQS

August 26, 2026

Deadline for EOI Submission

Selection Method

CQS

 

The Federated States of Micronesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience (PROPER), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services are for the assessment of existing coastal fisheries data systems and gaps and the design of a recommended coastal fisheries data management framework for future implementation. The assignment will cover the four FSM States of Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae and is expected to take approximately 12 months.

The FSM Department of Resources & Development (DRD), in collaboration with State Fisheries Departments, NORMA , now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

1. Objective and Scope of the Assignment

The objective of the consultancy is to assess existing coastal fisheries data systems and gaps, and to design a recommended data management framework for future implementation. The following areas are not within the scope of the assignment: 1) training, 2) conduct ecological field surveys, 3) build databases, 4) validate protocols, or and 5) produce management recommendations. These activities are intended to be undertaken under subsequent consultancies.

Stage

Main Activity

Expected Output / Focus

1

Desk Review and Data Inventory

Existing literature, research reports, available databases, catch and effort, landings, market, ecological data, and metadata catalogue.

2

Stakeholder Engagement

Fact-finding and prioritization with State fisheries departments, research institutions, and communities; information disaggregated by gender, age group, and fishing role where feasible.

3

Data Quality and Gap Assessment

Gap analysis and scoring matrix covering completeness, accuracy, timeliness, consistency, accessibility, and dataset quality tiers.

4

Institutional Assessment

Review of data-related capacity, systems, workflows, reporting, responsibilities, and data-sharing mechanisms.

5

Recommended Data Collection Protocols

Recommended SOPs for catch, effort, market, and biological data collection aligned with SPC, WCPFC, and FAO ASFIS references.

6

Data Storage, Access, and Governance Framework

Recommended database architecture, hosting, backup, user permissions, ownership, interoperability, sustainability, and accessibility arrangements.

7

State-Specific Ecological Assessment TORs

Four separate procurement-ready TORs for Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae, based on data assessment outcomes.

8

Ecological Assessment Data Needs Prioritization

Prioritized sequence of future State ecological data collection assessments, including maps and GIS coordinates of priority sites.

9

Data Management Implementation Roadmap

Phased implementation roadmap with estimated costs, sequencing, and dependencies.

10

Other Subsequent Consultancy TORs

Procurement-ready TORs for data training and mentoring, protocol validation, database build-out/deployment, and data entry mobile applications.

11

Final Report and Presentation

Final consultancy report, handover package, and presentation of findings.

3. Required Firm Experience and Shortlisting Criteria

Interested consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expressions of Interest should focus on firm-level qualifications and relevant experience. Key Experts will not be evaluated at this shortlisting stage.

Criterion

Indicative considerations

Suggested evidence

Relevant fisheries data management experience

Experience assessing and designing fisheries data systems, metadata catalogues, data quality frameworks, data gap assessments, and data governance arrangements.

Project descriptions, client references, outputs, dates, countries, and contract values.

Coastal fisheries and Pacific/small island context

Experience in coastal fisheries, community fisheries, ecological information needs, and Pacific Island or small island developing state contexts. FSM experience is preferred.

Examples of comparable assignments in Pacific Island countries or similar contexts.

Institutional and capacity assessment experience

Experience reviewing institutional workflows, data-sharing mechanisms, reporting responsibilities, and data-related capacity needs for public agencies.

Institutional assessment reports or project summaries.

Data standards and interoperability

Experience applying fisheries data standards, metadata, QA/QC, and relevant standards or references such as SPC coastal fisheries minimum datasets, WCPFC standards, FAO ASFIS codes, and other recognized ecological data methods.

Examples of standards-based data frameworks, metadata catalogues, or SOPs.

GIS and spatial prioritization

Experience in spatial data inventory, mapping, GIS prioritization, and preparation of maps and coordinates for ecological assessment planning.

GIS outputs, mapping work samples, and project references.

TOR and implementation roadmap preparation

Experience preparing procurement-ready TORs, implementation roadmaps, costed action plans, and phased system implementation recommendations.

Examples of TORs, roadmaps, or investment plans.

Stakeholder engagement

Experience consulting with government agencies, communities, research institutions, and fisheries stakeholders, including gender- and role-sensitive data collection where feasible.

Stakeholder engagement summaries and references.

4. Indicative Key Personnel

The firm should demonstrate that it can mobilize a qualified team. The TOR identifies the following indicative key personnel:

Key Personnel / Expertise

Description

Senior fisheries professional with expertise in data systems assessment and Pacific Island fisheries context. Minimum 10 years of experience. FSM or small islands experience preferred.

Data Management Specialist

Experience in data standards, metadata, gap analysis, QA/QC assessment, data-related capacity assessments, and institutional reviews of data systems. Minimum 10 years of experience. FSM or small islands experience preferred.

GIS and Spatial Data Specialist

Experience in spatial data inventory, gap analysis, and prioritization mapping. Minimum 5 years of experience. FSM or small islands experience preferred.

National Liaison Specialist

Knowledge of FSM institutions, fisheries sector, and stakeholder engagement. Minimum 5 years of experience.

Note: Detailed CVs are NOT required at this Stage. However, Firms may provide a brief staffing approach or indicate availability of the required expertise..

5. Selection Process, Associations, and Conflict of Interest

A consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection (CQS)  procedures set out in the  World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025.

Consulting firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment if selected.

Interested firms should provide information on any actual or potential conflict of interest arising from other assignments or conflicting involvement in related assignments.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the applicable provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations on conflict of interest, eligibility, and fraud and corruption.

6. Submission Requirements

The Expression of Interest should include the following information, preferably not exceeding 15 pages excluding annexes]:

  • Firm profile, legal status, country of registration, and contact details;
  • Description of the firm’s core business and years in business;
  • Summary of no more than five relevant assignments completed during the last 5 years, including client, country, contract value, duration, and firm role;
  • Evidence of experience in fisheries data management, coastal fisheries, metadata catalogues, data gap assessments, data governance, GIS mapping, and institutional assessment;
  • Brief statement on experience in FSM, Pacific Island countries, or small island developing states;
  • Description of any proposed association, joint venture, or sub-consultancy arrangement;
  • Statement confirming availability and ability to mobilize for a 12-month assignment involving travel to all four FSM States;
  • Conflict of interest declaration.

APPENDIX C - Summary Terms of Reference for Publication

FSM currently lacks nationally standardized approaches for fisheries data collection, storage, access, and governance. Prior to implementation investments, FSM requires an assessment of existing datasets, information systems, institutional arrangements, and data/ecological information gaps. The FSM Coastal Fisheries SAR 2023 is the foundational reference for identifying priority data and ecological assessment needs across Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae.

The assignment will produce a data inventory and metadata catalogue, data quality and gap assessment with scoring matrix, institutional capacity assessment focused on data-related capacity, recommended standardized data collection protocols, recommended data storage/access/governance framework, ecological assessment data needs prioritization, four State-specific ecological data collection TORs, a phased data management implementation roadmap, and procurement-ready TORs for subsequent implementation consultancies.

Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger (ci-après dénommé l’« Emprunteur ») a reçu de l’Association Internationale de Développement (AID)] (la « Banque ») sous la forme d’un crédit » (ci-après dénommé « fonds » en vue de financer le coût du PROJET LIRE NIGER (Learning Improvement for Results in Education) pour le programme la dynamisation du secteur éducatif post primaire, primaire, secondaire et de la formation professionnelle de modernisation, de développement de l’enseignement et de la formation professionnelle mis en œuvre par le Ministère de l’Education Nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des Langues (MEN/A/ PL).

Le Ministère de l’Education Nationale à travers le Projet Niger-Lire sollicite des offres fermées de la part de candidats éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour executer les travaux de construction des salles de classe dans les departements de Kantché, Tanout, Damagaram Takaya, Magaria, Mirriah et Dungass de la phase ouverte (Région de Zinder)

Les travaux sont répartis en neuf (09) lots distincts comme suit :

  • Lot 1 : Travaux de construction de 32 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes à Arikoua I, Ara Saboua, Gao Kollia 1, Magaria Quartier II, Gai Mixte dans les communes des Guidimouni, Magaria Et Wacha dans la région de Zinder ;
  • Lot 2 : Travaux de construction de 14 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes y compris les laboratoires aux CES Yékoua, CEG Makaouratchi dans les communes de Yekoua et Wacha dans la région de Zinder ;
  • Lot 3 : Travaux de construction de 12 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes y compris les laboratoires aux CEG 2 Matamèye, CES Gagaoua dans les communes de Matameye et Gangara dans la région de Zinder ;
  • Lot 4 : Travaux de construction de 14 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes y compris les laboratoires aux CEG Gouna, CEG Gojo Gojo dans les communes de Gouna et Dogo dans la région de Zinder ;
  • Lot 5 : Travaux de construction de 18 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes y compris les laboratoires aux CEG Koudouma, CEG Magaria Tounkour, CEG Didiki dans les communes de Droum et Zermou dans la région de Zinder ;
  • Lot 6 : Travaux de construction de 12 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes y compris les laboratoires aux CES Toumnia, CEG Zagon Dachi dans les communes de Dakoussa et Garagoumsa dans la région de Zinder ;
  • Lot 7 : Travaux de construction de 12 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes y compris les laboratoires aux CEG Maikonbarwa, CES Tirmini dans la Commune de Tirmini dans la région de Zinder ;
  • Lot 8 : Travaux de construction de 12 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes y compris les laboratoires aux CEG Alberkaram, CES Guidimouni dans les communes de Alberkaram et Guidimouni dans la région de Zinder ;
  • Lot 9 : Travaux de construction de 12 salles de classe et ouvrages connexes y compris les laboratoires aux CEG Takaye, CES FA Dungass dans la commune de Dungass dans la région de Zinder ;

            Adresse électronique : ucp@nigerlire.edu.ne avec copie à ayahaya@ nigerlire.edu.ne et asani@ nigerlire.edu.ne

1. Le Sénégal a obtenu dans le secteur de l’Education un financement de la Banque mondiale d'un montant équivalant à cent millions (100 000 000) $ USD pour financer le Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Educatif (PAPSE), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant « Consultant individuel pour appuyer le comité technique de la Refondation du Système Éducatif Sénégalais »..

2. Les services de consultant (« Services ») permettront de recruter un consultant individuel pour appuyer le comité technique de la Refondation du Système Éducatif Sénégalais pour apporter aux organes de gouvernance de la Refondation un appui méthodologique de haut niveau garantissant la cohérence, l'efficacité d'exécution et la redevabilité institutionnelle de la mise en œuvre, en contribuant aux indicateurs du Cadre de Résultats du PAPSE.

De façon spécifique et afin de veiller à l'opérationnalisation performante des orientations de la Refondation en appui des organes prévus par l'arrêté ministériel, le Consultant sera chargé (e) de:

  • doter la Refondation d'un cadre méthodologique intégré de pilotage opérationnel dans les quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours suivant le début de la mission ;
  • renforcer le fonctionnement du comité technique et des sous commissions, avec un taux de sessions techniquement préparées et capitalisées d'au moins 90 % ;
  • assurer un suivi consolidé de l'exécution et de la mobilisation des ressources, avec des rapports acceptés dans les délais convenus ;
  • garantir la capitalisation documentaire de la réforme, avec des livrables conformes aux exigences du MEN.

3. Le Coordonnateur du Projet d’Amélioration des Performances du Système Éducatif (PAPSE) invite les consultants individuels (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils disposent des qualifications requises et de l’expérience pertinente pour l’exécution desdits services.

À ce titre, les dossiers de manifestation d’intérêt devront comporter au moins : (i) un curriculum vitae détaillé et actualisé du Consultant, faisant ressortir ses qualifications académiques et professionnelles ; (ii) une présentation de l’expérience générale et spécifique du Consultant, notamment le nombre d’années d’expérience dans le domaine concerné ; (iii) des références pertinentes concernant l’exécution de missions similaires, dûment justifiées par des attestations de services faits, certificats ou tout autre document probant ; et (iv) une description des principales missions réalisées en lien avec les prestations objet de la présente mission, précisant notamment le rôle joué par le Consultant, la période d’exécution et, le cas échéant, le client ou l’institution bénéficiaire.

4. Les Consultants intéressées peuvent obtenir les termes de référence (TDR) en envoyant leur demande à l’adresse électronique suivante : bm.papse@education.sn .

5. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants intéressés que les dispositions relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts telles que décrites dans les paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 et suivants, du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) », daté du 1er Juillet 2016 révisé en septembre 2025, sont applicables.

6. Les Consultants individuels seront évalués sur la base de leurs qualifications, de leur expérience générale et spécifique ainsi que de leurs références pertinentes en rapport avec la mission. Les Consultants intéressés devront fournir les informations permettant d’apprécier leur aptitude à réaliser les services requis.

7. Un Consultant individuel sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultants Individuels (SCI), conformément aux dispositions du Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale applicables aux consultants individuels.

8. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations complémentaires à l’adresse suivante : PAPSE, 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor-Téléphone : (+221) 33 820 74 71-email : bm.papse@education.sn, tous les jours ouvrables de 9h30mn à 16h30mn TU.

9. Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées à l’adresse suivante : PAPSE au 2ème étage de l’immeuble CAC à Yoff, Cité Biagui, route de l’aéroport Léopold Sédar Senghor-Téléphone : (+221) 33 820 74 71–ou par email : bm.papse@education.sn, adressé au Coordonnateur du PAPSE, avec la mention « AMI N° SN-MEN-546836-CS-QCBS / C_PAPSE_239-Recrutement d'un Consultant individuel pour appuyer le comité technique de la Refondation du Système Éducatif Sénégalais», au plus tard  le mercredi 16 septembre 2026 à 10 h00mn TU.

Estimados señores:

1. El Programa de GESTION RESILIENTE DEL AGUA PARA RIEGO COMUNITARIO Y FAMILIAR a través del P178861 - CONTRATO DE PRÉSTAMO N° 9643-BO, tiene como objetivo la gestión integrada de recursos hídricos con enfoque de cuenca e incrementar la resiliencia ante la variabilidad climática de familias rurales vulnerables en microcuencas seleccionados. Sus objetivos específicos son: i) Apoyar a las familias más vulnerables en el acceso a agua para riego y el uso eficiente del recurso hídrico como respuesta al déficit hídrico, a través de la implementación de sistemas de riego menor y el fortalecimiento de la gestión y organización, para contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria. ii) Contribuir a asegurar la disponibilidad de agua para la conservación y recuperación de cuencas, a través de proyectos de manejo integral de cuencas (forestación, manejo de praderas nativas, vigiñas de infiltración, etc.) en cuencas con alta demanda hídrica y con riesgos de escasez hídrica, iii) Proteger las áreas productivas vulnerables a través de proyectos de gestión de riesgos (barreras vivas acompañadas de obras de encauzamiento, muros de hormigón ciclópeo y hormigón, diques longitudinales, etc.) que regulen, conduzcan y minimicen los impactos producidos por las inundaciones, torrenteras y crecidas,  iv) Promover una nueva Cultura del Agua para la Vida en el área de intervención del Programa, a través de acciones de formación, capacitación y sensibilización en niños, jóvenes, productores, regantes, técnicos y profesionales de los Gobiernos Autónomos Municipales (GAM) y Gobiernos Autónomos Departamentales (GAD), y otros actores de la cuenca, que contribuya a garantizar la sostenibilidad de las inversiones, v). Fortalecer la gobernanza local para la gestión y manejo sostenible del agua en las cuencas de intervención del programa, a través de la planificación hídrica estratégica y la elaboración de estudios de inversión que den respuesta a las demandas y necesidades en las cuencas.
