NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Engineer (2)

No: MW-NLGFC-563895-CS-INDIV/ MW-NLGFC-563897-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring two Project Engineer on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of two (2) Project Engineer tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for two (2) Project Engineer) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Project Engineer (Specialist) shall lead, coordinate and support local authorities and all relevant ministries, departments and agencies in the design and implementation of the project. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will lead and have approving authority for preparing and/or interpreting designs, bill of quantities (BoQs), tendering and engineering cost estimates prepared. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will work closely with relevant district authorities, including district engineers, other officers and specialists in the PIT, including safeguards, Project Coordinator, NLGFC, MoLGRD and other relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to supervision consultants. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will support monitoring of the sub-projects and will address and manage technical engineering questions in local investment projects implemented by the local authorities that are financed by GESD 2.0. 

 

  1. Duties and Responsibilities of the Project Engineer (Consultant)

 

The Project Engineers (Consultants) will be responsible for providing technical leadership and engineering oversight to ensure that project activities are planned, designed, implemented, monitored, and completed in accordance with approved specifications, quality standards, budget, schedule, and applicable regulations.

 

Specific tasks will include the following:

 

  1. Coordinate and support all engineering functions and activities related to infrastructure construction and rehabilitation in the local authorities, namely Department of Planning and Development and Department of Public Works;
  2. Support data collection for all proposed sub-project sites to aid development and customisation of architectural designs, production of BoQs and engineering estimates, tendering processes and ensuring that designs are in conformity with results of site-specific resilience and risk related investigations and analysis;
  3. Ensure timely and correct submission of information into the Public Management Information System (PMIS) by local authorities;
  4. Provide technical support to the Local Authorities in project selection, reviewing annual investment plans, works designs, BoQs, costs estimate, tendering, supervision and monitoring;
  5. Coordinate topographic surveys for the design of infrastructure to be developed under the Project;
  6. Support local authorities in conducting initial site investigation;
  7. Facilitate the production of location maps and sketches if necessary for all engineering sites that need maintenance and repair (selected as subprojects under GESD 2.0);
  8. Support and if necessary lead the review and approval of submissions by design engineers, including ensuring timely submission of the same;
  9. Support and if necessary lead design options stakeholder consultations with communities and relevant departments so that their inputs are incorporated in the designs to ensure acceptance and ownership of solutions to be developed;
  10. Conduct technical supervision of all construction works ensuring that the works are implemented to the required standards, within the assigned cost and time;
  11. Check Supervision Consultant’s work so as to conduct verification of contractors’ payment claims for works done;
  12. Manage changes to engineering constructions works ensuring that any changes have no adverse effect on the project and they are undertaken following project works change protocols, including documentation;
  13. Facilitate preparation of work plans and budgets for local investment projects to ensure relevance to outputs and outcomes of local investment project;
  14. Support the preparation of schedule of works and materials for project activities in collaboration with relevant stakeholders;
  15. Review and assess contractors’ and consultants’ payment certificates for engineering works
  16. Prepare and conduct training programs for Local Authority technical staff involved in contract and procurement management; and other related activities as directed by the PIT;
  17. Ensure compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements;
  18. Liaise with other project specialists and officers, including safeguards, occupational health & safety, procurement, and advise the PIT on all construction Engineering technical related matters;
  19. Collect projects’ progress reports from the LAs, liaise with the monitoring & evaluation officer in the PIT in producing reports for project activities, consolidate them and submit them to PIT/PC, Executive Director and World Bank Task Team;
  20. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual engineering project progress reports and other reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and the World Bank Task Team.
  21. Facilitating the review of Annual Investment Plans (AIPs) for Local authorities and provide guidance on cost and time estimates.

 

  1. Deliverables

 

Deliverables for the assignment correspond to the duties and responsibilities above. Specifically, they will comprise:

 

  1. Timely review of AIPs submitted by local authorities, including review of cost and time estimates;
  2. Reviewed and approved engineering designs and drawings.
  3. Technical specifications and BoQs.
  4. Engineering project progress reports and other reports timely compiled
  5. Site inspection reports.
  6. Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) reports.
  7. Defects and corrective action reports.
  8. Monthly and quarterly progress reports, aligned with PMIS information.
  9. Physical progress monitoring reports.
  10. Work completion certificates.

 

  1. Performance Criteria

 

The following performance criteria will be used to assess the performance of the Project Engineer annually and based upon these assessments the contract with the project (GESD 2.0) may be continued or terminated:

  • 100% of required technical reports submitted on time.
  • At least 95% compliance with approved engineering specifications and quality standards.
  • Site inspections conducted according to approved supervision schedules.
  • 100% of contractor payment certificates reviewed and processed within agreed timelines.
  • All identified defects and non-compliance issues addressed within specified corrective action periods.
  • Minimal cost and schedule overruns attributable to technical deficiencies.
  • No major engineering failures or quality-related incidents.
  • Timely completion and handover of project infrastructure.
  • PMIS utilization by local authorities.

 

  1. Qualifications, Skills and Expertise

 

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

 

  1. Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering/Architecture/Quantity Surveying
  2. Master’s Degree in Construction/Engineering related field and ;
  3. Registration with an approved professional body, such as Malawi Engineering Institution/Board of Architects and Quantity Surveyors
  4. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience;
  5. Excellent communications, writing/reporting skills;
  6. Proficiency in computer aided design packages (AutoCAD, ArchCAD, GIS etc)
  7. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Microsoft Project etc.);
  8. Strong organizational, self-starting and communications skills;
  9. Experience working with government institutions and organizations; working experience with local authorities in Malawi is considered an advantage;
  10. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  11. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills

 

  1. Reporting Arrangements

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social and Economic Services at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ in implementation of GESD 2.0 project.

 

  1. Location of Assignment

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Engineer (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to local government authorities in Malawi where the Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

 

  1. Duration of Assignment

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September 2026.

The National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) is committed to diversifying Gender equality in its operations and strongly encourages women to apply for the above vacant position.

recruitment@nlgfc.gov.mw/ ed@nlgfc.gov.mw

TÜRKYE FLOOD AND DROUGHT MANAGEMENT PROJECT (P179313)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FOR PROCUREMENT SPECIALIST

The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MoAF) of Türkiye, Directorate General of Water Management (GDWM) has received financing from the World Bank (“the Bank”) toward the cost of the Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

DGWM serves as the co-implementing agency for the Project. The overall objective of the Project is to support climate change projections, determine their impacts on scenario-specific flood and drought disasters, and improve and expand existing early warning systems. It aims to strengthen the technical and operational capacities of all stakeholders for the uninterrupted and effective operation of the system.

DGWM has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within its administrative structure to manage the project activities. DGWM intends to engage a Procurement Specialist (individual consultant) to provide technical support to the DGWM PIU in managing procurement activities under the Project. The Procurement Specialist will be responsible for planning and providing procurement services, including preparing procurement plans, bidding documents, evaluation reports, training activities and monitoring contract performance.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR), including the qualification requirements and scope of work for the assignment, can be found at the following web page address: https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/SYGM/Sayfalar/Detay.aspx?SayfaId=187

Hiring Methodology

The Procurement Specialist will be selected through the ‘Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants’ method in accordance with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023)”. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.

Individuals currently working as procurement consultants on another World Bank-financed project may also compete, provided they meet the requirements for early termination of their existing contracts to avoid disruption in project implementation.

Duration and Place of Work

The Procurement Specialist is expected to commence work in September 2026 with a one-year contract having a two-month probation period. The Procurement Specialist will work on a full-time basis and will be located in Ankara, with potential travel to project sites as required.

Application Procedure

Interested eligible candidates should submit their CVs in both English and Turkish (in the format specified on the website), clearly indicating the position title and the reference number TR-DGWM-564534-CS-INDV in the subject line.

Applications must be delivered in PDF format via e-mail to the address below no later than September 9, 2026, at 16:00 (local time).

Kyrgyz Republic 

Enhancing Resilience in Kyrgyzstan Project (ERIK, ERIK AF)

Loan No. IDA 66870 Grant No. IDA D6550

Tender No. KG-CS/CQS-09

Assignment Title: Consulting services «Enhancing Claims Management for the Mandatory Insurance of Residential Buildings Against Emergency Situations in Kyrgyzstan»

Component 3 of the project «Enhancing Resilience in Kyrgyzstan (ERIK)»: Enhancing Financial Protection and Insurance Against Natural Disaster Risks.

Responsible agencies: the Financial Market Regulation and Supervision Service under the Ministry of Economy and Commerce of the Kyrgyz Republic and State Insurance Organization OJSC.

The main objective of the Component is to support the efforts of the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic in reducing the financial impacts of emergencies.

To support the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic, the State Insurance Organization (SIO), and any future potential collective insurance pool to strengthen the institutional and operational foundations of claims management for the mandatory residential insurance in Kyrgyzstan.

Specifically, the assignment aims to:

•Analyze the current state and prepare proposals for modernizing claims management procedures to increase the efficiency of claim administration and loss assessment methodology, including development of internal regulations for claim settlement;

•Planning surge capacity to manage a high volume of claims following major disaster events;

•Reviewing OJSC “SIO” existing IT system and developing recommendations for the structure of claims processing for mandatory residential building insurance through OJSC “SIO” IT system;

•Deliver capacity-building to Gosfinnadzor, OJSC “SIO” and other relevant stakeholders on the proposed changes to the procedures and on the use of disaster relief bonds.

The consultant will deliver technical and advisory services on enhancing claims management for the mandatory insurance of residential buildings against Emergency Situations in Kyrgyzstan.

The start of the assignment is scheduled for October 2026. The expected duration of the assignment is approximately 6 months after the contract is signed with the selected Consultant and 12 months of advisory support after completion of the main contract.

The estimated budget for the assignment, including all taxes (including local taxes), should not exceed $250,000.00 USD.

Detailed terms of reference (TOR) can be found at the following links www.zakupki.gov.kg (Tenders announced by Projects), www.donors.kg  or at the address below.

The project "Enhancing Resilience in Kyrgyzstan" invites eligible consulting companies (Consultants) to express their interest in providing services: Enhancing Claims Management for the Mandatory Insurance of Residential Buildings Against Emergency Situations in Kyrgyzstan.

Interested companies must provide information confirming their qualifications and relevant experience in providing services. At the Expressions of Interest stage, the Consultant must meet the following minimum requirements:

  1. Experience in Insurance Claims Management: Demonstrated experience in successfully implementing at least two (2) similar projects over the past five (5) years, including:
  • Analysis of insurance claims settlement processes;
  • Development or revision of methodologies for damage assessment and determination of insurance compensation payments.
  1. Experience in Disaster Insurance and Work with Government Agencies: Proven experience in catastrophe risk projects, specifically at least two projects/programs related to property insurance products and/or claims settlement mechanisms for natural disasters. Experience working with government authorities will be considered a significant advantage.

After evaluating the received expressions of interest from consulting companies, only the most qualified company (with the highest score) will be invited to submit technical and financial proposals. Key people will not be assessed at the expression of interest stage.

Consultants should pay attention to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of Section III of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers issued in July 2016, revised in February 2025 (Procurement Regulations), which set out the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other companies to expand their qualifications, but must clearly state that the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultants. In the case of a joint venture, all partners in the joint venture must be collectively or individually responsible for the implementation of the assignment.

The consultant will be selected in accordance with the CQS - selection based on the qualifications of the consultant specified in the Procurement Regulations.

Special Notice on the Selection of a Financial Accountant WSIP-1-AF

Organization:   Project Implementation Unit of the Committee for Housing and Communal Services under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan

Project:            Water Supply and Sanitation Investment Project in Tajikistan (Phase-1) 

                        Additional Funding (AF)

Position:         Financial Accountant

Country:           Republic of Tajikistan

Grant No:         No E 0950-001 Tj

Released:          July 24 , 2026

 

  1. INTRODUCTION

The Water Supply and Sanitation Investment Project (WSIP-1), approved by the World Bank's Board of Executive Directors on June 23, 2022. WSIP-1 represents the first phase of the Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Investment Program and aims to improve access to safe and reliable water services in selected rural and peri-urban areas of the southwestern Khatlon region, taking into account climate risks. The project focuses on areas with limited access to safely managed water services, high dependence on poor water sources, high levels of poverty, and limited investment.

WSIP-1 will receive additional funding in the form of a grant from the European Union to help achieve the project's development objectives. The additional financing will help fill the funding gap and expand water supply services in priority settlements in the Vakhsh, Vose, Balkha and Dusti districts. The total financing of the project will improve water supply systems in 126 villages, covering about 280,000 people, and strengthen the institutional capacity of the housing and communal services.

The Committee for Housing and Communal Services (CHCS) of the Republic of Tajikistan established a Project Implementation Unit (PDC) in the field of drinking water supply and wastewater management, responsible for the implementation of Component 1 activities within the framework of additional financing. The PIU will have overall responsibility for the consolidation of financial statements, including interim financial statements (IFRs), reporting on the progress of the project and monitoring, as well as compliance with environmental, social and fiduciary requirements in accordance with the Project Implementation Manual (POM).

Component 1 provides for the financing of a set of activities aimed at institutional strengthening and capacity development of water sector institutions at the national, regional and local levels to ensure sustainable service delivery in the project area. Under Component 1, additional funding covers activities to strengthen the institutional capacity of the Housing and Utilities Sector, including the construction of a new training center/laboratory, an administrative building of the Vakhsh Utility Company, as well as the provision of technical assistance for the development of internal regulatory documents, operational procedures and support tools for SUE "Housing and Public Utilities" and water supply enterprises.

  1. OBJECTIVE

The purpose of the assignment is to ensure effective financial management and accounting within the Project. The Financial Accountant is responsible for maintaining accurate accounting, managing the funds and assets of the Project, preparing financial statements, complying with the requirements of the World Bank and the legislation of the Republic of Tajikistan, as well as ensuring effective internal control in accordance with the Project Implementation Manual.

 

  1. DURATION OF THE CONTRACT

The deadline for commencement of the task will begin in September 2026 and will initially be 6 months, including a three-month probationary period. The extension of the contract will be carried out by the Director of the PIU, subject to satisfactory performance and approval by the World Bank. The Financial Accountant will be directly subordinate to the Director of the PIU CHCS.

 

  1.  REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

The financial accountant should preferably have experience in implementing similar projects financed by the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), the European Union (EU), or other international development partners. The candidate should have a good understanding of public financial management and infrastructure project implementation, especially in the areas of water, sanitation, housing or utilities, and have at least ten (10) years of practical work experience.

Minimum requirements:

Qualification criteria

Requirements

Education

University degree (bachelor's degree or higher) in accounting, finance, economics, business administration, or a related field.

General professional experience

At least five (7) years of progressively responsible professional experience in accounting, financial management, or financial reporting. Practical knowledge of 1C is required.

Required experience and knowledge

A minimum of three (3) years of experience in financial management, allocation, and reporting of international financial institutions and donor-funded projects is required. Experience with the World Bank is an asset.

Knowledge of accounting and tax legislation

In-depth knowledge of accounting, taxation and financial legislation of the Republic of Tajikistan.

Professional competencies

Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks, and meet strict reporting deadlines.

Core competencies

Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.

Language

Fluency in written and spoken Tajik and Russian languages. Practical knowledge of English, especially for communicating with international development partners and preparing financial documentation, is considered an advantage.

Interested candidates should submit the following documents:

  • Resume (CV) containing information about education, work experience and qualifications
  • Copies of academic diplomas and professional certificates (in the field, etc.)

  • L’intitulé de la mission de consultant : Recrutement d'un cabinet pour la mise à jour de la Plateforme intégrée de télé déclaration et gestion des données du secteur extractif
  • N° de Prêt/Crédit/Don : Prêt n° IDA-73180-SN (CREDIT A) et 73190-SN (CREDIT B)
  • N° de référence (selon le Plan de Passation des marchés):  SN-ANSD-SN-548311-CS-CQS

 

1. Le présent appel public à manifestation d’intérêt fait suite à l’Avis Général de Passation des Marchés paru dans le quotidien « Le Soleil » n° 16 169 du 24 avril 2024.

 

2. Le gouvernement du Sénégal a obtenu un  financement de la Banque mondiale  dans le cadre du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ces fonds pour effectuer des paiements au titre du marché suivant: « Recrutement d'un cabinet pour la mise à jour de la Plateforme intégrée de télé déclaration et gestion des données du secteur extractif ».

 

3. Les  services de consultant (« Services ») prévus consistent à concevoir, développer et mettre en place une plateforme numérique intégrée, performante et durable permettant la collecte, la centralisation, la sécurisation et l'exploitation analytique exhaustive des données du secteur extractif, en conformité complète avec les exigences de la Norme ITIE 2023 et les standards de gouvernance numérique de l'État.

 

Pour ce faire les taches spécifiques suivantes seront réalisées par le cabinet :

 

  • Mettre en place un système intégré de collecte automatisée des données provenant des différentes sources (administrations publiques, entreprises extractives, institutions collectrices)
  • Centraliser et normaliser toutes les données fiscales, administratives et opérationnelles du secteur extractif dans une base de données unique et fiable
  • Implémenter des mécanismes robustes de validation, réconciliation et contrôle qualité des données
  • Générer automatiquement des tableaux de bord dynamiques et interactifs permettant l'analyse fine du secteur extractif
  • Produire automatiquement des rapports conformes aux exigences ITIE avec indicateurs, statistiques et analyses sectorielles
  • Mettre à disposition un portail public de consultation des données conformément aux exigences de transparence
  • Assurer l'interopérabilité du système avec d'autres bases de données publiques existantes (e-Tax, douanes, impôts, etc.)
  • Garantir la souveraineté des données avec hébergement sécurisé sur les infrastructures numériques de l'État
  • Mettre en place des mécanismes de sécurité robustes (chiffrement, authentification forte, audit trail complet)

Chapter III Technical Requirements

 

I. Scope of Services and Term

1. Scope of Services: The supplier shall be responsible for executing the "2026 Guangdong Province Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Publicity Week and Green Food Publicity Month" event (in the second half of 2026), organized and planned by the Buyer. Through professional designs of the stage, exhibition booths, etc., the supplier shall carry out science popularization and publicity for agricultural product quality and safety, as well as promotional campaigns for green food, to raise public awareness of agricultural product quality and safety.

2.Term of Services: The service period for this project is approximately 3 months, calculated from the effective date of the procurement contract until all event services are fully completed, and the final acceptance and settlement are concluded. The supplier must ensure that the corresponding work is completed before all key milestones.

II. Service Content and Requirements

The supplier shall provide a full-process integrated service for this project, covering professional event design, venue setup and materials provision, science popularization promotional materials and supplies, event logistics support, as well as event publicity and media coverage. The specific service contents include but are not limited to:

(I) Service Support for the 2026 Guangdong Province Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Publicity Week and Green Food Publicity Month

1. Event Design, Venue Setup, and Materials Provision

1.1 Venue Rental:
The event venue shall be designated by the Buyer, located in the space near the atrium of Jiangmen Darong City. The exact area shall be subject to the official demarcated scope by the final venue provider. The venue must be able to accommodate 28 standard exhibition booths, 2 float booths, the main stage, and the audience seating area. The rental period is 2 days, and the fee includes the use of a large screen and basic power supply.

The unit price for the venue rental is fixed at RMB 5,000 per day, with a total cost of RMB 10,000 for two days (in words: Ten Thousand Yuan only). This fee already includes the rental cost during the setup period.

The event is tentatively scheduled for 2 consecutive days in the second half of 2026 (initially planned to include one day on Friday and one day on Saturday; the exact dates shall be subject to the Buyer's final confirmation).

1.2 Stage Setup:

It shall include at least the following facilities:
a. One set of sound system: 2 speakers + 1 audio mixer + 6 handheld microphones (speech mics) + 1 audio engineer (the audio engineer is only required for the morning session on the first day of the event);
b. Stage perimeter: Decoration for the front backdrop and side wing panels of the stage;
c. Podium: Provision of a podium, complete with tabletop decoration (floral arrangements, tablecloths, etc.).

All setup materials must comply with national energy-saving, environmental protection, and low-carbon standards. Recyclable materials shall be prioritized to ensure the smooth execution of the event.

1.3 Event Design and Production:

Layout Planning:
The event site shall consist of a stage area, audience seating area, and exhibition area. The specific dimensions are as follows:

Stage: 7m (L) × 5m (W), equipped with a 5m (L) × 3.8m (H) LED display screen;

Audience Seating Area: 30 seats arranged in 3 rows × 10 columns. After the morning session on the first day, the chairs will be removed to make space for 2 floats;

Exhibition Area: 28 standard exhibition booths, each measuring 1.2m (L) × 0.6m (W), arranged around the atrium, on both sides of the stage, and directly in front of the stage;

Floats: 2.5m (L) × 0.7m (W).

The design proposal must treat all event areas, including the stage, as a cohesive whole for integrated design. This is to ensure an organic connection between visual aesthetics and traffic flow, reflecting unity and professionalism. During the design phase, full consideration must be given to pedestrian aisles, clear lines of sight, and product display requirements. During the setup phase, adjustments and optimizations shall be made based on actual on-site conditions to maximize space utilization and exhibition impact.

Design Theme:
The design style must deeply integrate the characteristics of green food and Lingnan culture, as well as modern agriculture. It should align with the theme of agricultural product quality and safety publicity to create a distinct and positive event image.

Craftsmanship and Materials:
All production materials must comply with relevant national standards and regulations for energy conservation, environmental protection, and low-carbon practices. Recyclable or reusable materials shall be prioritized.

Design Deliverables:
The supplier shall submit a complete design proposal, including but not limited to the following: overall and partial renderings (must reflect different angles and details), stage design renderings, exhibition booth renderings (with detailed dimensions and material specifications), float graphic design drafts, wayfinding signage design drafts (e.g., floor decals), full-process event PPT (including dynamic video for the launch sequence), and no less than 2 versions of the main visual poster suitable for different online and offline scenarios (e.g., print, screen display, social media). All design proposals must be implemented only upon the Buyer's written approval.

1.4 Exhibition Area Materials Provision:

Production Requirements for Exhibition Booths and Floats:

28 Exhibition Booths: The booths will primarily feature a wooden frame structure, including the production of booth fascias/signboards, etc.

2 Floats: The main function of the floats is publicity and attracting visitors, providing photo opportunities for the audience and tourists. The decorations must be securely fixed using lightweight, eco-friendly materials to ensure the safety of all personnel on-site.

Production Requirements for Wayfinding Signage:

Wayfinding signage that aligns with the event's on-site theme must be produced, including floor decals, directional signs, etc. These are to effectively guide the flow of visitors to the booths for viewing and tasting, thereby ensuring the overall success of the event.

2. Science Popularization Promotional Materials and Supplies

2.1 Printing of Science Popularization Brochures:

Print 1,000 copies of clear, full-color folded brochures. The content will be provided by the Buyer. The layout, as well as the material and style of the final print, must be implemented only upon the Buyer's approval.

2.2 Quiz Materials for the Science Popularization Zone:

Technical Requirements: Prepare relevant materials to ensure the smooth execution of 4 science popularization interactive quiz sessions over the 2-day event. All materials (including prizes and promotional tote bags) must be of qualified quality and safe to use. The promotional tote bags must feature the Green High-Quality Agricultural Products logo and an information inquiry QR code.

Specific Requirements: Includes 1 spinning wheel with a stand (for the public to draw question numbers on-site), 400 prizes (aligned with the promotional theme, must be green food products, with an average unit price not exceeding RMB 10), and 1,000 promotional tote bags.

3. Event Logistics Support

3.1 Exhibition Area Supporting Facilities:
The exhibition booth design must fully consider the display characteristics of the agricultural product industry. It should rationally plan functional areas such as the product tasting zone, freezer/refrigerator storage area, and centralized storage space. Normal water and power supply must be guaranteed for all areas.

a. Storage and Mailing of Goods for Participating Green High-Quality Agricultural Product Enterprises: The supplier shall be responsible for the mailing, receiving, and storage of agricultural products from participating enterprises before, during, and after the event. The supplier must also assist participating enterprises in transporting the agricultural products to the designated exhibition area. The supplier is responsible for the safe custody of the agricultural products during the event and shall bear the corresponding insurance liability. After the event, the supplier shall safely transport the agricultural products back to the designated location of the original providing units.

b. Rental of 1 Freezer: During the event, 1 freezer shall be rented for on-site preservation of chilled/fresh agricultural products.

c. Event Drinking Water: The brand must meet the Buyer's requirements (C'estbon, Nongfu Spring, Dinghu Mountain Spring, or brands of equivalent grade). The provision includes 1 water dispenser, 12 barrels of bottled water (18.9L/barrel), and 4 cases of bottled water (210ml/24 bottles per case × 2 cases; 380ml/24 bottles per case × 2 cases).

3.2 Audience Seating:

To meet the audience seating needs at the event site, 30 seats shall be set up. At least 31 chairs must be provided on-site (including no less than 10 folding chairs with backrests).

3.3 Makeup and Styling for the Event MC:

The Event MC will be provided by the Buyer, but the supplier shall be responsible for ensuring the makeup and styling of the MC on the day of the event.

3.4 On-site Event Support:

The supplier shall purchase insurance for this event to guarantee the safety of personnel and property during the event period.

During the event, the supplier must arrange no less than 2 staff members to be stationed on-site for emergency response. Their responsibilities include conducting safety inspections for electricity usage, performing emergency equipment repairs, handling emergencies, assisting enterprises with the loading and unloading of goods, and addressing various on-site inquiries and unexpected issues.

4.Event Publicity and Media Coverage

The supplier shall utilize diversified media formats and high-quality visual content to comprehensively enhance the breadth and depth of the event's communication.

4.1 Graphic and Text Feature Publicity

During the contract period, the supplier shall plan and publish no less than 1 high-quality original publicity article. The content of the article must be approved by the Buyer before publication. Furthermore, within one working day after the conclusion of the first day of the event, the article must be published on at least 3 provincial-level or above mainstream news media platforms and 2 local mainstream news media platforms in Jiangmen (such as authoritative news websites, mobile clients, newspapers, etc.).

4.2 Short Video Production and Promotion

Content Production:

Before and after the event, the supplier shall respectively plan, shoot, and produce no less than 1 creative short video each (2 videos in total). The video content should focus on the themes of agricultural product quality and safety, as well as the Green Food Publicity Week. The pre-event promotional video should be around 60 seconds in length, and the post-event summary video should be around 150 seconds, both conforming to mobile-friendly communication patterns.

Publication and Promotion:

The short videos must be published on at least 2 provincial-level or above mainstream media platforms (or their official new media accounts) and 2 local mainstream media platforms in Jiangmen (or their official new media accounts) (e.g., Douyin, WeChat Channels, Weibo, etc.). The total follower base of the media agency undertaking the publication or its publishing account on the corresponding platform must be no less than 50,000 to ensure basic coverage. The video content must be approved by the Buyer before publication.

 

(II) Collection and Organization of Publicity Outcomes, Summary Report, and Assistance with Project Acceptance

The supplier shall be responsible for organizing materials and establishing a complete archive of publicity outputs, summary reports, and relevant supporting documents. This includes the collection of publicity outcomes from various platforms and the statistical analysis of data such as readership/view counts.

The supplier shall draft an event summary and publicity outcomes report to evaluate the effectiveness of the publicity campaign in raising public awareness of agricultural product quality and safety in the host city, etc.

(III) Other Requirements

1.The supplier shall be responsible for the venue rental and stage setup for this event (the venue shall be designated by the Buyer).

2.During the service period, the supplier must ensure the quality and safety of all materials used for the event during their utilization, and maintain cleanliness at the event site throughout the event period.

3.During both the preparation and execution phases of the event, the supplier must dynamically adjust the on-site layout according to the Buyer's requirements.

4.After the event, the supplier shall be responsible for restoring the venue to its original condition and properly disposing of solid waste generated during the event.

5.All the above-mentioned services shall be submitted to the Buyer for review and may only be executed upon the Buyer's approval.

III. Response Time

During the event service period, the supplier shall provide satisfactory on-site services and resolve any arising issues at any time. In the event of an emergency, the response time shall not exceed 10 minutes, and the issue must be resolved within 1 hour.

IV. Deliverables

The service provider shall submit the publicity campaign outputs and summary report to the Provincial Project Office, including but not limited to the event summary report and relevant supporting documents.

All data, reports, converged media products, and research outcomes generated in the performance of this consulting task, along with their related intellectual property rights, shall be owned by the Buyer.

V. Support Provided by the Buyer

1.The Buyer will work closely with the service provider, designate a dedicated liaison, and provide relevant materials and other support to the service provider.

2.The service provider shall work closely with other relevant participating parties of this sub-project.

VI. Assessment and Evaluation Methods

1.Fully complete all the above-mentioned service contents;

2.Submit the deliverables on time and in full;

3.Take no less than 50 high-definition photos; publish no less than 2 short videos;

5.The satisfaction rate of participants for each event shall be no less than 90%.

15.1 The Supplier shall deliver the Goods and perform the Services in accordance with the schedule specified by the Buyer in the "Schedule of Requirements for Goods".

15.2 If, during the performance of the Contract, the Supplier encounters circumstances that may delay the timely delivery of the Goods or the performance of the Services, the Supplier shall promptly notify the Buyer in writing of the fact of the delay, the likely duration thereof, and the causes thereof. Upon receipt of such notice, the Buyer shall evaluate the situation as soon as possible and determine whether to extend the time for delivery at its discretion and whether to assess liquidated damages for delay. Any extension shall be mutually agreed upon through a modification of the Contract.

15.3 Except as provided in Article 18, unless an extension has been granted without the assessment of liquidated damages pursuant to Article 15.2, the Supplier's delay in delivery shall be subject to liquidated damages for delay as provided in Article 16.

 

16Liquidated Damages for Delay

If the Supplier fails to deliver the Goods or perform the Services within the time periods stipulated in the Contract, the Buyer shall, without prejudice to any other remedies available under the Contract, deduct liquidated damages for delay from the Contract Price. The liquidated damages shall be assessed at the rate of one percent (1%) of the price of the delayed Goods or the fees for the unperformed Services per week of delay, until the actual delivery or performance is completed. The maximum amount of liquidated damages for delay shall be ten percent (10%) of the total Contract Price. Once the maximum amount of liquidated damages is reached, the Buyer may consider terminating the Contract.

 

17Termination for Default

17.1 Without prejudice to any other remedies available to the Buyer for the Supplier's default, the Buyer may issue a written notice of default to the Supplier, proposing to terminate the Contract in whole or in part:
(1) If the Supplier fails to deliver any or all of the Goods within the period specified in the Contract or within any extension thereof granted by the Buyer pursuant to Article 15; or
(2) If the Supplier fails to perform any other obligation stipulated in the Contract.

17.2 If the Buyer terminates the Contract in whole or in part pursuant to Article 17.1, the Buyer may procure, upon such terms and in such manner as it deems appropriate, goods similar to those undelivered, and the Supplier shall be liable to the Buyer for any excess costs for such similar goods. However, the Supplier shall continue the performance of the Contract to the extent not terminated.

18.1 If the Supplier's performance of or delivery under the Contract is delayed or prevented by Force Majeure, the Supplier shall not be subject to forfeiture of its Performance Security, nor shall it be liable for liquidated damages for delay or termination of the Contract.

18.2 "Force Majeure" as referred to in this Article means those events that are beyond the control of the Supplier and are not foreseeable, but do not include the Supplier's default or negligence. Force Majeure events include, but are not limited to: actions by the Buyer within its sovereign jurisdiction, war or revolution, fire, flood, epidemic, quarantine restrictions, embargoes, and cancellation of the event as notified by the event organizer.

18.3 In the event of Force Majeure, the Supplier shall notify the Buyer in writing as soon as possible of the occurrence of the Force Majeure and the causes thereof. Unless otherwise requested in writing by the Buyer, the Supplier shall continue to perform its obligations under the Contract as far as is reasonably practicable, and shall seek all reasonable means to perform the other matters not affected by the Force Majeure.

Such termination shall not prejudice or affect any rights or remedies which the Buyer has already exercised or may exercise in the future.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

COUNTRY:                                                Federal Government of Somalia (FGS)

NAME OF PROJECT:                              Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)  

PROJECT ID:                                             P176181   

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:                             Pricing and Interconnection Specialist

REFERENCE NO.:                                    SO-MOCT-FGS-557026-CS-INDV

PLACE OF ASSIGNMENT:                     Mogadishu, Somalia

APPLICATION DEADLINE DATE:       August 15, 2026, at (2.00pm Local Time).

Project Background:

The Federal Government of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP). The Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT) intends to apply part of the proceeds of these Grants to finance for the position of Pricing and Interconnection Specialist in support of the implementation of the National Communications Authority (NCA) in the Federal Government of Somalia.

To support the National Communications Authority's (NCA) mandate to promote fair competition, consumer protection, investment, and sustainable growth in the telecommunications sector, the  NCA seeks to engage a qualified Pricing and Interconnection Specialist to support market data collection and analysis, monitor regulatory compliance, coordinate with operators, prepare technical reports, and maintain regulatory databases.

The Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP) addresses connectivity needs for countries in the Horn of Africa region. The program aims to advance the regional integration of digital markets in Eastern Africa through supporting cross-border connectivity, harmonization of data and e-commerce regulations and policies, and removal of trade barriers, with the vision of establishing a Single Digital Market (SDM). The EA-RDIP project has four components, as briefly described below:

  • Component 1. Connectivity Market Development and Integration.
  • Component 2. Data Market Development and Integration.
  • Component 3. Online Market Development and integration.
  • Component 4. Project Management and implementation.

 

Scope of Work:

National Communications Authority's (NCA) mandate to promote fair competition, consumer protection, investment, and sustainable growth in the telecommunications sector. The NCA is implementing various initiatives related to interconnection, pricing regulation, infrastructure sharing, roaming, licensing, and universal access. To support the effective implementation of these activities, the NCA requires a dedicated Pricing and Interconnection Specialist to provide technical, analytical, administrative, and operational support to the NCA. The Pricing and Interconnection Specialist will contribute to the day-to-day implementation of regulatory activities related to interconnection, pricing, roaming, infrastructure sharing, licensing, and market analysis, while assisting in stakeholder engagement, monitoring compliance, maintaining regulatory records, and preparing technical reports. Also, the Pricing and Interconnection Specialist shall assist in collecting and analyzing market data, monitoring compliance, coordinating with operators, preparing reports, maintaining regulatory databases. For more details refer to the Terms and Reference (ToR).

Required Qualifications and Experiences:

The shortlisting criteria for the Pricing and Interconnection Specialist position are as follows:

  • A Bachelor's degree in Telecommunications Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Economics, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Business Administration.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of professional experience in telecommunications regulation, telecommunications operations, interconnection, pricing, market analysis, licensing, infrastructure sharing, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience in telecommunications market analysis, tariff monitoring, regulatory compliance, or telecommunications policy implementation.
  • Experience working with telecommunications operators, regulatory authorities, government institutions, development partners, or ICT sector projects.
  • Experience in collecting, analyzing, and interpreting telecommunications market data and industry statistics.
  • Experience supporting stakeholder consultations, industry engagements, workshops, and regulatory coordination activities.

Duration and Reporting of the Assignment: The Pricing and Interconnection Specialist will be engaged for a period of one (1) year to renewal on an annual basis based on satisfactory performance certified by NCA and availability of funds. The consultant will report to the client, the National Communications Authority (NCA), through its Director General as a supervisor; the consultant should submit written monthly and quarterly progressive reports with the review and satisfactory approval of the client.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing these services. Interested Individual Consultants must submit their Curriculum Vitae (CV) and cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: https://nca.gov.so/ or it can be forwarded to the applicant upon written request to the project generic email address indicated below.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The selection will be conducted in accordance with the procedures for selection of Individual Consultants set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers dated September 2023 (Procurement Regulations).

Interested Consultant may obtain further information in a written communication to the below project generic email address during office hours from 8:30am to 3.30pm local time (Excluding public holidays).

A Complete application of Curriculum Vitae (CV) and Cover letter should be submitted electronically (by e-mail) to the address below on, or before August 15, 2026, at 2.00pm, (Local Time) marked clearly as “Expression of Interest for Pricing & Interconnection Specialist; SO-MOCT-FGS-557026-CS-INDV)”

 

To: Procurement Office, EA-RDIP

Project Implementation Unit (PIU)

E-mail: procurement.ea-rdip@moct.gov.so

And;

Copy to: The Director General of NCA. E-mail: Dg@nca.gov.so

REPOBLIKAN' I MADAGASIKARA
Fitiavana-Tanindrazana-Fandrosoana
MINISTÈRE DE L'EAU, DE L'ASSAINISSEMENT ET DE L'HYGIENE
PROJET D'AMÉLIORATION DE L'ACCÈS À L'EAU POTABLE (PAAEP)

APPEL A MANIFESTATION

PRESTATION D’ÉTUDES TECHNIQUES, ENVIRONNEMENTALES ET SOCIALES (E&S), ET MISSION DE SUIVI ET CONTRÔLE DES TRAVAUX D’ALIMENTATION EN EAU POTABLE (AEP) DANS 68 CENTRES DE LA JIRAMA

Crédit IDA : 7121-MG/Don IDA EO40-MG

AMI  N°003/26 WJIR – C

Date de lancement : 29 Juillet 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du « PROJET D’AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES A L’EAU POTABLE, PAAEP – JIRAMA et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat pour la prestation d’études techniques, environnementales et sociales (E&S), et mission de suivi et contrôle des travaux d’alimentation en eau potable dans 68 centres de la JIRAMA.

2. Les services, au titre de ce contrat, portent sur trois missions différentes, notamment :

(i) La réalisation des Etudes d'Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES)/ Plan de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (PGES) et Plan de Réinstallation (PR) des 10 centres en vue de remplacement des conduites vétustes ;

(ii) La réalisation des études techniques et des EIES/PGES et PR des 20 centres sur 68, dont les travaux d’Alimentation en Eau Potable initialement prévus qui n’ont pas été achevés par le Ministère et ;

(iii) La mission de suivi, contrôle et supervision couvrant les aspects techniques et la gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux des travaux d’Alimentation en Eau Potable dans les 68 centres JIRAMA.

La date prévisionnelle du commencement des travaux est prévue en fin décembre 2026 et prévue pour une durée de vingt-trois (23) mois.

3. Les termes de référence détaillés (TdRs) pour la mission à manifestation d'intérêt peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

4. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PAAEP-JIRAMA invite les Consultants (Bureaux d’études, Cabinets de consultants, etc.) éligibles ("Consultants") à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations (brochures, dépliants, fiches, attestations et autres supports …) permettant d’évaluer leurs capacités, expériences, champs d’expertise et missions accomplies à assurer ladite prestation.

5. Le Consultant, ou l’un des membres dans le cas d’un groupement doit avoir au moins Dix (10) ans d’existence. Dans leur dossier de manifestation d’intérêt, les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services et joindre dans leur dossier au moins les pièces suivantes :

  • une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt ;
  • la présentation détaillée du Consultant (format libre) ;
  • les références concernant l’exécution de contrats similaires durant les Dix (10) dernières années en précisant clairement l’intitulé, le nom, l’adresse et les contacts du Client, l’année de réalisation moyennant les dates de début et de fin de la mission, le montant du contrat, la liste des profils et nombre des experts clés ayant réalisé la mission, et tout document justifiant la bonne fin de la mission.

Les critères de sélection d’une liste restreinte sont les suivants :

- Justifier d'une expérience générale d'au moins dix (10) années dans les études techniques et/ou les missions de contrôle et de surveillance de travaux d'infrastructures;

- Justifier d'au moins cinq (05) références réalisées au cours des dix (10) dernières années portant sur des missions d'études de faisabilité, d'Avant-Projets Sommaires (APS), d'Avant-Projets Détaillés (APD), de préparation de Dossiers d'Appel d'Offres (DAO) et/ou de contrôle et surveillance de travaux d'alimentation en eau potable en milieu urbain ou périurbain;

- Justifier d'au moins trois (03) références relatives à des projets de réseaux d'adduction et de distribution d'eau potable comprenant notamment des conduites, des réservoirs, des stations de pompage ou des ouvrages hydrauliques similaires;

- Disposer d'une expérience avérée dans la réalisation de prestations intégrant les aspects environnementaux et sociaux (EIES, PGES, PAR ou instruments équivalents), conformément aux exigences des bailleurs de fonds internationaux ou de la réglementation nationale;

- Démontrer une expérience de prestations financées par des institutions financières internationales (Banque mondiale, BAD, AFD, UE, etc.) ou par des organismes de financement similaires, ce critère constituant un atout;

- Présenter des références démontrant la bonne exécution des missions, attestées par des certificats de bonne fin, des procès-verbaux de réception ou tout document équivalent délivré par les maîtres d'ouvrage;

Ces références devront démontrer une expérience couvrant l'ensemble des types d'ouvrages suivants :

  • Fourniture et pose de groupes électropompes d'une capacité minimale de 50 m³/h pour des stations de pompage d’Alimentation en Eau Potable ;
  • Construction ou réhabilitation de bâtiments d'exploitation ;
  • Pose de canalisations en PEHD de diamètre DN 110 mm ou supérieur, sur un linéaire d'au moins 5 km en milieu urbain ;
  • Construction ou réhabilitation de stations de traitement d'eau brute d'une capacité minimale de 5 000 m³/j ;
  • Construction ou réhabilitation de réservoirs en béton armé d'une capacité minimale de 200 m³.

Individual Consultant Services

Environmental and Social (E&S) Audit Consultant

Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC)

The Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP), through the Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC), invites qualified individual consultants to express their interest in providing consulting services for conducting an Environmental and Social (E&S) Audit of Component 1 – Labor-Intensive Infrastructure.

Background

The Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC) is financed by the World Bank and implemented under the overall oversight of the Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP). The project aims to:

  1. Increase employment opportunities for selected groups in targeted areas; and
  2. Improve the operational capacity of selected government institutions.

Under Component 1, implemented by the Municipal Development and Lending Fund (MDLF), the project finances labor-intensive public infrastructure activities across the West Bank.

In accordance with the project's Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), MoFP intends to recruit a qualified Environmental and Social Consultant to conduct an independent Environmental and Social Audit of a representative sample of sub-projects implemented under Component 1.

Scope of the Assignment

The Consultant will assess compliance of selected sub-projects with:

  • World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and relevant Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs);
  • Project Environmental and Social instruments, including the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), Land Acquisition and Livelihood Framework (LALF), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), and Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP);
  • Applicable Palestinian environmental, social, labor, and occupational health and safety regulations.

The Consultant will undertake document reviews, stakeholder consultations, field visits, compliance assessments, and prepare a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) identifying gaps and recommendations for improvement.

Key Deliverables

1. Inception Report – within three (3) weeks from contract signature.

2. Draft Environmental and Social Audit Report including Corrective Action Plan (CAP) – within eight (8) weeks from contract signature.

3. Final Environmental and Social Audit Report including CAP – within twelve (12) weeks from contract signature.

Duration of Assignment

The assignment is expected to be completed within three (3) months from contract signing.

Required Qualifications and Experience

The Consultant shall possess:

  • A Master's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Social Sciences, Planning, Development Studies, or another relevant discipline.
  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience in environmental and social risk assessment and management.
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting Environmental and Social Audits, with a minimum of three (3) similar assignments. Experience in donor-funded or development projects will be an advantage.
  • Proven knowledge of Palestinian environmental, social, labor, and occupational health and safety legislation.
  • Demonstrated experience with international environmental and social standards, particularly the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
  • Excellent analytical, report-writing, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Excellent command of English, both written and spoken.

Selection Method and Evaluation Criteria

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and based on the qualifications and experience of the applicant.

The evaluation will be conducted out of a total score of 100 points as follows:

Evaluation Criteria

Points

Academic Qualifications relevant to the assignment

15

General Professional Experience in Environmental and Social Risk Assessment and Management

25

Specific Experience in conducting Environmental and Social Audits, including donor-funded and infrastructure projects

35

Experience with World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and related safeguards requirements

15

Knowledge of Palestinian environmental, social and labor legislation and report-writing skills

10

Total

100

 

Only candidates obtaining a minimum technical score of 70 points may be invited for an interview, if deemed necessary by the evaluation committee.

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Indonesia

Name of Project: Indonesia Health System Strengthening (IHSS) Project

Loan No.: IBRD Loan No. 9626

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Legal Compliance and Documentation

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): ID-COMP 4 IHSS-550314-CS-QCBS

Date: August 18, 2026

 

  1. The Ministry of Health (MoH) of the Republic of Indonesia has received loan financing from the World Bank to support the implementation of the Indonesia Health System Strengthening (IHSS) Project, with total funding amounting to EUR 3.7 billion. The IHSS Project (“the Project”) is a national initiative aimed at strengthening primary healthcare, referral services, and public health laboratories through the provision of medical equipment and capacity building across health facilities nationwide. To support the timely and accountable implementation of the Project, the MoH intends to engage a qualified law firm to provide legal advisory services, ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations, and strengthen the Project’s documentation and record-keeping systems. The assignment is intended to promote consistent implementation of sound documentation, indexing, and legal compliance practices throughout the Project lifecycle.
  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise comprehensive legal and compliance support to the MoH for the implementation of the IHSS Project. The selected firm will assist the MoH in strengthening legal compliance and establishing robust documentation management, record-keeping, and indexing systems to promote sound governance and effective risk mitigation throughout the Project. The firm will conduct ongoing legal and compliance reviews across all Project implementing teams, including SOPHI, SIHREN, InPULS, and project management activities, regardless of the financing sources. In addition, the firm will provide practical recommendations and capacity-building support to MoH personnel to institutionalize a strong compliance culture and systematic documentation practices. The scope of services will include, but not be limited to, the following: i) Legal Compliance and Regulatory Review; ii) Documentation Management, Record-Keeping, and Indexing; iii) Compliance Monitoring and Reporting; iv) Legal and Regulatory Alignment; v) Governance and Risk Management Support; and vi) Training and Awareness. The assignment is expected to require approximately 162 professional staff-months over the implementation period. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://s.kemkes.go.id/LCDCIHSS
  3. The Services for Legal Compliance and Documentation Consultancy Firm is expected to commence in November 2026 and conclude by April 2028.
  4. The Ministry of Health (MoH) now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide sufficient information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (including the name and location/country of the Client, type and scope of services provided, period of contract, contract amount, role of the firm, starting and completion dates, key output delivered and experts involved in the assignment).

The shortlisting criteria are:

a. Legal Status and Registration: 

The consulting firm shall be a legally registered entity with a valid business license and shall provide evidence of such legal registration. The firm shall possess relevant national and/or international accreditations or certifications applicable to the scope of the assignment (e.g., ISO 37001, ISO 9001, or equivalent).

b. Core business and years in business:

Minimum seven (7) years of proven experience in legal advisory services or related services, which include, but not limited to any of the following areas: regulatory review and/or compliance, contract management, contract dispute resolutions, and governance frameworks.

c. Relevant experience:

1. Demonstrated experience in providing legal services to government agencies/SOEs, international organizations, and/or private entities in any of the following areas:

a) legal compliance review of procurement, contract or project documentation;

b) advisory services on contract drafting, negotiation, and/or dispute resolution;

c) development of legal compliance frameworks, manuals, guidance notes or documentation systems.

Similar experience in any of the above ares under projects financed by Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) such as the World Bank, ADB, AIIB, and IsDB, is an advantage.

2. Experience in Establising systems for documentation, indexing, and compliance monitoring is an advantage.

d. Technical and managerial capability of the firm:

Availability of a qualified multidisciplinary legal team (corporate law, public law, procurement law, dispute resolution, information/documentation management).

 

5. The qualifications and experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The MoH will evaluate the Expressions of Interest (EOI) and develop a shortlist of qualified firms. Shortlisted firms will subsequently be invited to submit full technical and financial proposals in accordance with the World Bank's “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”).

6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

7. The Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall clearly indicate in EOI whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) and/or a sub-consultancy arrangement. In the case of JV, the EOI shall clearly identify the lead member authorized to represent the JV, and all JV members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment if selected. For the purpose of EOI evaluation and shortlisting, only the qualifications and experience of the JV members shall be considered in assessing compliance with the shortlisting criteria. The qualification and experience of sub-consultants shall not be taken into account for the evaluation of the EOI.

8. MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (MoLGUD)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Country: Somaliland
Project ID: P508408
Project Name: Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Consulting Service: PIU Bulsho Project Manager
Selection Type: Individual Consultant

Reference No: SO-MOLGUD-567780-CS-INDV
Duty Station: Hargeisa, Somaliland, with potential travel to the target districts and cities of the Bulsho Project
Duration: 12 months, renewable subject to satisfactory performance
Application Deadline: September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time

1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD) of the Government of Somaliland is implementing the World Bank-financed Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408).

The Bulsho Project provides initial anchor financing to the Government’s multi-year Bulsho Program, whose main objective is to strengthen community and local institutions for improved social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. The Program places citizens and communities at the center of government action and supports decentralization, inclusive local governance, improved service delivery, community participation, and stronger citizen-government relations.

To support effective implementation of the Project, MoLGUD has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and intends to recruit a qualified and experienced PIU Bulsho Project Manager to head the PIU and oversee the overall implementation of the Bulsho Project.

2. SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The PIU Bulsho Project Manager will be responsible for the overall day-to-day management and implementation of the Bulsho Project, providing strategic leadership and supervision to the PIU and coordinating with MoLGUD departments, local governments, district authorities, communities, service providers, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders.

The Project Manager will oversee project planning and implementation; financial management and procurement; local governance and community-driven development; environmental and social safeguards; monitoring, evaluation and learning; stakeholder coordination; compliance and risk management; and sustainability and institutional capacity transfer.

The Project Manager will also oversee local governance and community-driven development processes, including participatory planning, Local Social Contract Platforms (LSCPs), Citizens’ Charters, community engagement, matching grants, community contributions, and community-level investments, ensuring that these processes are transparent, inclusive, accountable, and participatory.

The detailed scope of services, responsibilities, deliverables, reporting arrangements, and other requirements are provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

3. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The successful candidate shall meet the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • A university degree in Governance, Political Science, International Relations, Public Administration, Development Studies, Project Management, or a related field. A Master’s degree in a related field is an advantage.
  • A minimum of eight (8) years of progressively responsible professional experience in project management, coordination, or implementation.
  • At least four (4) years of experience managing or coordinating large-scale government or donor-funded programs in local governance, institutional building, or service delivery, preferably in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
  • Demonstrated experience in community-driven development (CDD), participatory planning, and community-level implementation of development projects.
  • Demonstrated professional knowledge of the Government of Somaliland and Local Governments, including their structures, functions, and operational frameworks.
  • Experience working in fragility, conflict and violence (FCV) settings, with an understanding of local security dynamics and the ability to support implementation of security management plans.
  • Proven experience in decentralization, capacity building, institutional strengthening, and coordination across different levels of government.
  • Strong leadership and team management capabilities, with sound knowledge and experience in financial management, procurement, monitoring and evaluation, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Strong negotiation, organizational, communication, representation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to deliver effectively under pressure.
  • Demonstrated commitment to gender and social inclusion and engagement of marginalized groups, including women, youth, minority groups, and IDPs.
  • High standards of integrity, ethical conduct, professional accountability, and leadership.
  • In-depth knowledge of Somaliland’s governance structures, political dynamics, and local context, and familiarity with international development partners working in community development, social cohesion, and local governance.
  • Proficiency in relevant project management tools and software.
  • Excellent command of English and Somali, including reading, writing, communication, and presentation skills.

4. REPORTING AND DURATION

The PIU Bulsho Project Manager will report administratively to the Director General of the Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD).

The assignment will initially be for 12 months and may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. The duty station is Hargeisa, Somaliland, with potential travel to the target districts and cities of the Bulsho Project.

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD), Government of Somaliland, now invites eligible and qualified Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing – Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations and applicable Government of Somaliland policies.

 

 

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Interested Consultants should submit:

  1. A detailed and updated Curriculum Vitae (CV), including contact details of three (3) professional referees;
  2. Copies of relevant academic qualification certificates; and
  3. A cover letter outlining the candidate’s relevant experience and qualifications in relation to the assignment.

Interested and qualified candidates should submit their applications by email with the subject line:

“Application for PIU Bulsho Project Manager – SO-MOLGUD-567780-CS-INDV”

To: bulsho.somaliland@outlook.com
Cc: dg.molgud@sldgov.org

Applications must be received no later than September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time.
