A pontuação mínima para um(a) candidato(a) ser incluído(a) na lista restrita é de 70 pontos; todos os candidatos com pontuação inferior serão eliminados. O objeto do concurso será atribuído ao (à) candidato(a) com melhor perfil e que tiver a melhor classificação. 

 VI. APRESENTAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÕES DE INTERESSE

Os candidatos interessados devem entregar ou enviar as suas candidaturas à Unidade de Coordenação do WACA ResIP 2 GB, Avenida Dom Settimio Arturo Ferrazzetta, Caixa Postal Nº 70, Guiné-Bissau, Bissau, à atenção do seu Coordenador Nacional, Sr. Leonildo Alves Cardoso ou por correio eletrónico: samuelfernandesspmwaca@gmail.com  com cópia para: leonildocardoso@hotmail.com  até o dia 3 de setembro  de 2026 às 16 horas em ponto, hora de Bissau.

VII.       INFORMAÇÕES COMPLEMENTARES

Os candidatos interessados podem obter mais informações sobre os documentos de referência no endereço abaixo: samuelfernandesspmwaca@gmail.com  ou visitando o departamento administrativo do projeto WACA ResIP 2 GB na sua sede, localizada na Avenida Dom Settimio Arturo Ferrazzetta, Caixa Postal Nº 70, Guiné-Bissau, Bissau, entre as 10 horas em ponto e as 15 horas em ponto de segunda a sexta-feira.

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS. 

SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

 

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo:  Formulación de Instrumentos Regionales y Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial y Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres. Región Cibao Norte y Región El Valle.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPYD-475021-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") incluyen: la formulación de los Planes Regionales de Ordenamiento y Desarrollo Territorial (PRODT) de las regiones Cibao Norte y El Valle; diez (10) Planes Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial (PMOT) priorizados, de nueva formulación, actualización integral o ampliación sustantiva de alcance: ocho (8) en Cibao Norte, correspondientes a la actualización, armonización y profundización del PMOT de Santiago de los Caballeros, incluyendo sus distritos municipales Hato del Yaque, La Canela, San Francisco de Jacagua y Santiago Oeste; los PMOT de Licey al Medio, Puñal, Villa González, Tamboril, Bisonó/Navarrete y Sosúa; y el instrumento asociativo de Gaspar Hernández, incluyendo Veragua (D.M.) y Jamao al Norte; y dos (2) en El Valle, correspondientes a San Juan de la Maguana y Azua de Compostela.

Los Servicios comprenden además la revisión, actualización, complementación o armonización de cuatro (4) PMOT vigentes o en proceso: Santiago de los Caballeros, San Felipe de Puerto Plata, Moca y Villa Montellano, precisando que la referencia a Santiago no constituye un producto adicional ni un doble conteo; dos (2) Instrumentos de Delimitación de Suelo Urbano (IDSU) para Las Matas de Farfán y Comendador; nueve (9) Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático, seis (6) en Cibao Norte y tres (3) en El Valle; y dos (2) Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación, una para cada región, en un período de dieciséis (16) meses calendario, conforme al alcance establecido en los Términos de Referencia. Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los Términos de Referencia (TDR).

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. Se requiere una firma con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia comprobable en el desarrollo de proyectos, planes o políticas relacionados con el ordenamiento y desarrollo territorial en las escalas nacional, regional, municipal y/o de desarrollo urbano. Se valorará especialmente que cuente con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia específica en la formulación de instrumentos supramunicipales de ordenamiento y/o desarrollo territorial o de instrumentos de delimitación y regulación de usos del suelo a escala municipal, incluyendo el desarrollo simultáneo de múltiples instrumentos de planificación territorial en distintos niveles de gobierno.

Asimismo, deberá demostrar un mínimo de tres (3) proyectos o siete (7) años de experiencia reciente en gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, incluyendo análisis multiamenaza, modelación hidrológico-hidráulica y sísmica, integración de escenarios climáticos y articulación de resultados con instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial e inversión pública y su aplicación en procesos de planificación territorial y toma de decisiones.

Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) proyectos similares en alcance, complejidad, niveles de gobierno y extensión geográfica, ejecutados satisfactoriamente y vinculados a la formulación de instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial a escala regional y/o municipal, con integración de la gestión del riesgo de desastres y la adaptación al cambio climático. En conjunto, los proyectos presentados deberán permitir verificar, según corresponda, experiencia en planificación regional, municipal o metropolitana; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; producción y gestión de información geoespacial; formulación normativa; procesos participativos; fortalecimiento institucional; portafolios de inversión; y estrategias de implementación. Las experiencias deberán estar respaldadas mediante certificaciones, contratos, actas de recepción u otra documentación equivalente emitida por los contratantes. En caso de APCA, podrán acreditarse de manera conjunta por sus integrantes, siempre que guarden relación directa con las responsabilidades que cada uno asumirá en la consultoría.

Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad técnica y de gestión para la ejecución de la consultoría, incluyendo la disponibilidad de recursos computacionales, tecnológicos y de producción digital necesarios, así como herramientas de gestión de proyectos, administración de entornos, repositorios y documentación técnica. Deberá evidenciar capacidad para gestionar contratos de magnitud y complejidad similares, cumpliendo tiempos y entregables, así como capacidad organizativa y operativa para iniciar oportunamente la consultoría, incluyendo la movilización del equipo.

Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas por cada postulante frente a la complejidad, escala y condiciones de ejecución de los servicios requeridos. Para estos fines, se considerará la capacidad demostrada para desarrollar de manera simultánea y articulada instrumentos regionales y municipales de ordenamiento territorial, instrumentos de gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, procesos participativos y de coordinación multiactor, gestión de información territorial y cartográfica, así como la capacidad operativa para prestar los servicios en idioma español y mantener presencia activa en las regiones objeto de la consultoría.

Los servicios se prestarán en idioma español e implican presencia activa en el territorio de las regiones Cibao Norte y El Valle y en el Distrito Nacional, República Dominicana.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia relevante, capacidad técnica y de gestión de la firma consultora de acuerdo con los requerimientos arriba mencionados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse de manera organizada, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados por la firma o integrante de la APCA, escala territorial, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales y recursos permanentes relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

Los TDR podrán solicitarse, sin costo, mediante comunicación dirigida al correo electrónico antes indicado, haciendo constar en el asunto la referencia del proceso, o descargarse desde el enlace correspondiente a este proceso, publicado en el Portal de Transparencia del Ministerio de la Presidencia: https://minpre.gob.do/transparencia/proyecto-de-respuesta-a-emergencias-y-resiliencia-de-la-republica-dominicana/.

Las expresiones de interés deben enviarse por escrito a la siguiente dirección (en persona, por correo o por correo electrónico) hasta el miércoles 12 de agosto de 2026, a las 16:00 horas.

  • Viceministerio de Ordenamiento Territorial y Desarrollo Regional
  • A la atención de: Domingo Matías. Viceministro de Ordenamiento Territorial y Desarrollo Regional. Ministerio de la Presidencia
  • Dirección:Calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48. Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana
  • Tel: +1 (829) 213 2707
  • Correo electrónico:adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do

Cuando la Expresión de Interés sea remitida por correo electrónico, deberá enviarse en formato PDF. El tamaño máximo por archivo adjunto será de veinte (20) MB. Si el expediente supera dicha capacidad, podrá remitirse mediante varios correos, indicando en cada envío el número de envío y el total de envíos.

Specific Procurement Notice

Request for Bids

Goods

(Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

Country: Georgia

Name of Project: Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor – Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project (Project)

Contract Title: Procurement of 45 Main Line DC Freight Electric Locomotives and Full Long-term Technical Maintenance

Loan No.: IBRD-99810

RFB Reference No.: GE-GR-563165-GO-RFB

 

  1. Georgia has received financing from the World Bank (Bank) toward the cost of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor – Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project (Project), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement of 45 Main Line DC Freight Electric Locomotives and Full Long-term Technical Maintenance. This contract will be jointly financed by Asian Development Bank (ADB). Bidding process will be governed by the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.

2.         The JSC Georgian Railway (GR) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Procurement of 45 Main Line DC Freight Electric Locomotives and Full Long-term Technical Maintenance to be to be delivered by a single manufacturer.

Permitted Locomotive Configuration

 

The Bidder shall offer one of the following locomotive configurations only:

 

  1. 2 × Bo-Bo integrated locomotive configuration — total quantity: 45 units; or
  2. Separate paired Bo-Bo locomotive configuration — total quantity: 90 units, forming 45 operational locomotive pairs.

 

Each proposed configuration shall meet all specified performance requirements, including traction capacity, rated power, operational efficiency, compatibility with the Purchaser’s network, and all other technical requirements.

 

No alternative quantity or mixed configuration shall be accepted. The Bid shall be based exclusively on either 45 integrated units or 90 separate Bo-Bo units forming 45 pairs (hereinafter referred to as "45 locomotives").

Delivery Requirement: The locomotives shall be delivered to the depot in city Khashuri, Georgia under the CIP conditions. The 1st locomotive shall be delivered within 27 months from the contract effectiveness date. The remaining 44 locomotives shall be delivered within the deadlines defined in Section VII – Schedule of Requirement to ensure completion of all deliveries within 55 months from the contract effectiveness date.

Scope of the contract includes design, manufacturing, delivery, testing, commissioning (supplied system fully operational, accepted, and ready for commercial service) of 45 Main Line DC Freight Electric Locomotives and at least 2-year warranty period. The contract will be financed by 50/50 from World Bank and ADB sources.

In addition, the scope includes the provision of full technical maintenance services (excluding major overhauls) for the delivered locomotives. These services shall commence upon the Operational Acceptance of the first Locomotive and shall continue throughout the Warranty Period and the subsequent ten (10)-year post-warranty maintenance period for each Locomotive. The overall duration of the Locomotives Maintenance Agreement shall expire upon completion of the ten (10)-year post-warranty maintenance period applicable to the latest delivered Locomotive or batch of Locomotives. The maintenance services shall cover spare parts, consumables, major components, and all necessary maintenance activities. For this purpose, a separate maintenance service agreement will be entered into with the successful Bidder. The terms and conditions of this agreement and are included in the bidding documents and incorporate performance-based Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), payment mechanisms structured on measurable performance criteria, and a price adjustment formula. The maintenance service agreement will be financed from the Purchaser’s own resources and may be extended subject to satisfactory performance.

Under this arrangement, the Supplier shall, as part of its maintenance obligations and at its own cost, design, construct, equip, and commission a new fully operational service center (depot) for the maintenance of at least the forty-five (45) locomotives. Subject to the Supplier’s full compliance with the performance, availability, and maintenance obligations under the Lcomotives Maintenance Agreement, the Purchaser grants the Supplier the right to use the depot facilities for third-party rolling stock and maintenance services. Under all circumstances, the Purchaser’s operational and maintenance requirements shall take precedence. The depot shall be completed and ready for operation prior to the Operational Acceptance of the first locomotive.

For the purpose of new depot, the Borrower shall provide the Supplier with a land plot located within the existing Khashuri depot. The land shall be made available free of charge for the entire duration of the maintenance service agreement under a right of superficies arrangement, granting the Supplier the legal right to design, construct, operate, and maintain the depot on the provided land for the contract period. The Supplier shall retain ownership of the depot, its infrastructure, and all installed equipment during the period in which it is responsible for maintenance services and depot operations under the maintenance contract.

Capabilities and Qualification Requirements: To implement the scope of the contract the Bidder shall meet the following requirements:

  1. Qualification

Qualification Criteria (ITB 32.1)

The Purchaser shall assess each Bid against the following Qualification Criteria. Requirements not included in the text below shall not be used in the evaluation of the Bidder’s qualifications.

 

  1. Financial Capability:
  1. The Bidder shall submit audited financial statements or, if not required by the law of the Bidder’s country, other financial statements acceptable to the Purchaser, for the last three (3) years (2023-2024-2025) prior to bid submission deadline, demonstrating the current soundness of the Bidder’s financial position. For a joint venture, this requirement shall be met by each member.
  1. Specific Experience:

(i) The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully completed at least two (2) contracts in the role of prime contractor within the last ten (10) years prior to bid submission deadline, each for delivery of at least ten (10) main line electric locomotives for the maximum operating speed 120 km/h that are similar in nature and complexity to the Goods and Related Services required under this RFB. The Bidder shall submit relevant completion certificates, taking-over certificates, or equivalent documents acceptable for the Purchaser, issued by previous clients and confirming the successful completion of delivery, testing and current successful operation of locomotives.

For a joint ventures, this requirement may be met by all members combined.

(ii) The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully substantially completed[1]  at least one (1) contract in the role of prime contractor within the last ten (10) years prior to bid submission deadline, each for provision of maintenance or overhaul services of at least twenty (20) main line electric locomotives that are similar in nature and complexity to the Full Technical Maintenance service required under this RFB. The Bidder shall submit performance certificates or reference letters acceptable for the Purchaser, issued by the previous clients confirming that the contract has been or is being performed satisfactorily.

For a joint ventures, this requirement may be met by all members combined.

  1. Documentary Evidence:

The Bidder shall furnish documentary evidence to demonstrate that the offered Goods meet the following requirements:

  1. Prospective bidders must be able to show from independent data that their offered electric locomotive is of mature technology, meaning that it has operated at required contractual levels of availability and reliability in revenue-earning service for at least one year.
  2. All major components, including bogies, traction motors, control equipment and braking systems must be individually shown to be of mature technology, meaning that they have been type tested and have been in successful revenue-earning service for at least one year.

 

  1. Manufacturing experience and Technical Capacity: For the items under the Contract that the bidder is a manufacturer, the Bidder shall furnish documentary evidence to demonstrate that:

 

  1. it has manufactured goods of similar nature and complexity for at least 10 years, prior to the bid submission deadline; and

 

(ii) its annual production capacity of goods of similar nature and complexity for any of the last 10 years prior to the bid submission deadline, is at least eighteen (18) locomotives.

 

The Bidder shall provide documentary evidence to demonstrate compliance with the above requirements.

 

The Purchaser reserves the right to request additional information or clarification to verify the Bidder’s production capacity.

 

  1. Cyber security experience. The Bidder will demonstrate its cyber security experience, practice and track record, including experience in navigating compliance requirements and regulatory standards related to cyber security. The Bidder shall provide documentary evidence of relevant cyber security accreditation such as IEC 62443 or EN 50159:2010 or ISO 27000 (ISO 27001) or equivalent.

 

The Bidder shall provide a cyber security risk assessment and management plan to ensure that the product meets legal and industry-specific security standards and ensures that there are no harmful algorithms in the control systems that can negatively affect operation of the locomotive.

Request for Expressions of Interest for Consulting Service

Country:        The Republic of the Gambia

Project Title: The Gambia Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery (PAMP) Project  

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to Support a Revenue Assessment of the National Environment Agency

Grant Number: IDA-E3820

Project ID NO:  P176924

Procurement Method: Individual Consultant Selection Method (IC)   

Reference No.   GM-CPCU-MOFEA-516921-CS-INDV

  1. Background:

The Gambia Public Administration Modernization for Citizen Centric Service Delivery Project (PAMP) supports the implementation of the Government program, the Recovery Focused National Development Plan (RF-NDP) 2023-2027. In January 2024, the GoTG approved and adopted the RF-NDP 2023-2027, i.e., program implementation is currently in its infancy. The RF-NDP aims to consolidate gains in democratic governance, accelerate green economic and social transformation, and build resilience to shocks and crises. It has three major strategic objectives: (1) building household and community resilience to address shocks and crises arising from climate change and economic volatility and to counter the effects of pandemics like COVID-19; (2) consolidating gains and addressing critical development gaps in governance and economic and social transformation; and (3) strengthening accountability, building partnerships and setting up robust and sustainable resource mobilization strategies for effective delivery of development actions and expected outcomes. The RF-NDP is organized across seven pillars.

The proposed PforR focuses on a subset of RF-NDP priority actions related to enhancing domestic resource mobilization and financial reporting, human resources management, and citizen engagement in the education sector. These include the second pillar on Governance Reforms priority actions to “enhance governance and management of civil society organizations” and “professionalize and instill meritocracy, ethical conduct, transparency and accountability in the public service and personnel management” and the third pillar on Macroeconomic Stability and Inclusive Growth priority action to “enhance Public Financial Management (PFM) for macro-fiscal stability and strengthening democracy.”

  1. Sectoral Context and Objective of The Assignment:

The National Environment Agency (NEA) established under the National Environment Management Act (NEMA), 1994 consistent with the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 as a semi-autonomous agency with an independent structure to serve as the “principal body responsible for overall management of the environment” in the Gambia.

The NEA is the advisory body to the National Management Council (NEMC) on formulation, review, revision and repealing of environmental policies, plans, standards, guidelines, criteria and regulations. The NEMC is the main policy-making body for the environmental management in the Gambia. This Council is chaired by the President of the Republic of the Gambia, with the Ministers responsible for the following Ministries as members: Natural Resources; Agriculture; Health and Social Welfare; Finance and Economic Affairs; Trade Industry and Employment; Local Government and Lands. The Executive Director of the NEA serves as Secretary to the Council. In addition to the composition of this council, the President may co-opt any person into the Council as member.

The functions of the NEA include; (a) implementing the policies of the Council on the environment; (b) liaising with the various ministries, departments, and agencies of Government on all issues relating to the environment and ensure that environmental concerns are integrated into all spheres of national planning and project implementation; (c) liaising with the private sector, inter-governmental organizations, non- governmental organizations, governmental agencies of other states on all issues relating to the environment; (d) preparing proposals for environmental policies and strategies for the Council; (e) initiating legislative proposals, standards, guidelines, and regulations in accordance with the provisions of NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 ; (f) reviewing and approving environmental impact assessments submitted in accordance with the  NEMA Amendment Bill 2025  or any other law; (g) undertaking studies and submit reports and recommendations to the Council on such matters as are likely to have an impact on the environment; (h) promoting public awareness of environmental issues through gathering, analyzing and disseminating information about the environment and publishing periodic reports on the state of the environment; attend to any complaint relating to the environment addressed to it; (j) carrying out environmental audits and monitoring; and (k) carrying out such other functions as the NEMC may assign to it or as may be incidental or conducive to the exercise by NEA of any powers provided for under the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025.

Administratively, NEA reports only to the NEMC, and is led by the Executive Director, who is assisted by a Deputy Executive Secretary and three directorates, namely, Technical Services (TSN), Inter-sectoral Services (ISN), and Administration and Finance (AFN).  Under these directorates, various programs and services are planned and carried out. 

The NEA as per the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 is overseen by the Board of Directors of the Agency which shall be the governing body of the Agency with two statutory committees namely, the Technical Advisory Committee and the Administration and Finance Committee providing day-to-day oversight and technical support to NEA management.

The overall strategic objective of the Revenue Assessment of NEA is to provide GoTG with a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative analytical assessment of the revenue framework and challenges (be they governance, administrative, regulatory, sources, thresholds and collection) of the NEA, to inform the preparation of detailed recommendations for how the NEA’s financial sustainability for the fulfillment of its mandate can be enhanced, for the consideration of the government in its quest to empower NEA with the tools it needs to be more effective

  1. Scope of Work:

 

  1. Scope of Services:
  • Review assessment of the governance (regulatory, institutional, technical, and financial) framework underpinning NEA’s revenue issues, concerns, and challenges across both the national and local government levels.
  • Preparation of a detailed and comprehensive report, including recommendations and implementation plan for the GoTG through the NEMC.
  1. Qualification and Competency
  • A relevant Master's degree (or higher) from a recognized university in Public Financial Management; Economics with a specialization in public or environmental finance; Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration; or Environmental Economics/Management with a strong finance component. A recognized professional accountancy qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CIPFA or equivalent) may substitute for the academic degree requirement.
  • Minimum 15 years of relevant professional experience in public finance, fiscal economics, or revenue management, of which at least 10 years must be post-qualification.
  • Proven track record in conducting revenue assessments, diagnostic studies, or fiscal sustainability analyses for public agencies, semi-autonomous bodies, or state-owned enterprises.
  • Experience applying financial modelling and revenue projection techniques to identify collection gaps and forecast income streams. Full econometric modelling capability is desirable but not required.
  • Ability to analyze budget execution reports, subvention systems, and mechanisms for withholding or reallocation of funds by central finance ministries.
  • Prior experience working in The Gambia is an advantage. Candidates with experience in comparable West African or small-state developing country contexts will also be considered.
  • Knowledge of The Gambia's environmental regulatory framework, including the NEMA Amendment Bill 2025 and its provisions on revenue sources, earmarking, and NEA's semi-autonomous status. Candidates are expected to review the Bill prior to submission.
  • Familiarity with environmental fiscal instruments such as pollution levies, royalty regimes, and environmental impact assessment fees.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and executing stakeholder mapping and consultation processes involving government ministries, revenue authorities, private sector operators, and civil society.

Full TOR Availability Notice

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) will be made available upon request. Please send your request via email to the addresses provided below. The assignment is expected to be completed within 3 months from the date of signing the contract.

This assignment will strengthen Zambia's data protection regulatory framework by supporting the Data Protection Commission in reviewing, developing, and enhancing regulatory instruments that facilitate the effective implementation of the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021. Project:                        Karachi Mobility Project, Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) “Yellow Line

Contract Title:             Procurement of Package 5:

Country:                      Islamic Republic of Pakistan

LOT I:                         Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 5, 6 &7  (From CH.0+000 at Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to CH. 3+875 at Kala pull)

LOT II:                        Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 4 & 5  (From CH. 3+875 at Kala pull to CH. 7+571.000 at KPT interchange)

Loan No.:                    IBRD-89950

RFB No:                      PK-SMTA-449988-CW-RFB

Issued on:                    July 13th 2026

1.      The Borrower “Islamic Republic of Pakistan” has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Karachi Mobility Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement of Package 5: LOT I: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 5, 6 &7  (From CH. 0+000 at Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to CH. 3+875 at Kala pull) and LOT II: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 4 & 5  (From CH. 3+875 at Kala pull to CH. 7+571.000 at KPT interchange).

         For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.

2.     The Sindh Mass Transit Authority (SMTA), Transport & Mass Transit Department, Government of Sindh, now invites sealed Bids from the eligible Bidders for Procurement of Package 5: LOT I: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 5, 6 & 7  (From CH.0+000 at Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull) and LOT II: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Corridor Segments 4 & 5  (From CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull to CH. 7+571 at KPT Interchange).

3.     The Yellow Line BRT Corridor is approximately 21 km long, starting from Dawood Chowrangi to Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection, and is part of the overall planned Karachi Mass Transit System (KMTS). Currently, Yellow Line BRT Corridor divided into five (05) packages i.e., (i) Package-1: Construction of Depots (Lot-I: Depot-I & Lot-II: Depot-II), which are (under implementation), (ii) Package-3B: Construction of Main BRT Corridor from Dawood Chowrangi to Indus Chowrangi approx. 6 km (Bid evaluation under process), (iii): Pacakge-3A: Construction of Main BRT Corridor from Brookes Chowrangi to Bilal Chowrangi approx. 6 km (Bid evaluation under process),  (iv) Pacakge-4: Construction of New Jam Sadiq Bridge (Currently Known as Taj Haider Bridge) (under implementation), and (v) Package-5: Lot I: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Line Corridor Segments 5, 6 & 7 (From CH. 0+000 at Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull), and Lot II: Construction of Road Corridor and BRT Infrastructure Yellow BRT Line Corridor Segments 4 & 5 (From CH. 3+875 at Kala Pull to CH. 7+571 at KPT Interchange) (being tendered).

4.     This Package 5, Lot-I: covers 3.875 km from Khalid Bin Waleed Intersection to Kala Pull. The scope includes construction of one underpass, one underground BRT station, three at-grade BRT stations, one pedestrian crossing bridge (V3), one vertical circulation (V5), Kala Pull Bridge, and one pump station at Tariq Road Underpass, BRT and mixed-traffic lanes, service roads, traffic signals, three electrical substations, street lighting, temporary traffic diversions, utility relocations and protection. The construction period shall be 660 days. Bidders must demonstrate financial capacity to meet the required construction cash flow of USD 6.30 million, supported by liquid and unencumbered assets, lines of credits, and other financial means, as well as sufficient funding for ongoing and future commitments. Audited financial statements for the last five years must show sound financial position and prospective profitability. Bidder must have a minimum average annual construction turnover of USD 37.60 million over the last five years, with at least seven (07) years of general construction experience. They must have satisfactorily completed either at least two (02) similar scopes contracts of more than USD 23 million each, or at least one (01) contract of more than USD 37 million, with demonstrated experience and production rates for key activities. Key activities including steel structures (>50 tons/year), urban road works (>58,000 m²/year), underpasses (>28,000 m³ concrete/year), and rigid pavements (>3,600 m²/year). All the key activities can be obtained from one contract or separate contracts, but one activity cannot be obtained from more than one contract. The State of Santa Catarina is in the process of contracting a loan operation with the World Bank to finance the SC Protected and Resilient Program, with part of the resources allocated for the procurement of specialized consulting services.

Within the scope of this procurement, the services comprise the hiring of a specialized consulting firm to prepare a detailed technical assessment, strategic planning, technical specifications, and a governance model aimed at structuring an integrated system for hydrometeorological observation, forecasting, and dissemination of information for the member States of the Council for the Development and Integration of the South – CODESUL (Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Paraná, and Mato Grosso do Sul). The initiative aims to strengthen regional capacity for monitoring, forecasting, and issuing alerts related to extreme hydrometeorological events.

The estimated period for the execution of the services is 10 (ten) months, counted from the contract signing date, with the procurement process expected to begin in December 2026, in accordance with the provisions established in the respective Terms of Reference (ToR).

The details of the services and procurement requirements are described in the Terms of Reference (ToR) attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest. The State Secretariat for Civil Protection and Defense of Santa Catarina invites qualified consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services under this procurement. Interested firms shall submit information demonstrating that they possess the technical qualifications, institutional experience, and operational capacity required for the proper execution of the Services, including the following requirements:

Experience in Similar Projects

Mandatory requirement: the firm shall have executed, within the last 10 (ten) years, at least 1 (one) project involving the following element:

  • Integration or development of hydrometeorological monitoring systems at the regional, national, or international level.

Desirable requirements: the firm shall have executed, within the last 10 (ten) years, projects involving the following elements:

  • Strategic planning or technical advisory services for national or state meteorological and/or hydrological services (National Meteorological Services, meteorological institutes, water agencies);
  • Technical specification and/or supervision of the implementation of early warning systems for natural disasters (floods, landslides, droughts, storms);
  • Consulting services for the modernization of information technology infrastructure applied to large volumes of environmental or scientific data;
  • Design of multi-institutional or multi-level governance models for shared information systems;
  • Diagnosis, assessment, or recommendations for meteorological, hydrological, or environmental observation networks
  • International experience demonstrating the capacity to operate in different institutional contexts and alignment with global best practices. Experience in projects financed by multilateral development banks, projects for international organizations, and/or initiatives conducted in multiple countries or within the framework of international technical cooperation will be considered.

Institutional Capacity

Mandatory requirement: The firm shall demonstrate institutional capacity through AT LEAST ONE of the following options:

Option A — Proven Consulting Experience and Mobilization Capacity: Certificate of at least 1 (one) relevant strategic or technical consulting project executed within the last 10 (ten) years (which may be the same project submitted under the Similar Projects Experience Requirement, if applicable).

Option B — Strategic Institutional Partnership: letter of support or formal partnership agreement with an institution of recognized national or international expertise in the fields of meteorology, hydrology, disaster risk management, or related areas, such as:

  • INPE (National Institute for Space Research);
  • INMET (National Institute of Meteorology);
  • Regional Centers of the WMO (World Meteorological Organization);
  • Leading universities with recognized programs in relevant fields;
  • National Meteorological and Hydrological Services or Institutes from other countries;
  • Research centers specialized in climate, water resources, or disaster management

Desirable requirements:

  • Meet Options A and B;
    • ISO 9001 (Quality Management System);
  • Quality Certifications – relevant and valid quality certifications, such as:
    • CMMI Level 3 or higher (Capability Maturity Model Integration);
    • Other recognized and equivalent international certifications.

The short list shall comprise a minimum of 5 (five) and a maximum of 8 (eight) selected consulting firms.

Interested Firms are hereby drawn attention to the provisions set forth in Section III, paragraphs 3.14 to 3.17, of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September 2025 edition, which address the policies applicable to conflicts of interest and unfair competitive advantage in procurement processes financed by the institution.

Firms may associate with other firms in order to complement their qualifications and technical capabilities and shall clearly indicate, in their Expression of Interest, whether such association will take the form of a joint venture and/or subcontracting arrangement. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the full performance of the contract, should the proposal be selected.

The Firm shall be selected in accordance with the applicable procurement procedures established in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September 2025 edition, and pursuant to the provisions set forth in the Request for Proposals (RFP).

Additional information may be obtained through the following email address comissaobird@sea.sc.gov.br by consulting the attached Terms of Reference, available on the website https://compras.sc.gov.br/sou-fornecedor.

Expressions of Interest shall be submitted exclusively by electronic means to the Contracting Committee, via the email address comissaobird@sea.sc.gov.br, by 7:00 p.m., Brasília time, on September 11, 2026, with the subject line: “EoI Nº 534/2026 – name of the interested party”.

REPUBLIC OF TAJIKISTAN

Tajikistan Women’s Economic Empowerment Project (TWEEP)

Grant No.: TF-D1600 (TWEEP, P511398)

Assignment Title: Conducting a Baseline Survey for the TWEEP Project

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TWEEP-CS-CQS-01

The Government of the Republic of Tajikistan has received financing in the amount of US$4.73 million from the World Bank toward the cost of the Tajikistan Women’s Economic Empowerment Project (TWEEP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) include the engagement of a consulting firm to conduct the Baseline Survey for the TWEEP Project. The objective of the assignment is to collect and analyze baseline data to assess the subsequent progress and results of the Project in accordance with its Results Framework indicators. The selected consulting firm will develop and agree on the survey methodology and sampling plan, prepare and program the survey instruments in the CAPI system, conduct pre-testing and field piloting of the questionnaires, organize training of field staff, data collection and quality control, data cleaning and analysis, and prepare a final analytical report on the results of the Baseline Survey.

The assignment will include conducting 1,080 interviews in six target districts of the Project, including 1,000 interviews with women and 80 interviews with existing MSMEs led or managed by women. In addition, the consulting firm will organize and conduct 12 Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), two in each Project district, with approximately 8–10 participants in each group.

The firm will also be responsible for developing a detailed fieldwork plan, translating the survey instruments into the relevant languages, programming the questionnaires in the CAPI system, regularly monitoring fieldwork, conducting back-checks, spot-checks and other data quality assurance activities, preparing cleaned databases in Excel, SPSS and Stata formats, conducting quantitative and qualitative data analysis, and preparing the final report in English and Russian.

The expected duration of the consulting services is 6 (six) months from the date of contract signing.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this assignment can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gv7XTFcscnOfgOsxwWLJqxjwRv0_QRloLLE8XLiOUAY/edit?usp=sharing

The State Committee on Investments and State Property Management of the Republic of Tajikistan (SCISPM), through its Project Implementation Group (PIG), now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting Criteria

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

(i) At least 5 years of experience in conducting comparable large-scale household surveys in Tajikistan, including at least five surveys involving no fewer than 1,000 respondents each using a Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI) system;

(ii) Availability of qualified key personnel, including field interviewers, to conduct the baseline evaluation study;

(iii) Direct experience in collecting research data in Tajikistan among entrepreneurs; knowledge or experience in interviewing women in rural areas will be considered an advantage; and

(iv) Experience in carrying out similar assignments under projects financed by international financial organizations, including the World Bank or other donors.

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

JOINT PROCUREMENT GRENADA & DOMINICA

Assignment: Outcome-Based Development of an Enhanced Lower-Secondary Curriculum and Assessment in Dominica and Grenada

Reference No.: GD-MOE-GRENADA-552260-CS-QBS
Project: WISTLE (P508559)

Grant No.: TF-C8594, TFC8596

 

Selection Method:  Selection shall follow the World Bank Procurement Regulations using the Quality-Based Selection (QBS) method.

1. Background

The Governments of the Commonwealth of Dominica and Grenada have received financing from the Global Partnership for Education through the World Bank for the Windward Islands Sector Transformation for Learning Enhancement (WISTLE) Project. The Ministries of Education intend to jointly procure a consulting firm to develop, pilot and support implementation of enhanced lower-secondary curricula and aligned assessment systems. The assignment will produce common regional solutions while contextualizing outputs for each country.

2. Objective

The consultancy will design and support implementation of an enhanced lower-secondary curriculum, strengthen national assessment systems, build institutional capacity, integrate digital delivery through an LMS, incorporate inclusive education and TVET pathways, and establish sustainable systems that remain after project completion.

3. Scope of Services

The selected consulting firm will: (i) review existing curricula and policies; (ii) develop curriculum frameworks and learning outcomes; (iii) prepare curricula, teacher guides and learning resources for Forms 1–3 in Dominica and Forms 1–2 in Grenada; (iv) develop a national assessment strategy, item bank and digital assessment library; (v) pilot and refine the curriculum; (vi) train curriculum developers, teachers and education officers; (vii) integrate resources into an existing regional LMS; and (viii) prepare sustainability and rollout plans.

4. Experience, Qualifications

The consulting firm shall demonstrate:

  • At least twelve (12) years' experience managing curriculum-reform projects, and at least twelve (12) years' experience in formative and summative assessment development, of comparable magnitude.
  • At least two (2) completed curriculum assignments and one (1) completed assessment assignment at basic/secondary level in the past five (5) years, the latter involving quality-assured items used in a large-scale assessment.
  • Graduate qualified team members in education, curriculum, or assessment, with proven research, statistical, and qualitative analysis skills.
  • Understanding of the Caribbean education context, with at least two (2) team members having demonstrated regional experience in the Caribbean or a small-island state; a local representative or partner in the Eastern Caribbean is required if the firm is not Caribbean-based.

5. Submission Requirements

Expressions of Interest shall include:

  1. Letter of interest;
  2. Company profile;
  3. Description of similar assignments;
  4. Evidence of technical and managerial capacity;
  5. Availability of key experts (Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage, CVs are not required at the EOI stage)
  6. Details of working in the region, specifically within Grenada and Dominica
  7. Contact information for client references.
  8. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

EOI’s should be a max of 10-15 pages.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered through electronic submission through the procurement system at https://in-tendhost.co.uk/gnd/aspx/Home. Candidates must register on this portal and submit all interest through this medium.

1. Background The Government of Saint Lucia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a Credit toward the cost of the Caribbean Digital Transformation Project. The Ministry of the Public Service, Transport, Information and Utilities Regulation, as the implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of the Credit to eligible payments under the contract for the Consultancy for the Development of a Government of Saint Lucia Secure Wallet with Digital Payment and Integration Solutions.

2. Objective of the Assignment The objective of the assignment is to design, develop and implement a secure Government of Saint Lucia Government Secure Wallet with an integrated Digital Payment System, secure document-management capabilities and integration with relevant Government services and platforms.

3. Scope of the assignment To deliver this objective, the Consultant will be required to undertake a comprehensive set of technical, operational, and regulatory activities, including the following:

Conduct detailed requirements gathering and analysis to inform system design and functional specifications.

Develop the overall system architecture and technical design for the Government Wallet and digital payment solution.

Build secure, scalable mobile and web applications supporting wallet functions and digital payments.

Integrate the solution with existing government platforms, including digiGov and the National Authentication Framework.

Implement secure digital payment capabilities and related documentmanagement features.

Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, and dataprotection controls aligned with international standards.

Establish business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements for the solution.

Deliver user training, operational guidance, and structured knowledgetransfer activities.

Provide warranty support to ensure stability and performance during the initial operational period.

Prepare all necessary documentation and support the Government of Saint Lucia in securing regulatory approval for the Government Wallet, including assessment of the FinTech legal and regulatory framework to ensure compliance with existing laws and policies

Deploy the solution within the hosting infrastructure provided by the Client, including servers, storage, networking, virtualization platform, and operating systems, and configure all required components to ensure full operational readiness

4. Duration of the assignment The estimated duration of the Services is 50 weeks.

iii. Proven experience in developing and deploying secure, scalable web and mobile applications with strong user-experience and interoperability features.

iv. Demonstrated capacity to implement secure solutions aligned with internationally recognized standards, including PCI DSS, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 20022 or equivalent standards.

v. Successful completion of at least three (3) assignments of similar scope and complexity, such as national-level payment systems, e-government platforms or enterprise-level systems-integration assignments.

vi. Demonstrated experience delivering assignments for public-sector clients in the Caribbean, the Organization of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) or comparable jurisdictions.

vii. Prior experience managing assignments financed by international development partners, such as the World Bank, Caribbean Development Bank or United Nations Development Programme, will be considered an advantage.

c) descriptions of comparable assignments, including the name of the client, country, scope of services, contract period, completion status and contact information for verification; and

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                       Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:        SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:       INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT REGIONAL WORKSHOP ON SYSTEMS OF NATIONAL ACCOUNTS (SNA 2025) AS A RESOURCE PERSON TOWARDS DEVELOPMENT OF A REPORT FOR THE REGION FOR MIGRATING TO SNA 2025. BW-SADC-563175-CS-INDV

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:      SADC/3/5/2/459

 

DATE OF ISSUE:              25th August 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services for Conduct a Regional Workshop on Systems of National Accounts (SNA 2025) as a Resource Person Towards Development of a Report for the Region for Migrating to SNA 2025, in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title             :  Individual Consultant to conduct Regional Workshop on Systems of National Accounts (SNA 2025) (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  90 calendar days

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to harmonize national accounts statistics compilation and dissemination practices in the region to ensure Member States produce and disseminate such statistics responsive to data demands performing to regional integration.

 

  1. Specific objectives

The specific objective of the assignment is to service a regional workshop on SNA 2025 as a resource person in support towards development of harmonized national accounts statistics.

  1. Expected results

 

The consultancy is expected to achieve the following results:

  • Enhanced technical capacity of National Statistics Offices (NSOs) in SNA 2025 concepts, definitions and standards;
  • Action Plan for each Member State in a report evaluating the readiness of migrating to SNA 2025 in line with specific actions and timelines for future implementation;

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant with the specific profile as provided below:

Qualifications and Skills

    • A minimum of a master’s degree in statistics, economics or related field.

General Professional Experience

    • Demonstrated experience of 20 years of experience in national accounts statistics subject matter at national and/or international level.

Specific Professional Experience

    • Demonstrable experience in undertaking technical assistance as consultant in at least 10 assignments pertaining mainly to SNA 2008 implementation;
    • Demonstrated experience in undertaking technical assistance in rebasing of GDP in at least 3 assignments; and
    • Demonstrated experience as a resource person in at least 3 assignments in delivering regional training courses on national accounts to developing countries in Africa.

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 90 calendar days.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to venue of the workshop.

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Tuesday, 8th September 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            CONSULTING SERVICES TO DEVELOP FEASIBILITY STUDIES FOR MONGOLIAN CIVIL AVIATION SECTOR AND MURUN (4C AERODROME CODE) AIRPORT IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

REFERENCE NO.

(AS PER PROCUREMENT PLAN):              ZTYA/20260804058

The Government of Mongolia has received a grant financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), through the Global Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) toward the cost of the Gobi Connectivity Improvement Project under Grant No. TF0D0692 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.  

The consulting services (“the Services”) include two distinct but complementary components.

Component A will establish the analytical and strategic foundations for aviation sector development in Mongolia. It will include a comprehensive aviation sector diagnostic, a proportionate first-pass review of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) safety and security compliance issues relevant to airport network planning and investment readiness, preparation of the Mongolia Airport Network Development Strategy to 2040, a companion Policy Recommendations Note, and a structured stakeholder consultation process. Together, these outputs will provide Government with a practical framework for airport classification, demand development, institutional strengthening, climate resilience, high-level investment prioritization, and identification of follow-on policy and technical assistance needs.

Component B will prepare a full feasibility study for Murun Airport. The Government has identified Murun Airport as a priority project requiring detailed assessment and project preparation. The feasibility study shall evaluate the technical, operational, environmental, social, financial, economic, fiscal, and institutional viability of the proposed investment and define an appropriate development concept for implementation.

The assignment is expected to run for approximately 6 to 7 months from the date of contract effectiveness. Component A and Component B shall proceed in parallel throughout the assignment period.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be found at the following website:

Tender.gov.mn

The Ministry of Road and Transport now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. General experience:

General experience implementing consultancy services in the field of civil aviation and transport sector strategy, planning and the feasibility studies; and preliminary/detailed engineering design of projects in cold climate regions, including economic/financial analysis and safeguard integration, during the last 10 years;

 

 

In addition, demonstrated experience in at least one assignment involving the preparation of environmental and social safeguard instruments for World Bank-financed projects or projects financed by comparable multilateral development banks, including at a minimum one of the following: Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plan (P-ESMP), and inputs into subsequent safeguard instruments such as a Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF). Evidence should be provided in the firm`s EoI.

  1. Specific Experiences: 
  1. Proven experience in preparing civil aviation sector development strategies and/or airport feasibility studies (including associated policy, institutional, or PPP/commercial advisory) during the last 10 years. At least 2 such similar contracts should be demonstrated, each with a contract value of not less than US$300,000 (Please be sure to include the contract value in your submission).
  2. The consulting team must include Environmental and Social Specialists with demonstrated experience applying the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent international safeguard/environmental and social risk management standards. At minimum, the team must demonstrate capacity to address environmental screening, social impact assessment, resettlement risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and GBV/SEA/SH risk management.
  1. Technical and managerial organization of the firm

General description of the firm's technical and managerial organization, including the structure of the organization, general qualifications of staff, and number of permanent professional staff. Do not provide CVs of key staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL)

First Date of Publication: 27th August 2026

Geotechnical Engineer - Ref No. KVWaSIP-IC-03-083/84

1.0 Background

The Government of Nepal (GoN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services include providing technical, procurement, financial management, environmental and social, contract management, and other professional support required for effective implementation of the Project through the Project Management Unit (PMU)

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide a detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating that they possess the required educational qualifications, professional experience, and technical competence to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria for each assignment are specified in the respective Terms of Reference (TOR), which may be obtained from the address or website indicated below

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Geotechnical Engineer and requests applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position.

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

As a team member of the Project Management Unit (PMU), the overall objective of this assignment is to provide specialist geotechnical expertise, independent technical review, and quality assurance support to the PMU for the planning, feasibility confirmation, detailed engineering design, and implementation readiness of the KV WaSIP. The Geotechnical Engineer will help ensure that site investigations, geological and geotechnical interpretations, foundation assessments, construction material evaluations, slope stability analyses, and related design inputs for the proposed dam and associated bulk water supply infrastructure are technically robust, risk-informed, constructible, and consistent with applicable national requirements, World Bank requirements, and international good industry practice.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

The duties of the Specialist is mentioned in the Terms of Reference in detail.

4. Qualifications and Experience

All applications will be evaluated against the assignment’s required qualifications below.  

Candidates who comply with the qualifications will be scored according to predefined criteria. A minimum of three candidates will be shortlisted and interviewed. The candidate with the highest score will be invited to negotiate a contract. Referees of the selected candidate may be contacted to verify prior experience, performance, and interpersonal skills. 

 The Geotechnical Engineer shall possess strong academic qualifications and demonstrated professional experience relevant to geotechnical engineering, dam foundations, slope stability, seepage control, construction materials, and multidisciplinary technical review of major water infrastructure projects. The expert should have proven capability to assess the adequacy of site investigations and geotechnical analyses, review engineering assumptions and design inputs, and advise on constructability, dam safety, geotechnical risk, and long-term performance of dam and associated bulk water supply infrastructure

Qualifications and Relevant Experience

  • Education:
    • The expert shall hold at least a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, geological engineering, engineering geology, water resources engineering, or a related discipline.
    • A master’s degree in geotechnical engineering, engineering geology, dam engineering, or a closely related field is required, and a PhD will be considered an added advantage.
  • Work Experience:
    • At least 15 years of relevant geotechnical engineering experience, including site investigations, dam foundation assessment, and design review or implementation support for major water resources, dam, or bulk water infrastructure projects.
    • Demonstrated expertise in geotechnical assessment and design review for large dams and associated infrastructure, including foundations, abutments, slopes, spillways, outlet works, access roads, reservoirs, and related facilities.
    • Proven capability in interpreting geotechnical investigations and advising on dam safety, long-term performance, and construction materials, including seepage, grouting, slope stability, seismic effects, monitoring, borrow areas, and constructability.
  • Interpersonal Skills
    • The expert shall have strong analytical, report writing, and communication skills, and shall be able to communicate clearly and effectively in spoken and written English.

5. Evaluation and Selection Method

The Senior Dam Specialist will be hired by the PMU using the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method following “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) Seventh Edition 2025. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations”.

6. Duration of the Assignment

The Geotechnical Engineer is expected to provide support to the PMU for an expected input of 132 person days during a 17 month project period on an intermittent basis. The Project Manager shall plan the inputs of the Engineer based on the project schedule and report deliverables of the Design Consultant. 

7. Remuneration

A market-based salary package commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications will be offered.

8. Reporting

The Geotechnical Engineer will report directly to the Project Manager, PMU.

9. Location

  • The consultant will be based at the PMU office and may be required to travel outside the valley as needed for project-related procurement activities.
  • The Project shall provide following facilities to consultant during his tenure of service:
  • Office space
  • Email and internet access
  • Required office stationery and other materials
  • Photocopying/printing facilities

10. Application Process

Interested candidates shall submit a complete application package comprising:

  1. Up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV).
  2. Copies of academic and professional certificates.
  3. Contact details for at least three (03) professional references familiar with the candidate’s relevant work.

Applications shall be submitted electronically no later than 17.00 PM on 11th September 2026 to the following e-mail address: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com. Only complete applications received by the deadline will be considered.
