The Project aims to increase efficiency and improve conditions to ensure quality and transparency in the higher education system of Ukraine.

The purpose of the Consultant's activities is to provide administrative and organizational support for the activities of the support team of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in the higher education sector and to coordinate with management, structural units, higher education institutions, the UIHERP Project, and other higher education stakeholders in order to facilitate an effective management process.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time September 8, 2026.

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for Consulting Services

(Individual Consultant)

Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist

Procurement No. MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20

Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project

World Bank Loan No. 9238-UA


 

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (hereinafter referred to as "IBRD" or the "World Bank") signed Loan Agreement No. 9238-UA in the amount of US$200 million to implement the Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (hereinafter, the "Project"). The Project is implemented in Ukraine by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) with support from the World Bank Group.

Project implementation period: 2021-2027.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve the efficiency, conditions for quality, and transparency in Ukraine's higher education system.

The Project comprises six components:

  • Component 1: Sector-Wide Improvements to Governance, Financing, Quality and Transparency.
  • Component 2: Alliances and Partnerships for Improved Efficiency and Quality.
  • Component 3: Capacity Building and Education Environment Enhancement.
  • Component 4: Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation.
  • Component 5: Support to Academic and Social Scholarships for Higher Education Students.
  • Component 6: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).

The Project will finance two expenditure categories: Category (i) - investments in goods, works, and services, with disbursements made against eligible expenditures; and Category (ii) - transfers to the budget upon fulfilment of certain results-based conditions, with disbursements likewise made against eligible expenditures subject to the achievement of specified results, as set forth in the Loan Agreement and the Project Operations Manual.

Within Part 3 of the Project, specialized consultants are planned to be engaged to support the effective management of the higher education and research system, as well as higher education institutions, and to provide support for the implementation of digital, financial, human resources, and other components of higher education reform at the institutional level.

More detailed information about the Project is available at: https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P171050

These Terms of Reference set out the objective and scope of the consulting services, as well as the qualification requirements for the Consultant.

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of this assignment is to provide administrative and organizational support for the activities of the support team of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in the higher education sector and to coordinate with management, structural units, higher education institutions, the UIHERP Project, and other higher education stakeholders in order to facilitate an effective management process.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant's scope of services shall include, but not be limited to:

  • ensure effective working interaction among the Deputy Minister, MoES structural units, consultants of UIHERP and other stakeholder;
  • collect and consolidate information required for UIHERP implementation;
  • organize the day-to-day work of specialists and consultants of the MoES UIHERP support team;
  • coordinate work-related matters, deadlines, and task priorities;
  • maintain working calendars and records of tasks, deadlines, status, and agreements; send reminders to responsible persons and provide timely notice of delays or the need for management decisions;
  • coordinate the preparation and conduct of working sessions, meetings, events, and visits under the Project; record agreements and monitor follow-up actions;
  • ensure the timely exchange of information among MoES management, structural units, the support consultant team, higher education institutions, partners, and UIHERP;
  • collect, verify for completeness, systematize, and technically format working materials, background information, draft letters, and meeting materials;
  • organize the clearance of documents and materials, track their routing and status, and monitor the completion of assigned tasks;
  • organize the collection of reports from engaged Support Team specialists for the preparation of monthly and other reports required under the Project, and perform other Project implementation tasks within the Consultant's competence;
  • perform other Project-related tasks within the Consultant's competence, as assigned by the Deputy Minister of Education and Science of Ukraine responsible for the higher education system.

The following outputs and results are expected from the services (the list is not exhaustive):

  • the day-to-day work of MoES specialists, consultants of the higher education support team, and UIHERP is organized;
  • working calendars, task lists, deadlines, status, and agreements are kept up to date; decisions and follow-up actions are recorded and tracked;
  • working meetings, sessions, events, and visits are organized in a timely manner; the necessary materials are prepared and information exchange among the parties involved is ensured;
  • working materials and evidence of task completion are systematized;
  • effective working interaction is ensured among the Deputy Minister, MoES structural units, the support team and UIHERP, higher education institutions, and other higher education stakeholders;
  • the day-to-day work of the team's specialists and consultants is organized.

IV. REPORTING

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Co-Coordinator, be accountable to the Deputy Minister of Education and Science of Ukraine responsible for the higher education system, and work under their supervision.

The Consultant shall coordinate their activities with the Project Manager - Head of the Consultant Team and ensure the administrative coordination of specialists and consultants engaged in implementing UIHERP tasks in higher education.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports in hard copy to the Project Coordinator/Co-Coordinator.

Each monthly report shall include a concise description of the administrative and coordination tasks performed, meetings and events organized, assignments and work processes supported, the status of interaction with engaged specialists, and the materials collected and systematized for UIHERP implementation and reporting. Where necessary, the report shall include agendas, minutes, links, task lists, or other evidence of performance.

V. RESOURCES PROVIDED

MoES shall provide the Consultant in a timely manner with the information necessary to perform the assignment.

MoES may provide the Consultant with a workspace, including the equipment necessary to perform the functions (e.g., a personal computer, communications equipment, and office equipment).

VI. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • a Master's degree or higher;
  • at least three years of professional experience in administrative coordination, project administration, or organizational support for managers or teams in the education sector;
  • experience organizing the work of a team or group of consultants while concurrently managing multiple tasks, deadlines, and clearances;
  • experience preparing working meetings and events, taking minutes or recording agreements, and monitoring their implementation;
  • experience organizing document workflows, clearance processes, and working interaction among structural units, partners, or contractors;
  • skills in collecting, systematizing, and consolidating information for working and reporting materials;
  • strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work with confidential information, manage multiple tasks, and meet tight deadlines;
  • fluency in Ukrainian;
  • English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or higher;
  • proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, videoconferencing platforms, and digital tools for task management and teamwork.

The following preferred (non-mandatory) qualifications, competencies, and experience will be considered an advantage:

  • an academic background in management, public administration, project management, international relations, political science, or a related field;
  • experience in higher education;
  • experience in the public sector;
  • experience providing administrative support to projects financed by international financial institutions or international technical assistance programs;
  • knowledge of other foreign languages will be considered an advantage.

MoES may invite the most qualified candidates for an interview to clarify information provided in their CVs.

VII. PERIOD AND PLACE OF WORK

The Consultant shall provide the services until 30 June 2027. with the possibility of extending the contract if UIHERP is extended.

The Consultant shall provide the services under this Contract on an ongoing basis throughout its term, with a level of effort equivalent to full-time engagement, to the extent necessary for the proper performance of the tasks specified in these Terms of Reference.

The Client and the Consultant may at any time agree on a different workload based on the actual volume of tasks.

Specific contractual terms and working arrangements shall be discussed and agreed separately.

VIII. APPLICATION PACKAGE

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org, marina.chubenko@mon.gov.ua indicating the email subject: «MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20: [NAME]».

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time September 8, 2026.

If the candidate fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the candidate’s application.

Contratación de Consultor Individual – Especialista Social
Referencia STEP: BO-UCP-PPCR-546633-CS-INDV

La Unidad de Coordinación del Programa Piloto de Resiliencia Climática (UCP–PPCR) invita a los profesionales interesados a presentar su Expresión de Interés para la contratación de un Consultor Individual que desempeñe el cargo de Especialista Social, en el marco del Proyecto de Gestión Resiliente del Agua para Riego Comunitario y Familiar, financiado por el Banco Mundial mediante el Contrato de Préstamo N.º 9643-BO.

Los Términos de Referencia (TDR) y demás documentos del proceso estarán disponibles a partir del 17 de julio de 2026 en el Sistema de Contrataciones Estatales (SICOES). Asimismo, podrán solicitarse al correo electrónico ppcr.contrataciones3@gmail.com o recabarse en las oficinas de la UCP–PPCR, ubicadas en la calle Guachalla entre Ecuador y Sánchez Lima, Edificio Nicole N.º 2186, zona de Sopocachi, ciudad de La Paz.

Los interesados deberán presentar su Expresión de Interés, incluyendo el formato de presentación y la documentación de respaldo requerida, hasta las 15:00 horas del 04 de agosto de 2026, mediante cualquiera de las siguientes modalidades:

  • Presentación física: En sobre cerrado, en las oficinas de la UCP–PPCR, ubicadas en la calle Guachalla entre Ecuador y Sánchez Lima, Edificio Nicole N.º 2186, zona de Sopocachi, ciudad de La Paz.
  • Presentación digital: Mediante envío de la documentación al correo electrónico ppcr.contrataciones3@gmail.com.

La Expresión de Interés deberá contener la Hoja de Vida documentada, elaborada conforme a los formatos establecidos en la convocatoria. El consultor que resulte seleccionado deberá presentar la documentación original para su verificación previa a la suscripción del contrato.

El proceso de selección se desarrollará de conformidad con las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial (quinta edición, septiembre de 2023), observando las disposiciones aplicables en materia de elegibilidad, conflicto de interés y demás requisitos establecidos en dichas regulaciones.

(“Procurement Regulation”) and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulation. In addition, please refer to paragraphs 3.14 to 3.17 in the “Procurement Regulation” on the Conflict of interest.

 

INVITATION:

Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from the State Project Implementation Unit (SPIU), through the Project Manager (PM) or Email: crsimpactproject@gmail.com and may also inspect the bidding documents during office hours between 9.00 am – 4.00 pm Monday – Friday at the address below.

Pays : République Démocratique du Congo

Date limite : 10 août 2026

 

1.       Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a obtenu un crédit et un don de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d’autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi « TRANSFORME/RDC » et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du marché de travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation d’infrastructures pour le Centre de PME WPD à Kananga.

 

2.       L’Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Autonomisation des Femmes Entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la Transformation Economique et l’Emploi (UCP/TRANSFORME/RDC) invite, par la présente, les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles à soumettre des Offres sous pli fermé, pour la réalisation des travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation d’infrastructures pour le Centre de PME WPD à Kananga.

 

La construction complète, tous corps d'état confondus, d'un entrepôt logistique, de quatre (4) usines de transformation, des bâtiments administratifs et des salles de formation, ainsi que la réalisation des voiries et réseaux divers (VRD), comprenant les réseaux de drainage des eaux pluviales, un forage, les réseaux d'adduction et de distribution d'eau, les installations sanitaires et l'ensemble des ouvrages connexes nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du site.

 

3.       La passation du Marché sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale, Appel d’offres national (AON) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projet d’investissement (FPI) » de juillet 2016, révisé en Novembre 2017, juillet 2018, novembre 2020 et septembre 2023, et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.

 

4.       Les Soumissionnaires intéressés de pays éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires dans les bureaux de l'UCP/TRANSFORME-RDC, à l’attention de Monsieur le Coordonnateur National, Alexis MANGALA NGONGO, E-mail : transforme@transforme.cd (avec copie à cpm@transforme.cd) et examiner le Document d’Appel d’Offres durant les heures de bureau si applicable par exemple entre 9h00’ à 16h00’ (heure locale de Kinshasa, TU+1) à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

 

5.       Le Document d’Appel d’Offres en langue française, peut être acheté par tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de 200 USD (Deux-cents dollars américains). La méthode de paiement sera le dépôt direct du montant au compte du Projet TRANSFORME/RDC logé à la RAWBANK, Intitulé du compte : Ministère des Finances v/c TRANSFORME-DAO, numéro du comte : 05100 – 05101 – 00003991006 – 61 (USD) « Code Swift : RAWBCDKIXXX ». Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé par voie électronique ou téléchargé à partir d’un site web autorisé du Projet TRANSFORME « www.transforme.cd ». Seules les offres des soumissionnaires ayant acheté le Dossier d’Appel d’offres seront acceptées.

 

6.      Les Offres doivent être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 10 août 2026 à 14h00’ précises (heure locale de Kinshasa, TU+1). La remise des Offres par voie électronique ne sera pas permise. Toute Offre reçue après la date limite de remise des Offres sera écartée. Les Offres seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants désignés des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne qui souhaite assister à l’ouverture des Offres à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous le 10 août 2026 à 14h30’ (heure locale de Kinshasa, TU+1).

 

7.       Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une garantie de l’offre, pour un montant de :

  • Lot N°1 : 42 250,00 USD (quarante-deux mille deux cent cinquante dollars américains) ;
  • Lot N°2 : 4 900,00 USD (quatre mille neuf cent dollars américains) ;
  • Lot N°3 : 2 420,00 USD (deux mille quatre cent vingt dollars américains).

          Qui sera une garantie d’offre émise par une banque locale en RDC de premier ordre ou par une banque à l’international de premier ordre ayant un correspondant en RDC.

 

8.      Veillez noter que le Règlement de Passation des Marchés exige que l’Emprunteur divulgue les informations sur les propriétaires effectifs du Soumissionnaire attributaire, dans le cadre de l’avis de Notification d’Attribution de Marché, en renseignant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs inclus dans le document d’Appel d’Offres.

THE DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF SRI LANKA

                                                                                  Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation

                                                                     Climate Resilience Multiphase Programmatic Approach (CResMPA)

                                                                                                           Request for Bids -Goods

                                                                                                    (Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

 

Country: Sri Lanka

Name of Project: Climate Resilience Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach 

Contract Title: Supply, Installation, and Commissioning of Five (05) Coastal Metocean Automated Observation Stations at Designated Coastal Locations in Sri Lanka for the Department of Meteorology

Loan No.: IBRD 89960

RFB Reference No.: SLMOI/CRES/DOM/G/ICB/119

 

1. The Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Climate Resilience Multiphase Programmatic Approach (CResMPA) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement and establishment of Coastal Metocean Stations. “For this contract, the Borrower shall process eligible payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.”

2. The Chairperson, Project Procurement Committee now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for the Supply, Installation, and Commissioning of Five Coastal Metocean Automated Observation Stations at off Delft Island, Pigeon Island of Trincomalee, Wisky Point of Arugambay, Hikkaduwa Fishery Harbor and Dikovita Fishery Harbor, Colombo in Sri Lanka for the Department of Meteorology, Sri Lanka, shall complete at a proposed location considering various environmental, safety, and operational aspects within 75 days from the date contract singed. Margin of preference shall not apply.

3. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB)  as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th edition September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Bidder must meet the following minimum qualification criteria

(i) General Experience: The Bidder shall have been actively engaged, in its own name, in the business of supplying, installing, commissioning and maintaining meteorological, oceanographic, hydrological, or environmental monitoring equipment for at least ten (10) years preceding the bid submission date.

(ii) Specific Experience:  The Bidder shall have successfully completed at least two (2) contracts within the last ten (10) years, each with a minimum contract value of LKR 60 million or USD 177,000.00 for the supply, installation, and commissioning of metocean stations or comparable marine monitoring platforms in WMO member countries.

(iii) Manufacturer’s Experience: The manufacturer of the equipment shall have at least fifteen (15) years of continuous experience in the design and manufacture of met ocean sensors and related equipment for marine meteorological and oceanographic observation purposes. The manufacturers shall have supplied and contributed to at least two (2) projects in WMO Member countries, and within such projects a minimum of twenty (20) Met-ocean Stations of similar or higher specifications shall have been successfully deployed.

(iv) Financial Capacity:  

  1. Average Annual Turnover: The Bidder shall demonstrate a minimum average annual turnover of LKR 330 million or USD 980,000.00 over the last three (3) financial years prior to the bid submission deadline.
  2. Liquid Assets / Credit Line: The Bidder shall have access to financial resources or confirmed credit facilities of at least LKR 165 million or USD 490,000.00.

5. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 60% for the technical part and for 40 % for non-technical part for the total bid cost

6. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from Project Director, Climate Resilience Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach and e-mail pdcresmpa@gmail.com of officer in charge and inspect the bidding document during office hours 9.00 am to 3.00 pm (SL local time) at the address given below or may be downloaded and reviewed from https://promise.lk/ and https://meteo.gov.lk/ websites only for reference purpose.

7. The bidding document in English may be purchased by interested eligible Bidders upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a nonrefundable fee of LKR 45,000.00 or in a convertible currency in Sri Lanka from July 22, 2026 between 9.00 am to 3.00 pm (SL local time) on any working day. The method of payment will be cash.

The Government of Kenya (GoK) in conjunction with the World Bank is implementing a five-year Supporting Access to Finance & Enterprise Recovery (SAFER) Project whose overall development objective is to increase access to financial services, enhance the capabilities, and support the COVID-19 recovery of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Kenya. This objective will be achieved through: (i) Innovation and Liquidity Support to MSMEs; (ii) De-risking Lending to MSMEs; and (iii) Technical Assistance and Project Management. The SAFER Project intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: (a) Assessing the existing supervisory practices against the current Risk Based Supervision Manual, best practices and identify gaps; (b) Reviewing the Supervisory policy framework and current Risk Based Supervision Manual; (c) Training technical staff on revised Risk Based Supervisory Approach; (d) Arranging for Benchmarking studies and knowledge sharing visits for selected staff to countries that have best practices in supervision of MFIs and SACCOs; (e) Supporting in the offsite analysis and onsite inspections. The assignment is expected to take five (5) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website www.treasury.go.ke/tenders.html; https://piu.treasury.go.ke/ or can be obtained at the address given below.

The National Treasury & Economic Planning (the Client), through its Project Implementation Unit, now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultants should provide their most recent profiles showing their experience, qualifications, capabilities, references and details of experience especially around their expertise, etc. The shortlisting requirements are: a) the consultant / resident advisor shall be an individual consultant who has experience gained from working for: a Sacco (credit union) regulatory agencies or Microfinance or commercial banking regulator in a senior technical capacity, with at least ten (10) years of experience in the implementation of Risk Based Supervision Framework; or a multilateral agency in a technical capacity and in which his/her duties have involved advising on Sacco (credit union) Banking or Microfinance sector reforms; Experience with credit union prudential regulation will be an added advantage; b) Should possess at least an undergraduate qualification in  accounting, economics, law, banking and finance, or financial cooperative systems. A postgraduate qualification in a relevant field will be an added advantage; c) Professional qualifications in financial analysis, accounting, forensic accounting or regulation of financial institutions; d) Experience in implementing risk-based supervision techniques; e) Strong familiarity with current developments in regulatory and risk management supervision especially with respect to Saccos or Credit unions, microfinance and commercial banks in Africa; f) Conducted previous related assignments within the banking sector and/or financial services sector for regulatory or similar institutions. Recently completed assignments specifically on risk issues related to Saccos or Credit unions, microfinance institutions will be an added advantage; g) Exposure to training courses, seminars and conferences on risk-based supervision techniques; h) Experience in training in risk assessment in supervisory authorities and financial institutions; i) Basic awareness of the Kenyan Financial System and other Africa jurisdictions and j) Strong familiarity with Saccos or microfinance in emerging economies

The expression of interest is also open to interested firms who may wish to propose individual consultants. In such cases, only the experience and qualifications of the individuals proposed shall be considered in the selection process and not the firm’s corporate experience.

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, July 2016, Revised September 2025, 7th edition which can be found at the following website: www.worldbank.org/procurement.

1.0       Background:

The Pacific Community (www.spc.int) has received financing in the amount of USD 6.0 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific Islands Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Statistics for Development Division

The SPC Statistics for Development Division leads the implementation of the Strategic Framework for Pacific Statistics, endorsed by PICT leaders in 2023. The framework promotes a regional approach to strengthening the quality, scope, and coordination of official statistics across the Pacific.

SPC supports national statistical offices by building capacity to produce reliable demographic, economic, and social data for evidence-based policy and decision making. As a regional technical provider operating across 22 PICTs, SPC plays a key role in adapting international statistical standards to Pacific contexts, particularly for small island developing states with limited resources.

Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific (PacStat) Project

The PacStat project is an International Development Association (IDA; https://ida.worldbank.org/) funded project that is to be implemented over the period of June 2020 to February 2027 including an additional financing phase.  The overall development objective of PACSTAT is to improve the quality of welfare data collection and accessibility to comparable welfare data in the Pacific Island Countries.

The context for this project is summarized as:

  • PICs are characterised by small populations spread across vast areas.
  • Better, more timely, and more comparable data is needed to understand deprivation between countries as well as identify and monitor regional trends.
  • Data deprivation in the PICs hinders evidence-based policy design.
  • National Statistics Offices (NSOs) lack funding to meet the costs of data collection in the Pacific.
  • Low statistical capacity is a major challenge in addressing data deprivation.
  • There has been some improvement in statistical capacity over time, but results have not been sustained.
  • There is potential for improvements and innovations in both administrative and survey data to lead to one or more of substantial cost savings, new statistics, or improved quality of statistics.

The additional financing under the Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific Islands project directly supports regional efforts to advance statistical innovation and capacity building, with a particular focus on operational enhancement of administrative data for official statistics. Through commissioned works endorsed by the Pacific Statistics Methods Board (PSMB), the project will assess and strengthen national administrative data systems, enabling their systematic integration into statistical production processes across Pacific Island countries.

This initiative addresses critical operational challenges including data governance, quality assurance, interoperability, and confidentiality by building institutional, legal, and technical capacity within National Statistics Offices and priority government agencies. The additional financing sustains and expands high-priority activities, such as regional workshops, technical assistance, and the development of standard operating procedures and metadata templates, ensuring readiness for regionally standardised data reporting and evidence use. By promoting the practical use of administrative data alongside traditional survey and census programmes, the project enhances the quality, timeliness, and comparability of welfare statistics, directly contributing to the achievement of project development objectives and laying the groundwork for the next phase of regional statistical innovation

2.0       Objective of the assignment:

The overall objective of the assignment is to enhance the operational readiness of national statistical offices (NSOs) and administrative data holding agencies in the Pacific region to use administrative data for the production of official statistics, building on the findings of a preliminary administrative data readiness assessment which is currently being completed by a separate assignment.

The objective will be achieved by supporting practical, implementation-oriented activities that address priority gaps identified during the readiness assessment, including:

  • Strengthening the capacity of Pacific NSOs to operationally access, manage, and use administrative data for statistical production, through the design and implementation of targeted pilots, improved workflows, and institutional collaboration;
  • Enhancing the operational usability of selected administrative data systems in the Pacific region for official statistics, including arrangements related to data access, governance, data management practices, and integration into statistical production processes, either as standalone sources or as part of a broader source mix.

The assignment is intended to move beyond diagnostic assessment and to demonstrate, through a limited number of pilots in selected Pacific countries, practical approaches and good practices for the effective use of administrative data in official statistics. It will support learning, documentation, and regional knowledge exchange, and inform the potential scalingup of successful approaches in subsequent phases.

3.0       Scope of Services:

The Scope of the assignment includes the following tasks:  

Task 1 – Selection of pilot countries and agencies: Identify and select three pilot countries, with one country selected if possible from each Pacific subregion (IDA countries) based on national contexts and involvement in the PacStat 2 project and identify relevant use cases for the production of official statistics using administrative data. Selection will be informed by previous readiness assessments, national statistical priorities, and the willingness and capacity of institutions to engage in pilot activities, and feasibility within the contract timeframe from a legal point of view. The selection process will be informed and validated by SPC, which will also be involved in initial consultations with participating countries to confirm scope, expectations, and roles. 

Task 2 – Development of agency level operational work plans: Develop agency level operational work plans for the use of administrative data in official statistics in each pilot country, in collaboration with national statistical offices (NSOs) and selected administrative agencies. Based on at least two meetings with NSOs and administrative agencies for each pilot country and building on the admin data readiness assessment project recently carried out by the World Bank, the work plans will define the intended statistical uses of administrative data, describe institutional roles and responsibilities, identify required legal, technical, and organisational arrangements, and outline a sequencing of activities and milestones. 

Task 3 – Design and documentation of administrative data flows: Design and document administrative data flows from source systems to statistical production processes for the selected pilot use cases. This will include documenting data extraction mechanisms and calendar, data structures and variables, metadata availability, data transformation and validation steps, and quality assurance procedures. The documentation will focus on clarity, consistency, and reproducibility, supporting both pilot implementation and potential future institutionalisation, with key design decisions validated by SPC. 

Task 4 – Development of data sharing protocols and arrangements: Support the development or refinement of data sharing protocols and related governance arrangements required for the regular use of administrative data for official statistics. This will include clarifying access conditions, data transfer modalities, update frequency, confidentiality and security requirements, revision policies, and roles related to data stewardship. Existing legal frameworks and institutional practices will be considered. 

Task 5 – Pilot implementation of administrative data pipelines: Support the pilot implementation of administrative data pipelines in each selected country, focusing on the operational use of administrative data for selected statistical outputs. This will include supporting the use of appropriate IT infrastructure, data ingestion, application of agreed data processing and quality checks, and the production of pilot or experimental statistical outputs. Statistical processing will be implemented using the R scripting language, with computer code hosted on a GitHub repository owned by the respective countries. The purpose of this task is to assess operational feasibility, identify practical challenges, and document lessons learned, rather than to establish full production systems. 

Task 6 – Regional workshop on administrative data for official statistics: Design and deliver a regional workshop on the use of administrative data for official statistics in the Pacific. The workshop will provide a platform for pilot countries to share experiences, challenges, and lessons learned, and to facilitate peer to peer learning and experience exchange among participating NSOs and agencies. The workshop agenda and content will be validated by SPC.

  • Regional workshop and final completion deliverables, including workshop agenda and materials, a summary of discussions, lessons learned and agreed good practices, a synthesis of results across all tasks, and recommendations for scalingup or institutionalisation.

The Finance and Administration Officer in SPC’s Statistics for Development division will be the focal point for all finance and administrative aspects of the Project. 

 All reports and deliverables should be submitted in English. 8.0       Selection Criteria – Qualifications, Experience, and Skills:

The consultant should meet the following minimum requirements:

Academic qualifications 

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s level or higher) in statistics, data science, economics, information systems, public policy, or a closely related field. 
  • A Bachelor’s degree with extensive relevant professional experience may be considered in lieu of a postgraduate qualification. 

Professional experience 

  • Minimum of 8–10 years of relevant professional experience in official statistics, administrative data systems, data integration, or statistical modernisation programmes. 
  • Demonstrated experience working with national statistical offices (NSOs) and government ministries or agencies that manage administrative data. 
  • Proven experience supporting the use of administrative data for official statistics, either through readiness assessments, system design, or operational implementation. 
  • Experience working in developing country contexts, preferably Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or similar capacity constrained environments. 
  • Experience working on donor funded projects, preferably World Bank–financed or multilateral development programmes. 

Technical expertise 

  • Strong understanding of administrative data ecosystems, including data quality assessment, metadata, classifications, identifiers, and data governance. 
  • Practical experience with data integration, data flows, and statistical production processes involving administrative data. 
  • Familiarity with legal, confidentiality, privacy, and data sharing frameworks relevant to the use of administrative data for statistical purposes. 
  • Experience designing or supporting data sharing protocols, operational work plans, or pilot data pipelines. 
  • For implementation focused work: experience using statistical or data processing tools (e.g. R or similar scripting languages) for data processing and quality assurance is an advantage. 

Analytical and reporting skills 

  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to translate technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations. 
  • Proven ability to produce high-quality written outputs, including assessment reports, technical documentation, implementation plans, and synthesis reports suitable for senior management and donors. 
  • Ability to document complex technical processes in a clear, structured, and reproducible manner. 

Stakeholder engagement and communication 

  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with NSOs, line ministries, and technical counterparts across multiple institutions. 
  • Strong facilitation and communication skills, including experience supporting consultations, workshops, or knowledge exchange activities. 
  • Ability to work effectively in a multicultural and regional environment and to manage multiple stakeholders with differing capacities and priorities. 

Language and availability 

  • Excellent written and spoken English is required. 
  • Knowledge of French or another Pacific regional language is an advantage. 
  • Availability to undertake the assignment within the specified timeframe and to travel internationally, if required.

MINISTERE DE L’ECONOMIE, Des finances et du budget (MEFB)

BUREAU DE STRATEGIE ET DE DEVELOPPEMENT (BSD)

PROJET DE MOBILISATION DES RECETTES INTERIEURES ET GESTION DES DEPENSES PUBLIQUES DE LA REPUBLIQUE DE GUINEE (P513145)

========================================

 

            SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

SELECTION D’UN CABINET POUR L’ELABORATION DU MANUEL DE PROCEDURES ADMINISTRATIVES, FINANCIERES, COMPTABLES, DE PASSATION DE MARCHES DU PROJET

       Date de fin : 17 Aout 2026

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Guinée a sollicité et obtenu de l’IDA un Fonds de Préparation du Projet de Mobilisation des Recettes Intérieures et Gestion des Dépenses Publiques de la Guinée pour un montant total de 400 000 USD. La phase préparatoire du Projet est confiée à l’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles, Minières et de l’Environnement (UGP/PGRNME) sous l’égide du Ministère des Mines et de la Géologie (MMG). La Coordination des activités du Projet sera assurée par le Ministère de l’Economie, des Finances et du Budget (MEFB), à travers son Bureau de Stratégie et de Développement (BSD).

 

Le Gouvernement de la République de Guinée à ‘intention d’utiliser une partie du montant du Fonds de Préparation du Projet pour effectuer des paiements au titre de services de consultants pour : élaboration du manuel de procédures administratives, financières, comptables, de passation de marchés du Projet.

 

  1. Objectif de la Mission

L’objectif général de la mission est l’élaboration du Manuel de Procédures Administratives, Comptables, Financières et de Passation de Marchés du Projet devant porter sur la mise en œuvre de toutes les composantes du projet aux fins de facilitation de leur exécution. Le Manuel devra décrire les grandes lignes relatives à l’organisation et le fonctionnement du Projet et être surtout complété par des annexes faisant partie intégrante (gestion financière, gestion des ressources humaines, suivi/évaluation et passation des marchés).

Les Termes de Références (TDRs) détaillés de la mission peuvent être obtenus aux adresses indiquées ci-dessous.

  1. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles, Minières et de l’Environnement (PGRNME) invite les firmes de consultants (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

 

  • Expérience générale :

 

Le consultant sera une firme/société/cabinet/groupement ayant au moins dix (10) années d’expérience en matière de gestion administrative et financière, d’audit et d’élaboration de manuels de procédures administratives et financières pour des projets financés par la Banque mondiale. Il doit avoir d’excellentes connaissances sur les systèmes de gestion financière, comptable, budgétaire et des procédures de passation de marchés, avec une expérience avec l’administration Guinéenne.

  • Expérience spécifique :

 

Le Consultant doit, conformément au point VIII des TDR, avoir :

  • Une excellente connaissance du système de gestion financière des projets financés par la Banque Mondiale ;
  • Une expérience confirmée dans l’élaboration de manuels de procédures administratives, comptables, financières et de passation de marchés pour des projets financés par la Banque Mondiale (avoir réalisées diverses missions pertinentes/similaires).

 

  • Disposer d’une capacité technique et administrative en présentant les pièces requises (Agrément/RCCM, Organisation/organigramme, inscription à un ordre professionnel, etc.).

 

Ce qui pourrait correspondre à la répartition ci-après :

  • Expérience générale (20 points) ;       
  •  Expériences spécifique (70 points) ; et
  • Capacité technique et administrative (10 points).

 

Le personnel clé ne sera pas évalué lors de l'établissement de la liste restreinte.

  1. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.14, 3.16, et 3.17 1.9 de la Section III de : « BANQUE MONDIALE, Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) », (Edition Septembre 2025), relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables. Veuillez noter les dispositions additionnelles suivantes relatives au conflit d’intérêts dans le cadre des Services objet de la présente Sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt :

Consultants ne peuvent être engagés pour des missions qui seraient incompatibles avec leurs obligations présentes ou passées envers d’autres clients, ou qui risqueraient de les mettre dans l’impossibilité de remplir leur mandat au mieux des intérêts de l’Emprunteur. Sans préjudice du caractère général de ces dispositions, les Consultants ne peuvent être engagés dans les circonstances énoncées ci-après :

  1. Aucune entreprise engagée par l’Emprunteur pour livrer des Fournitures, réaliser des Travaux ou fournir des Services Autres que des Services des Consultants pour un projet (ni aucune entreprise affiliée qui la contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’elle contrôle elle-même ou qui est placée sous un contrôle commun) n’est admise à fournir des Services de Consultants consécutifs ou directement liés à ces Fournitures, Travaux ou Services Autres que des Services de Consultants. Cette disposition ne s’applique pas aux diverses entreprises (Consultants, entrepreneurs ou fournisseurs) qui, collectivement, s’acquittent des obligations de l’adjudicataire d’un marché clés en main ou d’un marché de conception – construction ;
  2. Aucune entreprise engagée par l’emprunteur pour fournir des Services de Consultants pour la préparation ou l’exécution d’un projet (ni aucune entreprise affiliée qui contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’elle contrôle elle-même ou qui est placée sous un contrôle commun) n’est admise ultérieurement à livrer des Fournitures réaliser des Travaux ou fournit des Services Autres que des Services de Consultants consécutifs ou directement liés audits Services de Consultants. Cette disposition ne s’applique pas aux diverses entreprises (consultant, entrepreneurs ou fournisseurs) qui, collectivement, s’acquittent des obligations de l’adjudicataire d’un marché clés en main ou d’un marché de conception construction ;
  3. Aucun Consultant (y compris le personnel et les sous-consultants à son service) ni aucun prestataire affilié (qui le contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’il contrôle lui-même ou qui est placé sous un contrôle commun) ne peut être engagé pour une mission qui par sa nature, crée un conflit d’intérêt avec une autre de ses missions ;
  4. Les Consultants (y compris les experts, le personnel et les sous-consultants à leur service) qui ont une relation professionnelle ou familiale étroite avec tout cadre de l’Emprunteur, de l’organisme d’exécution du projet, d’un bénéficiaire d’une fraction du financement de la ou de toute autre partie représentant l’Emprunteur ou agissant en son nom qui participe directement ou indirectement à tout segment :
  1. De la préparation des Termes de référence de la mission
  2. Du processus de sélection pour le contrat ; ou
  3. De la supervision du contrat, ne peuvent être attributaires d’un contrat, saut si le conflit résultant de ladite relation a été réglé d’une manière que la Banque juge satisfaisante tout au long du processus de sélection et de l’exécution du contrat.
  1. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d’un groupement ou d’un accord de sous-traitant. En cas de groupement, tous les membres de ce groupement restent conjointement et solidairement responsables de l’exécution de la mission au cas où le groupement sera sélectionné. 
  2. Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément aux dispositions décrites dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés, Edition Septembre 2025, notamment la méthode « Sélection Fondée sur les Qualifications du Consultant (QC) ».
  3. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires aux adresses ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes : Lundi au Vendredi de 08h30mn à 16h30mn (heure de Conakry/Guinée).

TÜRKYE

TÜRKYE EARTHQUAKE, FLOODS AND WILDFIRES EMERGENCY RECONSTRUCTION PROJECT (TEFWER)

Loan No.: P176608

Assignment Title: Technical Assistance for Strengthening Urban Resilience Investment Preparation and Financing Mechanisms for Municipalities in Türkiye

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TEFWER-TA-01

 

1. LBANK has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Türkiye Earthquake, Floods and Wildfires Emergency Reconstruction Project (TEFWER) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include “Technical Assistance for Strengthening Urban Resilience Investment Preparation and Financing Mechanisms for Municipalities in Türkiye.”

The estimated duration of the Services is 6 (six) months.

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the following website https://www.ilbank.gov.tr/ihaleler/uluslararasi-finansmanli-ihaleler/5

4. LBANK now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

5. A consulting firm is allowed to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if consultants themselves choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, then such associations may either be as a Joint Venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally responsible) and/or Sub-consultants (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant).  In case of an association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission (a) the rationale for forming the association and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture (JV) and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association. Failure to provide the above explanation in the EOI may risk the association not being selected for the assignment.  Please note that in the evaluation of EOIs of associations for selection purposes, only the qualifications of the JV members will be taken into account whereas the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered.

6. The selection criteria are as follows:

 

 I. General Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) in providing consulting services:

  • At least 10 (ten) years of experience of as core business in consulting services prior to the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest (EOIs),
  • Experience in the successful completion of projects financed by international financial institutions; preferably under World Bank financing, within the last 10 (ten) years prior to the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest (EOIs).

 

II. Specific Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) relevant to the assignment in providing similar services under contracts of comparable size:

  • Successfully completed similar assignments within the last ten (10) years in Türkiye and neighbouring countries in urban resilience advisory and/or investment planning and project preparation for central and local governments, covering sectors such as water/wastewater, transport and mobility, energy, infrastructure, housing, and urban regeneration,
  • Experience in conducting financial and technical capacity assessments for public institutions, preferably local governments (analyses of financial intermediary structures, preparation of feasibility studies, investment facilities, financing modalities, and/or project preparation facilities for municipal infrastructure investments,
  • Experience in international climate policy organizations (engagement with previous COP Presidencies and COP action agenda processes are preferable)/multi-stakeholder international climate finance initiatives.

 

7. To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above selection criteria, Consultants are requested to submit, at a minimum, the supporting documentation listed below.  A consulting firm shall use only its own qualifications and experience and shall not use those of its parent, sister, subsidiary, or affiliated companies, or its employees. 

i. The firm's incorporation/trade/registration documents issued by the concerned government authority of the country of the firm.

ii. The firm’s company brochures, including core areas of business; and

iii. Completed Form-1 (attached to this Request for Expression of Interest) to provide information of similar contracts. This should include the name and reference number of the contract, brief description of the scope of work, contract amount, period of the contract, name of the client and country of assignment, and role of the Consultant in the contract.  Copies of completion certificates/references of the Clients of completed contracts are not required to be submitted with the EoI. In the subsequent stage at the time of submission of proposals, the Client may request the selected consultants to submit such supporting completion certificates.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to (i) paragraphs 3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing (Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services) (4th edition, November 2020), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

9. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultants’ Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method as set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.

10. Further information may be obtained at the address below during office hours from 10:00 to 16:00 (Türkiye time).

Le Gouvernement de la République du Sénégal a reçu un financement d'un montant de cent (100) millions de dollars, de la Banque mondiale pour le coût du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM), commun aux deux départements ministériels en charge des secteurs des pêches et de l’environnement.

Le SENRM/METE a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant, dans le cadre du projet :

Sélection d'un cabinet pour la prospection et la caractérisation des sites ciblés pour la désignation d’AMP hauturières.

Le SENRM/METE invite les firmes de consultants admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus.

Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations (maximum 30 pages) démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services, les activités principales et le nombre d’années d’exercice, l’expérience spécifique pour la mission, la capacité technique et administrative du cabinet (références concernant l’exécution de contrats analogues, expériences dans des conditions similaires, brochures et fiches).

Le consultant qui présentera le meilleur niveau de qualification et d’expérience en rapport avec la mission, sera invité à soumettre ses propositions technique et financière, aux fins de négociations.

Il est porté à l’attention des consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.13 à 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) édité en septembre 2025, relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts et d’avantage compétitif inéquitable, sont applicables.

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives sous la forme d’un groupement. Tous les membres de ce groupement sont solidairement et conjointement responsables.

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires et/ou disposer des Termes de Référence, à l’adresse mail ci-dessous, les jours ouvrables de 9 heures à 17 heures TU : passationdemarches.senrmmeddte@gmail.com

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT, HIGHWAYS AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

(MONITORING AND EVALUATION SPECIALIST)

Project: Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive and Viable Economies (REVIVE)

Grant   No.: 7985-LK  

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant – Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist to Support Results-Based Monitoring, Evaluation, Project Coordination and Management Information System (MIS) for the REVIVE Project

Reference No.:  LK-UDA-PMU-555701-CS-INDV

The Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of preparing and implementing the REVIVE Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Project aims to improve access to enabling infrastructure and promote local jobs in selected areas of the Northern and Eastern Provinces through targeted infrastructure investments, regional economic planning, local economic development, institutional strengthening, value-chain development and project management support.

The objective of this assignment is to provide technical advisory, operational and coordination support to the Project Management Unit (PMU) in establishing and implementing a robust results-based monitoring, evaluation, reporting and learning system for REVIVE. The Consultant will support the maintenance of an integrated Management Information System (MIS), project activity tracking, data quality assurance, baseline and evaluation studies, progress reporting, World Bank mission support and coordination of monitoring information across Project Management Unit (PMU) and Project Implementation Units (PIUs).

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.transport.gov.lk/

The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the assignment. The shortlisting criteria are set out below.

Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist

Qualifications

  • A postgraduate degree from a recognized university in Monitoring and Evaluation, Economics, Statistics, Development Studies, Public Policy, Project Management, Social Sciences, Management, Data Science, Information Systems, or another relevant discipline.
  • Additional professional training or certification in results-based management, monitoring and evaluation, project management, survey methodology, data analytics, MIS/database management, or data visualization will be an added advantage.

Experience

  • Minimum of ten (10) years of relevant professional experience in monitoring and evaluation, results-based management, project coordination, development planning, project performance reporting, or related fields.
  • At least five (5) years of demonstrated experience in designing, establishing, implementing, or managing M&E systems for government or donor-funded development projects.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing and maintaining Results Frameworks, indicator tracking matrices, M&E plans, baselines, targets, data sources, verification methods, reporting schedules, and data quality assurance arrangements.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing, operationalizing, or managing integrated Management Information Systems (MIS), databases, dashboards, or digital project-monitoring platforms.
  • Experience in designing, coordinating, supervising, or reviewing baseline surveys, beneficiary surveys, mid-term evaluations, end-line surveys, independent verification exercises, or similar studies.
  • Experience in project performance reporting, including the consolidation of physical, financial, procurement, safeguards, risk, beneficiary, gender, and results information.
  • Experience in coordinating with PMUs, PIUs, government institutions, Provincial Councils, local authorities, consultants, contractors, and development partners.
  • Experience with World Bank, ADB, or other donor-funded development projects will be a strong advantage. Familiarity with World Bank Results Frameworks, implementation support missions, progress reporting, and action tracking will be particularly preferred.
  • Experience in infrastructure, regional or local economic development, tourism, fisheries, enterprise support, private-sector development, urban development, or provincial/local government programmes will be an added advantage.
  • Experience in communication and knowledge management, including preparation of management briefs, dashboards, presentations, results stories, and project information products, will be an advantage.

Key Competencies

  • Strong knowledge of results-based monitoring and evaluation, logical/results frameworks, indicator development, baseline and target setting, data quality assurance, and project performance reporting.
  • Demonstrated ability to design and manage integrated MIS platforms, project databases, dashboards, reporting systems, digital data-collection tools, and data-verification protocols.
  • Ability to integrate physical, financial, procurement, safeguards, beneficiary, gender, youth, and implementation-risk information into consolidated project reports and management dashboards.
  • Strong knowledge of quantitative and qualitative survey methods, sampling approaches, field-verification procedures, data validation, and statistical analysis.
  • Ability to analyse project data, identify implementation delays and risks, track corrective actions, and prepare concise management reports and decision briefs.
  • Strong coordination, facilitation, follow-up, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work across multiple PMU and PIU workstreams.
  • Practical experience in using digital tools for project monitoring, database management, dashboard preparation, electronic data collection, and statistical analysis. Familiarity with one or more relevant platforms, such as Power BI, Tableau, KoboToolbox, ODK, Survey Solutions, SurveyCTO, Stata, SPSS, R, or equivalent tools, will be an added advantage.
  • Strong report-writing, presentation, communication, and knowledge-management skills.
  • Ability and willingness to undertake regular field visits to project locations in the Northern and Eastern Provinces.
  • Fluency in English is required. Working knowledge of Sinhala and/or Tamil will be an added advantage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the above Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 1400 hours.

Expressions of Interest, together with a detailed curriculum vitae and copies of relevant educational and professional certificates, must be delivered by e-mail or hand to the address below on or before 11th August 2026.

The Federal Government of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP). The Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT) intends to apply part of the proceeds of these Grants to finance for the position of Cybersecurity Capacity Development Specialist in support of the implementation of the National Communications Authority (NCA) in the Federal Government of Somalia.

To support the National Communications Authority's (NCA) mandate to promote fair competition, consumer protection, investment, and sustainable growth in the telecommunications sector, the  NCA seeks to engage a qualified Cybersecurity Capacity Development Specialist to support the implementation of national cybersecurity initiatives, institutional capacity development, workforce enhancement, cybersecurity awareness programs, and cyber resilience initiatives in Somalia.

The Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP) addresses connectivity needs for countries in the Horn of Africa region. The program aims to advance the regional integration of digital markets in Eastern Africa through supporting cross-border connectivity, harmonization of data and e-commerce regulations and policies, and removal of trade barriers, with the vision of establishing a Single Digital Market (SDM). The EA-RDIP project has four components, as briefly described below:

Component 1. Connectivity Market Development and Integration.

Component 2. Data Market Development and Integration.

Component 3. Online Market Development and integration.

Component 4. Project Management and implementation.

 

Scope of Work:

The client, National Communications Authority (NCA) requires a dedicated Cybersecurity Capacity Development Specialist to support the implementation of national cybersecurity initiatives, institutional capacity development, workforce enhancement, cybersecurity awareness programs, and cyber resilience initiatives in Somalia. The Specialist will serve as the National Communications Authority’s focal point for engagement with global digital and social media platforms, supporting the establishment and maintenance of effective relationships with major online service providers operating in Somalia. For more details refer to the Terms and Reference (ToR).

Required Qualifications and Experiences:

The shortlisting criteria for the Cybersecurity Capacity Development Specialist for  position are as follows:

  • Postgraduate degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, Telecommunications, Digital Transformation, or related field.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in in cybersecurity capacity development, cybersecurity awareness, SOMCIRT/CERT operations, or ICT security leadership roles in either the public or private sectors.
  • Relevant experience in cybersecurity capacity-building initiatives, ICT development programs, digital transformation projects, telecommunications, regulatory institutions, academia, international organizations, or consultancy assignments.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing cybersecurity awareness campaigns, workforce development programs, institutional strengthening initiatives, and cybersecurity training activities.
  • Proven experience in organizing cybersecurity trainings, workshops, CyberDrills, conferences, stakeholder engagement programs, and cybersecurity awareness events.
  • Demonstrated capability to coordinate with government institutions, academia, development partners, regional organizations, private sector stakeholders, and international cybersecurity communities.
  • The Candidate should have work experience and in-depth knowledge of Somalia generally and a sensitivity to the underlying state of fragility and prevailing challenges in particular.
  • Proven experience in cybersecurity-related assignments at high-level Government institutions, NGOs, regulatory authorities, international organizations, and various other stakeholders.

Duration and Reporting of the Assignment: The Cybersecurity Capacity Development Specialist will be engaged for a period of one (1) year to renewal on an annual basis based on satisfactory performance certified by NCA and availability of funds. The consultant will report to the client, the National Communications Authority (NCA), through its Director General as a supervisor; the consultant should submit written monthly and quarterly progressive reports with the review and satisfactory approval of the client.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing these services. Interested Individual Consultants must submit their Curriculum Vitae (CV) and cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: https://nca.gov.so/jobs/ or it can be forwarded to the applicant upon written request to the project generic email address indicated below.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The selection will be conducted in accordance with the procedures for selection of Individual Consultants set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers dated September 2023 (Procurement Regulations).

Interested Consultant may obtain further information in a written communication to the below project generic email address during office hours from 9.00am to 4.00pm local time (Excluding public holidays).
