WEST AFRICAN POWER POOL

Project:  WAPP GHANA-CÔTE D’IVOIRE INTERCONNECTION REINFORCEMENT PROJECT

NOTICE OF INTERNATIONAL RECRUITMENT

Revised 23.8.2026

Consultant Services

Selection of individual consultant

Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

Financing: World Bank IDA

Don IDA No: E4040

Reference: BJ-WAPP-568960-CS-INDV

Open to: All eligible individuals

Duty Station: Abomey-Calavi, Benin

Application Deadline: 24 September 2024

 

  1. CONTEXT

The West African Power Pool (WAPP) was created by the highest decision-making authority of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) at the Conference of Heads of State and Government of the Member States held in Lomé, in December 1999. The Headquarters of the WAPP Secretariat is in Abomey-Calavi, Republic of Benin.

The ECOWAS strategic objective being implemented by the West African Power Pool (WAPP) is based on a dynamic vision of integrating national power grids into a unified regional electricity market, so that such a mechanism would, over the medium and long term, ensure to the ECOWAS citizens access to adequate power quality at an affordable price, and enhance the economic development of the Member States including industrialization growth, Health and Education improvement, Poverty Reduction, various Employment Opportunities Creation, etc…

To achieve its vision of operationalizing a unified ECOWAS regional electricity market, the WAPP Information and Coordination Centre (WAPP ICC), a Department within the WAPP Secretariat has been designated to perform the functions of a System Market Operator (SMO) responsible for coordinating the reliability of the WAPP Interconnected Transmission System (WAPPITS) made up of the power systems of fourteen (14) ECOWAS Member Countries and administration of the regional electricity market.

To this end, the WAPP Secretariat with the support of the World Bank within the Project “WAPP Côte d’Ivoire Interconnection and operationalization of the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market” intends to reinforce staffing of the ICC Department by filling a key vacant position, that of a Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

The Engineer will be selected competitively, and the successful candidates will be joining the current team in the Information and Coordination Centre (ICC) as it prepares to operationalize the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market.

2. ROLE OVERVIEW

Under the supervision of the Head of the System Operations Coordination Division, the Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer is responsible for the management of the ICC's Power System Database. He/She extracts data from various sources (APIs, HIVE tables, and other structured and unstructured data sources) to process and store large volumes of data, ensuring their accuracy, consistency and security. He/She develops reporting dashboards and analytical tools to support the analysis of power system operations, and supports the design, testing and implementation of models and databases for all systems requiring the WAPP Network Model.

The detailed Job description for the assignment may be consulted and/or downloaded from the WAPP website at: www.ecowapp.org/en/tenders

The WAPP General Secretariat invites eligible Individual Consultants to express their interest in providing the required Services described in the Job decription. Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services by submitting: (a) a cover letter/motivation letter, and (b) an up-to-date detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV).

WAPP is an equal opportunity employer that offers equal chances to men and women. Qualified women are strongly encouraged to apply.  

3. LANGUAGE

Good oral and written communication skills in English and French  

4. DURATION OF MISSION

The successful candidate shall be offered an initial Consultancy Contract of approximatively 17 months from the beginning of the assignment ( i.e.until April 30, 2028). Upon completion of the World Bank funding, the position shall be absorbed by WAPP.

The beginning of the assignment is planned for November 2026

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the method of "Selection of Individual Consultants" described in the World Bank "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (edition September 2025).  

6. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Applications must be submitted exclusively by email and should bear the subject line: “Application for ICC Engineer- Reference: BJ-WAPP-568960-CS-INDV”.

Paper applications will not be accepted.

Applications may be submitted in either French or English and should be sent to: procurement@ecowapp.org

 Particular emphasis should be placed on references for relevant similar assignments previously carried out, which should be clearly highlighted and described.

Deadline for submission of applications:  September 24, 2026, at noon, 12:00 pm, Benin local time (GMT+1).

Further information may be obtained by sending an email to:

spos@ecowapp.org

With copies to:

cpm@ecowapp.org

 hdhra@ecowapp.org

Only shortlisted candidates shall be contacted for the next stage of the recruitment process.

The Government of Grenada has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean Project (UBEC) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the consulting services for the Support with development of legislation for expansion of fixed Fisheries Aggregating Devices (FADs).

 

The Fisheries Division of Grenada is seeking the services of a qualified consulting firm with demonstrated experience in fisheries management and governance to develop a national FAD Policy, FAD Management Plan, and associated Regulatory Instruments. The firm shall assign a team of key personnel to this engagement. The firm shall work in close collaboration with the Grenada Fisheries Division, the Grenada UBEC Project Team, the OECS Programme Management Unit (PMU), and fisheries counterparts in St. Lucia and St. Vincent and the Grenadines.

 

You can find the detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment at the following websites: www.procurement.gd or https://in-tendhost.co.uk/GND/aspx/Home. Alternatively, you can email beverley.jeremiah@procurement.gov.gd  for assistance with the TOR or help with registering on In-tend.

 

The Ministry of Mobilisation, Implementation, and Transformation hereby invites eligible consultants to express their interest in providing the required services. Interested consultants are requested to submit information that demonstrates their qualifications and relevant experience to effectively carry out the services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers September 2023, revised November 2020, August 2018 and November 2017(“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The best-qualified consultant to carry out the services will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Regulations and based on the following criteria:

The Consultant must have the following qualifications and experience:

  • Demonstrated institutional experience delivering fisheries management or marine governance assignments in the Caribbean region or comparable SIDS context. Minimum three completed assignments of comparable scope in the last ten years.

 

  • In-house capacity in: fisheries policy development; legislative gap analyses; FAD management; stakeholder engagement; and communications. Evidence of in-house capacity must be demonstrated through CVs of proposed key personnel.

 

  • Prior experience delivering assignments financed by the World Bank, IDB, CDB, GEF, or comparable multilateral institutions. Familiarity with World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (ESS) and procurement procedures.

 

  • Demonstrated track record of delivering structured on-the-job mentoring and capacity building programmes as an integrated component of technical assistance engagements in SIDS or developing country contexts.

 

Further information can be obtained by requesting clarification via Intend https://in-tendhost.co.uk/GND/aspx/Home .

Expressions of interest must be submitted electronically through the procurement system at https://in-tendhost.co.uk/GND/aspx/Home . Candidates must register on this portal and submit all interest and queries through this medium. Upon submission of documents, you will receive a confirmation email acknowledging receipt.

Deadline date of submission: September 18th, 2026, at 3:00 P.M.

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

 

Recrutement d’une ONG nationale pour l’accompagnement social des investissements et le renforcement des capacités communautaires dans la zone Est du projet RESITCHAD.

 

No de DON : IDA N° E207

 

N° de référence : TD-CHAD-RFSP-541713-CS-QCBS

 

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a reçu un financement sous forme de don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour la mise en œuvre du Projet de Développement Territorial et de Résilience au Tchad (RESITCHAD), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Recrutement d’une ONG nationale pour l’accompagnement social des investissements et le renforcement des capacités communautaires dans la zone Est du projet RESITCHAD ».

 

Le consultant assurera notamment les prestations suivantes :

  • Accompagner socialement les bénéficiaires pour garantir l'appropriation des investissements,
  • Renforcer les capacités techniques et organisationnelles des acteurs communautaires et locaux,
  • Structurer et formaliser les mécanismes de gestion pour assurer la pérennisation des acquis,
  • Mettre en place un système de monitoring pour garantir la durabilité des impacts.

 

La durée de la mission sera de vingt-quatre (24) mois.

 

La Coordination du Projet RESITCHAD, invite les ONG nationales (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont (i) l’existence légale et expérience générale du Consultant (ii) l’expérience spécifique en mobilisation communautaire et développement local (iii) l’expérience dans les projets financés par les partenaires techniques et financiers (iv) la présence opérationnelle dans la zone d'intervention ou capacité démontrée à intervenir (v) l’expertise en genre, inclusion sociale, gestion des conflits et renforcement de capacités.

 

Pour être valables, les renseignements à fournir sur les références doivent être accompagnés de pièces justificatives des missions similaires exécutées par le candidat (copies des contrats (comprenant la page de garde et la page de signature), attestation de bonne fin d’exécution y relatif…).  La recevabilité des missions en cours est conditionnée à un taux d'exécution minimum de 80 % avec attestation.

 

Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.14 ; 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant de la Banque Mondiale le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (Le Règlement) – 7é édition de Septembre 2025 », relatives aux règles de la Banque Mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts, sont applicables.

 

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d’un groupement solidaire ou d’un accord de sous-traitant.

Traitement des groupements et de la sous-traitance :

  •  Ancienneté du cabinet : il sera retenu l'ancienneté du mandataire (chef de file) du groupement.
  • Références similaires : recevables au titre du mandataire ou des cotraitants, à condition que la part du membre concerné dans le marché de référence atteigne un seuil minimum de 30% du volume, et avec mention explicite du rôle exercé (chef de file ou cotraitant). Les références des sous-traitants ne sont pas recevables.
  • Couverture multisectorielle : les secteurs couverts par chaque membre du groupement sont cumulables ;
  • Capacité organisationnelle : La capacité organisationnelle est appréciée au titre du seul mandataire. 

 

Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC), telle que décrite dans le Règlement.

 

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires ou les termes de référence de la mission à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes : du Lundi au Jeudi de 07 heures à 15 heures 30 minutes et le Vendredi de 07 heures à 12 heures (heure locale).

 

Votre manifestation d’intérêt écrite doit être déposée à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier, par facsimilé ou par courrier électronique au plus tard le xxxxxxxxxx à xxxxxxxx.

Título da Contratação: Contratação de serviços técnicos especializados de consultoria em engenharia para atuação como Engenheiro, conforme condições de contrato do Livro Amarelo (Yellow Book) da Federação Internacional de Engenheiros de Consultoria – FIDIC, Segunda Edição, 2017, e atuação como Gerente de Projeto conforme condições de contrato de Projeto e Obras Menores de 2025 do Banco Mundial do Programa Centro+4D

Método de Seleção: Seleção Baseada na Qualidade e Custo (SBQC)

Número de Referência: BR-SMPAE-PMPA-507893-CS-QCBS

 

A Prefeitura Municipal de Porto Alegre, por meio da SECRETARIA MUNICIPAL DE PLANEJAMENTO E GESTÃO (SMPG), recebeu um confinanciamento do Banco Mundial e da Agência Francesa de Desenvolvimento para a execução do Programa de Revitalização da Área Central de Porto Alegre – CENTRO+4D. Parte desses recursos será destinada à contratação de serviços de consultoria técnica especializada (serviços de engenharia) para atuação como o Engenheiro, conforme condições de contrato do Livro Amarelo (Yellow Book) da FIDIC, e atuação como Gerente de Projeto, conforme condições de contrato padrão de Projeto e Obras Menores do Banco Mundial de 2025, para os serviços e obras do Programa Centro+4D.

Os serviços de consultoria (“Os Serviços”) incluem o apoio à Prefeitura Municipal de Porto Alegre na gestão de todos os contratos de serviços e obras de engenharia do Programa Centro+4D, envolvendo: (i) analisar projetos; (ii) acompanhar e supervisionar, de forma presencial, os serviços realizados pelos Contratados, verificando sua conformidade aos projetos; (iii) auxiliar no controle tecnológico; (iv) assessorar o cumprimento dos aspectos técnicos e socioambientais exigidos pelos Bancos Financiadores; (v) dar instruções; (vi) fazer determinações e emitir ordens de variação vinculantes às partes. O Termo de Referência (TdR) detalhado e demais informações estão disponíveis no site da Diretoria de Licitações e Contratos da Prefeitura de Porto Alegre: <https://prefeitura.poa.br/smpg/diretoria-de-licitacoes-e-contratos/selecao-baseada-na-qualidade-e-custo-sbqc>.

A duração estimada desta consultoria estará vinculada ao prazo de execução de obras do Programa Centro+4D mais o Período para Notificação de Defeitos (PND) e o prazo para emissão do Certificado de Execução das obras, estimado em um total de 1671 (um mil, seiscentos e setenta e um) dias, equivalendo a aproximadamente 55 (cinquenta e cinco) meses. 

A SMPG convida empresas de consultoria elegíveis (“Consultores”) a manifestarem seu interesse em fornecer os serviços acima. As empresas de consultoria interessadas deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e a experiência relevante para executar Os Serviços. Os critérios de seleção são: experiência comprovada na gestão de contratos de serviços e obras de engenharia na modalidade do Livro Amarelo (Yellow Book) da FIDIC; estrutura gerencial compatível com a execução dos Serviços; tempo mínimo de atuação no mercado de 7 (sete) anos; portfólio técnico compatível com a natureza dos serviços.

Para Formação da Lista Curta serão avaliados os seguintes aspectos quanto à experiência da Proponente:

  1. Principal área de atuação, tempo de atividade nessa área, experiência relevante, capacidade técnica e estrutura gerencial da empresa;
  2. Contratos e clientes anteriores, informando detalhes de escopo, valor, duração, função no contrato, contato do gestor técnico de cada contrato pelo lado do contratante (nome, função, e-mail e telefone);
  3. Portfólio da empresa com destaque para a experiência em contratos de natureza e complexidade semelhantes.

Os Consultores serão selecionados de acordo com o método de Seleção Baseada na Qualidade e Custo (SBQC), estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento do Banco Mundial de fevereiro de 2025.

Os Consultores poderão associar-se a outras empresas para melhorar as suas qualificações, mas devem indicar claramente se a associação assume a forma de uma joint venture e/ou de uma subconsultoria. No caso de uma joint venture, todos os parceiros serão solidariamente responsáveis pela totalidade do contrato, se selecionados.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores para a Seção III, parágrafos 3.13, 3.15 e 3.16 do “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento” (Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers) do Banco Mundial de fevereiro de 2025, estabelecendo a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.

As Manifestações de Interesse, currículos e portfólios deverão ser entregues até as 10 horas do dia 31 de agosto de 2026, na sede da Diretoria de Licitações e Contratos da Secretaria Municipal de Planejamento e Gestão, aos cuidados da Comissão Especial de Licitações, no Edifício Montaury, 5º Andar, situado à Rua Siqueira Campos, nº 1300, Centro Histórico, Porto Alegre/RS, CEP 90010-001, ou enviada por correio eletrônico ao endereço de e-mail celfin@portoalegre.rs.gov.br, especificando no campo assunto: 507893-CS-QCBS_Nome da Empresa.

Na hipótese de não haver confirmação de recebimento dos correios eletrônicos pela Comissão Especial de Licitações no prazo de 48 (quarenta e oito) horas, os documentos deverão ser reenviados, mantendo-se no histórico da mensagem o e-mail originalmente encaminhado.

MINISTRY OF PLANNING

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Assignment Title: CONSULTING SERVICES FOR TRAINING AND CERTIFICATION FOR INSOLVENCY JUDGES AND ADMINISTRATORS  

Reference No. 82CS1/MINPLAN/26

The Government of Angola has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for training and certification for insolvency judges and administrators.

The consulting services (“the Services”) consist of:

  1. Design, development and delivery of specialized training programs for judges and insolvency administrators on business recovery and insolvency, in accordance with the Angolan legal framework;
  2. Organization and certification of training courses for judicial and related professionals involved in corporate recovery and insolvency proceedings;
  3. Preparation of training content and materials, covering, among others, the following areas: (i) Legal framework for business recovery and insolvency; (ii) Commercial law; (iii) Labour law; (iv) Civil procedure law; (v) Accounting and taxation; (vi) Economics and business management; (vii) Insolvency, economic development and the business environment;
  4. Implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the training activities, including assessment of participants and issuance of certificates upon successful completion;
  5. Preparation and submission of the required deliverables, including the training plan, teaching materials, training reports and certification documentation.

The assignment includes legal, institutional, procedural, accounting, tax, economic, business management and capacity-building work, structured around the preparation, implementation, evaluation and certification of training activities for judges and insolvency administrators.

The expected duration of the services cannot exceed 12 months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. To be legally constituted and authorized to operate in the areas of consulting, training, capacity building or professional certification.
  2. Demonstrate at least 5 years of consolidated experience in providing consulting services, curriculum design, and implementation of training programs.
  3. To have successfully completed at least 3 similar projects in the last 5 years, preferably focused on the justice sector, insolvency, business recovery, judicial administration or economic governance.
  4. To be legally authorized to validate and issue qualification/attendance certificates to trainees.
  5. Demonstrate practical experience in engaging with and listening to stakeholders (e.g., courts, judges, government entities, professional associations).

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” revised in September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

O Estado de Alagoas recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para custear parcialmente o Programa Progestão Alagoas, e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos para serviços de consultoria.

Os serviços de consultoria (“Serviços”) referem-se à contratação de empresa de consultoria especializada para a realização de diagnóstico arquivístico, dimensionamento da massa documental, elaboração de estratégia tecnológica e apoio técnico à futura contratação dos serviços de digitalização dos registros funcionais dos servidores e ex-servidores do Poder Executivo do Estado de Alagoas.

É parte integrante desta Manifestação de Interesse o e Termo de Referência (TdR) no qual consta a descrição detalhada das atividades a serem desempenhadas e dos produtos a serem elaborados, e que está disponível no website: www.sefaz.al.gov.br/licitacao

O Estado de Alagoas convida empresas de consultoria elegíveis a manifestarem seu interesse na prestação dos Serviços. Empresas interessadas devem fornecer informações que comprovem possuir as qualificações e experiência necessárias para executar os Serviços. Os critérios de pré-seleção são:

  • Possuir experiência na área de gestão documental, considerando aspectos inerentemente arquivísticos, documentais, operacionais, tecnoloógicos, institucionais e normativos;

  • Possuir experiência na definição de critérios técnicos de priorização para futura digitalização/virtualização da massa documental;

  • Possuir experiência no apoio técnico para estruturação de ação para futura digitalização/virtualização dos registros funcionais;

  • Possuir experiência na capacitação de equipes técnicas para acompanhar futura contratação de serviço de digitalização/virtualização dos registros.

 

Por fim, é necessário que possua capacidade gerencial compatível com projetos de alta complexidade, com múltiplas frentes de trabalho simultâneas, assegurando a entrega de todos os produtos dentro dos prazos estabelecidos e com o padrão de qualidade exigido pela Administração Pública. Os especialistas-chave não serão avaliados na etapa de pré-seleção.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para a Seção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 das “Normas de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (IPF)” do Banco Mundial, de novembro de 2020 (“Normas de Aquisições”), que tratam da política sobre conflito de interesses.

As empresas podem se associar para reforçar suas qualificações, devendo indicar claramente se a associação ocorre na forma de consórcio ou subcontratação. No caso de consórcio, todos os parceiros devem ser solidariamente responsáveis por todo o contrato, se selecionados.

A Consultoria será selecionada de acordo com o método Seleção Baseada em Qualidade e Custo – SBQC estabelecido pelo Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial, 4ª edição de novembro de 2020.

Government of Nepal

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) –

Sisneri Water Supply Project

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL)

First Date of Publication: 27th August 2026

Senior Hydrologist - Ref No. KVWaSIP-IC-02-083/84

1.0 Background

The Government of Nepal (GoN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services include providing technical, procurement, financial management, environmental and social, contract management, and other professional support required for effective implementation of the Project through the Project Management Unit (PMU)

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide a detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating that they possess the required educational qualifications, professional experience, and technical competence to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria for each assignment are specified in the respective Terms of Reference (TOR), which may be obtained from the address or website indicated below

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Senior Hydrologist and requests applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position.

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

As a team member of the Project Management Unit (PMU), the overall objective of the assignment is to provide specialist hydrological, hydraulic, sedimentation, and climate resilience support to the PMU for the feasibility confirmation, detailed design, and implementation readiness of the Sisneri Dam and associated bulk water supply system. The Senior Hydrologist will help ensure that the Project’s hydrological basis, reservoir yield assumptions, flood safety provisions, sediment management approach, and climate risk considerations are technically sound, robust, and consistent with international good industry practice and applicable World Bank requirements.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

The duties of the Specialist is mentioned in the Terms of Reference in detail.

4. Qualifications and Experience

All applications will be evaluated against the assignment’s required qualifications below.  

Candidates who comply with the qualifications will be scored according to predefined criteria. A minimum of three candidates will be shortlisted and interviewed. The candidate with the highest score will be invited to negotiate a contract. Referees of the selected candidate may be contacted to verify prior experience, performance, and interpersonal skills. 

 The Senior Hydrologist shall possess strong academic qualifications and demonstrated professional experience relevant to dam hydrology, sediment management, hydraulic analysis, and reservoir operations for large water infrastructure projects. The expert should have proven capability to review and guide hydrological investigations, assess design assumptions and modelling outputs, and provide technical advice on dam safety, flood management, sedimentation, and climate-related risks in the context of feasibility updating and detailed engineering design

Qualifications and Relevant Experience

  • Education:
    • The expert shall hold at least a bachelor’s degree in water resources engineering, hydrology, civil engineering, or a related discipline.
    • A master’s degree in hydrology, water resources, hydraulic engineering, or a closely related field is required, and a PhD will be considered an added advantage.
  • Work Experience:
  • At least 15 years of relevant professional experience in hydrological assessment, hydrological modelling, flood estimation, sediment studies, reservoir operation analysis, and review or design support for dam or major water resources infrastructure projects.
  • The expert shall demonstrate strong experience in hydrological data collection, interpretation, and modelling, including rainfall and streamflow analysis, rating curves, long-term flow generation, design flood estimation, probable maximum flood assessment, and flood routing for dams and associated hydraulic structures.
  • The expert shall have proven expertise in sediment assessment, reservoir sedimentation and management, reservoir operation studies, water availability and dry-season yield analysis, minimum release requirements, and evaluation of climate variability and climate change impacts on hydrological performance.
  • The expert shall have sound knowledge of hydrology-related dam safety, including dam-break analysis, emergency preparedness planning, downstream flood routing, inundation mapping, and risk mitigation, and experience coordinating with multidisciplinary dam or water supply teams; prior review, advisory, quality assurance, or panel-type roles will be an advantage.
  • Interpersonal Skills
    • The expert shall have strong analytical, report writing, and communication skills, and shall be able to communicate clearly and effectively in spoken and written English.

5. Evaluation and Selection Method

The Senior Dam Specialist will be hired by the PMU using the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method following “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) Seventh Edition 2025. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations”.

6. Duration of the Assignment

The Senior Hydrologist will perform the scope of these TORs for a duration of 15 months from contract signature on a full-time basis.

7. Remuneration

A market-based salary package commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications will be offered.

8. Reporting

The Senior Hydrologist will report directly to the Project Director, PMU

9. Location

  • The consultant will be based at the PMU office and may be required to travel outside the valley as needed for project-related procurement activities.
  • The Project shall provide following facilities to consultant during his tenure of service:
  • Office space
  • Email and internet access
  • Required office stationery and other materials
  • Photocopying/printing facilities

10. Application Process

Interested candidates shall submit a complete application package comprising:

  1. Up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV).
  2. Copies of academic and professional certificates.
  3. Contact details for at least three (03) professional references familiar with the candidate’s relevant work.

Applications shall be submitted electronically no later than 17.00 PM on 11th September 2026 to the following e-mail address: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com. Only complete applications received by the deadline will be considered.

The Ministry of Finance and Treasury of Bosnia and Herzegovina (the “Borrower”) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Sustainable, Integrated and Safe Road Infrastructure Project (SISRI) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise construction supervision, project management and contract administration for the rehabilitation of the main road MI-108 (M-4), Rebrovac - Kotor Varoš (Works RFB No. BA-RS-SISRI-W-RFB-26-1.2.2), covering approximately 30.9 km. The Works include rehabilitation and reconstruction of pavement layers; earthworks; draninage and culverts; curbs and roadside works; traffic signage and road markings; road safety equipment; repair and rehabilitation of related structures and ancillary works; temporary traffic management; and environmental, social, occupational health and safety measures.

The Intended Completion Date for the Works is 540 days after the Commencement Date. The Services are expected to commence in coordination with the commencement of the Works and to cover the construction period and the related completion, close-out and Defects Liability Period services as specified in the Terms of Reference. The Defects Liability Period under the Works contract is 730 calendar days. The detailed scope, deliverables, level of effort and implementation arrangements are set out in the Terms of Reference.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Public Company “Republic of Srpska Roads” Ltd. now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: “Procurement Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting, and Consulting Services, Seventh edition, September 2025” (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The best qualified firm to carry out the Services will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Regulations and based on the following criteria:

 Qualification requirements to be met by the Consultant:

1. Core business and general experience: at least seven (5) years of demonstrated experience in construction supervision, project management and/or contract administration of road or transport infrastructure works.

2. Relevant specific experience: successful completion, within the last ten (10) years, of at least two (2) assignments for supervision and contract administration of construction, reconstruction or rehabilitation of paved public roads of similar nature and complexity; at least one such assignment should have involved a road section or combined road sections of not less than approximately 20 km.

3. Similar technical scope: demonstrated firm-level experience supervising asphalt pavement rehabilitation/reconstruction, earthworks, drainage and culverts, curbs and roadside works, traffic signage and road markings, road safety equipment, related structures, temporary traffic management under live traffic conditions, and environmental and social requirements.

4. Technical and managerial capability: demonstrated organizational and management capacity for quality assurance/quality control, supervision of materials testing, measurement and certification of works, progress and cost control, contract administration, environmental and social compliance, occupational health and safety monitoring, and regular reporting.

5. Previous experience with World Bank or other international financial institution (IFI/MDB)-financed road infrastructure projects and related contract administration procedures will be considered an asset.

6. Experience in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Western Balkans or comparable legal, climatic and operating environments will be considered and asset.

Interested Consultants should submit a concise company profile and evidence of relevant assignments, including the client, country, scope, duration, implementation period, value of the supervised works where available, the Consultant’s role, and client contact details for verification. In the case of an association, the Expression of Interest should clearly state the form and proposed role of each member/partner.

The qualifications and experience of individual Key Experts shall not be evaluated at the REOI stage and CVs of Key Experts are not required with the Expression of Interest.

Evaluation criteria

Consultants meeting the minimum qualification requirements set out above will be evaluated and ranked on the basis of their demonstrated qualifications and relevant experience related to the assignment. The evaluation will be based on the information submitted in the Expressions of Interest and in accordance with the following criteria:

  1. Core business, general experience and organizational capacity of the firm (20%)
  2. Relevant experience in supervision and contract administration of road projects of similar nature, scope and complexity (60%)
  3. Technical and managerial capability demonstrated through previous assignments (20%)

1. Contexte

Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi, ayant obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour la mise en œuvre du Projet de Développement du Capital Humain (PDCH), entend en affecter une partie au marché référencé, dans le cadre de sa stratégie visant à investir dans le capital humain et à renforcer les secteurs prioritaires de l’Éducation et de la Santé pour assurer la stabilité nationale et soutenir un développement durable.

À travers le Plan National de Développement 20182027 et la Vision 20402060, le pays s’engage à :

  • Assurer l’accès universel aux services de santé.
  • Garantir une éducation inclusive et de qualité.
  • Développer les compétences pour diversifier les emplois formels et promouvoir l’entrepreneuriat.

Avec 41,5 % de la population âgée de 0 à 15 ans en 2022, la jeunesse constitue la principale richesse nationale et la clé de la stabilité à long terme.

Le Burundi accueille également une importante population de réfugiés (86 300 en mars 2024, dont 39 % âgés de 5 à 17 ans). Une stratégie actualisée en 2023 prévoit :

  • Intégration des réfugiés et rapatriés dans les systèmes nationaux.
  • Harmonisation des systèmes d’éducation et de santé dans les zones de développement intégré.
  • Élaboration d’une stratégie éducative spécifique pour l’inclusion des réfugiés et l’accès des rapatriés au système scolaire burundais.

Deux projets éducatifs sont actuellement en cours d’exécution, sous la tutelle du MENRS et gérés par une UGP unique :

  • PACEJ : Projet d’Appui à l’Amélioration des Compétences pour l’Employabilité des Femmes et des Jeunes.
  • PDCH : Projet de Développement du Capital Humain

2. Description du marché

Le marché est structuré en deux (02) lots :

  • Lot 1 : Kits scolaires pour les enfants vulnérables du préscolaire.
  • Lot 2 : Kits scolaires pour les enfants vulnérables du fondamental et du post-fondamental.

Les soumissionnaires peuvent participer à un ou deux lots et se voir attribuer les deux s’ils remplissent les conditions cumulatives. Chaque offre doit couvrir l’ensemble des articles requis pour le lot concerné. Aucune variante n’est acceptée.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

GEORGIA

Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land Project (GRAIL) – P175629

Loan No. 9504-GE

Assignment Title: Capacity Building Service Provider (CBSP) to Deliver Training and Demonstration Activities on Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA), Water-Efficient Irrigation, Climate Resilience, and Sustainable Agricultural Technologies for Farmers under the Tashiskari, Narekvavi, Shavghele Masif and Zeda Arkhi Irrigation Schemes in Kareli, Khashuri, Borjomi, Dusheti, Khobi and Bolnisi Municipalities’ Villages

Reference No: GR/CS/QCBS/05

Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land (GRAIL) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The project cost is 138.6 million EURO comprising of an equal share (50/50) by each co-financer.

The project development objectives are to: (a) improve irrigation, and drainage services, and agricultural production in project areas; and (b) strengthen national irrigation and land management institutional capacity for climate resilient planning.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Capacity Building Service Provider (CBSP) to Deliver Training and Demonstration Activities on Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA), Water-Efficient Irrigation, Climate Resilience, and Sustainable Agricultural Technologies for Farmers under the Tashiskari, Narekvavi, Shavghele Masif and Zeda Arkhi Irrigation Schemes in Kareli, Khashuri, Borjomi, Dusheti, Khobi and Bolnisi Municipalities’ Villages The main objective of this assignment is to:

The consulting services ("the Services") include the engagement of a Capacity Building Service Provider (CBSP) to design and implement an integrated farmer capacity building and technical advisory program promoting Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA), water-efficient irrigation, climate resilience, and sustainable agricultural practices within the command areas of the Tashiskari, Narekvavi, Shavghele Masif, and Zeda Arkhi Irrigation Schemes villages.

The assignment will cover 55 villages across six municipalities and support approximately 2,920 farmers through integrated capacity building, field demonstrations, technical advisory services, and dissemination of Climate-Smart Agriculture technologies and good agricultural practices. The Consultant will establish and manage approximately 55–65 demonstration plots serving as practical learning sites for technology demonstration and farmer-to-farmer knowledge exchange.

The overall objective of the assignment is to strengthen farmers' technical knowledge, practical skills, and investment readiness to improve agricultural productivity, enhance climate resilience, promote efficient water use, and accelerate the adoption of sustainable agricultural technologies and good agricultural practices in line with the objectives of the GRAIL Project.

The selected Consultant shall develop and deliver comprehensive theoretical and practical training programs, establish and manage or select relevant demonstration plots, provide field-based technical advisory services throughout the production cycle, prepare practical extension and knowledge materials, facilitate farmer-to-farmer learning and technology dissemination, support monitoring and evaluation of capacity building activities, and document lessons learned and good practices in the command target areas.

The assignment covers, among others, development of crop-specific training curricula, implementation of integrated theoretical and field-based training sessions, establishment and management of demonstration plots, farmer coaching and technical advisory services, grant application support, dissemination of knowledge products, monitoring and reporting of project activities, and strengthening the capacity of local extension services.

The Consultant shall provide also targeted capacity building and hands-on support to eligible farmers in preparing and submitting applications under the GRAIL Matching Grant Program. The Consultant shall assist farmers in understanding eligibility requirements, preparing and collecting necessary documents for the grant application, filling application forms, and complying with the requirements established by the Rural Development Agency (RDA), thereby improving the quality of applications and increasing farmers' access to investment financing.

The detailed scope of services, implementation requirements, deliverables, and reporting obligations are provided in the Terms of Reference (TOR) which can be found on the link below:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ncNpf9z7gFT4c2ntNTtQfiHuUZufBenS/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=111094613369888933218&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expression of interest should cover, but not limited to: corporate profile, years in business, experience relevant to the project activities, overall key staff resources, and core business. Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • At least ten (10) years of demonstrated experience in designing and implementing agricultural development, climate-smart agriculture, irrigation, agricultural extension, farmer advisory, or rural development programs.
  • During the last eight (8) years, the Consultant shall have successfully completed at least 2 assignments of similar scope, nature, and complexity involving the design and implementation of integrated agricultural capacity building programs, including practical field demonstrations, technical advisory services, and farmer training.

Note: the MEPA reserves it’s right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The experience of sub-consultants will not be taken into account while evaluating the corporate experience of the consultant.

To facilitate the development of EOI and further assessment, the interested consultants are provided with a Form for References for experience in the projects relevant to the assignment. The Form for References can be found on the link below:  https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hDeNiygk0vcp3qx-8uwz05_ZYcmAsjPQ/view?usp=sharing   

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection Method (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations:  Approved Selection Methods: Consulting Services under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers - July 2016, revised September 2025.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 10:00 a.m. to 17:00 p.m. at MEPA, Mr. Ioseb Tchonkadze, Procurement Consultant.

The hard copy of the Expression of Interest (accompanied by the electronic version of EOI) must be delivered in English in a written form to the address below (in person or by mail) by September 6, 2026, at 17:00 hrs. local time.

Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA)

Attn: Mr. Ioseb Tchonkadze, Procurement Consultant

32g, Marshal Gelovani Ave, 0159 Tbilisi, Georgia

 

E-mail To: iosebtchonkadze@gmail.com; Mariam.bakhtadze@mepa.gov.ge; Rusudan,manjgaladze@mepa.gov.ge.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Consulting Services: Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS)

SUPERVISION OF THE CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSEHOLD TOILETS

IN QUELIMANE

 

IDA No: IDA-E4730

Reference No: MOZ-DNAAS-UWSP/CS/28

 

1. The Government of Mozambique has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Urban Water Security Project (UWSP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the Supervision of the Construction of Household Toilets in Quelimane.

2. The consulting services ("the Services") include the supervision of the construction and rehabilitation of approximately 489 household sanitation facilities in the Mapiazua neighbourhood of Quelimane Municipality, including 387 new household toilets and the rehabilitation of 102 existing facilities.

3. The assignment includes:

  • Beneficiary validation;
  • Construction supervision;
  • Contract administration, quality assurance, schedule and cost management;
  • Preparation of as-built documentation and GIS database updates;
  • Environmental and social monitoring, and;
  • Reporting during the construction period and the Defects Liability Period.

4. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment may be obtained at the address given below during normal working hours or upon written request by email.

5. The National Directorate of Water Supply and Sanitation (DNAAS) as the implementing agency of the Government of Mozambique, now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

6. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Be a reputable Civil Engineering Consulting firm with at least 10 years of experience in supervision and contract administration services for projects of a similar nature and complexity.
  • Specific experience of at least 5 years in the supervision of construction and rehabilitation works related to household sanitation facilities and public sanitation facilities in Mozambique.
  • Demonstrated experience in the implementation and supervision of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including Environmental and Social Standards (ESS), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), Labour Management Procedures (LMP), Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEP), Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRM), and SEA/SH risk management.

 

          Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

7. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.

8. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, , but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy.

9. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality-and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

10. Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours, from 8:30 to 14:30 hours (Mozambique time), Monday to Friday.

11. Expressions of Interest must be submitted in English no later than 14:30 hours (Mozambique time) on 26 August 2026.

This REOI is for the above-mentioned Cluster 1A.

 

The primary objective of this assignment is to ensure that all civil works and maintenance services are executed in full compliance with approved designs, technical specifications, contract conditions, environmental and social safeguards, World Bank Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines and all other applicable World Bank requirements.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the following among others:

i. Review of detailed designs and related documents for the various lots in cluster 1A.

ii. Supervision of the various groups of road lots in cluster 1A

iii. Monitoring during the defect liability period of the constructed roads.

3. Eligibility Requirement for the Assignment

The Ministry of Roads and Highways (MRH), acting through the Department of Feeder Roads, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

(a) Minimum Mandatory Requirements (pass/fail):

  1. Core business in providing consulting services for road infrastructure projects, including design, supervision, and performance-based maintenance management.
  2. Minimum of ten (10) years of continuous business in providing consulting services for road infrastructure projects, including design, supervision, and maintenance management.
  3. Evidence of experience in at least three (3) road infrastructure consulting assignments of similar scope and complexity (design/design review and construction supervision) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  4. Evidence of experience in at least one (1) road infrastructure consulting assignment of similar scope and complexity (performance-based maintenance management) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  5. Demonstrate prior experience and knowledge in applying FIDIC Conditions of Contract.
  6. Experience in applying good Environmental and Social standards and practices to project management and supervision. Experience and knowledge of the Multilateral Development Banks’ Environmental and Social Framework(s) (ESF), including Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention and response requirements.

(b) Desirable qualifications and experience (added advantages):

- Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa, given the specific geographical, climatic, and social contexts.

- Experience with World Bank-funded or other multilateral/bilateral development bank-funded projects.

 

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, the Seventh (7th) Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The Joint Venture/Sub-consultancy agreement or letter of intent to form a joint venture/a sub-consultancy association signed by every participating member shall be submitted with the Expression of Interest (EOI).

 

4. Submission of Expression of Interest

Interested firms must organize their Expression of Interest in the following order:

Chapter 1

  1. Company Profile
  2. Legal Status (Certificate of Incorporation)
  3. Letter of intent or Agreement to form a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy
  4. Organizational chart, a list of Board of Directors, and beneficial ownership.

Chapter 2

  1. Evidence of experience in at least three (3) road infrastructure consulting assignments of similar scope and complexity (design/design review and construction supervision) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  2. Evidence of experience in at least one (1) road infrastructure consulting assignment of similar scope and complexity (performance-based maintenance management) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  3. A summary of assignments undertaken in Sub-Saharan Africa given the specific geographical, climatic, and social contexts, giving the client’s name and the year in which the assignment was carried out

Chapter 3

  1. Experience in World Bank-funded or other multilateral/bilateral development bank-funded projects.
  2. Experience in applying good Environmental and Social standards and practices to project management and supervision, and in assignments involving Multilateral Development Banks’  Environmental and Social Framework(s) (ESF), including Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention and response requirements.

The document must be properly paged, and a table of contents provided.

Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 to 1700 hours GMT.

description:
Objectives of the Assignment

 

To lead and implement the communication and public relations (PR) components of the regional One Health program, ensuring unified messaging, stakeholder engagement, and media visibility through both digital and traditional communication channels.

 

Scope of Work

 

The PR consultant will be responsible for the following:

 

  1. Strategy & Planning
     
  • Develop and implement the Regional One Health Communication Strategy, in coordination with PR manager, Project coordinator, national focal points and WB team.
  • Develop a brand identity and maintain visual consistency across all communication materials.
  • Prepare and implement a publication and content calendar, aligned with project milestones and thematic priorities.

 

  1. Media & Public Relations
     
  • Develop and implement a media outreach plan, covering traditional (TV, radio, print) and online outlets across the region.
  • Build and maintain a media contact database of relevant journalists and editorial contacts in participating countries.
  • Invite and coordinate media participation in project events, including forums, launches, consultations, and training.
  • Prepare press kits for events, including press releases, background briefs, speaker bios, visual materials, and quotes.
  • Draft and disseminate press releases, opinion articles, interviews, and news stories in collaboration with technical teams and national stakeholders.
  • Organize and moderate media briefings and press conferences as needed.
  • Liaise directly with journalists and editors to support coverage of project activities and secure interviews with project representatives.
  • Conduct ongoing media monitoring and analysis, collecting and archiving published materials and tracking media exposure on monthly basis and present this analysis to the project coordinator.
  • Prepare quarterly media monitoring reports, assessing visibility, tone, outreach scope, and communication impact.

 

  1.  Digital Communication & Social Media
     
  • Design and manage regional social media campaigns, including content planning, visual creation, and performance tracking.
  • Contribute to the Central Asian One Health Information Portal by uploading communications products and ensuring regular updates.
  • Use interactive tools (surveys, infographics, Q&A sessions) to increase engagement with the general public and stakeholder communities.
  • Coordinate with national focal points/partners to collect, verify, and package news, success stories, photos, quotes and event updates for publication.
  • Draft, design, schedule and publish posts (RU/EN) across agreed channels (e.g., Facebook/Instagram/LinkedIn/Telegram), including basic community management (replying/moderation per agreed SOP).
  • Maintain a shared content pipeline (news intake form + approvals tracker) and a monthly/weekly publishing plan

 

  1. Visual Design & Content Production (In-house)

 

  • Consultant is responsible for independent development of visual materials for the project, including (but not limited to): web-banners, website sliders/covers, social media templates, story/reel covers, infographics, event visuals, roll-up/banner layouts, presentation templates, news cards, email headers, etc.
  • Consultant must provide editable source files for all designs (e.g., CDR/.PSD/.AI/.INDD + exported .PNG/.JPG/.PDF) and maintain an organized archive (cloud folder) with version control.
  • Consultant ensures brand consistency across all materials

 

  1. Coordination with Contractors and Content Production
     
  • When external production is required (photo/video/printing/large-scale creative), Consultant prepares ToRs and supervises contractors; however, routine graphic design and digital visuals are produced by the Consultant in-house.
  • Coordinate the production of visual and promotional content (banners, roll-ups, branded merchandise, video explainers, photos, educational infographics).
  • Oversee venue branding and decoration for events in accordance with project identity standards.
  • Supervise contractors to ensure quality, timeliness, and consistency in all visual communications deliverables.

 

  1. Capacity Building and Training
  • Conduct a needs assessment on communications capacity among project partners.
  • Develop and deliver training for CAREC staff, national stakeholders, and focal points on effective communication, media engagement, and public messaging.
  • Support crisis communication preparedness, including simulations and guidance development.

 

  1. Monitoring and Evaluation
  • Define KPIs for communication activities and develop simple tracking tools (e.g., dashboards).
  • Conduct quarterly assessments of campaigns and PR performance; propose adjustments.
  • Contribute to donor visibility reports, CAREC publications, and knowledge products based on communication outcomes.

 

Assignment Duration

 

The assignment will last for 12 months, beginning from contract signing. Extension may be considered based on project dynamics.

 

Reporting

 

The PR consultant reports to the CAREC OH Project Coordinator and works closely with technical teams, the M&E specialist, and national communication focal points.

 

Assignment Conditions

  • The Consultant shall use their own hardware and software and maintain valid licenses for required design tools (e.g., CorelDRAW, Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator/InDesign and/or equivalent).
  • All costs related to creation of digital visual materials (software subscriptions, fonts, plugins, stock assets) are covered by the Consultant and included in the fee, unless explicitly pre-approved in writing by CAREC.
  • Printing and physical production (e.g., printing roll-ups/banners/merch) is not covered by the Consultant unless separately agreed and budgeted; Consultant provides print-ready files and technical specs.

 

Assignment Location

 

CAREC Headquarters in Almaty, Kazakhstan or one of the Central Asian countries with the possibility of remote work, with occasional travel within Central Asia for event support and stakeholder engagement.

 

Qualifications

 

Education

  • University degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or related field.

 

Experience

  • At least 5 years of experience in PR, media relations, or strategic communications for international/regional development programs.
  • Strong background in managing social media campaigns, organizing press events, and working with multimedia contractors.
  • Previous experience in working with donors such as the World Bank, WHO, or FAO is a strong asset.

 

Skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and Russian.
  • Strong media writing, storytelling, and content creation abilities.
  • Proficiency in design tools (e.g., Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, CorelDRAW,Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator (plus optional Figma/After Effects) and media monitoring software.
  • Organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Cultural sensitivity and ability to work with diverse stakeholders
  • Portfolio required demonstrating banner/social/event design.

 

Detailed Terms of reference is available at the link.

Interested candidates are required to CV and cover letter to smustafin@carececo.org with copy to okravtsova@carececo.org  not later than 04 March, 2026.  

 

Please be sure to indicate PR consultant in the subject line of the email.

description:
Introduction

On June 22, 2025, the World Bank Board of Executive Directors approved an allocation of US$3.45 million from the International Development Association (IDA) to finance the first phase of the ONE HEALTH FOR PANDEMIC PREVENTION, FOOD SYSTEMS RESILIENCE, AND ECOSYSTEM HEALTH IN CENTRAL ASIA PROJECT. This approved financing to be implemented by the Regional Environmental Center for Central Asia (CAREC) for day-to-day regional coordination and implementation.

Project Description

The objective of the Project is to establish the capacity of the Regional One Health Coordination Structure in managing priority zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and food safety issues in Central Asia through a regional One Health approach.

The Project constitutes a phase of the MPA Program, and consists of the following parts:

Part 1. Establishing One Health Governance.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for:

establishing and maintaining the Regional One Health Coordination Structure;

developing Regional One Health Action Plan(s);

establishing the Central Asia One Health Portal;

developing and implementing a regional One Health communication and stakeholder engagement strategy;

organizing regular consultations and meetings with key stakeholders;

developing a regional laboratory network strategy; and

conducting regulatory assessments and reviews relevant to regional One Health issues to suggest areas for policy improvement.

Part 2. Enhancing One Health Knowledge and Workforce Capacity.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for establishing an institutional mechanism for knowledge development and exchange, as well as technical capacity development at the regional level. Activities will include:

conducting regional risk assessments on priority regional threats from zoonoses, antimicrobial resistance and food risks;

conducting regional or cross-border outbreak response exercises;

establishing a regional training platform as part of the Central Asia One Health Portal; and

organizing targeted training and capacity building activities for key professions in the veterinary, human health and environment sectors in participating countries.

Part 3. Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Learning.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for project management activities, including:

the creation of a monitoring and evaluation framework; and

communications and supporting systems to enhance learning and tracking of effectiveness of Recipient-managed One Health activities.

In accordance with the Financing and Operating Agreements and the WB requirements, the project is subject to independent external audit to be conducted after the end of each financial year (or another period agreed with the WB) throughout the project period. The main objective of the external audit is to check whether the donor funds are used as designated and express an independent opinion on the project financial reports for the reporting financial year.

 

Objective

The objective of the audit of the Project Financial Statements (PFS) is to enable the auditor to express a professional opinion on the financial position of the Project as of the end of each fiscal year and on the Project’s sources and uses of funds for the respective reporting period, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

The audit shall cover the period from June 24, 2025 to July 31, 2027, and shall continue annually until the Disbursement Deadline Date of November 30, 2027, as applicable.

The Project’s books of account shall be maintained in accordance with sound accounting practices and shall provide the basis for the preparation of the Project Financial Statements. The accounting records shall reflect all financial transactions related to the Project.

Audit Periods

  • The first audit shall cover the period from June 24, 2025 to December 31, 2025.
  • The second audit shall cover the period from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026.
  • The final audit shall cover the period from January 1, 2027 to July 31, 2027 and include grace period.

 

 

Responsibility for preparation of financial statements

The project’s management is responsible for the preparation of financial statements, including the maintenance of adequate accounting records and internal controls, the selection and application of accounting policies, the safeguarding of the assets of the project, and adequate disclosure.  As part of the audit process, the auditor will request from management written confirmation concerning representations made to us in connection with the audit.

Scope

The audit will be conducted in accordance with International Standards on Auditing. Those Standards require that the auditor plans and performs the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatements. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.

In complying with International Standards on Auditing, the auditor is expected to pay particular attention to the following matters, including special considerations for public sector entities:

  1. In planning and performing the audit to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level, the auditor should consider the risks of material misstatements in the financial statements due to fraud, as required by International Standard on Auditing 240: The Auditor’s Responsibilities Relating to Fraud in an Audit of Financial Statements.
  2. When designing and performing audit procedures and in evaluating and reporting the results thereof, the auditor should recognize that noncompliance by the entity with laws and regulations may materially affect the financial statements, as required by International Standard on Auditing 250: Consideration of Laws and Regulations in an Audit of Financial Statements.
  3. The auditor should communicate audit matters of governance interest arising from the audit of financial statements to those charged with governance of an entity, as required by International Standard on Auditing 260: Communication with those Charged with Governance.
  4. The auditor should appropriately communicate to those charged with governance and to management any deficiencies in internal control that the auditor has identified in an audit of financial statements, as required by International Standard on Auditing 265: Communicating Deficiencies in Internal Control to Those Charged with Governance and Management.
  5. To reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level, the auditor should determine overall responses to assessed risks at the financial statement level, and should design and perform further audit procedures to respond to assessed risks at the assertion level, as required by International Standard on Auditing 330: The Auditor’s Responses to Assessed Risks.
  6. When certain aspects of an entity’s operations are performed by a third-party service provider, the auditor is expected to include an understanding and assessment of the internal control environment of the service provider during the audit process, as required by International Standard on Auditing 402: Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organization.
  7. As part of the audit process, the auditor is expected to obtain written representations from management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, as required by International Standard on Auditing 580: Written Representations. 
  8. When the external auditor decides to use the work of an entity’s internal audit function to modify the nature or timing, or reduce the extent, of audit procedures to be performed directly by the external auditor, the determination shall be in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 610: Using the Work of Internal Auditors.   In determining whether to use the work of an auditor’s expert or the extent to which the work of an auditor’s expert is adequate for audit purposes, the determination shall be made in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 620: Using the Work of an Auditor’s Expert.  

In evidencing compliance with agreed project financing arrangements, the auditor is expected to carry out tests to confirm that:

  1. All external funds have been used in accordance with the conditions of the relevant financing agreements, with due attention to economy and efficiency, and only for the purposes for which the financing was provided. Relevant financing agreements include financing agreement GRANT NUMBER TF-C7896.
  2. Goods, works, and services financed have been procured in accordance with relevant financing agreements,[1] including specific provisions of the World Bank Procurement Guidelines.[2]
  3. All necessary supporting documents, records, and accounts have been maintained in respect of all project activities, including expenditures reported using Statements of Expenditure (SOE) The auditor is expected to verify that respective reports issued during the period were in agreement with the underlying books of account.

Project financial statements

The auditor should verify that the financial statements have been prepared in accordance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)”Financial Reporting Under the Cash Basis of Accounting “cash-basis method. The financial statements should include:

 

) A statement of sources and uses of funds;

 

b) Accounting policies and explanatory notes[3] (including additional accounting policies and disclosures), which will include:

- Statement of Financial position;

- Statements of Expenditure used as the basis for submission of withdrawal applications in the notes;

- A statement on the Designated account in the notes; and

- When the entity makes publicly available its approved budget, a comparison of budget and actual amounts either as a separate additional financial statement or as a budget column in the financial statements

Review of Statements of Expenditure The auditor is required to audit all SOE submitted to the World Bank in support of requests for periodic replenishment of the project designated account(s). Expenditures should be examined for eligibility based on criteria defined in the terms of the financing agreement and detailed in the Project Appraisal Document. The auditor should report any ineligible expenditures identified as having been included in withdrawal applications and reimbursed. The auditor should pay particular attention to whether:

  1. the Summary Reports (or SOEs) have been prepared in accordance with the provisions of the relevant financing agreement;
  2. expenditures have been made wholly and necessarily for the realization of project objectives;
  3. information and explanation necessary for the purpose of the audit have been obtained;
  4. supporting records and documents necessary for the purpose of the audit have been retained, and
  5. the Summary Reports (or SOEs) can be relied upon to support the related withdrawal applications.

Review of designated accounts

During the audit of the project financial statements, the auditor is required to review the activities of the project’s designated account(s). Activities to be examined will include deposits received, payments made, interest earned, and reconciliation of period-end balances.

Audit Reports

Audit opinion

The auditor will issue an audit opinion on project financial statements. The auditor’s opinion shall be based on an evaluation of the conclusions drawn from the audit evidence obtained and shall be expressed clearly through a written report that also describes the basis for that opinion. The audit report shall be prepared in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 700: Forming an Opinion and Reporting on Financial Statements. 

A modified audit opinion shall be rendered in the financial statements when the auditor concludes, on the basis of the audit evidence obtained, that the financial statements as a whole are not free from material misstatement; or the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to conclude that the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement. Modified audit opinions shall be in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 705: Modifications to the Opinion in the Independent Auditor’s Report.

The auditor will include emphasis of matter paragraphs or other matter paragraphs in the audit opinion where the auditor, having formed an opinion on the financial statements, seeks to draw users’ attention, when in the auditor’s judgment it is necessary to do so, by way of clear additional communication in the auditor’s report. The paragraphs will refer to either a matter that, although appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements, is of such importance that it is fundamental to users’ understanding of the financial statements; or as appropriate, any other matter that is relevant to users’ understanding of the audit, the auditor’s responsibilities, or the auditor’s report. This form of opinion will be presented in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 706: Emphasis of Matter Paragraphs or Other Matter Paragraphs in the Independent Auditor’s Report.

Other audit reports

In addition to the audit opinion(s), the auditor will also, either in the audit report or in the report to management:

  1. provide comments and observations on the accounting records, systems, and controls that were examined during the course of the audit;
  2. identify specific deficiencies and areas of weakness in systems and controls and make recommendation for their improvement;
  3. report on instances of noncompliance with the terms of the financial agreement(s);
  4. quantify and report expenditures that are considered to be ineligible and either paid out of the designated account(s) or claimed from the World Bank;
  5. communicate matters that have come to attention during the audit that might have a significant impact on the implementation of the project;
  6. draw to the borrower’s attention any other matters that the auditor considers pertinent; and
  7. responses from management, including implemented and proposed remedial actions.

If, during the audit nothing has come to the attention that the auditor considers pertinent to be brought to the attention of the borrower, and a management letter is therefore not prepared, the auditor will issue a letter stating this.

The auditor’s opinion on the financial statements and management letter should be received by the Bank no later than of 30 June 2026.

Public Disclosure
