Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address shared issues and support cooperation. PIF works through regional governance, shared resources and policy alignment to support economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises eighteen members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.

Participating Countries

The Pacific Island Countries participating in the regional project comprise Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu. This assignment provides country-specific support to the Republic of the Marshall Islands under the regional project.

Overall Project Objective

The Project Development Objective is to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries.

Project Length

August 2024 to September 30, 2030

Project Background

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) for the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project. The project supports participating Pacific Island Countries (PICs) to maintain continuous access to correspondent banking services, and to address underlying payment, regulatory and financial integrity constraints that contribute to de-risking in the region.

PICs are exposed to the withdrawal of correspondent banking relationships (CBRs) that underpin international trade, tourism, remittances, development finance, disaster relief, and humanitarian financial flows. The project provides a short-term CBR safety net while supporting the enabling environment and regional harmonization needed for a medium-term sustainable solution.

Component 2 of the project, Enabling Environment and Regulatory Harmonization, includes support for Payment System Oversight and Regulation. The relevant activity areas include payment systems regulatory harmonization, oversight of national payment systems, and collection of remittance and gender-disaggregated data on usage of financial services. Component 2 also supports payment systems strengthening, CBR Roadmap implementation, the CBR Resilience Index, and the feasibility work for the Pacific Payment Mechanism (PPM), which aims to aggregate payment flows and improve economies of scale.

The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is in the early phase of operationalizing the MAMI. In June 2026, the Governor of MAMI requested support for an advisor to assist with implementation of the Authority's operationalization strategy, including review and tailoring of recommendations from the IMF Monetary and Capital Markets Department technical assistance report, Operationalizing A New Monetary Authority. The request also highlighted the need to establish the national payment system in alignment with the World Bank CBR Strengthening Project's payment system harmonization roadmap.

The IMF report identifies several payment-related priorities for MAMI. These include the development of a National Payments Strategy (NPS), the establishment of payment operations and payment oversight functions, the creation of a stakeholder consultation mechanism and National Payment Council, the preparation of payment operations and oversight procedures, and the design of an Integrated Payment and Clearing System (IPCS) that can combine ACH, RTGS and instant payment functionality in a phased manner. The report also notes that RMI currently has no centralized payment system, that payment services are dominated by checks, that there is no e-money provider, and that electronic payments remain limited outside selected card and POS use cases.

This assignment is designed as payment systems technical assistance under the CBR Project’s Technical Assistance component. It is framed around the project's Payment System Oversight and Regulation activities and is expected to support MAMI in converting payment-related IMF recommendations into a practical work plan, institutional arrangements, operating procedures, oversight tools, stakeholder coordination mechanisms, and capacity building outputs.

Objective of the Position

The main objective of the Payments System Advisor to MAMI is to provide technical advisory support to MAMI for the establishment of a safe, efficient, inclusive and scalable national payments system and payment system oversight function, aligned with the CBR Project, the CBR Roadmap, regional payment system harmonization work, and the emerging design of the PPM.

The Advisor will review the payment-related findings and recommendations in the IMF MCM report and assist MAMI to translate the relevant payment system recommendations into a practical implementation approach for RMI. This will include helping MAMI distinguish payment system actions from broader central banking, governance, accounting, audit, reserve management, HR, communications and corporate services matters, and sequencing the payment system actions in line with MAMI’s institutional capacity, staffing plans and expected operational priorities.

In doing so, the Advisor will consider the small scale of the RMI financial sector, the dominance of checks, limited electronic payment usage, geographic dispersion, government payment needs, remittance costs, digital financial-service developments, and MAMI’s current staffing and institutional capacity.

Scope of Services

The selected Payments System Advisor will provide country-level, time-based technical implementation support for RMI on payment system matters. The work will be coordinated with the PIFS PMU, the PIFS Payment Systems Specialist, the World Bank payments team, IMF MCM and other technical assistance providers as relevant. The Advisor will carry out the following tasks, with timing and level of effort agreed through the 12-month implementation work plan and periodic work planning discussions:

i. Inception, work planning and IMF recommendation mapping

  • Review the IMF MCM report, MAMI Act and related institutional materials, the CBR Project Operations Manual, the CBR Roadmap, available PPM materials, and other relevant documents provided by MAMI, PIFS or the World Bank.
  • Prepare an inception report that identifies the payment-related recommendations requiring action by MAMI and separates them from broader central banking, governance, accounting, audit, reserve management, HR, communications, and corporate services matters.
  • Develop a 12-month implementation roadmap for the establishment of MAMI’s national payments function, with milestones, dependencies, counterpart responsibilities, expected outputs, sequencing assumptions, and coordination points with the World Bank, IMF and PIFS. The roadmap should be aligned with MAMI’s expected recruitment of the Banking Operations Department Executive Manager and Payment Systems Operations Manager, anticipated around December 2026 to January 2027, so that the Advisor’s support helps prepare for, onboard, and transition responsibilities to these key MAMI counterparts.
  • Prepare and periodically update the Advisor’s own assignment work plan, aligned with the 12-month MAMI implementation roadmap, counterpart availability, agreed priorities, in-country inputs, and monthly or quarterly work planning discussions with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank.
  • Tailor payment system recommendations to the RMI context, including market size, transaction volumes, institutional capacity, staffing constraints, remittance corridors, public sector payment needs, and affordability for banks and end users.

ii. Establishment of MAMI's national payments function

  • Advise MAMI on the operational setup, sequencing, staffing profile and accountabilities for its national payments function, including the Payment Operations Division (POD) and Payment Oversight and Policy Division (OVD) recommended by the IMF report.
  • Provide advice on the separation of payment system operations and payment system oversight responsibilities within MAMI’s payments mandate, including reporting lines, decision processes, internal coordination arrangements, and safeguards to manage potential conflicts between operational and oversight functions.
  • Prepare a short skills and capacity building plan for MAMI staff involved in payment operations, payment oversight, payment      collection, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Assist MAMI to define working procedures and decision flows for its payment system operational and oversight functions, including issue escalation, internal reporting, consultation with supervised or participating institutions, coordination with IT, risk, legal and supervision functions, and referral of matters requiring specialist technical or legal input.

 

iii. National Payments Strategy

  • Support MAMI to develop a National Payments Strategy that sets out a phased modernization agenda for RMI’s national payment system, aligned with the National Financial Inclusion Strategy and coordinated with related work under the CBR Project, regional payment system harmonization agenda, and emerging PPM design.
  • Prepare or support a baseline diagnostic covering domestic and cross-border payment flows, CBRs, government payments, remittances, check usage, card and POS usage, payment access, digital infrastructure, consumer needs, and data gaps.
  • Identify practical measures to increase use of electronic payments, reduce reliance on checks and cash where appropriate, improve government payment flows, support remittance cost reduction, and expand access to payment services for businesses, households and the public sector.
  • Support stakeholder consultations on the NPS, including preparation of consultation materials, meeting notes, issue logs and revisions to the strategy based on feedback received.

iv. Payment infrastructure and IPCS implementation support

  • Advise MAMI on a fit-for-purpose and phased approach to payment infrastructure modernization, including the IMF recommendation for an Integrated Payment and Clearing System combining ACH, RTGS and instant payment functionality.
  • Advise MAMI on the preparation, review and sequencing of high-level business requirements and implementation planning for any future IPCS, including initial electronic clearing for wire transfers and checks, check truncation, settlement arrangements, participant onboarding, service levels, operating schedules and support arrangements. The Advisor will help MAMI frame the requirements and coordinate specialist inputs but will not be responsible for preparing detailed technical specifications or system design documents unless separately agreed with PIFS, MAMI and the World Bank.
  • Assess the sequencing of ACH, RTGS and instant payment functionality based on RMI transaction volumes, costs, operational readiness, risk profile and user needs.
  • Advise MAMI on the issues that should be considered when planning future payment infrastructure, including payment messaging, straight-through processing, ISO 20022 readiness, data security, operational resilience, business continuity, disaster recovery, liquidity risk, settlement risk and participant default arrangements. Where detailed technical design is required, the Advisor will help MAMI identify the issues, review options, and coordinate inputs from specialist payment infrastructure, IT, cybersecurity or World Bank experts.
  • Provide payment system technical inputs to procurement documents, concept notes or options papers for the IPCS, as requested by MAMI and the PMU, subject to World Bank procurement rules and conflict-of-interest restrictions.

v. Payment system oversight, data and risk-based supervision

  • Support MAMI to define a payment system oversight framework covering objectives, scope, standards, tools, reporting, escalation, corrective actions and coordination with other MAMI functions.
  • Advise MAMI on the scope, structure and phased development of oversight procedures for risk-based monitoring of payment systems and payment service providers, including e-money and non-bank PSPs where relevant. The Advisor may prepare outlines, review drafts and support capacity building, but detailed supervisory manuals, examination procedures or legal instruments should be developed with appropriate specialist and legal input as required.
  • Advise MAMI on the payment data and indicators that should be collected for oversight and policy purposes, including payment volumes and values, failed transactions, settlement incidents, fraud, customer complaints, operational incidents, participation, concentration, liquidity risk, credit risk and operational risk. The Advisor may support the development or review of reporting templates in coordination with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank, but the final templates should be agreed by MAMI and aligned with wider project data requirements.
  • Provide technical inputs to and reviews of payment-related regulations, rules, circulars or supervisory guidance as requested, including on electronic payments, PSPs, system participation and operational risk. This role does not include drafting primary payment system legislation or formal legal opinions.
  • Align oversight tools with relevant international standards and guidance, including the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures, ISO 20022, risk-based supervision practices, consumer protection principles and cyber-resilience expectations applicable to payment systems.
  • Review USDM1-related payment system implications, considering existing RMI AML laws and regulations and MAMI’s current regulatory treatment of USDM1, and advise on whether any payment system oversight, interoperability, reporting, operational risk, consumer safeguard or AML/CFT coordination measures should be reflected in MAMI’s national payment system framework. The Advisor will not provide advice on the sovereign debt, securities law, issuance, redemption, collateral, reserve management or investment aspects of USDM1 except where these issues directly affect payment system oversight or integration.

vi. Coordination, consultation and National Payment Council support

  • Assist MAMI to establish a consultation mechanism with banks, government agencies, SOEs, card schemes, telecom operators, payment service providers, major users and other stakeholders involved in payments modernization.
  • Prepare draft Terms of Reference, membership options, work program and first-year agenda for a National Payment Council or equivalent advisory body.
  • Support MAMI in coordinating with the Ministry of Finance on payment-related services, including government payment flows, account information, reporting expectations, service levels, and inputs to any payment-related SLA or MOU arrangements.
  • Prepare stakeholder maps, consultation papers, meeting agendas, minutes and action trackers to support implementation of the national payments work plan.

vii. Alignment with the CBR Project and regional work

  • Coordinate closely with the PIFS PMU, PIFS Payment Systems Specialist and World Bank payments team to align RMI support with the CBR Project's Component 2 work program.
  • Support RMI inputs into CBR data collection, the CBR Resilience Index and the PPM feasibility and design process, including payment flow data, remittance information, CBR information and stakeholder feedback.
  • Assist MAMI to collect and improve relevant remittance and gender-disaggregated data on the usage of financial services, where feasible and agreed with the PMU and World Bank.
  • Identify areas where RMI can participate in regional harmonization work, including PSP licensing, QR code standards, open banking/open finance, cross-border interoperability and common principles for cross-border data sharing.
  • Coordinate with IMF MCM and other technical assistance providers, through MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank as appropriate, to reduce duplication, sequence inputs, and keep the assignment focused on payment system matters within the agreed CBR Project scope. Where feasible, the Advisor may support periodic coordination discussions, including around the Annual Meetings or Spring Meetings, if requested by MAMI, PIFS or the World Bank.

viii. Capacity building and knowledge transfer

  • Identify MAMI staff training needs, develop a multi-year training plan, and identify opportunities for training and knowledge transfer aligned with MAMI’s payment system mandate, staffing plan and future development priorities.
  • Prepare training materials, practical templates and work aids that MAMI staff can continue to use after the assignment.
  • Identify peer learning opportunities with regional central banks or payment system operators, including short technical exchanges or virtual clinics where appropriate.
  • Provide mentoring to assigned MAMI counterparts and support handover of tools, procedures and work plans before the end of the assignment.

Scope Exclusions

The assignment is limited to payment systems technical assistance and payment-related operationalization of MAMI. The Advisor will not draft the Payment Systems Act, amendments to the Monetary Authority Act, primary legislation, or formal legal opinions.

The Advisor will not provide general central bank advisory services on reserve management, fiscal agency, accounting, audit, human resources, communications, procurement, general governance, or corporate services except where those topics directly affect payment system operations, payment oversight, payment infrastructure or payment-related stakeholder coordination.

Time-Based Reporting Obligations and Expected Outputs

This assignment will be contracted on a time-based basis. Payments will be linked to approved timesheets, agreed input days, and eligible reimbursable expenses, not to a fixed-price deliverables schedule. The outputs listed below are expected working products and reporting instruments for managing the assignment, tracking progress, supporting quality review, and documenting knowledge transfer.

The Advisor will prepare and update working products in line with the agreed work plan and counterpart needs. These may include the inception note and 12-month payments work plan, IMF recommendation mapping, National Payments Strategy materials, payment function setup notes, National Payment Council materials, payment operations and oversight procedures, data templates, IPCS options and requirements notes, training materials, mission notes and handover materials.

Because the role is advisory and embedded with MAMI for a substantial part of the assignment, outputs may be revised or reprioritized during implementation with agreement from MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank. The Advisor will document changes through monthly activity notes, quarterly progress notes and the action tracker.

Reporting Obligations

The Payments System Advisor will work closely with MAMI on a day-to-day technical basis and will report administratively to the Project Coordinator within the PIFS PMU. Technical priorities, work planning, and expected outputs will be agreed with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank payments team. The Advisor will also coordinate with the PIFS Payment Systems Specialist and the RMI Country Coordinator as relevant.

The Advisor will submit monthly timesheets and short monthly activity notes to the PIFS PMU, with confirmation from MAMI of the main activities undertaken. The monthly activity note should summarize days worked, in-country and remote inputs, meetings held, outputs prepared, issues requiring decision, and planned activities for the following month. Technical outputs will be shared with MAMI and PIFS, and PIFS will share them with the World Bank for review or no-objection where required under the project arrangements.

The Advisor will maintain a short action tracker covering agreed activities, responsible counterparts, due dates, risks, dependencies and decisions required. The tracker will be updated at least monthly, and more frequently if requested by the PMU or MAMI. The Advisor will also provide quarterly progress notes against the 12-month payments work plan and a final completion and handover note at the end of the assignment.

Institutional Arrangements

This is a time-based individual consultant assignment contracted by PIFS through the PMU under the Pacific Strengthening CBR Project. The assignment will be undertaken for the benefit of MAMI as the primary country counterpart. The procurement approach is competitive selection of an independent individual consultant, subject to the approved procurement plan, applicable PIFS procurement procedures, conflict-of-interest review, and World Bank review or no-objection requirements where applicable.

The Advisor is expected to spend significant time in Majuro during the assignment, estimated at 50-60 percent of total input days, especially during inception, stakeholder consultations, NPS preparation, payment function setup, capacity building and infrastructure planning. Remote work may be used for document preparation, virtual meetings, training, follow-up and coordination with PIFS and the World Bank.

Office space and access to meeting facilities may be provided by MAMI for in-country inputs and by PIFS for inputs in Suva, subject to availability. The Advisor will be responsible for maintaining secure records of documents, correspondence and data received during the assignment and for complying with all confidentiality requirements.

The Advisor's services will be subject to periodic performance review based on the performance indicators below. Performance review will inform continuation, extension, revision or termination of the assignment, subject to contract terms and World Bank requirements.

 

Performance Indicators

The following performance indicators will be used for contract management and performance assessment. They are intended to measure timely input, quality of advisory support, documented outputs, counterpart engagement and knowledge transfer under a time-based contract:

  • Monthly timesheets are submitted on time and accurately distinguish between in country and remote input days.
  • Monthly activity notes are submitted on time and summarize work undertaken, meetings held, issues requiring decision, risks, planned next steps and counterpart engagement.
  • The Advisor maintains and updates an action tracker covering agreed activities, responsible counterparts, deadlines, dependencies and pending decisions.
  • A 12-month implementation roadmap for MAMI’s national payments function is prepared, discussed with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank, and updated as required during implementation.
  • The Advisor’s own assignment work plan is maintained and aligned with the 12-month MAMI implementation roadmap, MAMI counterpart availability and agreed priorities.
  • Payment-related IMF MCM recommendations are mapped and separated from broader central banking, governance, accounting, audit, reserve management, HR, communications and corporate services matters.
  • MAMI receives documented advice, meeting notes or working materials on the setup of payment operations and payment oversight responsibilities, including staffing, reporting lines, procedures and capacity needs.
  • MAMI is supported in preparing or refining National Payments Strategy materials, consultation inputs and implementation roadmap elements.
  • Payment infrastructure advice is documented through advisory notes, review comments or options papers that support a phased and fit-for-purpose approach to any future IPCS, without requiring the Advisor to develop systems or detailed technical specifications.
  • Payment system oversight and data work is documented through advisory notes, outlines, review comments, reporting needs, draft structures or training materials, with specialist technical or legal work referred to appropriate experts where required.
  • Stakeholder engagement is documented through meeting notes, action trackers, consultation materials or National Payment Council support materials.
  • Capacity building activities are documented through training materials, attendance records, mentoring notes or handover materials.
  • Quarterly progress notes are submitted against the agreed work plan and discussed with MAMI, PIFS and the World Bank.
  • A final completion and handover note is submitted at the end of the assignment, summarizing work undertaken, outputs prepared, remaining actions, open risks and recommended next steps.
  • The Advisor maintains professional, objective and impartial advice, avoids conflicts of interest, records input days accurately, and complies with PIFS and World Bank rules on confidentiality, anti-corruption and fraud prevention.

Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

The Payments System Advisor shall comply with PIFS and World Bank policies and rules on anti-corruption, prevention of fraudulent practices, conflict of interest and confidentiality. The Advisor shall maintain confidentiality over all sensitive information obtained during the assignment and shall not publish or disclose any findings, data, reports or recommendations without prior written consent from PIFS and MAMI, and World Bank clearance where required.

Any draft reports and other documents produced by the Advisor will be discussed with and cleared by PIFS, MAMI and the World Bank before final issue. A non-disclosure agreement may be signed between PIFS, MAMI and the selected consultant and attached to the contract.

The Advisor must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest before contract signature and throughout the assignment. The Advisor shall not participate in downstream procurement activities where such participation would create a conflict of interest under the World Bank Procurement Regulations or the Project Operations Manual.

2. O principal objectivo do/a Especialista em Gestão de Riscos de Segurança é de assegurar a implementação actualização do Plano de Gestão de Segurança (PGS) do Projecto CRRN, garantindo a protecção de pessoas, bens, activos e infraestruturas, bem como a continuidade operacional das actividades do projecto.

3. Os Termos de Referência (TdR) detalhados para o serviço podem ser obtidos no seguinte link https://www.fe.gov.mz/storage/app/uploads/public/6a8/44d/d9b/6a844dd9b1325844730998.pdf ou alternativamente no endereço abaixo.

4. A Administração Nacional de Estradas, IP convida os Consultores Individuais elegíveis ("Consultores") a manifestar o seu interesse em prestar os Serviços durante dois (2) meses a tempo inteiro estará baseado em Maputo, com deslocações, se necessário, aos locais abrangidos pelo projecto nas províncias de Cabo Delgado, Nampula e Niassa.

5. Os Consultores interessados devem fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações exigidas e experiência relevante para executar os Serviços.

6. A avaliação das manifestações de interesse será feita numa base qualitativa de acordo com uma matriz robusta de pontos fortes e fracos e a lista curta será composta a partir da lista de consultores individuais qualificados considerando os seguintes critérios:

  • Licenciatura em Gestão de Segurança, Gestão de Riscos, Estudos de Segurança, Justiça Penal, Direito, ou área relacionada;
  • Formação especializada em Gestão de Riscos (ISO 31000 será uma vantagem);
  • Possuir certificações internacionais (é uma vantagem);
  • Mínimo de 10 (Dez) anos de experiência profissional relevante;
  • Experiência em gestão de segurança de infraestruturas;
  • Experiência comprovada em gestão de segurança em áreas afectadas por conflito ou elevado risco operacional será uma vantagem;
  • Experiência em coordenação com forças públicas;
  • Conhecimento da legislação moçambicana em matéria de segurança;
  • Experiência em projectos financiados por instituições internacionais (vantagem);
  • Excelentes capacidades de liderança, análise, comunicação e gestão de crises;
  • Domínio do Português e Inglês (obrigatório).

7. Chama-se a atenção aos Consultores interessados para a Secção III, parágrafos, 3.13, 3.15 e 3.16 dos “Regulamentos de Contratação para Mutuários da IPF” do Banco Mundial de Setembro de 2025 (“Regulamentos de Contratação”), que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.

8. O consultor será selecionado de acordo com o método do consultor individual (IC) previsto nos Regulamentos de Contratação.

ROAD TRANSPORT AND SAFETY AGENCY (RTSA)
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)
COUNTRY: REPUBLIC OF ZAMBIA
PROJECT NAME: TRANSPORT CORRIDORS FOR ECONOMIC RESILIENCE (TRACER)
PROJECT ID: P180801, IDA GRANT NO: E2930 ZM
REFERENCE NO.: ZM-RTSA-444824-CS-QCBS
NAME OF THE ASSIGNMENT: DESIGN CONSULTANT FOR THE SMART CORRIDOR PROJECT, DAR ES SA-LAAM CORRIDOR (LUSAKA–NAKONDE SECTION), ZAMBIA
1.    The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER) Project.
2.    The Consulting Services (“the Services”) comprise the design of the SMART Corridor System for the Lusaka–Nakonde section of the Dar es Salaam Corridor and the preparation of the associated tender documentation. The system includes four pillars: Corridor Monitoring, Traffic Manage-ment, Trade Facilitation and Road Safety.
3.    Duration of Assignment: The assignment is expected to be undertaken within a period of twelve (12) calendar months from contract commencement. The Terms of Reference for the as-signment may be obtained from the RTSA website at https://www.rtsa.org.zm/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Terms-of-Reference-Design-Consultant_v3-World-Bank-1.pdf, or at the address given below.
4.    The Road Transport and Safety Agency (RTSA), on behalf of GRZ, now invites eligible Consulting Firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information, with supporting documents, demonstrating that they have the re-quired qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.
5.    The shortlisting criteria are:
(i) Experience in similar assignments – successful execution of similar contracts (by size and complexity). The firm shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of proven experience in the Planning, Design or Implementation of Intelligent Transport Systems, Corridor Modernisa-tion or Comparable Multi-Agency Technology Programmes, and shall have completed, within the last seven (7) years, at least three (3) assignments of a similar nature and comparable complexity. For each assignment, state its name, the client’s name and full contact address, the contract value in equivalent United States Dollars and the dates of execution.
(ii) Experience in similar conditions. Experience in Sub-Saharan Africa is not mandatory but is an added advantage.
(iii) Technical and managerial capability of the firm — the structure of the Organisation, the Gen-eral Qualifications of Staff and the number of Key Staff only. Curricula Vitae should not be submitted and Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.
The detailed shortlisting requirements, including those applying to a Joint Venture, are set out in the Terms of Reference for this assignment.
6.    The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, Paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” [Procurement in Investment Pro-ject Financing: Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services], dated July 2016 and re-vised September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on “Conflict of Interest”.
7.    In addition, a firm, Joint Venture Member or Sub-Consultant participating in the selection of the Technical Advisor for the SMART Corridor Project (Reference No. ZM-RTSA-564876-CS-QCBS) shall not participate in this selection, whether as a firm, as a Joint Venture Member or as a Sub-Consultant, and the reverse shall apply equally, in order to preserve the independence of the Technical Advisor’s review function.
8.    Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture or a Sub-Consultancy, and in the case of a Joint Venture, which firm is the Lead Member. A Consultant will be selected in accord-ance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regu-lations.
9.    Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 08:00 to 12:30 and from 14:00 to 16:00 hours local time Zambia, Mondays to Fridays inclusive, except for weekends and Public Holidays.
10.    Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form to the address below, in person, by hard copy mail, or by e-mail to alumbuka@rtsa.org.zm with a copy to akchishimba@rtsa.org.zm, not later than 16:00 hours local time on 23rdA September, 2026. E-mail submissions should not exceed 15 MB and should be in PDF format. RTSA will acknowledge in writing the receipt of each Expression of Interest submitted by e-mail; a Consultant not acknowledged shortly after submit-ting should contact Mrs. Agness Lumbuka, using the telephone numbers or e-mail address given below, before the deadline. RTSA will not be responsible for any document not officially received or for any corrupted document.

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

***************

 

Nom du pays :

REPUBLIQUE CENTRAFRICAINE

Nom du projet :

PROJET DU CORRIDOR ÉCONOMIQUE DOUALA-BANGUI (PCE)

Intitulé de la mission :

Recrutement des Experts de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet PCE

N° de référence du STEP :

PCE – 23/SC/IND/26 ; PCE – 24/SC/IND/26 ; PCE – 25/SC/IND/26.

 

  1. La République Centrafricaine a obtenu un Don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour couvrir le coût du Projet du Corridor Economique DOUALA-BANGUI (PCE). L’objectif fondamental de ce programme est d’optimiser l’efficacité des transports et la sécurité routière, tout en transformant durablement le quotidien des communautés riveraines au Cameroun et en RCA. Les impacts économiques attendus sont majeurs, ciblant une baisse des coûts logistiques, un meilleur accès aux marchés et une réduction du prix des denrées et du carburant au profit du pouvoir d’achat des ménages.  

                                                                                                                   

  1. Concernant les activités à mettre en œuvre, il s’agira de : (i) Réhabilitation de l’infrastructure du corridor avec amélioration de la sécurité routière, (ii) Amélioration de l’entretien des routes, (iii) Soutien au développement économique inclusif le long du corridor, (iv) Facilitation des transports et du commerce, renforcement institutionnel et gestion de projet, (v) Composante d’intervention d’urgence.

Le projet se concentre sur le corridor Douala-Bangui qui est un axe vital pour le commerce régional, la sécurité alimentaire et la stabilité économique de l'Afrique Centrale. S'étendant sur plus de 1 400 km, dont environ 802 km au Cameroun, il achemine 80 % du commercer extérieur de la République centrafricaine (RCA) et garantit l'approvisionnement alimentaire, la disponibilité en carburant, l'accès humanitaire et la connectivité des marchés. La RCA, économie fragile et fortement dépendante de son territoire, est essentiellement tributaire de ce corridor pour son accès maritime, ce qui en fait avant tout une voie d'approvisionnement et de résilience stratégique, plutôt qu'un corridor économique pleinement développé.

 

  1. Pour la République Centrafricaine, le Projet est élaboré, le corridor relie les zones agricoles fertiles de l'Est du Cameroun et de l'Ouest de la RCA, productrices de maïs, de riz, de cacao, d'huile de palme et d'élevage, aux marchés, tout en traversant des régions riches en minéraux et en forêts, recelant des ressources en or, en diamants et en bois.

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République Centrafricaine a donc l’intention d’utiliser une partie des ressources du Don pour financer les services des Consultants individuels aux différents postes suivants pour assurer la gestion du Projet du Corridor Economique DOUALA – BANGUI.

 

  1. Les postes de recrutement mis en concurrence sont les suivants :
  • Spécialiste en Passation des Marchés, Réf. : PCE – 23/SC/IND/26 ;
  • Responsable Administratif(ve) et Financier(ère), Réf. : PCE – 24/SC/IND/26 ;
  • Comptable, Réf. : PCE – 24/SC/IND/26.

 

  1. Les tâches exhaustives des Experts sont décrites dans les Termes de Référence de chaque mission et sont à retirer au Secrétariat de la Coordination des Projets PURIC-CA, PRACAC et PCE situé au Ministère de l’Equipement et des Travaux Publics à l’adresse indiquée au point 12 ou envoyer par courrier électronique à la demande des candidats intéressés.

 

  1. La Coordination des Projets invite les candidats (consultants individuels) intéressés à manifester leur intérêt pour les postes décrits ci-dessus.

 

  1. Les Consultants intéressés par chaque poste doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services demandés. Le dossier de candidature comprendra les éléments essentiels suivants :
  • Une lettre de motivation précisant le poste et l’adresse du Candidat (téléphone, Email) ;
  • Un curriculum vitae détaillé, certifié, mis à jour, avec trois (3) références professionnelles à contacter, les copies légalisées des diplômes et attestation de travail datant de moins de trois (3) mois.

 

Les Experts seront recrutés sur la base de leurs qualifications académiques, de leurs expériences professionnelles pertinentes et de leur capacité à réaliser la mission. Les numéros de téléphones valides des écoles/universités fréquentées ainsi que des Employeurs passés et actuels devront être ajoutés au CV.

 

Les étapes du recrutement sont les suivants : (i) comparaison des dossiers de candidature et (ii) entretien/interview. La Coordination se réserve le droit de vérifier l’ensemble des informations fournies par les candidats lors de la procédure de sélection.

 

  1. L est porté à l’attention du Consultant que les dispositions du paragraphe 7.32 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque Mondiale », 7ème édition de Septembre 2025 relatives au recrutement du personnel d’appui à la mise en œuvre des Projets sont applicables. La participation des Fonctionnaires est sujette à l’application des dispositions du paragraphe 3.23 dudit Règlement.

 

  1. Un Consultant sera sélectionné par poste selon la méthode de comparaison des CV telle que décrite dans le Règlement de « Passation des marchés dans le cadre du financement des Projets de Développement « Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants » du 1er Septembre 2025 accessible sur le site Web de la Banque Mondiale sur http: //www.worldbank.org/procurement en cliquant sur « New Policy and Regulations »

 

  1. Les candidats intéressés peuvent obtenir les Termes de Référence de chaque mission à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures des bureaux de 9 heures à 15 heures à compter de la date de publication du présent avis.

 

  1. Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées par porteur sous pli cacheté en trois (3) exemplaires ou envoyer par courrier express au plus tard le Lundi 21 Septembre 2026 à 13 heures, heure locale à l’adresse suivante :

Attention : Monsieur Noël NGOYA, Coordonnateur du PRACAC

Ministère de l’Equipement et des Travaux Publics

B.P. 978 Bangui – République Centrafricaine

Tél. : (+236) 75 56 07 79 / (+236) 75 50 33 17 / (+236) 75 80 08 29

Courriel : ngoyawambai@yahoo.fr / biguekola@yahoo.fr / g.pounaba@yahoo.com / stephanedondri@gmail.com

 

  1. Elles doivent être transmises avec la mention : « Manifestation d’intérêt – Recrutement d’un Consultant individuel au poste de (à préciser) du Projet PCE ».

 

  1. L’ouverture des manifestations est prévue le Lundi 21 Septembre 2026 à 13 heures, heure locale dans la salle de réunion de la Coordination des Projets PURIC-CA, PRACAC et PCE.

 

Le Ministre d’Etat chargé de l’Equipement

et des Travaux Publics.

 

 

 

Arthur Bertrand PIRI

Refª.:                    MZ-CMM-490872-CS-QBS  

 

O Governo de Moçambique recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para o Projecto de Transformação Urbana de Maputo, implementado pelo Conselho Municipal de Maputo, e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para custear as despesas de serviços de consultoria para proceder à Elaboração do Plano de Estrutura Urbana do Município de Maputo (PEUMM), em conformidade com a Lei n.º 19/2007, de 18 de Julho (Lei de Ordenamento do Território) e o respectivo Regulamento, aprovado pelo Decreto n.º 23/2008, de 1 de Julho, com vista a materializar a visão estratégica de desenvolvimento territorial do Município face às transformações urbanas, demográficas, económicas, sociais, ambientais e institucionais ocorridas desde a aprovação do 1.º PEUMM em 2008.

 

Objectivo da Consultoria

A elaboração do PEUMM deverá dotar o Conselho Municipal de Maputo de um instrumento estratégico de ordenamento territorial, operacional e orientado para a implementação, capaz de orientar o crescimento urbano sustentável, promover a utilização eficiente do solo, reforçar a integração entre uso do solo, mobilidade e infra-estruturas, aumentar a resiliência urbana às alterações climáticas e apoiar a programação e coordenação dos investimentos públicos e privados.

Sem prejuízo de outros objectivos que decorram do desenvolvimento da consultoria, a elaboração do novo PEUMM deverá: (i) avaliar o grau de implementação do PEUMM (2008), identificando os principais avanços, constrangimentos, oportunidades e lições aprendidas, com vista ao fortalecimento da sua eficácia enquanto instrumento estratégico de ordenamento territorial; (ii) Elaborar o diagnóstico territorial, urbano, socioeconómico, ambiental, institucional e de mobilidade do Município de Maputo, incorporando as dinâmicas de crescimento urbano, as tendências demográficas, as alterações climáticas, os riscos naturais, a evolução do quadro legal e institucional e os investimentos estruturantes realizados ou em curso; (iii) Elaborar o modelo territorial do Município, definindo a estrutura espacial, o sistema de centralidades, a organização do uso e ocupação do solo, a estrutura ecológica, a rede de infra-estruturas e equipamentos, os corredores de mobilidade e as áreas prioritárias de desenvolvimento, regeneração, densificação, expansão e protecção ambiental; (iv) Assegurar a integração entre o ordenamento do território, o sistema de mobilidade urbana, em particular o Sistema MOVE/BRT, e os demais investimentos estruturantes, promovendo uma ocupação do solo orientada para o transporte público e uma utilização mais eficiente das infra-estruturas urbanas; (v) Definir uma estratégia territorial integrada que promova o desenvolvimento urbano sustentável, a inclusão social, a competitividade económica, a valorização do património natural e cultural, a adaptação às alterações climáticas, a redução do risco de desastres e o reforço da resiliência urbana; (vi) Harmonizar o PEUMM com o quadro legal e regulamentar em vigor, os Instrumentos de Ordenamento Territorial, as políticas públicas, os planos sectoriais e os programas e projectos estratégicos com incidência no território municipal, assegurando a sua coerência e complementaridade; (vii) Estabelecer orientações e directrizes para a elaboração, revisão e implementação dos Instrumentos de Ordenamento Territorial de nível inferior, promovendo uma gestão territorial integrada, articulada e coerente em todo o Município; (viii) Definir prioridades territoriais de investimento, mecanismos de implementação, monitoria, avaliação e revisão do Plano, incluindo um programa de acção faseado, indicadores de desempenho e um quadro institucional que assegure a efectiva operacionalização do PEUMM; (v) Promover um processo de planeamento participativo e inclusivo, envolvendo as instituições públicas, o sector privado, a academia, as organizações da sociedade civil e as comunidades locais, de forma a reforçar a apropriação institucional e social do Plano e a sua exequibilidade, conforme recomendado pela legislação aplicável e pelo PTUM (PEPI, QGAS, QPR e PCAS); (ix) Identificar áreas com potencial impacto de deslocamento físico e/ou económico, propondo princípios orientadores para a sua gestão em fases subsequentes de implementação, em conformidade com o QPR.

Os Termos de Referência (TDR) detalhados para a tarefa, bem como informações adicionais, podem ser obtidos enviando uma solicitação para o e-mail fornecido abaixo.

Perfil do Consultor

O Consultor deverá ser uma pessoa colectiva (empresa de Consultoria) legalmente constituída, com experiência comprovada na prestação de serviços de consultoria em ordenamento do território e planeamento urbano. E com capacidade de mobilizar e garantir a permanência de uma equipa multidisciplinar durante o período afecto à elaboração do plano. A empresa deve demonstrar capacidade para trabalhar em Moçambique, conhecimento do contexto institucional e legal, bem como capacidade para integrar as seguintes áreas: urbanismo e ordenamento do território, mobilidade urbana, infraestruturas urbanas, ambiente, componente social, economia urbana e Sistemas de Informação Geográfica (SIG). Deverá ainda ter disponibilidade de ferramentas e metodologias para análise territorial e espacial (SIG), modelação urbana, planeamento participativo e avaliação ambiental e social.

A empresa deverá estar inscrita no Ministério que superintende a área de Ordenamento Territorial.

 

Os critérios de pré-selecção

(i) mínimo 10 (dez) anos de experiência em ordenamento do território e planeamento urbano, sobretudo na elaboração de instrumentos de ordenamento do território e estratégicos de nível municipal, que tenham sido aprovados e submetidos a ratificação; (ii) Mais deve ter experiência comprovada em países em desenvolvimento, preferencialmente na África Subsaariana e a experiência em Moçambique, será considerada uma vantagem; (iii) Deverá ainda ter experiência em projectos financiados por doadores internacionais; (iv) Participação, nos ultimos 10 (dez) anos, em pelo menos 3 (três) projectos semelhantes, ou seja: elaboração de instrumentos de ordenamento do território de nível municipal, que cubram toda a área municipal e projectos que envolveram a integração de propostas de uso de solo, mobilidade e infraestruturas (água, saneamento, drenagem); (v) Experiência em: i) regularização fundiária (será considerada uma vantagem experiência em assentamentos informais), ii) planeamento participativo (consultas públicas), iii) integração de alterações climáticas e resiliência urbana e iv) desenvolvimento de planos de investimento urbano: (vi). Os principais especialistas não serão avaliados na fase de pré-selecção.

O Conselho Municipal de Maputo convida empresas de consultoria elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse na prestação dos Serviços. Os Consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem possuir as qualificações necessárias e a experiência relevante para a execução dos Serviços.

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para a Seção III, parágrafos 3.13, 3.15 e 3.16 do “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários do IPF” do Banco Mundial, 6ª Edição, fevereiro de 2025, que estabelece a Política do Banco Mundial sobre Conflito de Interesses.

Os consultores podem associar-se a outras empresas para aprimorar suas qualificações e devem indicar claramente se a associação se dá na forma de uma joint venture ou de uma subconsultoria. No caso de uma joint venture, todos os membros da joint venture serão solidariamente responsáveis por todo o contrato, se selecionados.

Um consultor será selecionado de acordo com o método de Seleção Baseada em Qualidade (QBS) estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições.

As Manifestações de Interesse, incluindo os documentos comprobatórios, devem ser entregues por e-mail para o endereço fornecido abaixo, até 16 de Sertembro de 2026.

Le Gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a reçu un don de l’Association internationale de développement (IDA) du Groupe de la Banque mondiale dans le cadre d’un Pré-Programme destiné à l’identification et à la mise en œuvre d’activités visant à améliorer le cadre urbain des villes secondaires et a l’intention d’affecter une partie des ressources de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif aux services de consultants décrits ci-dessus.

Sous l’autorité du Coordonnateur de la Cellule de Coordination des Projets d’Urbanisme (CPU) et en étroite collaboration avec les autres spécialistes de la Cellule, l’Expert(e) Urbaniste a pour mission principale d’appuyer les phases d’élaboration et de mise en œuvre du Programme de Développement des Villes Secondaires (PDVS), lequel vise à améliorer les conditions de vie des populations par une planification et une gestion urbaine de qualité. À ce titre, il ou elle coordonne les tâches des différents intervenants, impulse une stratégie cohérente et assure l’articulation des différentes activités urbaines programmées dans le cadre du PDVS, sur la base d’une vision cohérente d’aménagement et de planification urbaine.

Les Termes de Référence (TDR) détaillés relatifs à la mission de l’Expert (e) Urbaniste, font partie intégrante du présent avis d’appel à manifestations d’intérêt et sont joints en annexe à celui-ci.

Le Ministère de l’Urbanisme et Habitat, agissant à travers la Cellule de Coordination des Projets d’Urbanisme (CPU), avec l’appui de l’UG-PURUK invite les consultants indiviuels, à manifester leur intérêt pour la prestation des services décrits ci-dessus. Les candidats intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications et l’expérience requises. Les critères de présélection sont les suivants :

  1. Formation académique :
  • Être titulaire au minimum d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau BAC+5 (master, licence de type long, ingéniorat ou équivalent) en urbanisme, aménagement du territoire, planification du développement, programmation urbaine, architecture, géographie urbaine, économie urbaine ou toute autre discipline équivalente ;
  • Une spécialisation ou une formation complémentaire en développement urbain durable, en gestion de projets urbains ou en résilience urbaine constitue un atout.
  1. Expérience professionnelle :
  • Justifier d’une expérience professionnelle générale d’au moins sept (07) ans dans le secteur de l’urbanisme, des infrastructures, du transport, du développement urbain, des corridors de développement ou de tout autre secteur pertinent ;
  • Justifier d’au moins cinq (05) ans d’expérience spécifique dans la conception, la programmation ou la gestion de projets urbains ;
  • Avoir participé à au moins deux (02) missions d’études ou de projets de développement urbain financés par des bailleurs de fonds internationaux (Banque mondiale, BAD, UE ou autres) ;
  • Une expérience de la conduite ou de la supervision de documents de planification urbaine (schéma directeur, plan d’urbanisme, plan d’aménagement) est exigée ;
  • Une expérience en milieu urbain congolais et une bonne connaissance des villes secondaires de la RDC constituent un atout majeur.

Les candidats présélectionnés pourront être invités à un entretien destiné à confirmer leurs qualifications et leur aptitude à accomplir la mission. Le candidat ayant obtenu le meilleur score sera retenu.

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.13, 3.15 et 3.16 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement », édition de septembre 2025, qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.

Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuels (INDV), conformément aux dispositions des paragraphes 7.36 et 7.37 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI), septième édition, septembre 2025.

Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées en langue française, accompagnées de toutes les pièces justificatives de qualification (lettre de motivation précisant l’intitulé exact du poste, le curriculum vitae détaillé et daté (10 pages maximum), faisant apparaître pour chaque expérience la période exacte, l’employeur, l’intitulé du poste et les tâches réalisées ; copies des diplômes et attestations de formation, attestations de services rendus, Les noms et coordonnées complètes de trois (03) personnes de référence professionnelle, Une copie de la pièce d’identité en cours de validité etc.), doivent être transmises par voie électronique en un seul fichier en format PDF au plus tard le 14 septembre 2026 à 15h00 (heure locale de Kananga), à l’adresse ci-dessous, avec la mention : ZR-CPU-564194-CS-INDV–Recrutement d’un (e) Expert (e) Urbaniste de la CPU

The Government of Grenada has received financing from the World Bank towards the costs of the Caribbean Resilient Renewable Energy Infrastructure Investment Facility (RREIIF) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to eligible payments for consulting services under the project to support the ESIA for the Dual Circuit Transmission lines, substations and solar PV.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will be responsible for assessing the environmental and social impacts of the proposed transmission lines, substations (the project) and the potential Solar PV farm with associated Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at Pearls through an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and provide mitigation measures in an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP). The ESMP will be used by the Owners Engineer and design, construction, and operational contractors of the Project according to the policies of the World Bank and the Ministry of Climate Resilience.

The Contract duration is Five (5) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.procurement.gd  or through our E-Procurement Portal https://in-tendhost.co.uk/gnd/aspx/HOME

The Central Procurement Unit acting on behalf of The Ministry of Climate Resilience now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Firm Requirements

  • The firm should have a minimum of 4-5 years of demonstrated experience in conducting ESIAs and ESMPs for infrastructure projects. 
  • The firm must have prior experience in the energy sector, and ideally in electricity transmission and distribution infrastructure projects and/or solar projects. It should be able to demonstrate completion of at least one to two ESIAs of comparable nature, with references and project descriptions included in the proposal. 

Team Lead/ Environmental Specialist

  • Master's Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resource Management, or a related field. 
  • Minimum of eight (8) years of professional experience in environmental assessment and management.  
  • Minimum of three (3) years of project and team management experience.

Social Development Specialist

  • Master's Degree in Social Sciences, Sociology, Anthropology, Development Studies, Social Development, or a related field.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in social impact assessment and social risk management.
  • Familiarity with the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (ESS), particularly ESS1, ESS2, ESS4, ESS5, and ESS10.

General Experience

  • Experience working in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or the Caribbean region would be an advantage.

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

RECRUTTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL POUR L’AUDIT DE LA PERFORMANCE DES ACTIVITES DE PASSATION DE MARCHES DU PROJET NEDA

 

 

Le Gouvernement de la République de Côte d’Ivoire, à travers le ministère des Mines, du Pétrole, et de l’Energie et Côte d’Ivoire Energies (CI ENERGIES) a obtenu un crédit de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA), pour le financement de l’Opération Nationale de Numérisation et d’Accès à l’électricité en Côte d’Ivoire (NEDA), et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit pour le recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour l’audit de la performance des activités de passation de marches du projet NEDA.

Les services de consultant (« Services ») porte sur la vérification de la performance des procédures de passation de marchés et de la gestion des contrats du volet PforR au regard des dispositions de l’Accord de financement (AF) et telles qu'elles figurent dans les Plans de passation de marchés. Plus spécifiquement il s’agira de:

  • Vérifier la conformité du processus de passation de marchés, d'appel d'offres et d'évaluation des offres avec les dispositions de l'Accord de Financement, les Plans de passation de marchés, les dispositions de la loi et des règlements en matière de passation de marchés. À cet effet, l’auditeur vérifiera:
  • La conformité avec les mandats légaux et institutionnels, les règlements, les politiques, et les procédures ;
  • La cohérence entre les Plans de passation de marchés et les progrès réels dans la mise en œuvre ;
  • L’efficacité des contrôles internes appropriés couvrant la planification de la passation de marchés, les méthodes et procédures d'appel d'offres correspondantes et les processus d'exécution, y compris les processus de validation, d'approbation et de gestion des contrats ; et
  • La gestion des contrats, soit les amendements, les paiements, les réclamations et les calendriers de mise en œuvre.
  • Vérifier la conformité de la qualité technique et des quantités livrées conformément aux conditions du contrat tout en assurant la fiabilité et l'intégrité des informations financières et opérationnelles relatives aux réalisations, notamment :
  • Le caractère raisonnable des prix unitaires des contrats ;
  • La conformité du contrat final avec les documents de sollicitation approuvés, notamment en ce qui concerne la validité des addendas, des ordres de modification et de toute autre modification apportée au contrat initial pendant son exécution ; et
  • Relever les risques concernant le respect des principes de passation de marchés, le contrôle, les compétences et la capacité de gestion du personnel de l'Organe d’Exécution, et plus généralement ceux liés au système national.
  • Évaluer la capacité globale de l'Organe d’Exécution pour confirmer qu’elle est conforme à l'évaluation faite lors de la phase d'évaluation du projet. L'évaluation est fondée sur un triple processus de diligence raisonnable couvrant l'Organe d’Exécution sur la base d'une évaluation des performances passées et des antécédents opérationnels : 1) respect du cadre juridique et institutionnel du pays et des autres obligations légales et réglementaires ; 2) capacité qualitative et quantitative globale en termes de structure organisationnelle, de procédures internes, de ressources et de personnel qualifié ; et 3) capacité à mener à bien les processus de passation de marchés de manière diligente, efficace et efficiente.

            L'examen et l'analyse de chaque contrat sélectionné et la détermination de la conformité des mesures prises par l'Organe d’Exécution du projet avec les lois et règlements des PMR en matière de passation de marchés et de l'Accord de Financement.

 

La durée globale de la mission d’audit est estimée à dix (10) semaines

 

Les Termes de Référence (TDR) pour les prestations peuvent être téléchargés sur le site web suivant : https:// https://www.cinergies.ci/category/avis-communiques/ ou en faisant la requête par mail à akotchi@cinergies.ci avec en copie sdiarrassouba@cinergies.ci, jjassamoa@cinergies.ci, yamata@cinergies.ci et ckoffi@cinergies.ci.

L’unité de Gestion du projet d’Opération Nationale de Numérisation et d’Accès à l’électricité en Côte d’Ivoire (NEDA), invite dès à présent les candidats admissibles à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services décrits ci-dessus. Les candidats intéressés doivent fournir dans leur dossier une lettre de manifestations d’intérêts et les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

 Le Consultant doit démontrer les expériences et les compétences suivantes :

 

 

  • avoir fait au minimum cinq (05) années d’études universitaire et être titulaire d’un Master ou Ingénieur ou diplôme équivalent
  • être un auditeur qualifié et expérimenté en audit de passation des marchés publics. Une certification reconnue internationalement en passation des marchés serait un atout.
  • disposer d’au moins cinq (05) ans d’expérience professionnelle en passation de marchés suivant le système national ivoirien de passation de marchés.
  • avoir réalisé au moins quatre (04) missions d’audit de passation de marchés publics en qualité de chef de mission dont trois (03) en audit de passation des marchés dans un pays de l’espace UEMOA.
  • parler couramment le français.

.

L’attention des candidats intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale de septembre 2025 (‘’Règlement de Passation des Marchés’’), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.

 

Le consultant individuel sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuel (CI) par appel à manifestation telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

  1. L’Etat du Sénégal a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet de Gestion des Ressources naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché n° F_SENRM/ENV_009 (Réf. SYGMAP : F_SENRM_001) relatif à l’acquisition d’équipements pour l’extension du réseau de mesure de la qualité de l’air. Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera la méthode de décaissement par Paiement Direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement, à l’exception des paiements pour lesquels le marché prévoit l’utilisation de crédit documentaire. 
  2. Le Projet de Gestion des Ressources naturelles au Sénégal sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir les équipements pour l’extension du réseau de mesure de la qualité de l’air et réaliser les travaux connexes y relatifs pour les quantités et, suivant le délai de livraison et au lieu indiqués dans le dossier d’appel d’offres (DAO).

 Les exigences en matière de qualification sont :

a. Capacité financière :

Le Candidat doit fournir la preuve écrite qu’il satisfait aux exigences ci-après :

- Fournir les états financiers des trois dernières années (2023, 2024 et 2025), démontrant la solidité actuelle de la situation financière du Soumissionnaire. Dans le cas d’un groupement d’entreprises (GE), cette exigence doit être respectée par chaque membre, dûment certifiés par un expert-comptable ou un cabinet agréé par l’ONECCA (Ordre National des Experts Comptables et Comptables Agréés) du Sénégal ou un organisme assimilé.

- Avoir réalisé un chiffre d’affaires annuel moyen au cours de chacune des trois (03) dernières années (2023, 2024 et 2025) au moins égal à quatre milliards cinq cent millions (4 500 000 000) FCFA ;

- Fournir une attestation de capacité financière ou ligne de crédit délivrée par un organisme bancaire, d’un montant d’un milliard cinq cent millions (1 500 000 000) FCFA.

                           b. Capacité technique et Expérience :

Le candidat doit prouver, document à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences de capacité technique ci-après :

Prouver, documentation à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences d’expérience ci-après : 

 

  • Deux (02) marchés similaires exécutés par le candidat au cours des cinq (05) dernières années (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 et 2025) pour un montant au moins égal à deux milliards quatre cent millions (2 400 000 000) FCFA.
  • Apporter la preuve qu’il dispose au Sénégal d’un service après-vente de qualité pour l’entretien et la réparation des fournitures qu’il propose. Il en donnera les principales indications pour permettre au client de se déplacer pour en visiter les installations. Le soumissionnaire doit disposer d’un technicien supérieur en électromécanique (Cv à joindre).

Ministère deS MINES ET DE LA GEOLOGIE (MMG)

MINISTERE DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT ET DU DEVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (MEDD) PROJET DE GESTION DES RESSOURCES NATURELLES, MINIERES ET DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT (PGRNME)

 CREDIT IDA N° 6885 – GN ET DON IDA N° 8190 -GN

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR L’ÉLABORATION DES PLANS DE RESTAURATION DES SITES D’ORPAILLAGE DANS LES PREFECTURES DE SIGUIRI, MANDIANA, KOUROUSSA, DINGUIRAYE ET KANKAN EN FAVEUR DE L’AGEE

SMI N°09/PGRNME/MEDD/C/2026

       Date de fin : 16 Septembre 2026

Le Gouvernement de la République de Guinée a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir les coûts du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles, Minières et de l’Environnement (PGRNME), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce CREDIT IDA N° 6885 – GN et du DON IDA N° 8190 -GN pour effectuer des paiements au titre de services de consultants pour : la Recrutement d’un cabinet pour l’élaboration des plans de restauration des sites d’orpaillage dans les préfectures de Siguiri, Mandiana, Kouroussa, Dinguiraye et Kankan en faveur de l’AGEE.

Objectif de la Mission

Élaborer des Plans de restauration environnementale et sociale des sites d'orpaillage dégradés dans les préfectures de Siguiri, Mandiana, Kouroussa, Dinguiraye et Kankan, fondés sur des diagnostics techniques, environnementaux et socio-économiques, afin de restaurer durablement les écosystèmes dégradés, réduire les risques environnementaux et sociaux et fournir aux autorités compétentes des outils de planification et de mise en œuvre des actions de réhabilitation.

De façon spécifique, il s’agit de:

  • Actualiser et compléter les diagnostics environnementaux et sociaux réalisés par l'AGEE afin de caractériser l'état des sites d'orpaillage, les types de dégradations et les risques associés.
  • Identifier, analyser et hiérarchiser les impacts environnementaux, sociaux, sanitaires, sécuritaires et économiques liés aux activités d'orpaillage sur chaque site.
  • Évaluer les contraintes biophysiques, hydrologiques, géotechniques, foncières et socio-économiques susceptibles d'influencer les opérations de restauration.
  • Définir des scénarios de restauration adaptés aux caractéristiques de chaque site, en privilégiant des solutions techniques durables, économiquement viables et socialement acceptables.
  • Élaborer des plans détaillés de restauration intégrant notamment :
      • les techniques de reprofilage et de stabilisation des terrains ;
      • la restauration des sols et des cours d'eau ;
      • la revégétalisation avec des espèces locales adaptées ;
      •  les mesures de protection de la biodiversité ;
      • les mesures de gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux.
  • Proposer un programme de mise en œuvre comprenant les priorités d'intervention, le calendrier d'exécution, les coûts estimatifs, les modalités de financement et les responsabilités des différentes parties prenantes.
  • Définir un dispositif de suivi-évaluation comprenant des indicateurs de performance, des mécanismes de suivi environnemental et social ainsi que les modalités de contrôle de l'efficacité des actions de restauration.
  • Assurer la participation effective des collectivités territoriales, des services techniques déconcentrés, des communautés locales, des exploitants artisanaux et des autres parties prenantes tout au long du processus d'élaboration des plans.
  • Produire des Plans de restauration conformes aux exigences de la réglementation nationale, aux orientations de l'AGEE et aux Normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale, afin de servir de référence pour la mise en œuvre des futurs programmes de réhabilitation des sites d'orpaillage.

Les Termes de Références (TDRs) détaillés de la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

L’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles, Minières et de l’Environnement (PGRNME) invite les firmes de consultants (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

  • Expérience générale :
  • Avoir de l’expertise dans l’évaluations environnementales et sociales, en conception et élaboration de projets de réhabilitation et de restauration écologique et de projets socio-économiques.
  • Le Cabinet doit justifier d'au moins 10 années d'expérience dans les domaines de l'environnement, des ressources naturelles, des mines ou du développement durable.
  • Expérience spécifique :

Le cabinet devra avoir réalisé, au cours des dix (10) dernières années, au moins dans les domaines de l'environnement, des ressources naturelles, des mines ou du développement durable

  • Trois (3) missions de réhabilitation ou de restauration de sites miniers ou de sites d'orpaillage ; ou cinq (5) missions portant sur des études environnementales et sociales (EIES, audits environnementaux, plans de fermeture de mines, plans de restauration, plans de gestion environnementale et sociale) appliquées au secteur minier.
  • Une expérience en Afrique de l'Ouest, et en particulier en Guinée, constituera un atout important.
  • Disposer d’une capacité technique et administrative en présentant les pièces requises (Agrément/RCCM, Organisation/organigramme).

Ce qui pourrait correspondre à la répartition ci-après :

  • Expérience générale (20 points) ;       
  •  Expériences spécifique (70 points) ; et
  • Capacité technique (10 points).

Le personnel clé ne sera pas évalué lors de l'établissement de la liste restreinte.

  2. Aucune entreprise engagée par l’emprunteur pour fournir des Services de Consultants pour la préparation ou l’exécution d’un projet (ni aucune entreprise affiliée qui contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’elle contrôle elle-même ou qui est placée sous un contrôle commun) n’est admise ultérieurement à livrer des Fournitures réaliser des Travaux ou fournit des Services Autres que des Services de Consultants consécutifs ou directement liés audits Services de Consultants. Cette disposition ne s’applique pas aux diverses entreprises (consultant, entrepreneurs ou fournisseurs) qui, collectivement, s’acquittent des obligations de l’adjudicataire d’un marché clés en main ou d’un marché de conception construction ;
  3. Aucun Consultant (y compris le personnel et les sous-consultants à son service) ni aucun prestataire affilié (qui le contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’il contrôle lui-même ou qui est placé sous un contrôle commun) ne peut être engagé pour une mission qui par sa nature, crée un conflit d’intérêt avec une autre de ses missions ;
  4. Les Consultants (y compris les experts, le personnel et les sous-consultants à leur service) qui ont une relation professionnelle ou familiale étroite avec tout cadre de l’Emprunteur, de l’organisme d’exécution du projet, d’un bénéficiaire d’une fraction du financement de la ou de toute autre partie représentant l’Emprunteur ou agissant en son nom qui participe directement ou indirectement à tout segment :

CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO BUSINESS ADVISORY SERVICES TO BENEFICIARIES (GRANTEES) OF GENDER INCLUSIVE WORKPLACE INFRASTRUCTURE

Reference No.: MGLSD-GROW/CONS/25-26/00071-UG-MOGLSD-547665-CS-CQS Issued on: August 13, 2026

The Government of the Republic of Uganda has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of implementing the Generating Growth Opportunities and Productivity for Women Enterprises (GROW) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services.

The Project Development Objective is to increase access to entrepreneurial services that enable women entrepreneurs to grow their enterprises in targeted locations, including host and refugee communities. The Project is being implemented by the Ministry of Gender, Labor and Social Development (MGLSD) jointly with Private Sector Foundation Uganda (PSFU) as an implementing Entity.

Under subcomponent three (3A & 3B) the project intends to Establish and Equip Common User Production Facilities (CUPFs) and Enable Access to Gender-Inclusive Workplace Infrastructure respectively. It will provide grants to support innovation and business expansion for women-owned businesses through the establishment of common user production facilities. The aim is to provide demand-driven infrastructure and facilities to improve productivity of women as a step towards enterprise growth and transition. The target beneficiaries include women entrepreneurs who are managing micro and small businesses. Approximately 25,000 female entrepreneurs, including from refugee-hosting districts, are expected to benefit from this intervention for target beneficiary reach projection.

The implementation of this subcomponent will be done by the MGLSD with technical support from the Business Advisory Services firm

The Consulting Services ("the Service") include Consultancy services to provider Business advisory services to beneficiaries of Gender Inclusive Workplace Infrastructure and Common User Production Facilities (CUPFs) beneficiary enterprises for Lot 1 – Central Region, Lot 2- Northern Region, Lot 3- Western Region, Lot 4- Easter Region. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at https://mglsd.go.ug/procurement/

The Ministry of Gender, Labor and Social Development now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria is as follows:

  1. At least five (5) years’ proven experience in providing business advisory, enterprise development, business incubation, MSME support programmes or related consultancy services.
  2. Demonstrated experience in business planning, business model development, sustainability planning, financial management and operational strengthening for MSMEs, cooperatives, shared production facilities or similar enterprises.
  3. Proven experience in market systems development, value chain strengthening, market feasibility assessments and enterprise growth strategies in sectors such as agro-processing, dairy, leather, crafts or related productive sectors.
  4. Demonstrated experience in designing and delivering capacity-building, mentoring and technical assistance programmes for entrepreneurs, business associations, incubators or enterprise support institutions.
  5. Experience in grants management, financial oversight, operational efficiency improvement and support to enterprises funded by Government, Development Partners or Donor-funded programmes.
  6. At least five (5) years’ experience in implementing and monitoring Environmental and Social (E&S) safeguards, including stakeholder engagement, grievance redress mechanisms (GRM), occupational health and safety, and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) risk mitigation.
  7. Demonstrated experience working with Government Ministries, Development Partners, private sector organizations and multi-stakeholder programmes supporting women’s economic empowerment, entrepreneurship and MSME growth.
  8. Experience in monitoring, supervision and reporting for donor-funded projects, including establishment of performance monitoring systems and preparation of analytical and implementation reports.
     

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers July 2016” Seventh Edition, September 2025 “Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
